author: tobikrs
body:
Fixes #1695

Memories did not appear in the Android system gallery chooser when tapping a camera
thumbnail, using "Open with" from a file manager, or selecting media in app pickers.

## Approach

A new `ViewerActivity` is registered as the entry point for all incoming media intents.
On launch it resolves the incoming `content://` URI against MediaStore and the local
Room DB, then routes to one of three modes:

- **Mode A** (user is logged in + file is synced): redirects to `MainActivity` with a
  `#v/{dayId}/{localId}` hash, opening the photo directly in the Memories WebView viewer.
  `ViewerActivity` finishes immediately and is never visible.
- **Mode B** (file not synced / offline): full-screen native viewer with ViewPager2 swipe
  navigation, pinch-zoom images (PhotoView), video playback (ExoPlayer), share, and delete.
  An "Open in Memories" FAB triggers the Mode A redirect when the user later logs in.
- **Mode C** (picker intent): same native viewer as Mode B, but the toolbar shows a
  "Use this" action instead of share/delete, and returns the URI to the calling app via
  `setResult`.

## Intent filters added to `ViewerActivity`

| Action | Use case |
|---|---|
| `com.android.camera.action.REVIEW` | Camera thumbnail tap (legacy camera apps) |
| `android.provider.action.REVIEW` | Camera thumbnail tap (Android 10+ / Google Camera) |
| `ACTION_VIEW image/*` + `video/*` | "Open with" from file manager or share sheet |
| `ACTION_PICK` | Media picker (e.g. attach photo in messaging apps) |
| `ACTION_GET_CONTENT` | Media picker (alternative intent) |

`MainActivity` is changed to `singleTask` so that a Mode A redirect brings the existing
instance to the foreground rather than creating a second one.

## Other changes

- **`MediaResolverService`**: resolves a `content://` URI to structured media metadata
  (MediaStore `_ID`, `auid`, `dayId`, MIME type) by querying MediaStore then Room DB.
- **`PlayerController`**: ExoPlayer logic extracted from `MainActivity` into a reusable
  class (local URIs, remote HTTP/HLS, error fall-through). Both `MainActivity` and
  `ViewerActivity` use it.
- **`MainActivity`**: gains a `pendingPhotoHash` field consumed in `onNewIntent()`,
  `loadDefaultUrl()`, and `onPageFinished()` to handle the Mode A deep-link reliably
  regardless of whether the WebView has already finished loading.
- PhotoView (`com.github.chrisbanes:PhotoView:2.3.0`) added as dependency for pinch-zoom.

## Reviewer notes

- Mode A uses the URL hash as the deep-link mechanism because it is the only way to open
  a specific photo in the Memories frontend (Vue Router watches `#v/{dayId}/{fileid}`).
- In Mode B, swipe navigation loads all photos for the same day from Room DB and positions
  the pager at the current photo. When the file is not in the DB, a single-item pager is
  shown with swiping disabled.
- Delete uses `MediaStore.createTrashRequest()` on API 30+ and direct deletion on older
  versions. On success the item is removed from the pager; if no items remain, the activity
  finishes.

author: brandonpayton
body:
## Purpose

Support fixed-resolution native KMS/GLES applications in the browser presentation path without app-specific scaling or rendering behavior. The core feature is not LOVE-specific: Kandelo now lets a KMS consumer render at its intended connector mode while the browser UI stretches that scanout to the available canvas area, and the WebGL-backed GLES bridge exposes the render-target formats needed by native GLES renderers.

LOVE/BYTEPATH/SNKRX remain in this PR as consumers and regression fixtures. They are the applications that exposed the bug, but the runtime fixes are generic KMS/GLES behavior rather than a LOVE-only renderer path.

The immediate regression was BYTEPATH rendering its 480x270 game through RGBA4 canvases because Kandelo did not advertise RGBA8 render-target support on the GLES query path. BYTEPATH uses neutral 127-gray displacement maps for RGB glitch shaders; RGBA4 quantization moved that neutral value far enough to produce exaggerated red/green/blue copies. Advertising the equivalent GLES capability (`GL_OES_rgb8_rgba8`) keeps native renderers on RGBA8 targets and restores the intended small channel separation.

## Changes

- Expose `GL_OES_rgb8_rgba8` from the WebGL-backed GLES query path so native GLES renderers can use RGBA8 render targets.
- Make `glReadPixels` handle packed, 16-bit, and 32-bit formats with correct byte sizing and chunked reads under the GL query cap.
- Match browser `readPixels` destination typed arrays to packed GL types, including unaligned output spans.
- Replace the earlier KMS `maxCssScale` presentation knob with generic `presentation.kms.fit: "contain" | "stretch"` metadata.
- Let KMS demo metadata declare fixed target-resolution scanouts that the browser canvas can stretch, leaving user software at its original target resolution.
- Add a Chromium browser regression test that boots BYTEPATH gameplay through the native KMS/GLES path, captures the raw KMS canvas, and asserts full-pane fill plus bounded RGB channel separation.
- Keep the LOVE native package on the upstream renderer and document the browser presentation contract.

## Why LOVE Is Still In The PR

This PR is non-LOVE-specific at the platform layer, but it still carries LOVE package and demo metadata because that is the current end-to-end proof. BYTEPATH and SNKRX exercise fixed-resolution KMS presentation, GLES render-target selection, shader-driven post-processing, and browser canvas scaling in a way the simpler framebuffer demos do not.

There is no Kandelo runtime branch that detects BYTEPATH, SNKRX, or LOVE to fake success. The LOVE-specific pieces are package/build inputs and demo metadata for real consumers of the generic KMS/GLES path.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `git diff --check` | passed |
| `scripts/dev-shell.sh bash scripts/build-gles-stubs.sh` | passed |
| `scripts/dev-shell.sh bash packages/registry/love/build-love.sh` | passed; patch applies and `love.wasm` rebuilds |
| `scripts/dev-shell.sh bash images/vfs/scripts/build-shell-vfs-image.sh` | passed; shell VFS rebuilt with LOVE runtime |
| `../scripts/dev-shell.sh npx vitest run test/webgl-bridge.test.ts` from `host/` | passed: 25 tests |
| `scripts/dev-shell.sh npx vitest run web-libs/kandelo-session/test/kandelo-session.test.ts` | passed: 46 tests |
| `../../scripts/dev-shell.sh env KANDELO_PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=5424 CI=1 npx playwright test test/kandelo-kms-gles-rendering.spec.ts --project=chromium` from `apps/browser-demos/` | passed |

Final BYTEPATH browser capture from the renamed Playwright run:

| Capture | Backing store | CSS rect | Fill | RGB shift |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10s gameplay | 480x270 | 2048x1045 | width=1, height=1 | rg=1, rb=2 |
| 22s gameplay | 480x270 | 2048x1045 | width=1, height=1 | rg=1, rb=2 |

The same browser run syslog showed the normal native renderer path only:

- `love: using KMS/EGL/GLES presenter on /dev/dri/card0`
- `love: using upstream LÖVE OpenGL renderer on Kandelo KMS/EGL`

## Contract Notes

- Browser-facing KMS presentation behavior changed through image metadata.
- Host WebGL behavior changed for the browser KMS path. Node-visible POSIX behavior is unchanged.
- ABI was not changed.
- Package source/build inputs changed; local LOVE and shell VFS artifacts were rebuilt for validation, but binary release indexes were not published.

## Not Run

- Full browser Playwright suite.
- POSIX/libc/Sortix conformance suites.
- Full `./run.sh browser` end-to-end manual flow.

author: zerbina
body:
## Summary

Replace the diagnostic-based error recovery for symbol production with
creating a recovery symbol right away, which is a lot simpler.

## Details

1. turn `newSymGNode` from a procedure returning a node into one
   returning a symbol, and rename the procedure to `produceSymbol`.
   Errors are emitted right away, with the recovery symbol returned
   directly
2. update all callsites of the former `newSymGNode`; they don't need to
   handle error recovery anymore 
3. remove the now-obsolete routines for working with potentially
   erroneous symbol nodes (`defNameErrorNodeAllowsSymUpdate` and
   `getDefNameSymOrRecover`)
4. remove the diagnostics meant for carrying recovery symbols
5. add an `emit` procedure to the `errorhandling` module, for emitting
   diagnostics directly and without going through `newError`. This
   means that it's now possible for diagnostics that have no
   `wrongNode` attached to reach diagnostic handling
6. add a dedicated variant for `adSemDotOperatorsNotEnabled` and
   `adSemCallOperatorsNotEnabled`, so that they don't rely on the
   diagnostic having an attached `wrongNode`

For the AST produced by type-checking, this means that there's always a
valid `nkSym` node in symbol definition positions, even if the
untyped AST at that position is bogus (e.g., not an identifier, some
illegal symbol, etc.).

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

PR 1 of 3 for #626. Replaces `ClusterFactorCurve`'s linear-domain sigmoid (calibrated in simulator units, `w_mid=10M`) with the **normative log-domain construction** from the architect's sign-off-approved spec (last comment on #626), consumed in on-chain **picocredits**. This fixes the step-function collapse where all 463 live-testnet clusters were pinned at ~6x, and de-quantizes the factor (old code snapped to whole multipliers and capped at 5000, `fee_curve.rs:675`).

Implemented **exactly** as specified — the integer algorithm IS the curve definition.

## What changed

**`ClusterFactorCurve` (consensus curve)**
- `log2_fp(w)`: `127 - leading_zeros` integer part + top-16 mantissa bits (Q16), pure `const fn`, no floats
- `z_fp = log2_fp(W) - LOG2_WMID_FP`; `x = (z_fp * 1000) / 131_072` (i64 truncating division, normative); shared 7-knot sigmoid LUT with **tails changed to exact saturation** (`x ≤ −6000 → 0`, `x ≥ 6000 → 65536`)
- output `1000 + (5000 * σ) / 65536`; `W = 0 → 1000` exactly; midpoint (100k BTH) `→ 3500` exactly
- fields `w_mid`/`steepness` → `w_mid_pico: u128`/`log_width_fp: u64`
- **compile-time locks**: `W_MID_PICO == 100_000 * PICO_PER_BTH` (=1e17) and `LOG2_WMID_FP == 3_695_429`

**API widened u64 → u128.** `ClusterFactorCurve::factor` and `ZkFeeCurve::factor` take u128 picocredit wealth. Call sites (mempool / lottery / demurrage / store) pass `w as u128` for now; `FeeConfig` wrappers stay u64 and cast internally. **The `cluster_wealth_db` u128 widening is PR 2 and is NOT in this PR.**

**`ZkFeeCurve` re-anchored** to 5 segments at power-of-two multiples of `W_MID_PICO`: boundaries `[0, W>>8, W>>3, W<<3, W<<8, u128::MAX]`, factors `[1000, 1090, 2071, 4928, 5909, 6000]` (sampled from the sigmoid). Boundaries/`SegmentParams` widened to u128; ZK prover (`committed_tags.rs`, Phase-2 provisional) casts `wealth as u128` and saturates diffs.

**Doc fix**: `nanoBTH → picocredits` labels in `FeeConfig` (same unit-bug class, doc-only).

## Tests (all green)

- **Golden-vector** (`test_golden_vector_factor_table`): exact table — 0/10 BTH→1000, 100→1050, 1k→1265, 10k→1939, 100k→3500, 1M→5093, 10M→5745, ≥409.6M & `u128::MAX`→6000
- **Testnet baseline**: 50 BTH→1030, 97.5 BTH→1049 (the live median/max clusters, was 6x)
- **Monotonicity**: 200k random u128 pairs + exhaustive octave-boundary sweep (2^k−1/2^k/2^k+1, all k)
- **Unit-consistency guard**: `factor(50 BTH) < 1100`
- **LUT saturation tails**, `log2_fp` reference values, constant locks, ZkFeeCurve boundary/monotonicity/agreement

`cargo test -p bth-cluster-tax --lib`: **425 passed, 0 failed**. Doctests 5/0. `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

## ⚠️ Spec discrepancies flagged (not improvised — surfaced for the architect)

1. **ZkFeeCurve↔sigmoid agreement bound.** Spec §4 prose estimated ±450 (0.45x); the **measured max divergence is 1243 (~1.24x)** at 2^57 (~144k BTH), inside the wide central segment `[W>>3, W<<3]` where linear-in-W lags the log curve hardest. The boundaries/factors are the normative spec, so I kept them and set the agreement-test tolerance to the honest measured bound (≤1300), with a comment. **Phase-2 should either narrow segments or declare which curve is normative.**
2. **ZkFeeCurve `SegmentParams::slope_scaled` truncates to 0** at pico scale (segment widths 1e14..1e19 ≫ `SLOPE_SCALE`=1e12). `ZkFeeCurve::factor()` is unaffected (interpolates directly, not via slope), so the factor table is correct — but the Phase-2 ZK linear-relation proof needs a larger `SLOPE_SCALE`. Flagged in a test comment.

Both are Phase-2 / provisional territory per the spec; neither affects the consensus `ClusterFactorCurve`.

## Consensus impact

Consensus-breaking — changes the C7 fee floor, lottery tilt, and mempool progressive fee. **Rides the bundled protocol-4.0.0 testnet reset.** PR 2 (u128 `cluster_wealth_db` ledger widening) and PR 3 (sim harness that exercises the real curve) follow.

Updates #626

author: atoussec-ctrl
body:
## Summary

A consolidated round of hardening, a real LLM client for the AI/RAG module, a full challenge-compliance review with backlog/roadmap, and CI quality gates — all verified end-to-end across every layer.

### Security & robustness
- CORS allowlist via `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (was wide-open), Helmet headers, and rate limiting through `@nestjs/throttler` with a custom `GqlThrottlerGuard` (the stock guard crashed every GraphQL operation).
- GraphQL query-depth cap (`graphql-depth-limit`).
- Patched the fixable high-severity transitive vulns via pnpm overrides (`multer >=2.2.0`, `ws >=8.21.0`); the LangSmith advisories are consciously ignored with justification in `auditConfig.ignoreGhsas` (they need a coordinated LangChain major upgrade, tracked as SEC-01).
- New CI step `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` fails the build on new high/critical vulnerabilities.
- **Bug fixed:** the AI REST DTOs (`content`/`question`) were unvalidated — empty input passed the global `ValidationPipe`. Now validated (400 on blank/missing), verified live.

### Performance
- Resolved the `User.orders` GraphQL N+1 with a per-request DataLoader (one repository call per operation, proven by test).

### AI/RAG — real LLM client
- New `LlmPort` with adapters for OpenAI, OpenRouter (both via `@langchain/openai`), Ollama (`@langchain/ollama`) and HuggingFace Inference API (`@huggingface/inference`), selected by `LLM_PROVIDER`; `createChatModel` fails fast on a missing/unknown provider or missing key.
- `LlmAnalysisModel` implements `AnalysisModelPort` for real; without `LLM_PROVIDER` the module keeps the placeholder (no credentials needed in dev/CI).
- Per-call observability (provider/model/duration/outcome) wired to the existing Prometheus metrics and structured logs; LangSmith tracing works automatically once its env vars are set.

### Backend correctness/SOLID cleanup
- `AiService` now receives its `OrchestratorAgent` via constructor injection (was built in a field initializer — a DIP violation that forced unsafe test casts).
- Every `AgentTool` now routes port failures through `runTool()` into a `ToolResult` instead of throwing past its own contract; added tests for the previously unreachable error paths.
- Deduped repeated validation messages and a duplicated result-mapping branch.

### Documentation
- `docs/13-next-improvements.md` — spec-to-dev improvement report.
- `docs/14-conformidade-desafios.md` — requirement-by-requirement compliance of every challenge (backend/frontend/QA/data-science) against the code.
- `docs/15-backlog.md` / `docs/16-roadmap.md` — prioritized backlog (with stable IDs) and a phased roadmap.
- `@next/eslint-plugin-next` added, scoped to `apps/web`.

## Verification (all layers, live)

- `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` / `pnpm coverage` / `pnpm build` — green; **244 unit/integration tests**, every package >=95% coverage.
- **Backend (live):** Swagger `/docs` (200), OpenAPI `/docs-json` (valid 3.0.0), GraphQL happy path (order total + stock decrement), insufficient-stock -> 409, validation errors, Prometheus `/metrics`.
- **AI/RAG (live):** thread create -> message -> history (memory), `/threads` list, unknown thread -> 404, empty input -> 400, `/ask`.
- **Postman:** `newman run` — 21 requests, **35 assertions, 0 failures**.
- **Frontend (live):** anime page and `/pedidos` both serve 200; AniList integration returns real data with the correct score-color rule; API GraphQL integration confirmed.
- **QA (live):** ServeRest API tests 4/4 against a local instance; ge.globo E2E 3/3.

author: erayates
body:
## EP-18 · #183 — Replay timeline UI

Time-travel scrubbing for session replay, building on the v1.7 visual replay.

### What
- New `ReplaySession.seek(index)`: pauses playback and re-emits every frame from the start up to `index`, so a listener that applies frames (`applyReplaySignal`) rebuilds the state at that point. Clamped to `[0, frameCount]`. Re-emitting from the start converges last-write-wins engines (cursors/presence) to the scrubbed state.
- Non-breaking interface addition — all adapters typecheck clean.

### Demo (acceptance: "Replay demo")
The demo replay overlay's plain progress bar is now a **draggable timeline** (native `<input type=range>`): drag to scrub, and the sandbox room reconstructs presence/cursors at that frame; a `N/total · peers` position label tracks it. **Verified in-browser**: recorded 190 signals from the AI teammate, replayed, then scrubbed to frame 100 → position `100/190 · 2 peers` (state reconstructed), paused at the scrub point. No console errors.

### Tests
- Core: `seek(2)` re-emits the first two frames from the start and pauses at cursor 2; `seek(999)` clamps to the frame count. Core 424 tests green; demo typecheck + lint green; all adapters typecheck clean.

### Release
`@roomful/core` **minor** (changeset included). Demo change is private.

emergent record-time as the wall dimension).

  Brillouin-corner zeros, chiralities 4+/4− summing to zero (the N-N

## Honest scope (in the note)

Shown: at **free-field** level, chiral-from-achiral via a record-time domain
wall is a live route in the native Cl(3,0)/Z^3 architecture. **Not** shown, and
stated plainly: the record-time wall is **imposed by hand** (the runner does

matching, no electroweak maximality, no interactions, no strong-CP/theta/Koide

The work-order was run **twice independently** by GPT-5.5 xhigh (different

author: davidobando
body:
Fixes #2102

## Design decision: Option 2 (Remove)

Per the issue, two options were proposed: (1) rewrite the Unix mouse-scroll path with a minimal/well-scoped or library-based implementation, or (2) remove it and rely on keyboard-driven scrolling on Unix. This PR implements **Option 2**.

Rationale: the Unix raw-mode mouse path was already dead in practice — it is opt-in via `GSI_MOUSE=1`, defaults off, and is known to mangle keyboard input on macOS (e.g. typing 'f' producing '!', Ctrl+C not exiting) when enabled. It represented a large amount of bespoke terminal-handling code (stty toggling, libc read/poll, SGR escape sequence decoding) for a feature nobody could safely use. Removing it is the simplest correct fix (YAGNI) — rewriting/replacing it (Option 1) would be much higher risk/scope for marginal benefit given the feature is effectively unused today.

## What changed
- `src/Repl/Shell/ConsoleInputReader.cs`: removed the Unix raw-mode setup (`TrySetupUnix`, `stty` process invocation, libc `read`/`poll` P/Invoke, SGR mouse enable/disable escape sequences) and the `GSI_MOUSE` env var gate. Unix input now always goes through the `Console.ReadKey(intercept:true)` fallback — this was already the only path exercised in practice since the feature defaulted off.
- Deleted `src/Repl/Shell/VtInputDecoder.cs` (the ~360-line VT/SGR escape decoder used only by the removed mouse path).
- Deleted `test/Interpreter.Tests/VtInputDecoderTests.cs` (~20 tests covering the deleted decoder).
- The Windows `ReadConsoleInput` mouse-wheel scroll path is untouched — this issue and fix are Unix-only.
- Grepped the repo for `GSI_MOUSE`, `VtInputDecoder`, and related raw-mode helpers (`stty`, libc `read`/`poll`) — no other references found in docs or other source/test files.

## Verification
- `dotnet build GSharp.sln -c Release` — succeeds, 0 errors/warnings.
- `dotnet test test/Interpreter.Tests/Interpreter.Tests.csproj -c Release` — 411/411 tests pass.
- Manually reviewed the resulting `ConsoleInputReader` — Windows path (`ReadConsoleInput`) is unchanged; Unix/other platforms now unconditionally use `Console.ReadKey` for keyboard input, same fallback behavior previously used whenever `GSI_MOUSE` wasn't set (the default).

author: mlcyclops
body:
## What

The **preview-review epic (ADR-0137)** — the LUCID agent can now review *and* test its work live in the Preview panel, in front of the user. Three increments, all with a visible signal so the user sees what the agent is doing.

### P-PREVIEW.6a — live "reviewing/testing" indicator (`964504e`)
Pure `desktop/preview_activity.ts` maps a preview tool-call (screenshot/open/inspect/click/type) to a user-facing label. `acp_backend` emits an additive `preview-activity` ChatEvent; the renderer adds a pulsing accent glow to `#preview` + a `#prevPill` pill ("Reviewing/Inspecting/Testing the preview"), surfaces a hidden panel so the user sees the review, debounces, and clears on turn `done`. Visuals-only — never a gate.

### P-PREVIEW.6b — the agent READS the live preview DOM (`8c42eb9`)
The preview iframe is opaque-origin sandboxed, so the renderer can't touch its DOM. A **read-only** `postMessage` bridge (`preview_bridge.ts`) is injected into the served HTML (inline JS is CSP-allowed; `connect-src 'none'` still blocks egress) — it answers page-text/headings/controls, element details by CSS selector, or captured console errors, and posts a clipped snapshot back. **No eval, no mutation** (proven by a grep test). A held **relay** (`preview_inspect_relay.ts`) bridges the process gap: the new read-tiered `preview_inspect` omp tool GETs a held request; the renderer polls, runs the query via the bridge, and POSTs the result (8s fail-closed timeout). Also fixes a real pre-existing bug: `preview_screenshot` read `body.png` while the endpoint wraps `{ok,data:{png}}`, so the agent had never actually seen its screenshots — now reads `body.data.png`.

### P-PREVIEW.6c — the agent CLICKS/TYPES in the live preview (`b14eff2`)
Built on 6b's relay + bridge: `InspectCommand` gains `action`/`value`; the bridge's `act()` is a **fixed allowlist — click / type / focus / scroll only** (never eval/Function/innerHTML/document.write, proven by a grep test). New `/api/preview/act` endpoint + read-tiered `preview_click` / `preview_type` omp tools over the same held relay + 8s fail-closed timeout; both light the 6a pill. Read-tier is safe because the preview is fully sandboxed + egress-blocked.

## Verification
- Suite green at each increment (up to **1306 pass**); root + desktop `tsc` clean.
- **Verified live end to end:** the bridge answered a real inspect query (title/heading/controls/body text from a served sandboxed preview); `preview_click` on `#go` fired the button's onclick and the `<h1>` actually changed idle→clicked; `preview_type` set an input's value.
- No frozen-prefix or contract change; **no version bump**.

## Notes
- Stacked below the design/Figma epic (ADR-0138) — see the follow-up PR, which targets this branch. **Merge this one first.**
- The 5 pre-existing `fs_browse` test failures on the Windows/home-dir host are environmental and unrelated (they fail identically on master).

author: phytoritas
body:
## Summary

Unifies every routed screen on the exact HOME experience and retires the remaining landing-era layouts:

- **Backend Runtime Bridge removed** from the Overview Dashboard tab; Scenario Lab's `ModelScenarioWorkbench` keeps snapshot/scenario/sensitivity, and the integration inventory now records replay/reindex as hook-only.
- **One global top nav everywhere**: the landing `TopNavigation` became a shared `GlobalTopNav` rendered on every route with the correct active tab; the duplicate WorkspaceTopNav global row and the TopBar brand mark are gone.
- **CONTACT is a real page** at `/contact` (channel cards + onboarding CTA) instead of a scroll-to-footer hack.
- **Knowledge quick tools stay in KNOWLEDGE**: pesticide/nutrient/correction launchers open the in-page material search presets instead of jumping into `/growth`/`/nutrient` dashboard lanes.
- **Same compact frame on all routes**: `AppShell` reuses the `overview-browser` shell/frame/body canvas (width `min(100%, 1190px)`), so DASHBOARD/INSIGHTS/SCENARIOS/KNOWLEDGE/CONTACT match HOME's width.
- **Dated surfaces modernized to the compact Command scale**: shared `PageHeader` typography; INSIGHTS weather outlook (six-stat grid), KAMIS market header (toggle + inline meta), decision snapshot grid; crop-work operating report (one-row summary + six-stat grid + 3-column memos) and 7-day forecast; knowledge quick-tools launcher, legacy AI connectivity panel, and the chat field-tools banner.

## Decisions

- Stacked the redesign on top of the merged #131-#135 stack as one branch of 12 single-concern commits (each within the 5-file phase contract).
- Kept `/api/models/replay` and `/api/knowledge/reindex` wired through `useModelRuntimeWorkbench` without a dedicated panel after the bridge removal — documented in `backend-integration-inventory.ts` rather than dropping the endpoints.
- The assistant page keeps an `sr-only` page heading for accessibility after dropping the visual header; the 질문/자료 찾기 switch lives only in the WorkspaceTopNav action row.

## Validation

- `npm run lint`: 0 errors.
- `npx vitest run`: **225/225** across 50 files, including the command-design-parity and operation-compatibility (PRD-008 phase-limit) contracts; routing/nav/panel tests updated to the new structure and a new `GlobalTopNav` test added.
- `npm run build`: production build ok (no chunk-cycle regression; ChartFrame chunk unchanged).
- Live Playwright smoke on `/overview`, `/control`, `/trend`, `/assistant` (both subtabs), `/contact`, `/crop-work` (생육/작업/수확): identical top nav and frame width on every route, knowledge tools stay on `/assistant#assistant-search`, console errors 0.

## Risk / rollback

- Frontend-only; no API or schema changes. Revert the branch to restore the previous shell.
- Legacy `/api/models/replay` and `/api/knowledge/reindex` have no UI trigger anymore (hook wiring intact); re-expose in Scenario Lab/Settings if operators ask.

Closes #141

author: alexander-turner
body:
## What

The `Bash coverage (kcov)` gate intermittently reports `bin/lib/sbx-launch.bash: 8 uncovered line(s): 304-308, 310-312` — the body of `_sbx_signal_cleanup` — on sbx PRs, while main stays green.

## Root cause

The end-to-end signal test (`test_delegate_signal_reaps_services_and_sandbox`) kills the launcher's **process group** (`os.killpg`). Under the kcov wrapper the vehicle runs as a kcov-traced child, and the group signal also hits the **tracer** wrapping it. Whether the handler's lines make it into the coverage report then depends on a race: they're recorded only when the tracer flushes before the SIGTERM propagates. Green when the race falls one way, red when it falls the other — a non-deterministic 100% gate.

## Fix

Add `test_signal_cleanup_reaps_and_reraises_deterministically`, which drives `_sbx_signal_cleanup` directly through `drive-sbx-launch.bash` (new `signal_cleanup` dispatch). The handler signals only its **own** BASHPID via its closing `kill -s`, so the tracer's DEBUG trap records every line before the process dies — deterministic on every run.

The test is non-hollow: it also asserts the handler *body* ran (the named sandbox is torn down via stub `sbx rm`, and the synthesized per-session kit dir is removed), so it kills a mutant that drops the teardown branch or the kit cleanup. The existing end-to-end test stays as a behavioral check of the real signal path.

Test-only (`tests/` — no shipped-path change), so no changelog fragment.

## Lessons Learned

- **A coverage gate that signals a whole process group is racy under a line tracer** (kcov/coverage.py wrapping the target as a traced child). If the tracer is in the signalled group, coverage of any post-signal handler is nondeterministic. Cover such handlers with a direct invocation that signals only the target's own PID; keep the group-kill test for behavior, not coverage.

author: spxrogers
body:
Closes #58 — the two bug families that four companion review loops found independently now have ONE shared guard instead of six hand-derived ones.

## The fixture

`codegen/conformance/auth-cases.json` — the single source every companion suite iterates **from the file** (never hand-copied):
- **10 hostile-but-2xx token responses** (missing/null/empty/wrong-typed `access_token`; missing/zero/negative/non-numeric `expires_in`; non-JSON and JSON-array bodies) → must fail with the language's TYPED error and leave the store byte-identical (a blank/expired Bearer must never persist and burn the rotated refresh token).
- **10 hostile store files** (literal `null`, malformed JSON, arrays, partial records, wrong-typed and null fields, both records) → typed store-format error, never a default-filled record, never an NPE/panic/KeyError.
- **Canonical valid records** → exact field-value loads + a round-trip through each language's own persist path (the #54 cross-language store-fixture-drift check).

CLAUDE.md → TESTING & VERIFICATION and CONTRIBUTING carry the law: new hostile cases go into the fixture, never into one language's suite; a failing companion gets fixed, the fixture never weakened.

## The fixture caught two real bugs while landing

- **Rust (the reference!)**: accepted an empty `access_token` / non-positive `expires_in` from a 2xx — exactly what the issue's scope note predicted. New typed `AuthError::InvalidTokenResponse` guard in `post_token` (covers exchange AND refresh; distinct from the 400-retry arm, no misfire — reviewer-verified).
- **Java**: `{"client_id": 7}` loaded as `clientId="7"` — Jackson's default scalar coercion converted the number before the required-field checks. The store `ObjectMapper` now fails number/boolean→textual coercion (store mapper only; full module still 71/71 — legit numeric/nullable fields unaffected).
- Python grew the empty-token / non-positive-`expires_in` guards (its loop had only fixed the `KeyError` half). TS, Go, C# needed **zero** source changes — their loop-added guards covered all twenty cases (C#'s System.Text.Json strict defaults reject the coercion that bit Jackson).

## The six legs

| Leg | Suite | Result | CI job |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rust | `tests/conformance.rs` (test-util-gated; empty under `-p` builds) | 3/3 in workspace test | `ci` (3-OS) |
| TypeScript | `tests/conformance.test.cjs` | 44/44 | sdk-compile |
| Python | `tests/test_conformance.py` | 80/80 | sdk-compile |
| Go | `auth/conformance_test.go` | green `-race` | sdk-compile |
| Java | `ConformanceTest.java` | 71/71 | sdk-compile |
| C# | `ConformanceTests.cs` | 83/83 × net8.0+net10.0 | sdk-compile |

Shared strength: fixture-shrink guards (≥8 per table, independent of the loops), exactly-one-endpoint-request assertions (reload-retry arms must not misfire on a 2xx), store byte-identity read AFTER the error, `raw_body`-verbatim-else-JSON replay in every leg, and (Java/C#) an unknown-fixture-table tripwire so a NEW fixture table fails in CI instead of going silently unexercised.

## Review loop (budget-adapted: one combined four-lens pass, Opus) — VERDICT: CLEAN

The reviewer **executed** all six legs, reproduced the Rust break-verification in a clean clone (neutered guard → the exact fixture case fails), confirmed the Java coercion change breaks no legitimate record (full module green), traced all six legs to their per-PR CI jobs, verified the `raw_body`/ordering/shrink-guard adversarial surfaces, and confirmed the CLAUDE.md law text is literally true. Findings: two optional NITs (one applied — a comment on the Rust variant set; the unknown-table tripwire on the other four legs judged not load-bearing since the property is enforced repo-wide via Java+C#).

## Merge gate (Actions quota-limited → local equivalents)

`just ci` ✅ · all five `just sdk-test-*` ✅ · `just coverage` ✅ 93.04% vs 85 floor · every leg break-verified against its own companion's neutered guards (3 sabotages per language, 18 total) ✅

Built as sequential durable checkpoints (one commit per verified leg) after a spend-limit interruption killed the first parallel fan-out.

author: jbecker-it
body:
## What and why

**User report (Apple TV, 0.3.10, default MPVKit engine):** watching a 1080p remux of Dexter, playback starts fine, then a few minutes in the video begins lagging and never recovers. Restarting the video plays normal for a few seconds, then lags even harder with distorted audio. After a *long* pause, playback is fluent again for a while, then frame drops return, and eventually the app crashes. Follow-up testing (Release IPA built by this repo's own GitHub Action) showed micro stutter and audio crackle on **720p and non-remux 1080p too**, with a brief video speed-up after pause/unpause — and the reporter directly observed the ambient hero trailer still playing when the video closed.

This PR fixes **two independent 0.3.9 regressions** that both put a second full video/demux pipeline behind real playback:

### Root cause 1: community-subtitle extraction re-downloads the whole streamed file

Since 0.3.9, `uploadEmbeddedSubtitlesIfNeeded()` (the community-subtitle P4 "share the file's embedded text tracks" path) runs at first playback tick and hands the *currently streaming URL* to `SubtitleEmbeddedExtractor.extractTextSubtitles`. That extractor's `av_read_frame` loop walks the **entire container** — subtitle cues are interleaved through the whole file — so for a streamed play, libav **re-downloads the full 20+ GB file at line rate next to the player**:

- **Remuxes specifically**: remuxes are exactly the files that carry embedded text subtitle tracks; most WEB-DLs have none, so the extractor bailed early and those played fine.
- **Restart makes it worse**: the extraction runs in an unscoped `Task.detached` that is never cancelled, and `embeddedUploadDone` resets per stream — every restart and episode switch **stacks another concurrent full-file read**.
- **Fluent after a long pause**: while paused, a read finishes the file, freeing resources.
- **Eventual crash**: accumulated CPU/memory pressure gets the app jetsam-killed.

**Fix:** embedded-subtitle pooling is now **local-files-only**. `extractTextSubtitles` hard-refuses any non-file input (new `isLocalFileInput`; the `127.0.0.1` torrent loopback counts as remote), and both call sites (`TVPlayerView`, `PlayerScreen`) check the same predicate first so a streamed play never spawns the task. A finished download still contributes its embedded subs via a quick local disk pass.

### Root cause 2: the ambient hero trailer keeps playing behind the fullscreen player

The browse UI stays mounted under the presented player on every platform (opacity-hidden shell on tvOS per `RootView`, `fullScreenCover` on iOS, hoisted host on Mac), and since 0.3.9 the in-hero ambient clip is the **real full trailer** on its own libmpv instance. Nothing stopped that instance when playback started, so a muted looping 1080p trailer kept **decoding and re-fetching from the CDN underneath the whole movie** — a second video pipeline causing constant micro stutter, audio crackle and a brief video speed-up after pause/unpause, and doubled bandwidth on *every* stream started while a hero clip was up, independent of the file being played.

**Fix:**
- **tvOS**: `TVInHeroTrailerView` mounts in `HomeView` and `DetailView` are gated on `presenter.request == nil` (the single player-presentation path), so the clip's libmpv instance is torn down the moment the player presents and remounts fresh on close.
- **iOS/Mac**: players present from several places with no global presenter, so `PlayerScreen` now drives a new shared `FullscreenPlaybackGate` from appear/disappear, and `InHeroTrailerView` unmounts its clip while a player is up (resetting the reveal beat so the remount fades in after a decoded frame, never a black flash). The gate counts mounted players rather than toggling a Bool so an `.id`-rebuild overlap can't reopen it early.

Not touched (possible follow-up): the Lite/no-server WKWebView fallback (`InHeroYouTubeTrailerView`) is not gated; on Lite builds the iframe could similarly keep running under a player.

## Changed files

- `app/SourcesShared/SubtitleEmbeddedExtractor.swift` — hard local-only guard + new `isLocalFileInput` predicate (root cause 1)
- `app/SourcesTV/TVPlayerView.swift`, `app/Sources/PlayerScreen.swift` — skip embedded-subtitle extraction for streamed plays (root cause 1); `PlayerScreen` additionally drives the new playback gate (root cause 2)
- `app/SourcesShared/FullscreenPlaybackGate.swift` — new shared "a fullscreen player is up" signal (root cause 2)
- `app/SourcesTV/HomeView.swift`, `app/SourcesTV/DetailView.swift` — tvOS hero-clip mounts gated on the player presenter (root cause 2)
- `app/SourcesiOS/InHeroTrailerView.swift` — iOS/Mac hero clip unmounts while a player is up, with an iOS 16-compatible `onChange` form (a first iteration used the iOS 17-only overload and broke the CI iOS build; fixed in `fe39f20`)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — both fixes documented under Unreleased

## Testing (real hardware, by the reporter)

- **Reproduced before the fix** on the official 0.3.10 release build (Apple TV, default MPVKit engine): 1080p remux → lag building minutes in, worse after restart with audio distortion, recovery only after a long pause, eventual crash; micro stutter and audio crackle also on 720p and non-remux 1080p; hero trailer observed still playing when closing a video; a full buffered-ahead indicator ruled out the network; toggling the streaming cache (2 GB ↔ off) changed nothing.
- **After the fix** (Release IPA built from this branch with the repo's own `release-tvos.yml` GitHub Action, sideloaded to the same Apple TV): playback performance is much better, and the hero trailer verifiably no longer runs in the background during playback.
- **CI**: tvOS/macOS targets built throughout; the iOS build failure from the first iteration is fixed and all targets build on the current head.

Diagnosed and fixed by Claude (Fable 5) via Claude Code, from the user's playback reports and on-device observations.

## Screenshots

Not applicable — no UI change (playback/runtime behavior only; the only visible difference is the hero trailer correctly stopping while a video plays).

## Checks

- [x] Builds for tvOS (the CI run on this PR uses GitHub's runner SDK, which lags the newest Xcode)
- [x] If this touches watched state, progress, or resume: both profile paths handled (`activeUsesEngineHistory`, see CONTRIBUTING.md) — not touched
- [x] Screenshots attached for UI changes — no UI change

author: tihonove
body:
## Что и зачем

**WP5** большого плана «стоковый editorconfig-vscode работает в Vexx»: ядро редактора было LF-only (`split("\n")` / `join("\n")`), из-за чего CRLF-файл при открытии получал `\r` в конце каждой строки, а при сохранении EOL терялся. Этот PR добавляет EOL-модель в ядро.

## Изменения

- **`src/Editor/EndOfLine.ts`** (новый): `enum EndOfLine {LF=1, CRLF=2}` (значения как в public API VS Code), `eolToSequence`, `detectEndOfLine` (преобладающий `\r\n`/`\n`, ничья → LF).
- **`TextDocument` / `ITextDocument`**: детект EOL при загрузке, хранение строк строго LF, `serialize()` (join с учётом EOL — только для записи на диск), `setEol()`; `getText()` остаётся LF-каноническим (все внутренние потребители — undo, clipboard, поиск, токенизация — видят только LF).
- **`IUndoElement` / `UndoManager`**: опциональные `eolBefore/eolAfter`, undo/redo восстанавливают EOL (по образцу `SingleModelEditStackData` в VS Code). `setEol` не бампит `versionId` — dirty от EOL считается отдельной осью (`savedEol` в `EditorController`).
- **`EditorController`**: `save` пишет через `serialize()`; открытие CRLF-файла не помечает изменённым; roundtrip без правок — байт-в-байт; `get eol` / `setEol`.
- **`Actions/EolActions.ts`** (новый): команды палитры `End of Line: Convert to LF / CRLF / Toggle` (undoable, dirty).

## Инварианты

- Внутри всё LF, конверсия CRLF — только на границе диск↔модель.
- Открытие CRLF ≠ modified; сохранение без правок — байт-в-байт (проверено на байтах: `0d 0a` сохраняются).
- Смена EOL → dirty + undo, `versionId` не трогается (version-guard `UndoManager` цел).

## Проверка

- `src/Controllers` + `src/Editor`: все тесты зелёные, включая ~30 новых EOL-кейсов (`EndOfLine`, `TextDocument.Eol`, `UndoManager.Eol`, `EditorController.Eol`, `EolActions`).
- `tsc --noEmit` чисто.
- Ручной e2e: CRLF-файл → open (detected CRLF, not modified) → save (байты идентичны) → Convert to LF → save (чистый `0a`) → undo возвращает CRLF.

## Границы

Extension-слой, wire-формат RPC и save-pipeline (WP6) не тронуты. Команды EOL — небольшое дополнение сверх исходного объёма WP5 (план откладывал UI выбора EOL), опираются только на ядровой `setEol`.

## 📋 Descrição

Corrige o **erro 500 ao criar um token de API** (`POST /api-tokens`).

**Causa (confirmada nos logs):** `SequelizeUniqueConstraintError` no `ApiToken.create`. A coluna `ApiTokens.token` foi criada como **UNIQUE** no desenho antigo (quando guardava o token puro). No fluxo atual, guarda-se apenas o **hash** (`tokenHash`, que já tem índice único próprio) e a coluna `token` fica `""` em **todos** os registros — então, ao criar o **2º** token, o `""` colidia com o `""` já existente e o backend retornava 500.

**Correção:** migration que **remove o índice único da coluna `token`** (localizando o nome real do índice via `SHOW INDEX`, já que o nome varia). O `tokenHash` continua único, preservando a segurança.

## 🧩 Tipo de mudança

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix

- [x] TypeScript tipado
- [x] Build do backend passa (`npm run build` — migration compila para `dist`)
- [x] Sem `console.log`

- [x] Adiciona migration (incluída nesta PR) — remove um índice único obsoleto; roda automática no deploy (`sequelize db:migrate`).

## 🧪 Como testar

1. Antes: criar um 2º token de API → 500.
2. Após a migration: criar vários tokens de API → funciona (cada um com seu `tokenHash` único).

## Summary

按深度审查报告（`docs/deep-review-upgrade-plan-2026-07.md`）路线图分 3 批次实施，每批次完成后经多角度并行 code-review 验证并修复问题。测试用例从 188 增至 251（含新增专项回归测试），全部通过。

### 批次1（P0，风险/安全类）
- 替换 `xlsx`（CVE-2023-30533/CVE-2024-22363）为 `exceljs`
- 移除零引用冗余依赖 `https-proxy-agent`
- 修复技能生产加载链路：`package.json` `imports` 字段新增 `#skill-kit/*` subpath（dev 解析到 `src/` 由 tsx 转译，prod 解析到已编译 `dist/`），替换脆弱的 `../../../src/` 相对路径引用；Docker/`npm pack` 场景均实测验证
- `server.ts` 从 2013 行拆分为 8 个 Fastify 路由模块（`src/gateway/routes/*.ts`）
- `claude-code` skill 治理加固：`allowed_tools` 收敛只读上限、`cwd` 沙箱、`continue_session` 强制 `session_id`（防止 `--continue` 跨会话串扰）
- 记忆召回止血：修复 `embed`→`embeddings` 方法名 bug、FTS5 tokenizer 改 trigram 支持中文子串检索

### 批次2（P1，架构与能力）
- 收敛双多智能体体系：删除已废弃且从未被实际调用的 `MultiAgentOrchestrator`，委派统一走 `AgentPool`

### 批次3（P2，锦上添花）
- `claude-sdk-engine` 消息类型化：用 SDK 自带 `SDKMessage` 类型替代 `any`
- `gpt-tokenizer` 精确计数：`o200k_base` 真实 BPE 编码替代启发式估算，启发式保留作降级 fallback

author: freeeve
body:
## Problem

Two related defects in the GQL start-scan path (`src/gql/executor/PathTraverser.cpp`):

1. **Silent truncation.** Queries with no explicit `LIMIT` capped the start-node / relationship-anchor scan at a hardcoded `100000`. On graphs with >100k candidates, results -- **including `COUNT` and other aggregates** -- were silently truncated, with no warning or knob.
2. **Multi-filter intersection.** Each per-filter `FindNodesPeered` list was independently capped at that limit *before* the leapfrog intersection, so the join could miss valid nodes whenever any single filter matched more than the cap.

## Change

**Commit 1 -- remove the cap, bound scans by real counts.** When a query has no explicit `LIMIT`, derive the scan bound from the actual candidate count (`AllNodesCountPeered` / `FindRelationshipCountPeered`) instead of the magic number. Using the real count scans every candidate while keeping the underlying `reserve()`/`max` bounded (a `SIZE_MAX` sentinel would over-reserve/overflow). This also fixes the multi-filter intersection: each list is now bounded by the label's full count, so nothing is truncated before the join.

**Commit 2 -- count without materializing nodes.** Deploying commit 1 to a real SF1 graph surfaced a regression: `count(Comment)` over ~1.7M rows now materialized every `Node` (with properties) just to size the group, causing `std::bad_alloc`. Added a guarded fast path in `execute_query_internal`: a query shaped like `MATCH (n:Label) RETURN count(n)` (single node, no edges, optional single property filter, no WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT/DISTINCT, single MATCH, single RETURN) is answered directly from the shard count indexes (`AllNodesCountPeered` / `FindNodeCountPeered`) with no `Node` materialization. Any more complex shape falls back to the normal executor unchanged.

## Verification

Built and deployed to the SF1 bench instance (LDBC SNB BI, graph `ldbc`; Post 1,121,226 / Comment 1,739,438 nodes). The fix compiles cleanly and, end-to-end:

| Query | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `count(Comment)` | `std::bad_alloc` | 1,739,438 (0.7ms) |
| `count(Post)` | `std::bad_alloc` | 1,121,226 (0.5ms) |
| `count(n)` (all types) | `std::bad_alloc` | 2,888,570 (0.4ms) |
| `count(Person)` (10,295) | 10,295 | 10,295 |
| `MATCH (c:Comment) ... LIMIT 3` | ok | ok |

Pre-fix, `count(Comment)` silently returned `100000`; it now returns the true 1,739,438 as an index read.

## Known remaining edge

A non-aggregate unbounded scan that genuinely returns millions of rows (e.g. `MATCH (c:Comment) RETURN c` with no `LIMIT`) still materializes the full result set -- that's a client requesting all rows, distinct from the cap bug. Multi-filter counts (>1 filter) also fall back to the materializing path. Both are candidates for follow-up (streaming / most-selective-driver).

Closes task `008_gql_scan_limit_100k_truncation`.

## Summary

Stage-1b unit **U6** (docs/rebuild-plan.md §4). Seeds `packages/presentation-core` — the third new package — by extracting the live-cue `videos[]` merge rule out of the frontend god-file, and lands the long-deferred characterization test that is its whole point. Behavior is preserved byte-faithfully.

Cites: docs/rebuild-plan.md §3/§4/§5, docs/rebuild-architecture.md §7, docs/edge-cases.md §7.

## Changes

- **`packages/presentation-core/`** (new runtime package, mirrors `packages/local-sync-arbitration`):
  - `name: @ontime/presentation-core`, vitest runner, tsconfig.
  - Owns the `CueVideo` entry type (shape lifted exactly from `packages/shared-types` `LiveCue.metadata.videos[]`: `id?, name?, duration?, elapsed?, remaining?, playing?, status?`).
  - Exports `mergeCueVideos<T extends { cue: { metadata?: { videos?: CueVideo[] } } }>(existing: T, incoming: T): T` — generic over the record so all non-video fields pass through unchanged and the caller's return type is preserved. The merge logic (empty-incoming branch keeps existing videos, id-then-name match, per-field `video.X ?? match.X` fallback) is byte-faithful to the historical closure.
- **`frontend/src/context/UnifiedDataContext.tsx`**: deleted the inline `mergeCueVideos` closure (was lines 5124–5168); added one import line `import { mergeCueVideos } from '@ontime/presentation-core'`. The merge loop that calls it (5170–5193) is left unchanged. Line endings preserved (the file is CRLF/mixed; only the two semantic edits were applied — `git diff` is 1 insertion / 46 deletions, no renormalization).
- **`frontend/package.json`**: added `@ontime/presentation-core: 0.0.0` to deps (resolves via the existing npm-workspace symlink at root `node_modules/@ontime/`).
- **`frontend/src/utils/timer-utils.test.ts`**: the `TODO(rebuild/presentation-core)` marker at line 80 is replaced with a `NOTE` pointing at the now-landed regression in `packages/presentation-core/src/index.test.ts`.
- **`scripts/check-rebuild-guardrails.mjs`**: god-file ratchet `UnifiedDataContext.tsx` baseline **6707 → 6662**; `PACKAGE_POPULATION_BASELINE` **4 → 5**.

## The deferred regression (now pinned)

The `videos[]` empty-overwrite bug (docs/edge-cases.md §7): an incoming live-cue record with empty `videos[]` must NOT blank the videos the UI is already showing, or Windows PowerPoint slides flicker "No video on this slide." The characterization in `packages/presentation-core/src/index.test.ts` covers:
- (a) incoming empty + existing has videos → **KEEPS existing videos** (the bug fix);
- (b) both empty → returns incoming;
- (c) existing empty + incoming has videos → returns incoming;
- (d) id-match → per-field fallback merge;
- (d.2) id-match when incoming carries a value → incoming wins;
- (e) name-match when no id → fallback merge;
- (e.2) existing has id but incoming does not → falls back to name match;
- (f) no match → incoming video returned unchanged;
- plus passthrough of arbitrary extra record fields, and id-match-preferred-over-name-match.

11 tests, all asserting deep-equality on the returned record.

```
npm install
npm run -w @ontime/presentation-core typecheck    # clean
npm run -w @ontime/presentation-core test          # 11 tests passed
cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit                     # clean
cd frontend && npm run test                         # 25 files / 218 tests passed
npm run guardrails                                  # population 5/10 baseline 5; boundaries green; both ratchets; G1
git --no-pager diff --check                         # clean
```

```
Rebuild guardrail checks passed.
✔ no dependency violations found (144 modules, 317 dependencies cruised)
```

- This is a runtime package (real logic + vitest), not type-only like `shared-types`.
- `mergeCueVideos` is generic; the frontend's `LiveCueRecord` is structurally assignable to the constraint (`{ cue: { metadata?: { videos?: CueVideo[] } } }`) with no frontend type changes.

author: s19514tt
body:
## What

Completes the code generator for Wave-2 control flow (roadmap **cg-two-way**, **cg-if**, **cg-for**), plus the runtime support it targets.

- **Two-way `::name`** — property bind (read side) + write-back listener (write side). `::checked` commits on `change`; everything else on `input`. A two-way *member* lvalue (`::value="o.k"`) marks its root a `deepBox` and reactive; `resolve()` scans the whole template (incl. `:if` branches / `:for` bodies) for two-way mutation roots.
- **`:if` / `:elseif` / `:else`** — a plain `:if` compiles to the cheap `ifBlock`; a cascade to one `ifChain` with a `which()` index selector and a parallel array of branch builders. Each branch is its own hoisted static skeleton, built by `fromHTML` when shown, wired recursively (nested binds/events/refs work).
- **Keyed `:for`** — `forBlock` in compiled `html`/`wire` mode: hoisted item skeleton, bulk-`innerHTML` initial render, per-item wiring + per-item reactive scope, loop bindings shadow reactive vars (no `.v` rewrite; refreshed via `runScope` on the item's patch path), `:key` → `keyOf` (stripped from the DOM), LIS keyed diff on update.
- **Nesting** — `:if`-in-`:for` and `:for`-in-`:if` wire and react correctly. Depth is capped (`MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH`) and voided with a *warning* diagnostic beyond it — never a panic. The `compile()` API and never-panic guarantee are preserved.

## Why

The previous handoff snapshot had the emitter ~90% there but (a) left two stale "voided" tests asserting the old behavior, and (b) had an unfinished analysis change: `items.push()` inside a handler was **not** detected as a mutation, so `:for` over a pushed array (and nested control flow reading it) never became reactive. Two supporting fixes landed:

- `feat(script)`: `AssignCollector` now treats in-place array/collection mutators (`push`/`splice`/`add`/`clear`/…) as deep mutations of the receiver's root, while excluding non-mutating chains (`filter`/`map`). This is what makes the nested cases actually react.
- Robustness: a user binding whose name collides with a runtime helper (e.g. a reactive var named `on`) previously shadowed the helper and produced a broken module. Colliding helpers are now imported under a `$`-prefixed alias and referenced by it.

## Test evidence

- **Emit snapshots** (`codegen_emit.rs`): two-way `value`/`checked`, `if`/`elseif`/`else`, `:if` without `:else` (→ `-1`), keyed `:for` with `keyOf`, `:if`-in-`:for`, `:for`-in-`:if`, helper-collision aliasing, and a never-panic fuzz over arbitrary `:if`/`:for` nesting (depth 0–40).
- **Node exec tests** (`codegen_exec.rs`, dom-shim): input → state → dependent-text write-back; `:if` toggle via a click event (branch built/inserted, then removed); keyed `:for` initial render + push/splice/reorder asserting DOM order **and** node identity for a surviving key across a reorder.
- **Analysis unit tests** (`lunas_script`): mutating-method detection, non-mutating-method exclusion, member-receiver root reporting.
- Runtime suite (`packages/lunas/test/run-all.mjs`) green.

Gates: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, and the node runtime suite all pass.

roadmap.yml: `cg-two-way` / `cg-if` / `cg-for` flipped to `done`.

author: msiric
body:
## Problem
The content and resource syncs each wrapped their **entire** persist phase in one Prisma interactive transaction (`prisma.$transaction(..., { timeout: 30000 })`). That transaction issues one awaited round-trip per entity, so its runtime grows with the catalog. At ~620 entities against the production database it exceeded the 30s cap, Prisma closed the transaction, and the next write threw **P2028** ("Transaction not found") — rolling the whole sync back.

This was the **first full content sync since the transaction was introduced (PR #11)** — the last content push predated it — so the scaling limit had never been exercised until the catalog reached its current size. In its current state, **every** content update fails.

## Fix (option B — idempotent upserts)
A single global interactive transaction is the wrong tool: its duration is unbounded in the catalog size and it holds write locks for the whole sync.

Persist via the existing idempotent, `contentId`-keyed upsert helpers directly on the base client. Parents are written before children (FKs always valid); a mid-run failure leaves a partial-but-consistent catalog that the next run completes (CI surfaces the error). Stale-row removal is already handled separately by the sanity-capped `prune:content` step, and readers are unaffected (Postgres MVCC). The timeout is gone and the sync scales with the catalog.

## Verification
- Ran the **real** content + resource syncs end-to-end against a local Postgres with the full catalog (~620 entities): both complete, EXIT 0, no P2028.
- DB after sync: `THEORY 341, CODING 165`, `0 IMPLEMENT/CODE` — matches expectations.
- `tsc` clean, `next lint` clean, **871 tests** pass (sync tests updated to assert the upserts run and that persistence errors still propagate).

author: randomparity
body:
Adds handler-level end-to-end coverage for the three folder-mutation
tools — `create_folder`, `rename_folder`, `delete_folder` — which
previously had only a protected-folder unit test (audit finding H-4c,
part of #446). The suite drives the production stdio JSON-RPC wire
against the Dovecot fixture, the same pattern as `e2e_wire_destructive.rs`.

## What it covers

- **Round-trip:** create → rename → delete, with a `list_folders` call
  after each mutation asserting the listing reflects it.
- **Protected-folder guards** (destructive account): `create_folder`,
  `rename_folder`, and `delete_folder` on a protected folder (INBOX /
  Sent) are refused with `ERR_PROTECTED_FOLDER`.
- **Expunge-allowlist gating:** `delete_folder` on a folder outside the
  expunge allowlist is refused with `ERR_EXPUNGE_DENIED` — the same
  allowlist that gates `expunge` also gates folder deletion (the handler
  runs `check_protected` then `check_expunge`).
- **Posture boundary** (full account): `create_folder`/`rename_folder`
  are advertised but `delete_folder` (destructive-only) is not, and
  calling it is refused with `ERR_POSTURE_DENIED`.
- **Audit attribution:** each handler dispatch pairs a `tool_start` with
  a `tool_end` one-to-one, attributed to the right account, with the
  recorded `(status, error_code)` outcome asserted per call.

## Notes

- Adds `build_dovecot_folder_config` (two accounts: `destructive` +
  `full`) to the shared wire config builders.
- The two-account catalog exceeds one `tools/list` page, so the
  advertisement check walks `nextCursor` pagination to completion —
  incidentally exercising the pagination path.
- Silent-skip when no container runtime is available;

  suites. Verified locally against Dovecot 2.4.4; `just ci` green.

author: dmj786
body:
## Summary
- Module 5's photo picker and selfie flow crashed on Flutter web because `permission_handler`, `dart:io File`, and `google_mlkit_face_detection` are mobile-only
- This PR guards each web-hostile call so the flow completes end-to-end in Chrome for design review, while keeping iOS/Android behaviour byte-for-byte identical

## Root causes
1. `photo_picker_service.dart` called `Permission.camera/photos.request()` unconditionally — `permission_handler` has no web plugin, so it threw `MissingPluginException`
2. `add_photo_screen.dart` and `selfie_validator_service.dart` read image bytes via `File(file.path).readAsBytes()` — `dart:io File` isn't supported on web (XFile.path is a `blob:` URL there)
3. `selfie_validator_service.dart` invoked `FaceDetector` on every selfie — Google ML Kit has no browser backend
4. Four widgets rendered `Image.file(File(path))` — same `dart:io` issue

## Changes
- `photo_picker_service.dart` — wrap `Permission.camera/photos.request()` in `if (!kIsWeb)`; browsers handle permissions natively via `getUserMedia` / the file input dialog. `openSettings()` is a no-op on web.
- `selfie_validator_service.dart` — auto-return `SelfieValid` on web (real ML validation only runs on-device on iOS/Android); swap `File(file.path).readAsBytes()` → `file.readAsBytes()` for cross-platform bytes access
- `add_photo_screen.dart` — same `XFile.readAsBytes()` swap for the size + decode validation
- **New:** `lib/widgets/platform_image.dart` — small helper widget that renders `Image.network` on web (for blob URLs) and `Image.file` on mobile
- Callers migrated to `PlatformImage`: `photo_grid_slot.dart`, `selfie_grid_slot.dart`, `selfie_confirmation_view.dart`, `selfie_rejection_view.dart`

## Mobile impact
**Zero behaviour change on iOS/Android.** Every guard is `if (!kIsWeb)` (mobile falls through the existing code path) or a like-for-like swap (`XFile.readAsBytes()` internally delegates to `dart:io File` on mobile; `PlatformImage`'s mobile branch is `Image.file(File(path))` — same as before).

## Test plan
- [ ] `flutter analyze` — passes clean on the 8 touched files
- [ ] `flutter run -d chrome`, navigate to `/photos-verification`, tap a photo slot → gallery/camera picker opens without crash, picked photo renders, size validation runs
- [ ] Same flow with the selfie slot → capture flow shows, confirmation view renders with the picked image, submit works
- [ ] `flutter run -d android` (or iOS) — verify permission prompts still fire, ML Kit face detection still rejects no-face / multi-face / eyes-closed selfies
- [ ] Existing `FakePhotoPickerService` / `FakeSelfieValidatorService` widget tests still pass (only real impls behind `kIsWeb` guards were touched)

author: karmafeast
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Manual Gateway compaction (`sessions.compact`) rotated the active transcript but could leave durable `core/continuation-post-compaction` TaskFlow rows queued. That stranded post-compaction lifeboat delegates until an unrelated later compaction, or let stale proof/task restore instructions fire out of context.

This patch makes manual compaction use the same post-compaction release machinery as volitional/auto compaction, while addressing the Codex P2 review findings:

- preserve legacy delivery route fields (`lastChannel` / `lastTo` / `lastAccountId` / `lastThreadId`) via `deliveryContextFromSession(...)`
- release delegates after successful `maxLines` manual compaction too
- skip post-compaction lifecycle/context injection when no staged or persisted post-compaction delegate exists
- route session-store lookup through `session-accessor.ts` instead of direct legacy reads from the migrated Gateway surface

## What Changed

- Extracted/reused `releasePostCompactionDelegatesAfterCompaction(...)` for the Gateway manual compaction path.
- Added `releaseManualPostCompactionDelegatesIfNeeded(...)` so manual compaction checks for durable/session-store post-compaction delegates before invoking release work.
- Updated manual release follow-up context construction to use reconciled delivery context rather than `entry.deliveryContext` directly.
- Routed both model-backed manual compaction and successful `maxLines` trimming through the same guarded release helper.
- Added `loadSessionStoreEntrySnapshot(...)` in `session-accessor.ts` for the storage-neutral lookup needed after `maxLines` trim updates.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - queued post-compaction delegates releasing after manual compaction
  - legacy route preservation during manual release
  - `maxLines` trim releasing staged delegates
  - ordinary compaction with no delegates not injecting post-compaction lifecycle/context

## Evidence

Local gates run on Cael from `/tmp/oc-1165-fix` at commit `12caef1b04f350cbc93c15d05f6582bd28b9e4a4`:

```text
pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts -t 'sessions.compact releases queued post-compaction delegates after manual compaction|sessions.compact preserves legacy route fields when releasing post-compaction delegates|sessions.compact maxLines releases queued post-compaction delegates after trim|sessions.compact skips post-compaction lifecycle when no delegates exist'
# Test Files 1 passed; Tests 4 passed / 18 skipped
```

```text
pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts
```

To make the global search feature more discoverable and accessible for keyboard power users, allowing them to quickly jump to search without reaching for the mouse.

author: rajnishkhatri
body:
## What

Advances the Subject-Coach agent's **Phase 3** (judge validation → enable policy) through three SDD-lifecycle tasks. The `answer_leakage` judge is validated, a provisional gold set is assembled, and the enable-policy certifier is built — all **fail-closed**, with the real ENABLE decision deferred to a human double-label pass (3.9).

## Tasks

### 3.6 — rubric revision + judge-validation data-plane fix (ADR-0017)
- **Root-cause finding:** the judge's low TPR was a **data-plane gap** (the judge was fed a bare `question_id` and never the item's answer options), *not* rubric abstraction. `scripts/enrich_coach_judge_cases.py` + recorder wiring now pass the rendered item.
- Fixed **3 mislabeled/non-collapsing fixtures** (A1/A2/B1) in lockstep across `cases.jsonl` **and** the source `judge_test_cases.jsonl` (FR-14).
- Honest 4-run Opus baseline (B1 4/4, G3 4/4, A3 2/4, A1 0/4, A2 0/4, TNR=1.0); the strict 5/5 acceptance gate is rescoped to the ≥20-trace out-of-sample round.

### 3.7 — `coach_goldset_v1` assembly (provisional)
- `services/governance/coach_goldset_dataset.py` + `scripts/assemble_coach_goldset.py` (mirror the GoalJudge precedent; Invariant #7 — `LeakChannel` mirrored locally, no `components` import; α **reuses** `iaa.krippendorff_alpha_nominal`, NaN→None).
- **Provisional artifact** `tests/fixtures/coach_goldset/coach_goldset_v1.json`: 21 scorable rows, `provisional=true`, α=null → **refuses the cert by construction**.

### 3.8 — `evaluate_coach_enable_gates` certifier (machinery)
- `services/governance/coach_calibration.py`: frozen `CoachGateDecision` + `evaluate_coach_enable_gates`. Positive class = `leak`.
- **Fully self-contained** confusion + rate helpers (AP-6 decoupling documented in `decisions.md`) — imports **nothing** from `goaljudge_calibration`; κ reuses `iaa`; **no `meta/` import** (services↛meta).
- Binding floors **TPR≥0.90 / TNR≥0.95 / κ≥0.75** (inclusive). Augmenting precision/false-action/flip + per-axis κ + production-subset precision are **diagnostic-only — never gate** the verdict.
- **Fail-closed proven:** `REFUSE_PROVISIONAL` on the real 3.7 artifact (short-circuits before any metric); ENABLE/REFUSE/undecidable proven on synthetic non-provisional fixtures.

## Fail-closed by construction

The cert on the committed provisional artifact:
```
verdict : REFUSE_PROVISIONAL
gates   : {}
reasons : ('manifest is not a v1 freeze: manifest is provisional=true',)
```

## Testing / gates

- All tasks red/green TDD, failure-path-first. 17 L1 tests for the cert; `make check` green (**5037 passed**); `pytest tests/architecture/` green (**160 passed** — Invariant #7 + no services→meta).
- Code review (deterministic, `origin/main...HEAD`): **approve, 0 findings** after fixing one TAP-4 classifier false-negative (strengthened reject tests to assert the empty-gates fail-closed contract). Design/style pass (agent reasoning, no `--llm`): approve; one deferred diagnostic-honesty refinement noted for 3.9.

## Deferred to 3.9 (needs a human, not machinery)

- The real ENABLE/REFUSE cert run requires the **non-provisional human-double-labeled** gold set (α≥0.80, populated 60/40 test split).
- Diagnostics currently report bare floats without support counts — to surface `(value, n)` pairs when 3.9 consumes them.
- **`COACH_LEAKAGE_GATE_ENABLED` is untouched** — flipping it is the human Phase-5 step.

author: zazack641
body:
## Résolu — décision d'Isaac

L'app couvrait à tort **trois groupes d'années dans un seul fichier** (N1 10–99 ≈ 3H-4H, N2 100–999 ≈ 5H-6H, N3 1000–9999 ≈ 7H-8H) sous une carte unique `5H–6H`/`MSN 22`, en violation de la convention « une app = un groupe d'années » (`CLAUDE.md`). Signalé initialement en `CONFLIT À ARBITRER`.

**Isaac a tranché : scinder.** Fait :
- `apps/saut-de-nombre-3h4h.html` (nouvelle app, MSN 12, C1)
- `apps/saut-de-nombre-5h6h.html` (nouvelle app, MSN 22, C2)
- `apps/saut-de-nombre-7h8h.html` (ancien `saut-de-nombre.html` renommé, MSN 22, C2, plage jusqu'à 9999 reprise du N3 d'origine)

Chaque fichier garde 2 niveaux internes progressant **à l'intérieur** de son propre groupe d'années (1re partie / 2e partie du cycle, cf. `skills/pedagogie-per/SKILL.md`) plutôt que de sauter d'un groupe à l'autre. Le jeu de boutons de saut (±1/±10/…) est désormais fixe par fichier (une seule échelle par app), ce qui simplifie aussi le code par rapport à l'original (plus de table `configs`/`btnDefs` par niveau — la duplication relevée en revue de code sur l'ancien fichier ne se pose plus).

`index.html` mis à jour : la carte unique est remplacée par 3 cartes (une par groupe d'années, badges/`data-harmos`/`data-per` corrects). `SUIVI.md` mis à jour avec une ligne par app.

Vérifié en preview (Playwright) sur les 3 fichiers et sur le portail : cartes et liens corrects, parcours complet aux 2 niveaux de chaque app, aucune erreur console.

**Aucun CONFLIT À ARBITRER restant. Aucun point À VALIDER PAR ISAAC restant** (celui-ci vient d'être tranché).

---

## Résumé de l'audit initial (avant scission, sur l'ancien fichier unique)

**Pédagogie (MSN 22, Nombres) :**
- Progression interne cohérente, ancrage dans des contextes concrets (kangourou, train, grenouille, fusée, robot) conforme au principe didactique « toujours un contexte ».
- Feedback formatif déjà explicatif (indique le sens et l'ordre de grandeur du saut à faire, pas seulement juste/faux) — conservé intact dans les 3 fichiers issus de la scission.
- `TYPE_TACHE='instance'` déclaré (absent jusqu'ici) et cohérent avec le comportement déjà implémenté : une réponse incorrecte n'invalide rien, l'élève ajuste sa trajectoire de sauts et revérifie sur le même nombre cible jusqu'à réussite.

**Accessibilité :**
- Les boutons de saut sont déjà de vrais `<button>` (accessibles au clavier nativement) — seule la gestion du focus manquait : `newBtn.focus()` après réussite, focus sur `feedbackEl` (`tabindex="-1"`) après une réponse incorrecte, `questionBox.focus()` en fin de `newExercise()`.
- `.number-label` : 14px/`#94A3B8` → 18px/`#475569`. `.target-label` : 15px → 18px (contraste déjà conforme). `.jump-btn` : porté à 22px minimum (seuil texte interactif) ; `:focus-visible` ajouté.

**Forme :**
- Styles inline dupliquant `app-base.css` retirés (`.app-header`, `.back-link`, `.app-header h1`, `.header-spacer`, `main`).
- `--color-units/tens/hundreds` et `colorForRank`/`PLACE_COLORS` redéfinis inline en doublon d'`app-base.css`/`appUtils.js` — retirés (CLAUDE.md #2).
- Icône `▶` ajoutée sur `new-btn`.

## Revue de code (`/code-review --comment`, 8 angles)

**Corrigé directement** (qualité de code pure, comportement inchangé) : override CSS partiel de `main` retiré, `document.querySelectorAll('.jump-btn')` mis en cache dans `state.jumpBtns`, champ `grid` par niveau redondant retiré, `tabindex` résiduel nettoyé. Repris dans les 3 fichiers de la scission.

**Laissé en commentaires inline** (touchent le contrat `TYPE_TACHE`/refactor non trivial, non appliqués automatiquement) : `TYPE_TACHE` déclaré mais jamais lu par une condition ; double appel de focus dans `newExercise` actuellement sans risque mais fragile. La duplication `btnDefs`/`configs` par niveau signalée en commentaire ne se pose plus après la scission (une seule échelle de sauts par fichier désormais).

author: zaxbysauce
body: Closes #1715 ## Summary The knowledge feedback loop was an open circuit — outcome signals were recorded but nothing acted on them. Three gaps fixed (G1/G2/G3 from the gap catalog): - **G1 — phase-failure outcomes now record.** `phase-complete` previously called `updateRetrievalOutcome(dir, name, true)` with a hardcoded `true` at a point in the flow before `success` was determined. The call now runs after the real outcome is finalized and passes that value, so a failed phase (`policy=enforce` + missing required agents) emits `'failure'` outcome events and `failed_after_shown_count` can finally increment. - **G2 — confidence-floor action.** Both feedback bridges (`applySkillUsageFeedback`, `applyKnowledgeVerdictFeedback`) bumped `entry.confidence` but nothing acted on low confidence — the bumps dead-ended at the floor. Now `bumpKnowledgeConfidenceBatch` runs a post-bump sweep that demotes (`confidence_floor_demoted` flag → strips retrieval `statusBoost`) or quarantines per config entries that are floor-clamped AND have a net-negative outcome signal over ≥3 outcome events. Reversible by default. - **G3 — contradiction signals unified.** `contradicted_count` (incremented only via `knowledge_receipt`) and the curator's `flag_contradiction` (tag-only) were disconnected. The curator now emits `contradicted` events post-transaction (with `agent: 'curator'` for audit), and a new `maybeQuarantineOnContradiction` auto-quarantines entries whose in-window contradicted count crosses the threshold (default 3 in 30d). Counts come from the RAW event log, not the mtime-keyed rollup cache, to avoid stale-count risk. The genuinely-closed sub-loop was previously only the violation-count → escalator → enforce-block path. This change closes the confidence/contradiction/phase-failure halves. ## Invariant audit - 1 (plugin init): not touched — no plugin-registration changes. - 2 (runtime portability): not touched — pure TS, no runtime-specific code. - 3 (subprocesses): not touched. - 4 (.swarm containment): not touched — new artifacts (`contradicted` events, `confidence_floor_demoted` flag) write only to existing `.swarm/` knowledge + events files; no new locations. - 5 (plan durability): not touched. - 6 (test_runner safety): not touched. - 7 (test writing): touched — 4 new/updated test files co-located with source per convention; each runs in its own process to avoid the cross-file contamination tracked in #1712. - 8 (session state): not touched. - 9 (guardrails/retry): not touched — fail-open semantics preserved (`bumpKnowledgeConfidenceBatch` and the new floor-action are best-effort, never throw). - 10 (chat/system msg): not touched — the G2 `statusBoost` gate is read-only on retrieval scoring. - 11 (tool registration): not touched. - 12 (release/cache): touched — release fragment added at `docs/releases/pending/1715-close-knowledge-feedback-loop.md`; no version files edited. ## Test plan Validation commands run + results: ``` $ bun run typecheck # tsc --noEmit (empty — clean) $ bun run lint # biome lint . Checked 2313 files. No fixes applied. # Each affected test file in its own process (per repo convention; the # combined single-process run has pre-existing cross-file contamination # tracked in #1712 — see proof below). $ bun --smol test tests/unit/config/knowledge-config.test.ts # 43 pass / 0 fail $ bun --smol test tests/unit/hooks/knowledge-reader.test.ts # 20 pass / 0 fail $ bun --smol test tests/unit/hooks/knowledge-events.test.ts # 24 pass / 0 fail $ bun --smol test tests/unit/hooks/knowledge-store.test.ts # 39 pass / 0 fail $ bun --smol test tests/unit/hooks/knowledge-verdict-feedback.test.ts # 10 pass / 0 fail $ bun --smol test tests/unit/hooks/curator.test.ts # 118 pass / 0 fail $ bun --smol test tests/unit/hooks/knowledge-escalator.test.ts # 5 pass / 0 fail $ bun --smol test tests/unit/hooks/knowledge-floor-action.test.ts # 6 pass / 0 fail (NEW) $ bun --smol test tests/unit/hooks/knowledge-contradiction.test.ts # 8 pass / 0 fail (NEW) $ bun --smol test tests/unit/hooks/search-knowledge.test.ts # 14 pass / 0 fail $ bun --smol test tests/unit/tools/phase-complete-outcome-regression.test.ts # 3 pass / 0 fail (NEW) # = 290 pass / 0 fail ``` **Pre-existing-failure proof (combined run is NOT a regression):** the combined single-process run produces 24 failures — but I verified this is identical on clean `origin/main` (worktree at HEAD c5eb59cd, before any of these edits): same 24 failures, same pass count. This is the documented cross-file mock/state contamination tracked in #1712, not caused by this change. **Independent review:** GLM-5.2 reviewer (fresh context) returned NEEDS_REVISION with 5 findings (2 HIGH broken config fixtures + missing tests; 1 MED hive quarantine no-op; 2 LOW). All addressed. GLM-5.2 critic (separate fresh context) returned APPROVE with 2 optional LOW improvements, both applied (floor-action `console.warn`, behavioral retrieval-ranking test). New test coverage: - G2: floor-demote on net-negative signal, min-outcomes gate, net-positive skip, recovery clears stale flag, `none`=legacy, idempotency, retrieval down-ranking. - G3: curator emits `contradicted` event, tag preserved (back-compat), threshold quarantine, below-threshold skip, idempotency on already-quarantined, window respected, curator→quarantine end-to-end, `tag_only`=legacy. - G1: source-level regression guard (no literal `true`, passes `success` var, old false-premise comment gone). Companion behavioral test (`false` → `'failure'` event) already exists at `knowledge-reader.test.ts` Test 12. ## How to use New config knobs (all optional, conservative defaults): - `knowledge.confidence_floor_action`: `'none' | 'demote' | 'quarantine'` (default `'demote'`). - `knowledge.confidence_floor_min_outcomes`: default `3`. - `knowledge.confidence_floor_signal_threshold`: default `0` (net-negative). - `knowledge.contradiction_threshold_action`: `'tag_only' | 'quarantine'` (default `'quarantine'`). - `knowledge.contradiction_quarantine_threshold`: default `3`. - `knowledge.contradiction_quarantine_window_days`: default `30`. For the legacy dead-end behavior: `confidence_floor_action: 'none'` + `contradiction_threshold_action: 'tag_only'`. ## Migration No migration required. New config fields default to conservative behavior. Existing entries without `confidence_floor_demoted` read as `undefined` → not-demoted (legacy). Hive floor-entries get the flag (honored by retrieval) but not quarantine (the quarantine mechanism reads only the swarm file — documented in the release fragment).

Fallback (no regime artifact): symmetric split of the 9.811ms authoritative ack round trip. - Constant mode: BOTH ns values required explicitly; each leg through validate_replay_latency_ms — no bypass path remains anywhere. - Receipts per run: latency_model, per-leg ns + sources, offensive_tick_to_send_us_added, cancel_latency_policy=send_to_ack_proxy_until_cancel_ack_measured (defensive cancel→ack still UNMEASURED — proxied honestly). - _economics_stamp includes latency → pre-fix resume receipts can never satisfy --resume. - Tests: 8 new; suite 640 passed / 4 pre-existing known failures. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

 This PR makes replay latency default to measured CHI404 data instead of silent constants. - Adds `latency_truth.json` lookup for offensive tick-to-send p99. - Requires explicit in-band constants for `constant_order_latency`. - Adds latency provenance fields to replay receipts. - Includes latency in campaign resume stamps. - Adds tests for measured latency enforcement.

Confidence Score: 4/5

 The measured latency changes still leave runtime paths that can fail with missing or out-of-band latency values. The campaign default can pass None into numeric feature-building code, the standalone runner can reach constant latency mode without required values, accepted measured regime suffixes can abort during per-leg validation, and resume stamps can miss refreshed measured values. scripts/run_hftbacktest_only_campaign.py, scripts/run_hftbacktest_only.py, packages/backtest_pipeline/src/hftbacktest_only_pipeline.py

T-Rex Logs

 **What T-Rex did** - The focused campaign-row harness reproduced that running \_run\_row\_task with latency values omitted triggers a TypeError during latency resolution, confirming that entry\_latency\_ns=None blocks the measured latency path. - A direct standalone CLI run with missing latency arguments reproduced exit code 1, and a focused harness logged that latency defaults were parsed as latency\_model='constant\_order\_latency' with entry\_latency\_ns=None and response\_latency\_ns=None. - The latency regime resolver harness reproduced that chi404\_measured:fast and chi404\_measured:extreme resolve to the checked-in measured regime models but fail replay band validation because their timing falls outside the allowed window. - Before/after tests around constant-latency-band show the base run\_campaign accepted omitted constants in the before state but the after state rejects those omissions and only accepts explicit latency pairs with latency\_model='constant\_order\_latency'. - Economics stamp analysis shows that after changes the \_economics\_stamp includes latency\_model, entry\_latency\_ns, and response\_latency\_ns, whereas the before stamp lacks these fields and constant stamps differ unless the latency values align. Ran code and verified through T-Rex

Important Files Changed
