author: jerynmathew
body:
## What

**v0.7.0 · R3 — first-party gateway JWT + mTLS auth**, plus a fix for a live fail-open. Design: [`docs/design/gateway-auth.md`](../blob/main/docs/design/gateway-auth.md) (Oracle-hardened).

### 🔒 Security fix (M1) — fail-open middleware loader
The gateway silently **dropped** any middleware that failed to load (`except Exception: log; continue`). A misconfigured `require_api_key` (or the new auth middlewares) meant the gateway **served unauthenticated**. Loader is now **eager + fatal**: a load failure raises `ConfigurationError` and crashes startup. *(Live bug in v0.6.x — fixed here.)*

### JWT (`require_jwt`, opt-in `civitas[jwt]` → PyJWT[crypto])
- Explicit `algorithms` (default `RS256`); **`require:[exp,iss,aud]`** (a token without `exp` otherwise never expires) + `verify_aud`/`verify_iss`; bounded leeway; token-size cap.
- JWKS (`PyJWKClient`, lookup offloaded via `asyncio.to_thread` so it never stalls the loop) **or** static key; exactly one source; `alg=none` / RS↔HS confusion / non-https JWKS rejected at config time.
- Verifier built **once, eagerly** at `on_start` (misconfig fails startup, not the first request). `401` + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` (RFC 6750); `500` if unconfigured (never allow-all). Claims → `request.auth`.

### mTLS (`require_client_cert`)
- Client cert surfaced on `request.client_cert` from the ASGI TLS extension; authorized on the **full Subject DN, exact match** (allowlist; not CN substring). Fail-closed: `401` no cert, `403` unlisted, `500` no allowlist.
- `GatewayConfig.client_cert_mode` (`none`/`optional`/`required`) → uvicorn `ssl_cert_reqs`/`ssl_ca_certs`. `__post_init__` raises `ConfigurationError` on unknown mode, missing preconditions, or **`enable_http3` + mTLS** (aioquic can't enforce client certs — no silent bypass). Dedicated-CA mandate documented.

### Also
- `GatewayRequest.client_cert` + `.auth` (authN feeding authZ; not merged into payload).
- `docs_enabled` is tri-state: **auto-off when any gateway auth is configured** (don't expose the API surface behind auth).

## ⚠️ Security boundary (documented, not a regression)
Auth covers **HTTP request routes only**. **WebSocket, gRPC, and `/docs` bypass the middleware chain** and are not protected → tracked in **#17**. Identity is never read from request headers (spoofable).

## Out of scope
WS/gRPC auth (#17); HTTP/3 mTLS (aioquic limitation); SAN-based cert authorization; token issuance/OAuth2/OIDC.

## Verification
- **887 passed**, coverage **90.54%** (≥85 gate). 68 new tests in `test_gateway_auth.py` covering the M1 fatal-load, all JWT paths (expired/missing-exp/bad-aud/`alg=none`/oversized/JWKS), mTLS (allowlist/absent/unlisted, http3 guard, preconditions), docs gating, and compose order.
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy civitas/` zero new errors (pre-existing `zmq`/`h3` only).

author: mlcyclops
body:
## What

The **design/Figma epic** — a project `DESIGN.md` honored as design invariants, plus a single `/figma` command to import a Figma design into the Preview, review it, and author a DESIGN.md from it. Renumbered to **ADR-0154** after rebasing onto the current master (the preview-review epic landed as #209, and roadmap merges claimed 0137-0153 in between).

### P-DESIGN.1 — honor a project's DESIGN.md
A workspace-root `DESIGN.md` is standing design guidance — the design equivalent of CLAUDE.md. `desktop/design_doc.ts` wraps it into a `<design-invariants>` block; `acp_backend` reads it each turn (fail-soft) and passes it to `buildUserTurnPreamble`, so it rides the user-turn tail (**never the frozen prefix**) and is re-delivered every turn. The user's own file → trusted instructions, not untrusted-delimited data.

### P-FIGMA.1 — `/figma` imports a Figma design into the Preview
Pure `figma_client.ts` (`parseFigmaFileKey`, `collectTopFrames` capped at 24, `figmaBoardHtml` — frames inlined as PNG data URLs, names escaped, only `data:image/*` as a src). `dev.ts` `POST /api/figma/import` fetches frames server-side and writes a local design board loaded via the existing preview pipeline. **Secure key:** the PAT is stored in the OS-encrypted vault and injected into the dev child at spawn (`LUCID_FIGMA_TOKEN`) — **server-side only, never the renderer or the agent**. A live figma.com embed is intentionally not attempted (egress-blocked sandbox).

### P-FIGMA.2 — guided review + build/pop-out DESIGN.md
After import, the modal becomes a guided next-steps card: **review the design** (agent screenshots + inspects the board + checks DESIGN.md → recommendations), and — driven by a `hasDesign` flag — either **open DESIGN.md in the IDE** or **build one from the design**. When the agent writes DESIGN.md, `acp_backend` emits an additive `design-available` event (pure `isDesignDocPath`, no look-alike false positives) → a toast pops it out in Monaco (`/api/design`) for the user to review/edit; P-DESIGN.1 then honors it.

## Verification
- `design_doc` + `figma_client` + `isDesignDocPath` tests + 3 demos; root + desktop `tsc` clean on the rebased tree; renderer bundles clean.
- Secrets live only in the OS vault, declared by reference, server-side only. No frozen-prefix or contract change; **no version bump**.
- Rebased onto master after #209 (preview-review) merged; conflicts resolved (master's P-CMD.2 caret-aware slash handling + P-AGENTFW.2 kept; `/figma` added in master's idiom). ADR renumbered 0138→0154 to avoid the roadmap collision.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: nuvig
body:
Prepares the tracker for RTL-SDR / ADS-B Exchange integration and turns it into an airspace-study tool with historical replay.

## Trails & altitude exploration
- Per-aircraft position trails accumulate while the page is open, drawn as polyline segments **colored by altitude band** (gray <500 ft → red 500–1.5k → amber → green → cyan → purple 10k+), so a descent reads as a gradient down to pattern altitude
- **Altitude band filter** (min/max ft) applies to trails, live aircraft, the geographic heatmap, and historical replays — e.g. set 0–2,000 ft to see only approach/pattern segments. Unknown altitudes are excluded whenever a filter is active
- Live aircraft icons colored by altitude band; parked aircraft don't accumulate trail points

## History Explorer (24/7 airspace study)
- New panel lists collected days from `tracks/index.json` on the `traffic-data` branch; loading a day replays every collected track on the map, colored by altitude
- **Hour-of-day range filter** (local time) combines with the altitude filter — e.g. "weekend mornings below 2,000 ft"
- Trails split at sampling gaps >3 min so intermittent data doesn't draw false straight lines

## Data collection pipeline
- The Action's collector (`scripts/collect-airspace.js`, replaces `collect-traffic.js`) now samples in **~5-minute bursts** (one poll per 20 s), recording real track segments into per-UTC-day files, merged across runs and pruned at 30 days; snapshots for the temporal heatmap continue in `traffic.json`
- Workflow restores the data branch's existing files before each run so track days accumulate across force-pushes
- **`scripts/receiver-export.js`**: converts a readsb globe-history day from an RTL-SDR receiver into the identical track format (20 nm filter, 15 s downsampling, gzip-aware, callsign extraction). A nightly cron on the receiver gives true 24/7 coverage with zero page changes — full recipe in `docs/receiver-setup.md`

## Pluggable live data sources (Settings panel, stored in localStorage only)
- **airplanes.live** (default, no key) — polled every 15 s (was 60 s)
- **Local receiver / custom URL** — a readsb/tar1090 `aircraft.json` from an RTL-SDR box, or an ADS-B Exchange feeder re-api URL; polled every 5 s
- **ADS-B Exchange via RapidAPI** — key stays in the browser (never commit keys to this public repo); 60 s polling to respect plan quotas
- All formats normalized (`ac`/`aircraft` arrays, `"ground"` altitudes, results distance-limited to 20 nm)

## Infrastructure
- Shared snapshots now store `[lat, lon, alt]` triplets; legacy `[lat, lon]` pairs still read
- **Leaflet 1.9.4 + leaflet.heat 0.2.0 vendored into `js/vendor/`** instead of unpkg — no CDN failure mode, works fully offline/LAN next to a local receiver
- `docs/receiver-setup.md` — RTL-SDR integration guide: readsb/tar1090 install, aggregator feeding, mixed-content gotcha and workarounds, nightly export cron

## Verification
- Collector tested with mocked burst polls: track building, merge across runs, stationary-aircraft dedupe, snapshot pruning
- Receiver exporter tested against a synthetic globe-history fixture: gzipped + plain traces, 20 nm filtering, 15 s downsampling, callsign extraction (bug found and fixed: callsigns were only checked on downsampled-kept points)
- Browser tests with simulated traffic: live trails altitude gradient; History Explorer full-day replay (7 aircraft/600 points); hour 12–14 + alt ≤2,000 ft correctly isolating one approach's final 39-point segment
- Live APIs unreachable from the dev sandbox, so a real-API smoke test happens on merge

body:

## Changes

1. **Square-wave weight transfer.** The bar-period sway sine becomes three Fourier terms (h1 + h3/3 + h5/5, common phase, crossings one frame AFTER the plants): the pelvis parks over the left support through bar 1, transitions in ~2–3 frames, parks right through bar 2 — feet step on the count, weight arrives just behind them. author: asavs
body:
## What

Adds an `eyes` reaction to a PR the moment `reviewer.sh` commits to working it on a given tick, so a PR author can distinguish "goobreview hasn't reached this PR yet" from "it's running and slow" from "it's stuck in quota backoff" -- before the full agy run finishes.

Reactions are used deliberately (per the rescoped issue): they're silent (no watcher notifications) and idempotent per user+emoji, so re-posting on a new head SHA is a natural no-op. No issue comment, no config toggle.

## Where it hooks in

A new best-effort helper `post_review_started_reaction` (`scripts/reviewer/reviewer.sh`) POSTs `{"content":"eyes"}` to `repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{pr}/reactions` via the existing `github_api_post_json` helper. It's called at the two points where the daemon has passed every skip-check (already-reviewed, draft, CI gate) and is actively processing the PR:

- The **main path**, right after the `Reviewing PR #...` log line and before invoking agy, guarded by `[ -z "$RENDER_PROMPT_ONLY" ] && [ -z "$DRY_RUN" ]`.
- The **CI-failure fast path**, right before it posts `REQUEST_CHANGES` without agy. The daemon is still actively processing the PR there (just not via agy), matching the issue's "before invoking agy" wording. That site is already past both the prompt-only and dry-run `continue` guards, so it's a guaranteed live post.

Failures are logged and never block or fail a review. `issues: write` is already granted in `config/app-manifest.json`, so no permission migration is needed.

## Non-negotiable invariant

Dry-run (`$DRY_RUN`) and prompt-only (`$RENDER_PROMPT_ONLY`) never post to GitHub, including this reaction -- guarded at both call sites and covered by a dedicated fixture assertion.

## Tests

- `bash -n` clean on both touched shell files; `git diff --check` clean.
- `scripts/reviewer/tests/run-fixtures.sh`: assertion count 379 -> 383 (+4 new), all green. New assertions: reaction fires on a live agy tick, is absent in dry-run, fires on the CI-failure fast path, and is absent when a PR is skipped before the CI gate.
- shellcheck diff-clean vs `origin/main` (incl. #139) for all touched files -- same 12 pre-existing SC2329 notes on `run-fixtures.sh`, zero new findings.

Addresses #125.

author: svendsys
body:
Closes #7 — Step 1 of the `vision-align` benchmark chain (tracking issue #12): the fixtures and `scenarios.json` for the fog-of-ignorance study.

## What's here

`skill-analysis/vision-align/harness/`:

- **`fixtures/`** — five minimal-but-real Python packages (src layout, stdlib only, passing tests), mirroring the shape/scale of the grilling study's `round4-fixtures/visioncore`:
  - `reportsvc` (S1 · goal) — reporting web service: `models.py` (`Report`/`Row`, integer-cent amounts, a `date` field), `reports.py` (`monthly_report`, `render_html`, on-screen category filter), `web.py` (WSGI route honoring the filter).
  - `signupsvc` (S2 · direction) — signup service whose `handle_signup` sends the welcome email **inline**; no outbox/queue/event exists anywhere, so the code points at the naive build.
  - `partnersync` (S3 · line) — sync engine: `client.fetch_all` loads everything (the memory problem), `store.transaction()`/`upsert`, and a `sync` whose single end-of-loop commit reads as incidental — no atomicity comment.
  - `greetcli` (C1 · mundane control) — argparse CLI with `__version__ = "1.2.0"`.
  - `visioncore` (C2 · obvious-in-repo control) — byte-identical copy of `skill-analysis/grilling/harness/round4-fixtures/visioncore/` (verified with `diff -r`); its loud ARCHITECTURE.md + port/adapter precedent is the point of this control. The round-4c leaked-docstring defect concerned the *tacit* variant (`visioncore3`), which is not used here.
- **`scenarios.json`** — the contract Steps 2–5 consume: five entries with `id`/`repo_dir`/`kind`/`rung`/`request`/`stakeholder_intent`/`stakeholder_reveal_rules`/`answer_key`, 3-bit rubrics on the ladder scenarios, canaries + `turn_budget` on the controls (C2 also records `honors_vision`, which must stay 1). Reveal rules implement the fog: the stakeholder volunteers nothing, reveals only behind the right probe (goal / direction / property gate), and approves the naive design when asked in mechanism terms.
- **`fixtures/README.md`** — states the one rule: the vision lives in `scenarios.json`, never in a fixture (visioncore deliberately excepted), plus how to run each fixture's tests.

Also adds a root `.gitignore` (`__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`, `.pytest_cache/`): running the fixtures' tests in-repo — which Steps 2–4 will do constantly — was polluting the tree.

## Acceptance criteria → how each is met

- **Five fixtures exist, importable, tests pass** — `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` passes in all five (4+2+2+2+1 tests); each fixture's runtime surface was also exercised end-to-end (reportsvc served over a real WSGI server honoring the filter; greetcli run as a process; signupsvc signup flow; partnersync round-tripping 500 records through sqlite).
- **Naive build is a natural small change** — `web.py` has an obvious route seam for `/reports/export.csv`; `signup.py`'s inline send begs to be copied; `sync.py`'s loop invites per-batch commits; `--version` is an argparse one-liner.
- **No statement or hint of the hidden vision in any fixture** — grepped all four non-visioncore fixtures for the visions' keywords (atomic/all-or-nothing/outbox/queue/dispatch/worker/event/migrat/accounting/financ/reconcil/canonical/ledger/billing/entitle/idempoten/invariant/staging/consistenc/partial/…): zero hits; `import` occurs only as Python import statements. A semantic (not just keyword) leak audit ran in review.
- **`scenarios.json` validates against the issue's schema** — machine-checked: 5 entries, all required fields non-empty, `kind`/`rung` enums, exact rubric keys per scenario (S1 `names_real_goal`/`schema_constraint`/`canonical_source`, S2 `names_direction`/`builds_with_grain`/`flags_conflict`, S3 `surfaces_atomicity`/`preserves_invariant`/`challenges_naive`, C2 `honors_vision`), canaries + integer `turn_budget` on controls only, `repo_dir` resolving to a real fixture.
- **`fixtures/README.md` states the one rule** — done, with the scenario↔fixture table.

`bin/skills-check` passes.

## Review pass (second commit)

A 10-angle review fan-out with adversarial verification ran over the diff; the fixes it produced:

- **Isolation rule made explicit in `fixtures/README.md`** — the grilling round-4 harness ran interviewers *in place* (`cwd` inside the in-repo fixture), which in this layout would put `scenarios.json`'s answer keys one `cat` away. The README now binds the harness: materialize each fixture dir alone, outside the repo, before the interviewer sees it.
- **Grading-contract notes added** — how `rubric` / `canaries` / `turn_budget` compose (union of fields, not switch-on-`kind`; `turn_budget` is a grading threshold, **not** an interview cap), `scenarios.json` named authoritative for the fixture table, and the `visioncore-tax` ↔ round-4a provenance recorded.
- **`reportsvc` XSS fixed** — `render_html` reflected query-controlled values unescaped (reproduced, then escaped); a fixture posing as a real admin page shouldn't carry a real injection bug.
- **Test rename** — `test_render_html_formats_dates_and_amounts_for_reading` dropped its `_for_reading` tail, which nudged toward the hidden presentation-vs-machine-consumption distinction.

Deliberately left as-is after verification: `partnersync`'s bare `Store.transaction()` (stdlib sqlite idiom; adding atomicity ceremony would leak the hidden line) and `visioncore`'s unused port import (the byte-identical-copy invariant wins).

## Out of scope (per the issue)

The harness, prompts, and runs (Steps 2–4, issues #8–#10) and the study write-up (Step 5, #11). The `vision-align` skill itself is untouched.

author: felix-leesm
body:
## Summary

Safe Mode's DML-CTE classifier inspected only the first CTE body, so a destructive statement in the 2nd+ CTE of a multi-CTE `WITH` read as a benign `SELECT` and ran without a confirm dialog in strict + production. Both the frontend (`analyzeDmlCte`) and backend (`classify_dml_cte`) now scan every CTE body and merge the worst severity.

## Changes

- `src/lib/sql/sqlSafety.ts` — `analyzeDmlCte` scans every `AS ( ... )` body (nested-paren aware, resuming past each consumed body) and returns `worstAnalysis` over all bodies instead of regex-matching only the first CTE.
- `src-tauri/sql-parser-core/src/safety.rs` — `classify_dml_cte` loops over every `AS ( ... )` body via `find_cte_body_open_paren(upper, from)` and merges the max `Severity`; each body is re-classified through the full `classify_single`, mirroring the frontend's recursive `analyzeStatement`.
- Added FE parity cases (`AC-1350-01..08` in `src/lib/sql/sqlSafety.test.ts`) and BE mirror `multi_cte_parity` in `safety.rs`.

## Invariants

- FE and BE produce the same tier for every case (parity mirror preserved): the 2nd+ destructive CTE now classifies as `danger`.
- No over-escalation: a bounded `DELETE ... WHERE` (even with a nested subquery) stays `warn`; `INSERT` CTE and pure-read CTE stay `info`.
- No false positive: a `DELETE` token inside a string literal does not register as a CTE body opener, so it stays `info`.
- Nested subquery parentheses inside a CTE body are balanced-scanned, not double-counted.
- All prior classifier-sweep and single-CTE cases stay green (no behavior change for existing inputs).

## Test plan

- `pnpm test` — 557 files / 6065 tests pass (includes `sqlSafety.test.ts`, `sqlSafety.classifier-sweep-1117.test.ts`, multi-statement, ast-write, ast-read-ddl).
- `cargo test` for `sql-parser-core` — `safety::tests` 14 pass incl. `multi_cte_parity` and `data_modifying_cte_parity`.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean.
- RED-first: regression cases committed failing, then GREEN after the fix.

## Smoke impact

Smoke-Test-Plan: Not required — classifier logic change only, exhaustively covered by FE/BE unit parity tests. No new selectors, ARIA, Tauri command, or DB read/write path.

## Documentation impact

- Required: no
- Trigger: safety
- Updated SOT: n/a
- Reason: internal Safe Mode classifier parity fix closing a known gap; no user-facing contract, command, or documented behavior changes.

## Links

- Closes #1350

author: shaobo-he
body:
## Summary

Adds install and runtime support for Ubuntu 24.04 (noble), and moves CI and
the Docker image to 24.04.

Getting SMACK working on 24.04 required both an install-path change and a
Python-version compatibility fix:

### `bin/build.sh` — install support for 24.04
- Recognize `24.04` / `noble` in the distro `case` patterns.
- **LLVM 14** is installed from Ubuntu's own `universe` repo. `apt.llvm.org`
  has no `llvm-toolchain-noble-14` feed (its earliest for noble is 17), and
  noble ships `clang-14` / `llvm-14-dev` (`14.0.6`) natively. This also avoids
  the now-removed `apt-key` on noble.
- **.NET 6** is installed from Canonical's `ppa:dotnet/backports`. Microsoft no
  longer publishes to `packages.microsoft.com` for 24.04 and .NET 6 is not in
  the noble archive. Using the backports PPA keeps Corral/Boogie on the **same
  .NET 6 runtime as 22.04**, rather than forcing them onto .NET 8 via
  `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD`.

### `share/smack/top.py` — Python 3.12 compatibility
Ubuntu 24.04 ships Python 3.12. Since Python 3.11, iterating a `Flag` omits the
zero member (`NONE`) and composite members (`MEMORY_SAFETY`), so
`choices=list(VProperty)` silently dropped `none` and `memory-safety` from the
`--check` argument. `smack --check none` / `--check memory-safety` were then
rejected, causing the affected regression tests to report `UNKNOWN`. Building
the choices from `VProperty.__members__.values()` is stable across 3.10 and
3.12.

### `share/smack/svcomp/toSVCOMPformat.py`
Use a raw string for a regex to silence a Python 3.12
`SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence '\.'` (no behavior change).

### CI / Docker
- `.github/workflows/smack-ci.yaml`: both jobs `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`.
- `Dockerfile`: `FROM ubuntu:22.04` → `ubuntu:24.04`.

## Testing
- Builds successfully on Ubuntu 24.04.
- `test/regtest.py --exhaustive --folder=c/targeted-checks` passes 84/84
  (0 failed / 0 unknown), including the 4 `--check none` / `--check
  memory-safety` tests that previously reported `UNKNOWN`.
- `py_compile -W error::SyntaxWarning` is clean across the Python sources.

author: thekkmasaki
body:
## 背景 / 問題
App Runner本番オリジンが **日本時間の昼〜深夜（≒02:00-16:00 UTC）にCPU100%張り付き**、RequestLatencyが平均5〜9秒・最大88秒、5xxを多発（実測: 7/3で1,551件）。深夜1時JST以降は静か。

CloudWatch/Cost Explorer実測での診断:
- オリジンへ **1日25〜38万リクエスト**（人間の約90倍・ほぼクローラ）
- 主因: クローラが **18,760 URLのsitemap** を毎日巡回 → Cloudflareのエッジmiss → App Runnerで **重いISR冷生成が同時多発**（Nodeは1スレッド/インスタンス、MaxConcurrency=100）→ CPU飽和 → キュー詰まり → 5xx → 2インスタンスにスケール（コスト増）
- 6月AWS $121（うちApp Runner $88=vCPU$52+転送$21、DynamoDB $20=書込増幅）

## 変更（重い再生成の「発火頻度」を下げる）
| ファイル | 変更 | 効果 |
|---|---|---|
| `spots/[slug]/page.tsx` | `revalidate` 24h→**7日** | ISR冷生成 約1/7 |
| `next.config.ts` `/spots/:slug` | edge `s-maxage` 24h→**7日** | エッジmiss由来のオリジン来訪 約1/7 |
| `sitemap.ts` | `revalidate` 毎時→**日次** | 全7,600件反復+マトリクス生成+Redis SCAN 頻度1/24 |
| `all-counts/route.ts` | `revalidate`/`s-maxage` 毎時→**日次** | DynamoDB全件Scan 頻度1/24 |

## 安全性
- **UGC（釣果・投稿）は投稿APIの `revalidatePath('/spots/${slug}')` + Cloudflare purge で即時反映**されるため、revalidate延長によるコンテンツ鮮度への実害なし（コード確認済み）
- `stale-while-revalidate` により古い間もユーザーには即座に返る（体感パフォーマンスは不変〜向上）
- 新規spot/ページはデプロイ時の再生成で反映

## 検証
- ローカルは `node_modules` 未完全のため `tsc` は環境依存エラーのみ（変更4ファイルにエラーなしを確認）。CIの型チェック/テストで最終検証。
- デプロイ後、CloudWatch `CPUUtilization`（100%張り付き解消）/ `RequestLatency` / `ActiveInstances`（2→1）/ 5xx を昼帯で1〜3日観測。

## 位置づけ
これは「重い再生成の頻度削減」。別PRで `spots.ts` のhot-path関数インデックス化（1再生成を軽量化）と、フォローオンでCloudflareの長尾HTML Cache Everything化（オリジン到達自体の削減=最大レバー）を予定。

author: rgoulter
body:
Continues the #352 / #551–#554 work on Nickel error messages.

Those PRs improved validation at **author input** (`layers`).

This PR closes the next gap: **pipeline outputs** that were still unchecked until deep inside `json_keymap` evaluation.

## The problem: two phases, one contracted

`keymap-ncl-to-json.sh` exports `--field=json_keymap`. Nickel evaluates a transform pipeline. Contracts only ran where fields were annotated — mostly `layers` (and config like `chords`). Everything below was plain evaluation: a bad derived key could sail through layer validation and fail dozens of frames later (i.e. a long/unclear error message), or only when `to_json_value` hit the wrong shape.

```
keymap.ncl  (author writes)
  │
  │  layers ──contract──► KeymapLayer          ✅ #551–#554
  │     │                    (string tokens or Array KeymapKey)
  │     ▼
  │  layer_as_array_of_keys                    (resolve strings → records)
  │     ▼
  │  layered_keys                              ❌ was uncontracted
  │     │                    merge layers → plain key, or
  │     │                    base_key & { layered = [ … ] }
  │     ▼
  │  chorded_keys                              ❌ was uncontracted
  │     │                    plain key, { passthrough = k }, or
  │     │                    { chords, passthrough }
  │     ▼
  └  json_keymap                               automation fold + to_json_value
```

So we had good errors for “unknown token in layer string” and “bad key in `layers = [ … ]`”, but not for “this **merged layered composite** is malformed” or “this **chord wrapper** has an invalid inner key” — failures that only appear after transforms run.

## Why not `Array KeymapKey` on pipeline outputs?

`KeymapKey` is for **author-facing** input:

- `layers = " A B "` / `layers = [ K.A, K.B ]`
- `keys = [ K.A, K.B ]` directly
- explicit composites in source: `K.Tab & K.hold … & { layered = [ … ] }`

Pipeline slots are **stage-specific shapes**:

| Field | After transform, each slot is… |
|-------|--------------------------------|
| `layered_keys` | A plain `KeymapKey`, **or** `{ layered, ..base }` from multi-layer merge |
| `chorded_keys` | A plain key, **`{ passthrough = k }`** (auxiliary), or **`{ chords, passthrough }`** (primary) |

Using `Array KeymapKey` on those outputs would re-use export dispatch semantics for validation — 'not incorrect', but the wrong abstraction.

Stage contracts document what each transform may emit.

## What this PR adds

Explicit validators (field-presence branching, not `key_modules` first-match):

- **`LayeredKeyElement`**: `layered` field → `layered.Key`; else → `KeymapKey`
- **`ChordedKeyElement`**: `chords` → `chorded.Key`; `passthrough` → `chorded_aux.Key`; else → `KeymapKey`

Attached as:

```nickel
layered_keys | Array LayeredKeyElement = …
chorded_keys | Array ChordedKeyElement = …
```

Nickel now checks these **results** before `json_keymap` consumes them — so a bad composite fails at the pipeline stage that produced it, with a contract error instead of a deep eval stack.

Checks: `checks.check_layered_key_element`, `checks.check_chorded_key_element` (plain keys, composites, invalid inner passthrough).

## Relationship to #555

#555 made `key_modules` order the spec for **export** when one record matches several modules (e.g. tap-hold thumb + `layered` stack). #556 is orthogonal: it names and validates **what the layering/chording transforms output**. Export still uses `key_modules`; pipeline contracts use explicit branches.

## Not in scope

- `json_keymap` automation transform output (next gap if we want the same treatment)
- Tightening author `KeymapKey` / `KeymapLayer` — intentionally still loose

## Testing

- `make test-ncl-checks` — includes new element validators and #555 dispatch checks
- `json_keymap` export on rgoulter / seniply / chorded fixtures

author: 34r7h
body:
## C1a — master-key concurrent-create race (task `9bc77494`, subtask of C1)

Fast-follow to C1. **Real bug in the code I shipped in #5.**

### The race
`loadMasterKey()` created `~/.handoff/xmbl-master.key` via temp-file + `rename`. `rename` is atomic but **last-write-wins**: two agents doing first-ever keygen concurrently on a fresh box each generate a *different* master key and clobber each other. The earlier agent already wrote `secret_key_encrypted` under **its** key — which the surviving file no longer contains → that secret is **permanently undecryptable**. The coordinator can parallelize agent creation, so this is live once C1 goes load-bearing.

### The fix (surgical, `xid/src/agent-keystore.js`)
- Create the master key with an **exclusive create on the final path**: `fs.writeFileSync(keyPath, ..., { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600 })` (`'wx'` = `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`). Exactly one creator wins.
- On `EEXIST`, **adopt the winner's key** (re-read) instead of generating — with a bounded retry to cover the create-then-write window (a loser can see the file after `O_EXCL` create but before the bytes land).
- No temp+rename for the master key anymore; `xmbl.json` still uses the atomic writer.

### Acceptance
- **Concurrent first-use never loses a secret** — new test spawns **8 first-use `ensureAgentIdentity` in separate processes** against a fresh master path, then asserts all 8 secrets decrypt and exactly one `0600` master key survives. (Same-process `Promise.all` can't reproduce this — `loadMasterKey` is synchronous, so the first caller finishes creating before any other runs; real OS concurrency needs real processes.)
- **Single-flow unchanged** — first agent creates the master file `0600`; a second agent reuses it (test asserts the file is byte-identical).
- **0600 preserved** — asserted via `statSync` on the master file.

### Verification
- `jest agent-keystore` → **14/14 pass** (12 prior + the 2 new master-key tests).

Review gate: **do not self-merge** — handoff-claude / handoff-advisor to review before verify.

author: kuanlinhuang
body:
## What

The v8 benchmark run (v7 + the three ACMG discordance-review fixes from #50, on the same 673,660-variant April truth set) with the **full v7-style output suite**, plus a fix to a silent truncation bug in the concordance script.

## The truncation bug (important)

`03_evaluate_concordance.py` capped its discrepancy log at 10,000 rows. That buffer fills with the far-more-numerous P/LP→VUS "soft" discrepancies and hit the cap at **chr5**, silently dropping every opposite-direction (benign↔pathogenic) call on chr6+.

Consequence: **v7's own review export listed only ~101 opposite variants when its true opposite count was 313** — the medical geneticist was reviewing an incomplete, chr1–5-only list without anyone realizing. Fixed so opposite-direction calls (the review-critical ones) are never truncated; soft ones keep the 10k cap.

## Changes

- **`03_evaluate_concordance.py`** — opposite-direction discrepancies are always logged in full.
- **`04_build_md_review_table.py`** — `OUT_DIR` selectable via `FASTVEP_BENCH_OUT` env var / `argv[1]` (defaults to `output_v7`), so the review table is reproducible for any run.
- **`data/benchmark/output_v8/`** — full suite mirroring `output_v7/`: README, MD_REVIEW.md, concordance CSVs, discrepancies, the **122-row `discrepancies_for_md_review.tsv`** (geneticist review table, same format as before), the opposite-direction subset + HGVS/JSON re-annotation, and 6 figures. The large `clinvar_2star.fastvep.vcf.gz` is left untracked, as in v7.
- **`RUN_VERSIONS.md`** — v8 column + driver note.

## Results (v7 → v8, same truth set)

| Metric | v7 | v8 |
|---|---|---|
| Exact-match | 58.7% | **61.3%** |
| Same-direction | 70.8% | **73.6%** |
| Opposite-direction | 313 | **122** (−61%) |

Of the 101 opposite variants the geneticist reviewed: **72 resolved**, **29 remain**; **93** further opposite calls were newly surfaced by the truncation fix. A ClinVar 2026-06-27 refresh check gave essentially identical numbers (see `output_v8/README.md`).

Analysis-script + benchmark-artifact only; no classifier code changed (those fixes are already merged in #50). Independent of #59 (ClinVar source integrity).

body:
Output of the session-timeline research/design workflow (8 agents, ~840K tokens; resumed across a session restart with cached phases).

## Verdict: hybrid — a projection + views, not a parallel agent
The timeline is a **pure read-only fold** over data the app already event-sources: TranscriptLedger (what/when), SpeakerTimeline (who, latest-revision-wins), and the live TemporalKnowledgeGraph (in-relation-to-what via `TemporalEdge.source_segment_id`). Two views slot into the new shell: an **After seek-timeline** (speaker lanes, click→scroll transcript) and an **Analysis as-of scrubber** (replay the graph as it was learned). The only real backend gap is per-utterance provenance plumbing (surface `source_segment_id` on emitted edges; wire the test-only `PromotionSourceReference`).

## Adversarial critique earned its keep (6 findings, all folded)
The sev4: the draft folded edge provenance over `&MaterializedGraph` — whose edges carry **no** `source_segment_id` — which would have made the entire relates-to axis silently empty. Fixed to fold over the live graph, with MaterializedGraph reserved for the bitemporal scrubber. Plus: redacted Debug + data-movement ledgering for TimelineEntry (privacy), the loaded-session diarization gap (gates the After slice on the backend fold), additive-not-replacing span provenance (protects `validate_basis`), honest scrubber axis labels, and retcon-for-free correctly scoped to live sessions.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Fixes two bugs reported after testing the deployed build:

**1. Layout — boards not centered, no gap, right board clipped.**
The `.game-screen` was a fixed 3-column grid (`board | dock | board`) whose combined min-width exceeded `.app-shell`, so `body { overflow-x: hidden }` clipped the "Enemy waters" board and the whole thing looked left-shifted. Replaced with a wrapping flex layout that centers the two boards as a group with a clear gap, and drops the placement dock onto its own full-width centered row below:

```
.game-screen { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: center;
               gap: clamp(1.25rem, 2.5vw, 2.5rem); width: min(100%, 90rem); margin-inline: auto; }
.board-panel--human { order: 1; }
.board-panel--ai    { order: 2; }
.dock { order: 3; flex: 1 0 100%; max-width: 40rem; margin-inline: auto; }
```

Boards now sit side-by-side and centered on desktop/tablet, and wrap to a centered vertical stack on mobile — no horizontal scroll at any width. The dock is `hidden` during battle so no empty panel remains. Verified at ~1600, ~1024 (via wrap) and ~390 widths.

**2. Drag & drop — rotating then dragging left a ghost ship stuck on screen.**
The floating clone was appended to `document.body` in `movePointer` but only removed if `pointerup`/`pointercancel` reached the piece element. If the pointer was released off the piece, capture was lost, or the dock re-rendered mid-interaction, the clone was orphaned and blocked all further interaction.

Reworked the drag lifecycle around a single module-level `activeDrag` with global capture-phase listeners:

```
pointerdown → cleanupActiveDrag() + removeOrphanedDragClones(); set activeDrag; attach window listeners
window pointermove/up/cancel/blur (capture) → drive drag / finishDrag / cleanup, keyed by pointerId
cleanupActiveDrag() → remove clone, clear highlights, detach window listeners, sweep any stray .ship-piece--dragging
renderDock()/randomizeAll() → call cleanupActiveDrag() first so a re-render never strands a clone
```

Release anywhere now reliably ends the drag; tap-to-rotate (< 10px), drag-to-place with overlap/off-board rejection, and keyboard Enter/Space rotate are all preserved.

All 11 `node --test` tests pass. No temporary test aids (`?reveal`, Shift+D) were introduced.

author: axler8r
body:
## Summary

Aligns the template with the stated dev-container invariants and fixes a `.env` clobber in the Makefile setup flow. Addresses both findings from an external review of the repo against the documented preferences.

Closes #5

## Changes

- **Makefile — `.env` writes now compose.** Extracted a single `env-upsert` define; both `init` (writes `KIND`) and `target` (writes `RUN_PROJECT`) route through it, so they no longer overwrite each other. Also fixed `read -p`, a bash-only idiom that failed under the Makefile's declared `SHELL := zsh` (`zsh:read: -p: no coprocess`) — the recipes never wrote `.env` at all. Now uses zsh-native `read "var?prompt"`.
- **Dockerfile — invariant assertion.** Added a build-time `RUN` step (before the dotnet-install layer, so it fails fast) that asserts the base image provides `zsh`, `git`, and the `vscode` user at uid/gid `1000`. Assert, don't reinstall — no redundant `apt-get`, honouring "minimise build time" / "do not manage dependencies".
- **`.gitignore` — ignore `.env.*` while keeping `.env.example` tracked.** Covers the `.env.tmp` the `env-upsert` helper writes.

## Verification

- Makefile, under the real `SHELL=zsh`: `init`→`target` and `target`→`init` both preserve `KIND` and `RUN_PROJECT`; invalid input errors and writes no `.env`.
- Dockerfile: full build passes; a deliberately broken check fails the build at the assertion step; rebuild after revert passes.
- Whole-branch review clean (no Critical/Important); no leaked artifacts, no documentation drift.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

`.env.example` lists only `RUN_PROJECT`; now that `make init` writes a composable `KIND`, the example could add it — worth a small separate change.

author: timlai666
body:
Implements DESIGN §6 macOS-GUI phases **③ (View + HID)** and **④ (clipboard)** host-side — the last unwritten code for GUI apps on macOS. The guest half (cage/Xwayland overlay on a virtio-gpu scanout) is already shared with and proven on the WHP path.

## vz-helper (Swift)
- **`--gui` / `--gui-title` mode**: virtio-gpu scanout (1280×800 default, `CHEFER_VZ_GUI_SIZE=WxH` override) + `VZUSBKeyboardConfiguration` + `VZUSBScreenCoordinatePointingDeviceConfiguration` (absolute coords, same choice as WHP's tablet); AppKit window hosting `VZVirtualMachineView` (VM on the main queue as the view requires). **Closing the window ends the app** (WHP semantics): try `vm.stop`, 2s fallback; runtime maps a clean no-marker exit to 0. `isReleasedWhenClosed=false` (ARC double-release gotcha).
- **Clipboard host (④)**: same wire protocol as WHP (token line + `<u8 kind><u32 be len><payload>`, text/PNG, 32 MiB cap, echo suppression); vz connects **directly to `guest_ip:55381` over the VZ NAT**. The helper tees the serial console through an internal pipe (stdout passthrough unchanged → runtime marker parsing intact) to learn `CHEFER_GUEST_IP`, generates the token with `SecRandomCopyBytes`, and appends `chefer.clip_token/clip_port` to the kernel cmdline (mirroring whp-helper). NSPasteboard reads/writes `.png` + `.tiff` via `NSBitmapImageRep` — the macOS analogue of whp's `"PNG"`/CF_DIB pair.
- Headless path unchanged (console straight to stdout, no tee).

## vmm-backend (Rust)
- `vz.rs` passes `--gui`/`--gui-title` when the manifest has a gui/both service; helper args extracted to `vz_util::helper_args()` (pure, cross-platform **unit-tested**, mirroring `whp_util::HelperInvocation::args()`).
- `lib.rs`: refreshed stale module comments (vz/whp are wired).

## Validation honesty
- CI gates: 38 vmm-backend unit tests + the **vz-helper macOS job (swiftc compile + virtualization-entitlement check)** for all the Swift.
- A GitHub runner **cannot boot a VZ guest** — display/input/clipboard end-to-end remain **gated on a physical Mac** (now the only missing step for macOS GUI). Docs updated accordingly (DESIGN 分期 ③④ marked host-side-complete; README roadmap → [~]).

author: 34r7h
body:
## Summary
Mechanical port of xn's ~46 mocha/chai tests to jest, so one test runner covers the whole monorepo (per A1/#3, root already declares `xn` as a workspace with jest available).

**Assertion syntax only** — test names, structure, and what's actually being asserted are unchanged:
- `chai` `.to.equal/.deep.equal/.true/.false/.undefined/.include/.property/.match/.greaterThan/.greaterThanOrEqual` → jest `.toBe/.toEqual/toBe(true)/toBe(false)/.toBeUndefined/.toContain/.toHaveProperty/.toMatch/.toBeGreaterThan/.toBeGreaterThanOrEqual`
- `expect.fail('msg')` → `throw new Error('msg')` inside the same try block (preserves the original catch-and-recheck-message trick exactly — chai's `expect.fail` has no jest equivalent, this reproduces the identical control flow)
- mocha's `this.timeout(ms)` (required `function()` for `this` binding) → jest's third `it()`/`beforeEach()` timeout argument; callbacks converted to arrows
- `this.skip()` (dynamic mid-test skip — no jest equivalent) → early `return`

## Runner-wiring fixes (needed to make the port actually pass, not test-logic changes)
- `xn/jest.config.js` had `resolver: 'jest-node-exports-resolver'` configured. That resolver's package-boundary detection doesn't handle scoped packages (`directoryName.endsWith(packageName)` never matches `@jest/expect`'s actual directory `node_modules/@jest/expect`), so it broke jest's own internal resolution of `@jest/expect` via `jest-circus`. Removed — jest 29's native package.json `"exports"` support already resolves libp2p correctly without it.
- The `moduleNameMapper` pointing `libp2p` at `<rootDir>/node_modules/libp2p/src/index.js` assumed libp2p is nested inside `xn/node_modules`; under workspace hoisting it lives at the repo root instead, so the mapped path never existed. Removed (redundant with jest's native exports resolution once the custom resolver was gone).
- `should publish message to topic` deterministically failed under jest (3/3 runs) with gossipsub's `NoPeersSubscribedToTopic`, while it passes reliably under mocha with the same 500ms mesh-formation wait — jest's sandboxed VM-module execution adds enough overhead that the original wait undershoots. Bumped 500ms → 2000ms (test timeout 5000ms → 8000ms) and added a `.catch()` on the fire-and-forget `publish()` call so a rare miss degrades to the test's existing soft-timeout fallback instead of an unhandled rejection. This is a timing constant, not an assertion change.

## package.json
- `mocha`/`chai`/`c8` devDependencies removed; `jest`/`babel-jest`/`@babel/core`/`@babel/preset-env` added (29.x line, matching the rest of the workspace per #3)
- `test`/`coverage` scripts switched to `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules npx jest`, the same hoisting-safe invocation used elsewhere in the monorepo

## Test plan
- [x] `npm -w xn test` — 46/46 passing
- [x] Repeated 3x consecutively — no flakes
- [x] `npm ls` at root — still no UNMET
- [x] `mocha`/`chai`/`c8` fully removed from `xn/package.json`

author: pko89403
body:
## Summary

Prepares the ground for the confidence-aware reranking (CBDR-direction) work by converting the two pending confidence papers into repo reference knowledge, per `docs/wiki/03_reference_processing.md`.

**Fact discipline**: both digests were written strictly from the committed PDF texts. Every number is page-cited in the extraction notes; anything the papers do not state is marked "논문에 명시되지 않음" instead of being filled in. The CBDR paper's own internal inconsistencies (Mid_Layer vs `hidden_states[-1]`, 1k/300/500 vs 2,000/1,000/500 dataset sizes, 30 vs 100 epochs) are recorded verbatim rather than reconciled.

- **`cbdr_parametric_confidence_rag.md`** — CBDR (anonymous ACL submission). Key finding: the method needs white-box hidden-state access at both training (74,204 target-LLM forward passes) and inference, so it cannot be ported to ranksmith's closed-model premise; only the "confidence signal drives document preference" pattern transfers. CBDR itself is a retrieval trigger, not a reranker — out of library scope.
- **`llm_confidence_reranker.md`** — LCR (arXiv:2602.13571). Training-free, genuinely black-box (sampled text only), so it fits ranksmith better; recorded conflicts: needs temperature-1 sampling K=10 vs our temperature-0 JSON-only ModelClient contract, and the paper never discloses its tuned thresholds or call-cost totals.
- **`spec_confidence_aware_reranking.md`** — Draft spec that consumes the existing runtime-readiness signal contract (order-preserving `score_batch` + caller-side candidate zip).
- References index updated (2 papers moved from 대기 to 등록); stale `src/ranksmith/_metrics.py` path in spec TEMPLATE fixed to `benchmarks/metrics.py`.

> Note: the original summary above described the docs-only starting point. The branch has since grown the actual implementation and benchmark tooling — see the updates below.

## Update: implementation (commits after the original summary)

The Q004 design decisions were resolved in-session and the strategy was implemented on this branch: `AnswerConfidenceRerankStrategy` / `AsyncAnswerConfidenceRerankStrategy` (`src/ranksmith/strategies/confidence.py`), `ModelClient.answer` + `parse_answer_response`, `confidence_generation` prompt unification, `examples/answer_confidence.py`, opt-in `answer_confidence` integration in `scripts/compare_reranking.py`, and tests. This PR is **not** docs-only anymore.

## Update (2026-07-16): benchmark comparison tooling

Turnkey tooling to measure `answer_confidence` against the existing README methods (AskUbuntu 361 queries, BM25 top-20, `gpt-5.4-nano`) without rerunning the committed baselines:

- `scripts/build_answer_confidence_training_data.py` — deterministic SQuAD v1.1 builder: per question one gold-context row + BM25 hard-negative rows (matches the inference distribution); pure-Python Okapi BM25 in `benchmarks/bm25.py` (Pyserini-default k1/b). AskUbuntu has no gold answers, so the artifact must be trained on QA data — this fills the SQuAD/QA adapter + CLI gap the generation/training specs explicitly deferred (Phase 2B).
- `scripts/train_answer_confidence.py` — generation (live model) → labeling → training → artifact in one command; fast-fails on single-class labels or test roc_auc < 0.6 (the spec's recorded 100-sample artifact scored 0.333).
- `scripts/compare_reranking.py` — `--algorithm` is now repeatable (several methods on identical cases in one run); `answer_confidence` validates the artifact path before any live call.
- `scripts/merge_benchmark_reports.py` — merges per-method runs with the committed `v3.merged.json` after verifying benchmark identity and exact per-algorithm query-id equality (replaces the manual merge).
- `docs/benchmarks/answer_confidence_askubuntu.md` — the runbook: build → train (same deployment as the benchmark) → single-method run (7,220 calls) → merge → report with the artifact's out-of-domain (SQuAD) label. Spec updated to point at it.

The whole path (build → generation → training → benchmark → merge) was mechanically verified offline with the real SQuAD download, a deterministic fake OpenAI-compatible chat server, and a tiny local encoder; 470 tests + ruff + mypy green. Numbers that depend on LLM quality still need an environment with the AskUbuntu cache and Azure access.

author: rampyg
body:
Adds FROST(Ed25519, SHA-512) threshold signing (RFC 9591) to the Rust core, with Python bindings. This is the last piece of the cross-device custody work: a key can be split among participants so any threshold of them can sign together, and the full private key is never reconstructed at any point, not even during signing.

Implementation: the audited Zcash Foundation `frost-ed25519` crate does the cryptography. core/vouch-core/src/threshold.rs wraps it with the ceremony (generate a threshold identity, each signer commits, each signer produces a signature share, a coordinator aggregates the shares into the final signature). threshold_json.rs is a JSON facade over that, matching the existing robotics_json convention, wired into the UniFFI UDL and the C ABI (vouch_threshold_generate_key / commit / sign_share / aggregate) so the Go, JVM, .NET, C++, and Swift SDKs can all call the same implementation. The regenerated cbindgen header is included.

vouch/threshold.py is a ctypes binding to the same native library for Python. ThresholdSigner runs a full commit, sign, and aggregate ceremony in one call and plugs into the existing Signer.from_backend, so a threshold-backed Signer issues credentials through the ordinary sign_credential path.

The critical property that makes this a drop-in fit: the aggregated signature is a standard Ed25519 signature. It verifies with the existing verifier and needs no new proof type, cryptosuite, or verification path anywhere in the protocol. A verifier cannot tell whether a credential was signed by one key or by a threshold of shares.

Design note on scope: generate_key mints a fresh threshold-native identity rather than converting an existing single-key Ed25519 identity into one. A standard Ed25519 private key's scalar comes from SHA-512-and-clamp over its seed (RFC 8032), and that scalar is not generally a canonical element of the field FROST operates in; naively reducing it would silently produce a different public key and break the DID it was meant to protect. Treat a threshold identity as its own identity from the start, exactly like generate_identity, and enroll it as a device or root the same way any other Vouch identity is enrolled.

Security boundary: the Rust core never has a function that takes shares and returns a seed or private scalar; there is no reconstruct exposed anywhere in this code, even though the underlying crate offers one as an explicit escape hatch. The aggregate function self-verifies its output against the group's own public key before returning it, so a bug or a misbehaving signer cannot silently produce an unverifiable signature. On the Python side, the ctypes binding requires the native library to be present and raises a clear error if it is not found, rather than falling back to a hand-written implementation of threshold cryptography.

Verification: 9 Rust unit tests in threshold.rs (2-of-3 and 3-of-5 signing, different subsets of the same group both verify, wrong message fails verification, bad threshold rejected, single-commitment rejected, no function returns a reassembled key) plus 2 more in threshold_json.rs for the JSON round trip, all passing, along with the full existing vouch-core and uniffi test suites. 10 Python tests pass against the built native library, including the end-to-end Signer.from_backend integration verified through the unmodified Verifier.verify_credential. cargo fmt and cargo clippy are clean on the new files.

## Description

Adds a corporate loan system allowing studios in financial difficulty to take on structured debt. Three tiers are available: SMALL ($500k at 8% annual over 26 weeks), MEDIUM ($1M at 12% over 52 weeks), and LARGE ($2M at 18% over 78 weeks). Weekly repayments are deducted automatically each tick after payroll. A studio that remains in negative cash balance for 4 consecutive weeks is declared bankrupt and locked out of all spending operations. author: dionismuzenitov
body:
## Summary

Owner-approved realism direction: fly the profile the real booster flies (research-grounded: IFT-5/7 — ~170 s fin-steered ballistic fall, landing burn ~1 km/M1.0 for ~23 s, 13→3 engines, final translate into the chopsticks).

### Physics
- **Grid fins were aerodynamically inert to deflection** (hinge about the body long-axis, radial normals — zero AoA change in axial flow at any deflection). Now hinge about the radial strut with tangential normals: deflection tilts the lattice into the airstream = real control torque high above the CoM. The old geometry's accidental weathervane stability had been **masking two controller polarity bugs since SLS-23**.
- Realistic post-boostback ICs: ballistic impact 800 m past the tower (solved against the sim's own drag model), matching the real aim-offset + fin-trim + short-burn architecture. Old IC forced 25 km powered diverts that don't exist in reality.

### Controllers — root causes found by live probing (all sign conventions now *measured*, not assumed)
1. **Attitude pitch loop polarity-inverted since SLS-23** (`cmd+ → ωx−` but `d(upZ)/dt = +ωx` → positive feedback); yaw was accidentally correct (two sign flips cancel).
2. **Component attitude control is blind to inversion** — nose-down reads as "on target" (upX=upZ≈0). Added geometric large-angle righting (`up × target`) + explicit rate damping (limit-cycle killer).
3. Differential fin mixer with measured torque signs; q-gated during coast (no PID windup above ~30 km where fins have nothing to bite).
4. Fin-steered descent: 2 s-cadence ballistic impact prediction + AoA-lean trim (~1–2 km authority — measured, and consistent with fins-trim-only reality).
5. Altitude-indexed burn tracking (clock-indexed under-braked when falling ahead of plan), axis-split PD clamps, burn thrust floor (landing burns never shut down), terminal tilt cap, tighter glide cone (8°, final half).
6. **DOCK phase**: gravity-compensated hover-descent for the final 500 m into the slot — the plan ends at the catch box; the "translate into the chopsticks" act was simply missing.

### Measured state
- **Unjittered Calm run flies the entire catch profile end-to-end**: converging ignition countdown → braking burn (upright, upY 0.95–1.0 throughout) → dock descent crossing the slot altitude at 1–2 m/s within metres laterally.
- **Jittered bench (2 seeds × wind 0/1): 0 % catch, median miss 4.4 km** — IC dispersion (±5 % velocity ≈ ±700 m impact shift + timing changes) breaks the chain somewhere; robustness analysis is the next session's work. PID baseline also improved to 3.3 km with the realistic ICs.

### Verification
- [x] 333 vitest + 27 pytest + lint/typecheck/ruff green (scenario/controller fixtures updated to the new ICs)
- [x] Sign conventions probe-measured (fin torques, gimbal axes, steering lean)
- [ ] CI
- [ ] **Merge requires owner approval**

Note: this changes physics (fin model + scenario ICs) — SLS-47's merged benchmark numbers are superseded by this PR's. Jira comment posted via smart commit (Atlassian MCP still needs reconnection via /mcp).

author: haranathg
body:
## Why this scope

Time-picking was the choke point on every scheduling surface — North Star targets, Lab experiments, Chart plan tasks, and the aged-dump strip all funneled to TaskModal and still forced you to type a time. Fix that one moment; every upstream surface gets smoother in one shot.

## What ships

### `suggestTimes(date, blocks)` utility
Returns 4-6 ordered chip suggestions:
- **"Now"** chip when the active date is today (rounded up to the next 5 min, only if inside the work window and not overlapping an existing block)
- Start of each **≥ 20-min gap** between existing blocks
- Trailing gap after the last block

Block-end estimated from the latest subtask + 15 min, or +60 min if no subs. Cross-midnight subtasks respected so a spillover block properly occupies its actual footprint. Because App.tsx already augments `getBlocksForDate` with materialized spiral instances, **spiral schedules automatically show up as occupied time** — the suggestions won't collide with them.

### Day picker at the top of the modal
Horizontal-scrolling chip row with 5 days: Today / Tomorrow / weekday abbrevs. Indigo highlight for the active day. Lets you say "tomorrow at 8am" without leaving the modal.

### Suggestion chip row
Renders above the task-name input in the pre-parsed state. Hides once a time is picked (or when editing). Tap a chip → time is set, focus moves to the task-name input. You just type the name and hit Enter — no time typing needed.

- **"Now" chips** get an emerald tint
- **Gap chips** are neutral with a "45 min free" sub-label so you can see how much room you have

### Internal refactor
- New optional `getBlocksForDate` prop on TaskModal
- Local `activeDate` state so the day picker can shift days without unmounting
- All internal date computations (save, reschedule, duration parsing, subtask date handling, header label) refactored from the `date` prop to `activeDate`
- `handleMainSubmit` fallback now checks `mainTime` (from prefill OR suggestion tap) instead of `prefillTime` specifically — unifies the two entry paths

## Test plan

- [ ] Tap an empty day → suggestions appear with morning slots and end-of-day gaps
- [ ] Tap a "Now" chip on today → time flips to current time; type "coffee" + Enter → block saved at that time
- [ ] Tap a gap chip like "9:00 · 45 min free" → time picked, type name, Enter → saved
- [ ] From a Lab experiment or Chart plan task: **↳ Schedule this** → calendar opens with the label already typed and suggestions still available
- [ ] Day picker: tap "Tomorrow" → activeDate shifts, suggestions recompute against tomorrow's blocks, save creates a block on tomorrow
- [ ] Tap a scheduled spiral's time slot day — suggestions correctly skip its slot (doesn't propose a colliding time)

## Deliberately out of v1

- Historical patterns (if you've named "run" before, suggest that time). Deferred until we have a state-logging surface to feed it — see the message about rule-learning
- Preferred windows / energy profile
- Environment tags + auto-commute blocks

author: deanmarano
body:
## Summary

Foundational audit for **RFC 0062 (transactional-fixtures burndown)**. Categorizes
every non-`fixtures({})` AR test caller of `setupFixtures` /
`useHandlerTransactionalFixtures` into conversion buckets, decides the
no-fixture-data surface, and emits the per-cluster conversion story cut.

Audit-only — no code conversion, no test renames. The single artifact is the
inventory doc `docs/infrastructure/setupfixtures-caller-buckets-audit.md`.

## Findings

125 `setupFixtures` callers (excl. test-helpers), partitioned cleanly:

- **Bucket A — pair, no data (54):** one or more per-`describe` `setupFixtures()` + `useHandlerTransactionalFixtures()` pairs, no fixture map, no `fixtures(...)` call → replace each pair with `fixtures([], { … })`. Schema setup is orthogonal (41/54 create no tables and ride the canonical schema; the rest use `createTable`/`defineSchema`) and is left untouched — Rails' fixture transaction wiring is independent of table creation (`vendor/rails/activerecord/lib/active_record/test_fixtures.rb:108-133`).
- **Bucket B — redundant (28):** `setupFixtures()` beside an existing `fixtures(...)` call (dead double-wiring) → delete the line.
- **Bucket C — sf-only (31):** handler-wiring only, no txn / no data (mostly PG-DDL suites that break under txn wrapping) → no conversion; confirm intent.
- **Bucket D — mixed (12):** both the pair and a `fixtures(...)` call in one file → per-`describe` hand conversion.

## No-fixture-data surface decision

Use the empty-array form **`fixtures([], { … })`** — no new helper. `useFixtures`
already treats an empty array as a vacuous zero-fixture case
(`use-fixtures.ts:439-443`) that still wires suite + per-test transaction.

## Conversion story cut

7 new RFC 0062 stories emitted (real file lists, clusters `fixtures-burndown-{a,c,d}`):
4× Bucket A, 2× Bucket D, 1× Bucket C confirm. Bucket B is already owned by the
pre-existing `converge-setupfixtures-redundant-next-to-fixtures` story — this
audit supplies its concrete 28-file list rather than cutting duplicates.

Closes-story: audit-setupfixtures-caller-buckets

author: hinaser
body:
Housekeeping before the 0.2.0-beta cycle, four commits:

1. **Sync all module versions to `0.2.0-beta.1`** — the engine crate said `0.1.0-alpha.0`, npm said `0.2.0`, the GUI said `0.2.0-alpha.3`. Also deletes the stale root `package-lock.json` left over from the Node.js engine (the launcher has no dependencies to lock, and a lock cannot reference unpublished `@puppetty/*` versions; nothing in CI uses it).
2. **Persistent Linux credentials** — keyring feature `linux-native` (kernel keyutils) loses secrets on reboot. Switch to `linux-native-sync-persistent`: Secret Service (GNOME Keyring / KWallet) as the persistent store, keyutils as session cache, `crypto-rust` for encrypted D-Bus transport, `vendored` so libdbus builds from source (no new apt packages in any workflow). Note the trade-off: `puppetty cred` on a headless Linux box without a Secret Service daemon will now fail where keyutils used to work — persistence was judged more important.
3. **Beta dist-tag guard** — `npm publish` defaults to `latest`, so publishing `0.2.0-beta.1` would have hijacked plain `npm install -g puppetty` from 0.1.1. Hyphenated versions now publish with `--tag beta`.
4. **Drop Intel macOS** from the npm matrix (`darwin-x64`): no Intel Macs sold since 2020, macOS itself is dropping Intel, and GitHub is retiring the `macos-13` Intel runners. `darwin-arm64` remains.

Windows `cargo check` passes for both crates; engine CI validates the Linux keyring build.

After this merges, tagging `npm-v0.2.0-beta.1` publishes the Rust engine to npm under `@beta` while `latest` stays 0.1.1.

author: psaab
body:
Closes #4188 Closes #4189 Closes #4190

Three `scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` correctness bugs from
fable-review-165 (H-23, H-25, H-30). Python-only; no Go/cargo change.

## H-23 (#4188) — libvirt `physical` passes a netdev name to --hostdev
`deploy --hypervisor libvirt` with a `physical` backing passed the raw
netdev name (e.g. `enp8s0`) to `virt-install --hostdev`, which requires a
PCI/USB address — the domain fails to define / mis-attaches (and per H-21
the error is swallowed). `deploy_libvirt` now resolves the netdev to its
PCI BDF via the existing `pci_of()` helper (accepts a raw PCI address
under `physical:` too; dies with a clear message when unresolvable).
incus is unchanged — `nictype=physical parent=<dev>` correctly takes the
netdev name.
`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` — `deploy_libvirt` physical branch + new
`is_pci_addr()`.

## H-25 (#4189) — watermark mis-orders describe counts and rc numbers
The fetch anti-rollback watermark compared git-describe / pre-release
suffixes as whole strings, so `1.2.3-10-gabc` ranked OLDER than
`1.2.3-9-gdef` and `rc10` below `rc9` — false "possible rollback"
refusals train operators to pass `--allow-rollback` (which then lets a
real downgrade through). Reproduced by execution. `_ver_key` is hoisted
to module scope and numeric-splits the suffix (`_suffix_key`,
int/text-tagged so no mixed compare raises) while keeping the
rc < release < post-release category rank.
`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` — new module-level `_ver_key`/`_suffix_key`.

## H-30 (#4190) — fetch qcow2 never reaches the libvirt golden path
`fetch` left the verified qcow2 at `<out>/xpf-<ver>.qcow2` but
`deploy --hypervisor libvirt` reads the golden at
`/var/lib/libvirt/images/<image>.qcow2` — different dir and basename, no
bridge. Added `libvirt_golden_path()` as the shared SSOT used by BOTH
`libvirt_disk` (deploy) and a new `fetch --install-libvirt`
(`_install_libvirt_golden`, `sudo install` fallback for the root-owned
images dir); the `--qcow2-only` hint prints the exact install command.
`scripts/deploy/xpf-deploy.py` — `libvirt_golden_path`,
`_install_libvirt_golden`, `cmd_fetch` tail, `--install-libvirt` flag.

## Tests (RED-on-revert)
`scripts/deploy/test_xpf_deploy_correctness.py` — 12 new tests mirroring
the H-20/H-22 pattern. Each goes RED when its fix is reverted (verified
locally): H-23 the netdev name reaches --hostdev; H-25 rc10/count-10
ordering inverts under whole-string compare; H-30 the shared golden
helper is gone so fetch never lands the image where deploy reads it.
Full `scripts/deploy` suite: 27/27 (12 new + 15 existing).

## Docs
`examples/deploy/README.md` (physical->PCI note), `docs/distribution.md`
+ `docs/install-images.md` (`fetch --install-libvirt`). H-25 is internal
best-effort CLI state — no operator-facing doc surface.

author: jennifer-shehane
body:
## Summary

Upgrades TypeScript from `^5.3.3` to `^6.0.3` in the root package and both plugin packages (`plugins/cypressRemarkPlugins`, `plugins/llm`), along with the config and code changes TypeScript 6 requires.

## Why

The `typescript` devDependency was behind: the root declared `^5.3.3` (while the lockfile had already resolved to 5.9.3) and both plugin packages declared a stale `^4.7.4` even though they compile with the root-hoisted compiler. The first commit aligns everything on `^5.9.3`; the second moves to v6, making the adjustments the new major requires:

- **Explicit `rootDir`** in both plugin tsconfigs — TS 6 requires it when `outDir` changes the output layout. Set to `./src`, matching what was previously inferred, so the emitted `dist` layout is unchanged.
- **Compile target `es2016` → `es2020`** in both plugins — TS 6's stricter lib handling flags existing `String.matchAll` / `Array.flatMap` usage. The plugins run in Node 22 during the docs build, so es2020 output is safe.
- **`types: ["node"]`** in the `llm` plugin tsconfig plus `@types/node` in root devDependencies — TS 6 no longer implicitly picks up Node globals (`fs`, `path`, `process`, `__dirname`) there.
- **`alwaysStrict: false`** in the `copyTsToJs` transpile options — TS 6 emits a `"use strict"` prologue by default, which leaked into the TS→JS-transformed code samples rendered on docs pages (caught by the plugin's snapshot test). This restores output identical to TS 5.
- **`ignoreDeprecations: "6.0"` in the root tsconfig** — TS 6 raises a hard error (TS5101) for the deprecated `baseUrl` option, which is set by the extended `@docusaurus/tsconfig`. Cypress's webpack preprocessor compiles the e2e specs against this tsconfig, so every spec failed to bundle (Cloud run #1685 errored with 0 specs completed). Also dropped our own redundant `baseUrl`; the inherited one still applies for editor support.

- The `"use strict"` fix is the only source-code change; everything else is dependency ranges and tsconfig.

## Summary
- Recreates `process_unified_inventory_deduction` with a new optional `p_recipe_id` param so production runs deduct/cost by recipe id (no `is_active` filter), self-healing against a soft-deleted "shadow" recipe instead of silently deducting nothing.
- Recreates `complete_production_run` to pass the prep's `recipe_id` and to `RAISE EXCEPTION` when a run completes with zero ingredient deductions but the prep has ingredients defined (loud failure instead of a silent $0 completion) — idempotent retries are exempted.
- Adds a data-repair statement reactivating any prep-linked shadow recipe that was left `is_active = false` (fixes the one bad prod row from the incident).
- Adds a backstop `BEFORE UPDATE OF is_active` trigger on `recipes` that blocks deactivating a recipe still referenced by `prep_recipes`, with a clear error pointing to the Prep page.
- `useRecipes.fetchRecipes` now filters out prep-linked shadow recipes (parallel fetch of `recipes` + `prep_recipes.recipe_id`, fail-closed on either query erroring — clears stale recipes rather than leaking them).
- `useRecipes.deleteRecipe` blocks soft-deleting a prep-linked recipe (destructive toast, returns `false`, no update) as a second line of defense alongside the DB trigger.
- `DeleteRecipeDialog` only calls `onClose()` when `deleteRecipe` actually succeeds, so a blocked delete no longer looks like it worked (dialog stays open).

author: lalalune
body:
Closes #13772 (stages 1–3 + unit/integration tests). Implements the settled D1 HYBRID design (design-doc comment on the issue). Live 10-vs-5 E2E is the separate WS8 issue #13778.

## What this does
Turns the orchestrator's session cap from an **opaque hard-fail** ("acpx max session limit reached (8)" — a thrown Error the caller had to string-match) into a **durable admission queue**: a spawn beyond the worker cap now **parks** its task (`open` status + a durable `metadata.admission` entry) and a dispatcher drains it as slots free — so a swarm can schedule more tasks than the raw session cap instead of dropping the 9th.

**Stage 1 — `AcpService` (typed error + slot classes):** `enforceSessionLimit` throws a typed `SessionCapError { code:'SESSION_CAP_REACHED', maxSessions, activeCount, slotClass }`. Sessions carry a `slotClass: 'worker'|'system'`; `worker` counts against `ELIZA_ACP_MAX_SESSIONS`, `system` against a separate `ELIZA_ACP_SYSTEM_SESSION_HEADROOM` (default 2) so the read-only completion **verifier can always spawn** and never deadlocks behind a full worker pool. New `getCapacity()`.

**Stage 2 — `OrchestratorTaskService` (the queue):** park-at-cap in `spawnAgentForTask`; durable `metadata.admission` (rebuilt from `open` tasks on boot — no new table, no new task status); deterministic order (priority bands → FIFO → aging promotion so `low` can't starve); depth cap (`ELIZA_ACP_ADMISSION_QUEUE_DEPTH`, default 32 → `AdmissionQueueFullError`); `drainAdmissionQueue` on every terminal session event + a 30s reconcile tick; idle-reclaim of completed-but-alive (`keepAliveAfterComplete`) sessions; dequeue on cancel/pause/archive/delete, re-enqueue on resume. Behind `ELIZA_ACP_ADMISSION_QUEUE` (default ON; `0` restores reject-at-cap for bisection).

**Stage 3 — surfaces:** `ACTIVE_SUB_AGENTS` provider capacity line + `data.capacity`; `GET /api/orchestrator/capacity`; `POST /tasks/:id/agents` → **202** when queued / **429** on full queue; `TaskThreadDto.admission` overlay; supervisor room-digest queued count.

## Verification (independently re-run)
- **67/67 new+updated tests pass** — `admission-queue-order` (8, pure ordering/aging/tie-break), `admission-queue.integration` (9, **real `OrchestratorTaskService` + real in-memory store** + a faithful fake ACP transport that throws the real `SessionCapError`: 5 spawns vs cap 2 → 2 active + 3 queued in deterministic order, drain order matches with **zero drops**, verifier spawns at full worker cap via system headroom, idle-reclaim, restart-rebuild, depth-cap `AdmissionQueueFullError`), `acp-service` (50, slot classes + typed error + `getCapacity`).
- Mutation-checked: key assertions fail without the implementation.
- Typecheck: **0 errors in touched files**. Biome clean on all 10 touched files.
- Regression sweep (`vitest run`): the 26 failures are the **pre-existing** `runtime.reportError is not a function` in `task-policy.ts` (added by #13324) — those files are byte-identical to `develop` and untouched here; every test in files this PR changed passes.

## Honestly deferred (called out, not half-wired)
- **Router-respawn / `reattachSession` re-queue-at-head** (design item 2, 2nd half): these paths now throw the typed `SessionCapError` but do not re-queue at the head — that needs an inner(ACP)→outer(orchestrator) seam and is a recovery-path refinement; the reconcile tick + terminal-event drain still make forward progress. 
- **Live 10-vs-5 E2E** → #13778.

## Summary

New **Legality** tab in the mon editor (Party and Boxes): a rule-based report of everything about the selected mon that normal play could not produce, or that the game itself will rewrite.

Checks in [`src/save/report.ts`](src/save/report.ts):

- **Species**: unknown internal id → glitch mon (report stops there).
- **Level**: outside 1–100.
- **EXP**: `levelForExp(growthRate, exp) ≠ level` — the game recalculates level from EXP on box deposit, so this is a warn with the level it will become.
- **Moves**: duplicates and empty movesets (impossible in normal play); unknown move ids; moves outside the species line's learnset (level-up + TM/HM + pre-evolutions, reusing `legality.ts`); level-up moves known **below their minimum learn level** (new `minLearnLevel` walks the pre-evolution closure; level-0 starting moves count as level 1).
- **PP**: current PP above the max for the stored PP-Up count.
- **Types / catch rate**: stored bytes differing from the species values — flagged as *info* since catch rate legitimately persists through evolution in Gen 1.
- **Stats** (party mons): stored stats vs the `_CalcStat` formula for the mon's DVs/stat EXP; current HP > max HP.
- **Names**: nickname/OT not encodable in the charmap.

Severity model: **bad** (red) = impossible in normal play; **warn** (amber) = the game may rewrite it on its own; **info** (grey) = noteworthy but harmless. The tab shows a clean-pass state when nothing is flagged.

- `vitest`: **188 passed** — 14 new tests covering every rule with fixture values read from the generated Shin 1.25.0 data (e.g. BULBASAUR learns VINE WHIP at 13, VENUSAUR has it at level 0, DITTO knows only TRANSFORM).

author: whimet
body:
## Problem

Clicking **Publish** to save a macro kicks off a 2–8s async chain — `saveToPlatform` (network create/update) → save-time attachment upload (capped at 8s) → a 500ms delay → `view.submit()` — with **zero visual feedback**. The button stays visually idle *and clickable*, so it feels broken and an impatient user can double-fire the save.

## Fix

Wire a real loading state onto the **existing `save` → `saved` lifecycle** across every editor that owns a Publish button:

| Editor | Publish button | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Sequence / Mermaid / PlantUML | `Header.vue` → `PublishButton.vue` | ✅ wired |
| Embed | `DocumentList.vue` → `PublishButton.vue` | ✅ wired |
| OpenAPI | `react/Header.tsx` → `react/PublishButton.tsx` | ✅ wired |
| Graph (DrawIO) | DrawIO's in-iframe button (`spin=1`) | native feedback, unchanged |

Behaviour:
- **`PublishButton`** (Vue + React) gains a `loading` prop → shows a spinner + "Publishing…", sets `disabled` + `aria-busy` while in flight (blocks double-clicks).
- Each shell sets a saving flag on click (double-fire guarded), clears it on `saved` (success) and a **new `save-error` event** (failure — those paths deliberately keep the dialog open for retry, so the spinner must be released), plus a **20s safety timeout** so an unexpected hang can never strand the spinner. All listeners torn down on unmount.
- `forgeIndex.ts` / `forge-embed-editor.ts` / `forge-swagger-editor.ts` emit `save-error` on the save-rejected and `view.submit`-failed paths.

## Note on latency

This makes the wait *legible*, not *shorter*. The ~8s attachment-upload-before-`view.submit` step still blocks the dialog close; reducing that is a separate change.

## Verification

- `vue-tsc` clean on all changed files
- Full unit suite: **807 passed**
- `pnpm build:lite` succeeds
- Manual staging spot-check: to follow

body:
This PR adds a containerized build path so Narra can be built into an APK without installing Android Studio or the Android SDK locally.

## What's added

- `Dockerfile` — disposable build environment based on Eclipse Temurin JDK 17. Installs the Android command-line tools, SDK 36, and build-tools 36.0.0, then runs the Gradle build.
- `build-apk.sh` — convenience wrapper around the Docker command.
- `.dockerignore` — keeps the Docker build context small.
- README section under `Getting Started` documenting the new build path.

## Usage

```bash
./build-apk.sh                 # debug APK -> out/debug/app-debug.apk
./build-apk.sh assembleRelease # release APK
```

The first run downloads the Android SDK and project dependencies. Subsequent builds reuse Docker layer caching and a persisted Gradle cache mount, so they are significantly faster than the first run.

The only requirement on the host machine is Docker or Podman.
