## What changed
- Reuse the renderer's serialized MenuBarExtra item payload and action map when the registry version and assets path are unchanged.
- Keep tray title, tooltip, and tray icon updates flowing while avoiding stable menu item walks and icon serialization.
- Cache the visible-payload item hash when the serialized item array identity is stable.
- Add focused regression coverage for title-only ticks, handler-only registry updates, and item-hash reuse.

## Why
Title-only menu-bar ticks were still sorting and serializing the full registered item tree, resolving every item and alternate icon, and hashing the full item payload before discovering that only tray-visible fields changed.

## Compatibility impact
Registry, handler, submenu, alternate, section, disabled-label, icon, and extension-context behavior is preserved. Registry version or assets-path changes invalidate the item/action cache, and actions are still installed before unchanged visible payloads are skipped.

## How tested
- `node --test scripts/test-menubar-payload-cache.mjs scripts/test-menubar-renderer-serialization-cache.mjs`
- `node scripts/run-node-tests.mjs --exclude-perf`
- `PATH=/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/npm/bin:$PATH node /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js run typecheck:renderer`
- `PATH=/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/npm/bin:$PATH node /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js run build:renderer`
- Codex LSP diagnostics on `menubar-runtime-parent.tsx` and `menubar-runtime-payload-cache.ts`: no errors

## Performance evidence
Actual-module baseline before edits, 60 stable items with 12 alternates over 120 title ticks: 7,200 item serializer entries, 8,640 item icon payload calls, 120 tray icon payload calls, 120 IPC sends, 148.81 ms in the timer-based harness.

After edits with the same timer-based harness: 0 item serializer entries, 0 item icon payload calls, 120 tray icon payload calls, 120 IPC sends, 155.35 ms. That wall-clock sample is timer-harness dominated, so I also ran a direct `syncMenuBar`-awaited comparison in the same process: cache-disabled shape 14.61 ms vs current cache 4.25 ms for the same 120 ticks, with item icon calls dropping from 8,640 to 0.

## Stack validation
Started from required branch state `codex/perf-wave4-integrated-stack-20260705` at `ac90ce403aeddab98d0a1b245afce268c48b8bfd`. Implementation branch is `codex/perf-menubar-renderer-serialize-cache-20260705`, commit `51242473dd126f4d9a8cbd84bfa6a1b99b9f81fb`.

No previous PR. This replaces the parent audit's synthetic renderer serialization-cache model with measured actual-module behavior and regression coverage.

body:
## Resumen

Permite usar **modelos anatómicos reales** en el capítulo del Cuerpo Humano, con el mismo patrón (offline) que planetas/dinos y **respaldo automático** a la anatomía procedural si no hay modelo.

- **`npm run anatomy`** + `src/data/anatomy.manifest.json`: descarga un GLB por pieza a `src/assets/anatomy/<key>.glb` (`corazon`, `pulmones`, `cerebro`, `estomago`, `intestinos`, `huesos`, `musculos`, `cuerpo`). Fuentes CC recomendadas en el manifiesto: **BodyParts3D**, **NIH 3D**, **Z-Anatomy**, Sketchfab.
- **`GltfModel`**: cargador GLB robusto reutilizable — aplana a mallas estáticas (evita los fallos de mallas con esqueleto), normaliza la altura y centra.
- **`OrganModel`** usa el GLB real si existe (por id) y, si no, el procedural. **`BodyScene`** igual para esqueleto, músculos y cuerpo completo.

## Cómo usarlo (en local)
1. Consigue GLBs (o convierte STL/.blend a .glb con Blender / gltf-transform) y pon su URL en el manifiesto — o coloca los `.glb` directamente en `src/assets/anatomy/`.
2. `npm run anatomy` → `npm run dev`. Cada pieza con modelo real se ve automáticamente; el resto siguen procedurales.
3. `git add src/assets/anatomy CREDITS-anatomy.md && commit && push`.

## Verificación
- `npm run build` y `npm run dev` OK. Sin modelos, el capítulo funciona igual (procedural).

## Nota honesta
No he podido incluir URLs directas verificadas: los repositorios de anatomía CC sirven sobre todo `.blend`/`.stl` (no `.glb` con enlace directo estable). El pipeline queda listo; solo hay que rellenar las URLs o soltar los `.glb`. Si me dices qué piezas priorizas, te ayudo a encontrar modelos concretos y su licencia.

author: laboef1900
body:
Closes #118

> **Stacked on #130 pt1 (PR #137)** — base is `chore/130-claude-md-contracts` (shares the error-contract surface). Per CLAUDE.md's stacked-PR rule, **retarget this PR's base to `main` before merging** (after #137 lands).

Roles were derived from the IdP claim and stored on `User`, but **not enforced** — any authenticated user had full access (spec D8 deferred). This ships enforcement whole.

## Server (the real boundary)

A post-authentication `onRequest` hook gates every **mutating** (`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`) `/api` route on the `ADMIN` role → `403 FORBIDDEN` for VIEWERs.

- **Exempts** `/api/auth/*` and the read-only `POST /api/clusters/:id/forecast/scenario` (a query, not a mutation) — a blanket "non-GET = admin" rule would wrongly block that scenario route, which is exactly the trap the issue calls out.
- In `AUTH_MODE=disabled` the anonymous principal is `ADMIN`, so nothing is gated.
- `FORBIDDEN` (in `SERVICE_ERROR_CODES`) and `ForbiddenError` (403) already existed — this wires them up. `settings-auth`'s own admin gate (which also covers its GET read) is left in place.

`requiresAdmin(method, routePath)` is a pure, unit-tested helper.

## Web (affordance)

- `useIsAdmin()` hook (reads the root router context; disabled-mode = admin) + an `AdminOnly` wrapper.
- Primary create CTAs hidden from viewers: **New cluster** (via `AdminOnly`), **Add host / Add item** (via a `canManage` prop on the tab components, so they stay router-independent and unit-testable).
- 403 messages already surface through the existing per-mutation error toasts (`describeApiError` → the server's `ForbiddenError` message), so the server + toasts fully cover any control not explicitly hidden.

## Verification

- **Full server suite: 344 ✅** (new: viewer 403 on mutation, viewer 200 on GET + on the scenario POST, admin allowed, disabled-mode ungated, `requiresAdmin` matrix).
- **Full web suite: 272 ✅** (new: `AdminOnly` admin/viewer/disabled, Add host/item hidden for viewers).
- `typecheck` (server + web) ✅, `lint` ✅.

  `nixos/monitoring/grafana-dashboards/`.
- Extend `.gitattributes`: `**/*.generated.json` → linguist-generated, Grafana
  dashboards → linguist-vendored. Correct the wrong tokei comment.

author: lakshay122007
body: ## What does this PR do? Adds a new **ORAM (Oblivious RAM) Simulator** to the Algo Infinity Verse visualizers collection. It's a two-part comparison built around Path ORAM: first showing how naive encrypted memory still leaks information through access patterns, then showing how Path ORAM eliminates that leakage entirely. **Part 1 — The Problem (Naive Memory):** 8 encrypted data blocks the user can click to "read." Every click immediately reveals the exact block identity to a simulated adversary log, demonstrating that encryption alone doesn't hide *which* data was accessed. **Part 2 — The Solution (Path ORAM):** A full working Path ORAM implementation: - Binary tree with 4 levels, 8 leaves, 15 nodes, each bucket holding up to Z=4 blocks - Position map tracking each block's current randomly-assigned leaf, re-randomized on every access - Clicking a data block triggers a real Path ORAM access: fetches the entire root-to-leaf path (animated node-by-node), locates the block (in a bucket or the stash), re-randomizes its leaf assignment, and evicts the stash back into the path - Animated tree canvas — active path nodes glow purple, the node where the target block is found glows green, leaf nodes are cyan, bucket fill shown as count/capacity - Stash panel showing displaced blocks awaiting eviction - Adversary log for this side shows only path node addresses — it's mathematically unable to tell which block was accessed, and the "blocks identified" counter stays at 0/8 regardless of how many accesses happen - Stats panel: total accesses, buckets fetched per access (4), overhead vs. naive (4×), max stash size seen **Part 3 — Learn section:** four cards covering the pattern-leakage problem, why a tree structure is used, Intel SGX's real-world use of ORAM, and the bandwidth cost of obliviousness. ## Related issue Fixes #1623 ## Type - author: omritoptix
body:
Closes #2179

## What

Adds a governance-gated revocation denylist to `x/agent`, keyed by a fingerprint of the agent's TEE policy (lowercase hex SHA-256 of its deterministic proto marshaling). When an enclave image is found vulnerable, one gov action kills the whole fleet pinned to it — instead of trusting each operator to self-deactivate per agent.

- **`MsgRevokePolicy` / `MsgUnrevokePolicy`** — authority is the x/gov module account (same pattern as `x/sponsorship`); any other signer gets `ErrPermissionDenied`. Both are idempotent.
- **Enforcement** — `SubmitAttestedAction` and `RegisterAgent` reject when the policy fingerprint is in the denylist (`ErrFailedPrecondition`). O(1) point lookup per submit; no iteration over agents at revoke time.
- **Pure denylist** — `agent.Active` is never mutated, so unrevoking a false alarm restores every affected agent with zero side effects.
- **Queries** — `RevokedPolicies` (ascending), `PolicyRevoked(fingerprint)`, and the single-`Agent` query now returns derived `fingerprint` + `revoked` fields so governance can obtain the fingerprint to revoke from a query instead of computing it. `EventRegisterAgent` also surfaces the fingerprint.
- **Genesis** — the revoked set round-trips through export/import; `GenesisState.Validate` rejects entries that aren't 64-char lowercase hex.
- **CLI** — `tx agent revoke-policy|unrevoke-policy`, `q agent revoked-policies|policy-revoked`.

## Proof of execution

### Revocation logic: authority gating, fleet-wide submit block, register block, reversibility, fingerprint stability, queries, genesis round-trip

=== RUN   TestGenesisValidate_BadFingerprint
--- PASS: TestGenesisValidate_BadFingerprint (0.00s)
PASS
ok  	github.com/dymensionxyz/dymension/v3/x/agent/keeper	0.151s
```

### Module and full test suite
**How:** `go test ./x/agent/...` then `go test ./...`
**Evidence:**
```
ok  	github.com/dymensionxyz/dymension/v3/x/agent/keeper	0.503s

```
Full suite: 35 packages `ok`, one failure that turned out to be a pre-existing build break on `origin/main` (`x/eibc/keeper`: `lp_test.go:165` called `types.NewDemandOrder` with the pre-#2168 arity — a semantic merge conflict between #2168 and #2170). This PR carries the one-line fix in its second commit; after it:
```

$ go vet ./...

```

### Lint and generated code are clean
**How:** `golangci-lint run ./x/agent/... ./app/...` (v2.x), `gofumpt -l x/agent app/keepers.go`, re-ran `make proto-gen` and checked `git status`

### Live chain end-to-end: queries, non-gov rejection, gov proposal executes the revocation
**How:** built `dymd` at HEAD, ran a throwaway single-validator chain (10s voting period), exercised the new queries and txs, then passed a real gov proposal carrying `MsgRevokePolicy`
**Evidence:**

}

### Rotation × revocation (post-merge of #2176): promote-then-check ordering, update-time denylist, effective-fingerprint query
**How:** merged `main` (timelocked policy rotation) into the branch; `SubmitAttestedAction` now promotes a matured pending policy *before* the denylist check, `UpdateAgentPolicy` rejects scheduling an already-revoked policy, and the `Agent` query fingerprints the effective policy. Regression tests: `go test ./x/agent/keeper/... -run 'Revoked|RevokePolicy|Fingerprint' -v`

**Not verified:** the on-chain `SubmitAttestedAction` block/unblock path — a genuine GCP TEE attestation token cannot be minted locally, so that path is proven at the keeper layer with the fake verifier (`TestSubmitAttestedAction_RevokedPolicy` above).

author: zijie6080
body:
## 概要

实现"巨型手卷"视口:用户可在 16384×4096 的世界坐标长卷上平移、缩放,画面由三级图块金字塔组成。包含两轮工作:第一版(数据 + 基础视口 + 锚点缩放)与手感/性能升级(交叉淡入、惯性、软边界、懒加载、panTo)。

## 变更内容

**数据与基础视口**
- `src/data/tiles.json`:世界坐标固定 16384×4096;L0×1 / L1×4 / L2×16 横向均分;scaleRange 为 L0 [0,1.2]、L1 [0.8,3]、L2 [2.5,999](刻意重叠供交叉淡入)。
- `ScrollViewport.tsx`:Pixi v8(`resizeTo: window`,背景 `#0d0b08`),world 容器承载图块,相机 = world 的 position/scale;`next/dynamic` + `ssr: false`(Pixi 禁 SSR)。
- 交互:Pointer Events 拖拽平移、滚轮/双指捏合缩放,严格以指针(捏合中点)为锚;canvas `touch-action: none`;缩放下限 = 整幅适配窗口(随 resize 重算)。
- `src/lib/store.ts`(zustand):`{ camX, camY, zoom, levelAlphas, panTo }`。

**手感与性能升级**
- **层级交叉淡入**:各层按 zoom 与 scaleRange 计算目标 alpha(区间内 1,边缘 0.15 宽过渡带),每帧 0.08 插值;过渡期相邻层同时渲染;alpha≈0 的层 `visible=false` 跳过渲染。
- **惯性滑动**:拖拽中采样最近 ~100ms 指针均速,松手续滑,每帧 ×0.92,低于阈值停止;惯性中再按下立即停止并进入拖拽;仅平移有惯性。
- **软边界**:画缘最多拖出 10% 视口;越界位移 ×0.4 橡皮筋;松手指数逼近弹回(临界阻尼,无振荡);画高小于视口时垂直锁定居中;惯性撞界额外衰减(×0.7/帧)并同样弹回。
- **懒加载与内存**:仅加载"视口外扩 1 屏"内且目标 alpha>0 的层的图块;`Assets.load` 完成后从 0 淡入;移出 2 屏销毁 Sprite 并 `Assets.unload` 释放纹理(加载/销毁阈值拉开形成迟滞,防抖动);加载失败画 `#1a1712` 占位矩形 + `console.warn`,无未捕获异常。
- **panTo API**:`panTo({x, y, zoom, duration})` 经 store 暴露,easeInOutCubic 飞行,把目标世界点带到屏幕中心;pointerdown/wheel 立即中断动画交还控制权。调试面板(常驻左下角,显示 zoom 与各层 α)新增"测试 panTo"按钮。

## 验证(playwright-core + 无头 Chromium,驱动 `next build` 静态导出产物)

组件把相机状态、各层 alpha、图块 loading/ready 计数镜像到 `window.__cam` 供断言。

**缩放锚点**:缩放前取指针屏幕点 p,算世界点 `w = (p − cam)/zoom`;发真实滚轮事件后反算 `s = w × zoom′ + cam′`,断言 `|s − p| < 1px`。多位置、双方向(含缩放上下限钳制路径)测试,**漂移全部 0.000px**。

**快速反复缩放的加载/销毁稳定性**(第 6 条要求):30 轮随机位置、正反交替的滚轮急缩放后——ready 计数峰值从未超过图块总数(无重复加载,`Assets.load` 同 URL 去重 + 图块状态机双保险);停止操作 2.5s 后 loading 归零、ready 稳定不再变化(无加载/销毁往复抖动,因为加载 1 屏/销毁 2 屏的迟滞区间);过程无一 console error。另在最大缩放(视口仅覆盖 ~512 世界单位)下长距离平移 ~15000 世界单位,ready 计数保持在小窗口值(5→4),证明远端图块确实被销毁回收而非只增不减。

**其余断言**:重叠区(zoom≈1.0)L0/L1 alpha 同时 >0.9(交叉淡入生效);最小缩放下拖拽 600px 撞界,拖拽中 camX 仅 193(橡皮筋生效),松手后精确弹回 128(=10% 视口上限);快拖松手后续滑 >26px(惯性);点"测试 panTo"飞至 zoom 2.200(误差 <0.01),动画中 pointerdown 立即将 animating 置 false 且相机停稳。

## 已知问题 / 决策

L2 图块 2048px 覆盖 1024 世界单位,"1:1 像素"对应 zoom = 2.0,但 L2 scaleRange 自 2.5 起——按字面 L2 永不可见。故最大缩放取 `max(1:1, L2 下限) = 2.5`(代码有注释),L2 在最大缩放可见,仅 1.25× 轻微上采样;后续调 scaleRange 时可一并消除。

author: calumjs
body:
Closes #200

## Problem
The dashboard's live activity feed (`spyglass-run-app.html`, `renderFeed`) only shows a run that carries a `progress.phase` from a liveness beat. shipwright beats while building, but **muster emitted none** — so a PR under review showed nothing on the feed and the review lane went silent on-stream (it had to be hand-patched by manually emitting `beat --run <n> --phase reviewing` per PR).

muster's SKILL already had a §0b beat block, but it was framed *conditionally* — only "when crows-nest runs you as a background review subagent", motivated solely by stall-detection (#134). That reads as "beat only in the background pipeline", which is why reviews weren't reliably populating the feed.

## What changed
Reworked **§0b of `skills/muster/SKILL.md`** so muster beats on **every review** (foreground or under crows-nest), documenting the two reasons it matters (the live feed / review lane #200 **and** stall-detection #134). Beats, in order:

- `reviewing` **at the start** (two lenses fan out, §1), with a **refreshed `reviewing` note** as it progresses — "running the two review lenses" → "consolidating findings" (§2) — so the ticker note keeps moving.
- `visual-inspection` just before the §1b render.
- `posting` when the review is posted to the PR (§3).
- terminal `done` when the review completes (§4).

Also documents: notes must be **short, plain-language, viewer-friendly** (shown live on the stream ticker); the run is keyed by **branch (else PR number)** — the same key shipwright/crows-nest use, so the dashboard resolves it onto the same run; and beats are **best-effort, side-channel and reap-safe** (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` main-repo resolution) — a liveness write must never block or fail a review. Mirrors shipwright §0a's discipline/wording.

Bumps `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` → `0.48.45`.

## Verification

author: aryaethn
body:
Closes #588. Corrects the **statement** of `large_agreement_set_on_curve_implies_correlated_agreement`
in `ProximityGap/BCIKS20/Curves.lean` — the two defects #588 reports (a vacuous `∃ v` and a false
`… = Finset.univ`) are removed. The proof of the corrected lemma is left as `sorry`, exactly as it was
before this change (the `sorry` count is unchanged); #588 is about the *statement* being wrong, which
this fixes.

The current conclusion has two defects, both machine-checked in #588:

1. **Vacuous `∃ v`.** `v := u` discharges the existential with *no* hypotheses
   (`δᵣ(curve u z, curve u z) = 0 ≤ δ`, and `{x | ∃ i, u i x ≠ u i x} = ∅`), so its only real
   content was the first conjunct.
2. **False `… = Finset.univ`.** `rho` occurs only in `hδ` and is otherwise unconstrained by `V`, so
   the statement is equivalent to its `rho := 0` instance. Concretely (`F = ZMod 5`, `n = 1`, `l = 2`,
   `V = {const 0, const 1, const 2}`, `δ = 1/2`): `S = {0,1,2}`, so both `hδ` and `hS` (`n·l = 2 < 3`)
   hold while `S ≠ univ`. The counterexample in #588 compiles and `#print axioms` reports only
   `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

This PR restates the lemma to mirror the correctly-shaped Johnson-regime sibling
`large_agreement_set_on_curve_implies_correlated_agreement'`, sharing its conclusion, and keeping the
unique-decoding hypotheses (`hδ : δ ≤ (1 - rho) / 2`, `hS : n * l < #S`):

```lean
∃ v : Fin l → Fin n → F,
  ∀ i, v i ∈ V ∧
    (1 - δ) * n ≤ ({ x : Fin n | ∀ i, u i x = v i x } : Finset _).card
```

Notes:
- The `sorry` count is unchanged (the lemma was already `sorry`); no declaration consumes it, so no
  downstream code is affected. `lake build` / `validate.sh` green locally.
- **Design question:** the primed sibling *also* leaves `rho` unconnected to `V`. Should both lemmas
  additionally tie `rho` to `V` (e.g. `V` a rate-`rho` linear code, or `(1 - rho) * n ≤ Code.dist V`)
  so that `δ ≤ (1 - rho)/2` sits inside `V`'s unique-decoding radius? Glad to adjust to whatever shape
  you intend.

Happy to follow up with a proof of the unique-decoding regime once the target statement is confirmed.

body:
Replaces the binary show-done with a viewer-side cooldown: how long a `done` tile lingers (from its `seen` stamp) before it fades off the board.

- Toolbar cycles off / 1m / 5m / 10m / 30m / always; default 5m.
- 0 = hide instantly, Infinity = show forever (subsumes old show-done); setShowDone(bool) kept as a shim over the two extremes.
- Purely client-side: board.js reuses `seen`; the 60s liveness timer re-clones to expire done tiles when a finite cooldown is set. Persisted per-viewer in localStorage via a new onDoneCooldownChange callback (dashboard.html).
- Old/unstamped done tiles count as expired (hidden) unless cooldown is always.

Gives a moment of "handled" feedback after the mute->done flow without permanent clutter; long/always is the power-user opt-in.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide OWNER/ADMIN full control over transactional email subject/text/html while keeping automatic sending from system events.
- Use Resend as the live provider while preserving a debug-only logging mode and always persisting `EmailLog` entries with provider metadata.
- Support safe template rendering with order-driven variables and built-in seeded defaults so the system ships with usable templates.

### Description
- Add Prisma models `EmailTemplate` and `EmailTemplateVersion` to persist templates, enabled state, versioning, and history and include a migration SQL file and seeding hook via `seedDefaultEmailTemplates` (run from `prisma/seed.ts`).
- Implement template system and rendering: `DEFAULT_EMAIL_TEMPLATES`, `renderEmailTemplate`, `variablesFromOrder`, `itemsListFromOrder`, and `itemsTableFromOrder` in `lib/email/*` and expose `renderTemplateForOrder` and `previewDefault` for previews and seeding.
- Add provider/send flow `sendAndLogEmail` that respects `EMAIL_MODE=debug | live`, uses Resend in live mode (`EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend`) and always writes `EmailLog` with `provider`, `status`, `providerMessageId`, and `error` in `metadata`; `sendAndLogEmail` is used by `sendOrderTemplate` and `sendCustomerOrderTemplate`.
- Wire templates into system events: replace debug-only calls with `sendCustomerOrderTemplate` / `sendOrderTemplate` for order confirmation, payment confirmation, admin notifications, and shipment emails; email failures are caught so they do not roll back order/payment/shipment flows.
- Add admin UI at `/admin/email-templates` (OWNER/ADMIN only) to list, edit subject/text/html, preview with fake order data, send test email, reset to default, enable/disable, and view recent logs and version history via `lib/email/admin-actions.ts` and `app/admin/email-templates/page.tsx`.
- Security/dev hygiene: add `resend` to `package.json` (manifest updated), add `EMAIL_*` placeholders to `.env.example`, and update `.gitignore` to exclude `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.production`, and `.env*.local`.
- Add static launch checks in `scripts/static-check.mjs` to fail when `resend` is missing, when `EMAIL_MODE=live` but `RESEND_API_KEY`/`EMAIL_FROM` are missing, when `.env.example` contains real-looking secrets, or when shipment confirmation still calls the old debug-only provider.

### Testing
- `npm run prisma:generate` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck` — passed after code updates to admin actions signatures.
- `npm run lint:static` / `npm run lint` / `npm run smoke` / `npm run build` — all passed (static checks included the new Resend validations).
- `npm install resend@latest` — attempted but failed with HTTP 403 in this environment, so `package.json`/`package-lock.json` were updated manually to declare the `resend` dependency; runtime install should succeed in CI or proper environment.
- `npm run launch:audit` (regression smoke/launch audit) — blocked here because `DATABASE_URL` was not provided for regression tests; migration and seed were added (`prisma/migrations/...` and seed invocation) and should run in an environment with database configured.

author: dkkyai
body:
## Overview

Phase 3 + Phase 4 of the containerization epic. Two more cross-cutting concerns are extracted from the host-pinned Processor into lightweight, containerized bridge consumers, and the bridge's completed-feed becomes a **multi-consumer event stream** (so more consumers can be added cheaply later).

- **JSearch** (`jobfit-jsearch`) — the daily job-board API intake, off the host cron into a container.
- **Notifier** (`jobfit-notifier`) — Discord/Telegram messaging, out of the Processor into a completed-feed event consumer.

After this, only `jd-processor` remains on PM2 (host-pinned: Chrome/CDP + local LLMs); everything else is a container.

## Technical Details

### JSearch — `services/job-fit-apply-ai-jsearch`
- `JSearchClient` (RapidAPI), `IngestRunner` (fetch → submit `JD_SCRAPED` to the bridge), `RunState` (persisted last-run gate), `Cursor`-free.
- **One-shot JVM in a shell loop** (`--once`) so steady-state memory is a sleeping shell (~3 MB), not a 24/7 JVM. The last-run gate makes restarts free — important for the **150-calls/MONTH** quota (once/day × 4 calls ≈ 120/mo).
- `--jsearch` removed from the pipeline (`JSearchClient`/`JSearchConfig`/`JobListing`/handler) → the old host cron is now an inert no-op.

### Notifier — `services/job-fit-apply-ai-notifier`
- Long-running poll loop (near-real-time). `NotificationClient` (Discord/Telegram) + `Notifier` (formatting, ported from `notifyJobResult`) + `Cursor` (client-side, **seeded at feed head on cold start → no history spam**) + heartbeat health.
- **At-least-once**: a crash mid-batch re-sends a few messages — harmless for chat pings.

### Bridge — multi-consumer event stream
- `GET /api/jobs/completed?all=true` reads by `completed_seq` cursor, bypassing the Poller's `writeback_done` ack (the Poller keeps its default work-queue behavior; consumers coexist).
- `GET /api/jobs/completed/head` for cold-start cursor seeding.
- Widened `CompletedJob` with `company / role_title / fit_score / pipeline_action / job_url / artifact_url`.
- **Fix:** `artifact_url` (the markserv report URL) was sent by the Processor but silently dropped — `ResultRequest` had no field for it. Now captured + persisted.

### Processor
- Messaging removed: `BatchNotificationService` deleted; `NotificationClient` **kept** (used by `AlertService`). Error results now carry `company/role_title/job_url` so `JD_Error` events still show what failed.

_Incidental: an unrelated pre-existing doc tweak to `tuner/env-llm-tuner/ENV_LLM_TUNER_SKILL.md` that was already in the working tree is included._

## Testing & Quality

- **JSearch:** 16 tests — JobListing parse, `IngestRunner` (gate skip/fire, short-jd filter, dedup/queued/failed counting), `RunState`, CLI parse, **+ a real-bridge contract test** (`submit → JD_SCRAPED`, 422 short-jd, dedup).
- **Notifier:** 22 tests — `Notifier` formatting/gating (no-channels, non-job skip, below/above threshold, error line, Discord/Telegram HTML links), `NotifierLoop` (cold-start head seed, cursor advance, pagination), `Cursor`, CLI parse, **+ a real-bridge contract test** (widened event fields + `?all=true` + `/head`).
- **Bridge:** +4 write-back-store tests (`all=true` includes acked jobs; new event fields round-trip; result `job_url` overrides null enqueue).
- **Pipeline:** `ProcessorCommandHandlerTest` / `ProcessingPipelineTest` / `CommandParserTest` updated (messaging + `--jsearch` removal). All suites green.
- **Verified live:** all 7 containers healthy; the widened feed + `?all=true` + head cursor were exercised against a **real disposable bridge** (contract tests), and the notifier cold-start seeded at head=54 (skipping ~1,900 historical jobs).

### QE notes
- No new Playwright/e2e scripts (these are backend services; verification is unit + real-bridge contract, matching the Poller/JSearch pattern).
- **Not yet exercised live:** an actual Discord/Telegram *send* — the queue was idle at cutover, so it fires on the next real completed job. The send path itself is covered by unit + contract tests.
- **At-least-once dupes** on notifier restart are acceptable for chat, but flagged for any future stream consumer where dupes would matter.

body:
## Summary
Iterates on the v2.4 review: Mikan out of the all-time top 5, centers restored without letting any single fix over-shrink 1980s guards, era greats headlining their eras, and LeBron/Jordan at the top. Engine + report only — no shipped data modified.

## Changes
- **Role defensive-impact multiplier** (big 1.15 / wing 1.0 / guard 0.95), applied *after* within-role standardization: compare centers to centers, then weight the role's defensive importance — impact-metric distributions consistently show bigs dominating the defensive top end.
- **Load term in OFF** (0.10): z(minutes) within the era window. Sustaining production over a 40-minute burden beats 34 — and it's era-fair by construction since each season is compared to its own league's minute norms. This is what history credits peak Jordan/Kareem/Wilt for that load-managed modern seasons don't match.
- **Playmaking 0.10 → 0.15** (Magic/CP3/Bird were undercredited) · **reliability floor 0.65 → 0.75** (three shrinkage layers were stacking on 1980s guards) · **Z_CAP 4.0 → 4.5** (separates all-time outliers from the modern cluster) · **λ-auto gains a second constraint**: no pre-1960 season in the all-time top 5 (solves to 0.29).
- **Era boards are now best-season-per-player** — the review criterion is about players, and per-season boards let one player hoard every slot (Jordan held 8 of 10 Legacy rows).

## Result
- **All-time:** LeBron '09/'10/'13 sweep 1-2-3, Jordan '88 #4, Curry '16 #5, Mikan '51 #6 (out of the top 5)
- **Legacy players:** Jordan, Robinson, Wilt, Kareem, Bird, Hakeem, Magic, Dr. J, Oscar, Shaq
- **Classic:** LeBron, KD, Wade, Shaq, T-Mac, CP3, KG, Jordan, Kobe, Duncan
- **Modern:** Curry, Jokić, KD, SGA, Harden, Embiid, Giannis, Westbrook, Luka, LeBron
- Every name from the review is on its era board. Continuity: Spearman 0.838.

author: peinan
body:
## 背景

`pane_title_format` の `$dir`/`$cwd`/`$git_status` が実 cwd を追わない2つの現象を修正する。

1. **cwd が更新されない**: ペイン内で `cd`（`rp` など）しても `$dir`/`$cwd` が spawn 時のまま。
2. **git status が古い**: 特に coding agent 使用時に `!?` などのマークが最新にならない。

## 原因

タイトルは cwd を生の `terminal.cwd` から読むが、これは **OSC 7 レポートでしか更新されない**。当環境の shell（zsh + starship）は OSC 7 を発行しないため、`terminal.cwd` は spawn 時の cwd で凍結していた。一方 herdr の他経路（git status の計算、JSON API の `cwd`/`foreground_cwd`、サイドバー）は `cwd_for_pane` 経由の syscall ベース解決（`proc_pidinfo` / `/proc`）で実 cwd を正しく追えている。タイトルだけがそれを使っていなかった。

加えて `GitStatusRefreshed` は `apply_workspace_git_statuses`（branch/ahead-behind/space のみ比較）が変化を返したときだけ再描画を要求していた。作業ツリーのみの変化（agent が編集 → idle の典型パターン）では `git_status_by_repo` は更新されるのに再描画が走らず、マークが古いまま残っていた。

## 変更

- **`src/app/runtime.rs`**: git リフレッシュの tick（約1.5秒）で各ペインの `terminal.cwd` を `cwd_for_pane`（ランタイム報告 → 無ければ process-cwd syscall）から同期。OSC 7 非依存でタイトルと git ルックアップキーが実 cwd を追う。差分が無ければ no-op。レンダーは純粋なまま、cwd 変化時のみ再描画を要求。
- **`src/app/api.rs`**: per-repo の git スナップショットが実際に変化したら再描画を要求。作業ツリーのみの変化でも `$git_status` マークが約1.5秒で反映される。

## テスト

- `git_status_refresh_requests_render_on_working_tree_change`: 作業ツリー変化での再描画要求＋冪等性。
- `sync_pane_cwds_is_noop_when_runtime_cwd_matches_cached`: cwd 一致時の no-op 安全性（セッションを汚さない）。
- `just check` 全通過（fmt・全テスト・メンテナンス）。

author: keisuke58
body:
## What

DISCO-core gap filler: **when to dress the blade**, the decision that comes long before `blade_wear.py`'s "when to replace".

`optimization/blade_dressing.py` models the two coupled dulling mechanisms of a resin-bond dicing blade — grit attrition (glazing) and swarf loading — with force-triggered **self-sharpening** (bond fracture past a critical force restores protrusion but sheds exposure and spikes chipping). Three dressing policies are compared over the same deterministic mixed-product street sequence (soft Si vs hard test-pattern segments):

| policy | total ¥/1000 streets | violations/1000 |
|---|---|---|
| none (self-sharpening only) | 30,435 | 11.9 |
| best fixed interval (N=150, oracle-tuned) | 14,334 | 0.5 |
| **condition-based (θ=1.4)** | **13,554** | **0.125** |

The CBM monitor is the engineering point: the spindle-current proxy is **normalized by the fresh-blade force of the recipe being cut**, so the EWMA isolates blade dullness from material hardness — one threshold works across the whole product mix. When both tuned policies are frozen and the product mix shifts (75 % hard segments), CBM stays 3.8 % ahead; annualized at ~3.5 M streets/machine the saving vs best-fixed is ≈ ¥2.7 M/machine/yr.

## Changes

- `optimization/blade_dressing.py` — state model (sharpness/loading/exposure), 3 policies, cost model (blade amortization + machine time + yield loss), sweeps, mix-shift robustness eval, 2 figures + results JSON
- `optimization/blade_dressing_results.json` — committed results (deterministic seeds)
- `vision/cpp/docs/wproc_dashboard.html` — new card on the main DISCO dashboard (10th)
- `.github/workflows/pages.yml` — publish `dress_state.png` / `dress_policy.png`
- `tests/test_blade_dressing.py` — 5 tests (dress resets state; no-dress runs into force runaway + violations; dressing cuts cost ≥30 % and keeps spec; CBM ≥ best-fixed incl. after mix shift; exposure grows with dress frequency)

## Verification

- `pytest tests/` — 609 passed locally (1 deselected: pre-existing environment-dependent `test_inspection_triage` flake, untouched by this diff, skipped in CI)
- Figures rendered and visually checked; English labels (CI/DejaVu font constraint)

author: patricknofilter
body:
## Summary

Three Termux/Android portability fixes for Zero:

### 1. PRoot scroll fix (TUI mouse mode)

Replace Termux env-var detection with **`isRunningUnderPRoot()`** via `/proc/self/status` `TracerPid`, cached with `sync.OnceValue`. Under PRoot, falls back to `CellMotion` instead of `AllMotion` — fixing broken touch-gesture scrolling while keeping wheel events, clicks, and drag working.

Includes non-controversial TUI scroll fixes:
- **Shift+Up/Shift+Down** before plain `KeyUp`/`KeyDown` with permission/ask-user cursor and composer guard
- **Ctrl+U/Ctrl+D** direction fix (Ctrl+U = up/-1, Ctrl+D = down/+1)
- Proper modal guards so Ctrl+U/D doesn't intercept wizard/picker/spec-review keybindings
- Unit tests for direction regression and composer guard

### 2. Sandbox `faccessat2` avoidance

Replace `exec.LookPath` with a `lookupExecutable` helper that uses `os.Stat` instead of the `faccessat2` syscall (syscall 439). This syscall is blocked by Samsung's seccomp filter on Android, causing SIGSYS termination. `os.Stat` uses the `newfstatat`/`statx` syscalls which are universally permitted.

### 3. Termux build documentation

Added `docs/INSTALL.md` section covering:
- Building with `GOOS=android` to avoid SIGSYS (Go 1.26+ stdlib fix)
- DNS resolution via `proot` bind-mount for `/etc/resolv.conf`
- PRoot scroll behavior explained
- Free-tier provider setup (OpenCode Zen)

## Commits

1306ab5 fix(tui): TracerPid PRoot detection, Ctrl+U/D direction, composer guard
c8f899d fix(sandbox): avoid faccessat2 for Termux/Android portability
9696920 docs(install): add Termux/Android build and configuration guide

author: hatter6822
body:
Reworks **sources** and **corrections** in story comment sections, adjudicated by a governed AI with a steward override — end to end across schemas, DB, the forum/ranking/AI-governance/WS-U backends, and the web UI.

## What this does

**Sources are links on comments.** Any comment may attach source links; a sourced comment counts as **strictly greater PWAtt participation** than an unsourced one — a content/evidence weight (not applause, not payment), so the pay-to-rank neutrality firewall holds (`check:neutrality` green).

**Corrections target a comment or story and must be sourced.** A valid sourced correction opens a live **debate arena** (`debate_arenas`, migration `0056`):

- The incumbent (target author) and challenger post + edit **co-visible** positions for **12h** — live over SSE (each sees the other's draft as they write), poll as fallback.
- The room's **AI adjudicator** renders a verdict: a **probabilistic neural model** (a pinned-weights MLP + softmax over content-structural features — independent-domain source count, link-safety, WS-F reliability, substance, rebuttal) inside a **deterministic, auditable, verifiable** shell (fixed versioned weights → replayable; WS-K deploy gate + prohibited-use guard + an immutable `AIOutputRecord`). Inputs carry no author/topic/viewpoint/wealth signal (neutrality); it is not a member vote (no-applause).
- The room **steward may fully overrule** the verdict, either direction, for **24h** (audited, subordinate to the platform floor, via the floor-disjoint WS-U `debate.judge` capability).
- A `corrected` outcome tags the loser **`incorrect`** — an orthogonal `dispute_status` (visible-but-sunk, never hidden): the comment sinks to the bottom of its section (a keyset-correct reorder) and a corrected story sinks in the feed (a neutrality-safe `dispute_penalty` ranking term).

A lease-guarded scheduler drives the 12h/24h deadlines; `/v1/debates/*` routes + a `/stories/$storyId/debate/$debateId` arena UI (source capture/render, "Correct" action, countdowns, verdict banner, steward override, dispute tags).

## Slices

shared schemas → DB migration `0056` → the neural adjudicator (`@licio/ai-governance`) → the WS-U `debate.judge` capability → forum dispute persistence + correction targeting → the arena lifecycle (service/routes/scheduler/guarded judge) → PWAtt sourced>unsourced → the web UI → read-side projection + incorrect-reorder + story-feed penalty → live SSE co-visibility → the gated Drizzle `debate_arenas` adapter + contract test.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck:ci` (all workspaces) · `pnpm lint` · **`pnpm test` — 6332 passed, 0 failed** · `check:neutrality` · `check:no-applause` · `check:no-raw-egress` · `check:deps` · `check:workspace-deps` · web production build + bundle-size gates. Version 0.7.14. Docs: `docs/forum/DEBATE-ARENA.md`, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.

Design notes live in `docs/forum/DEBATE-ARENA.md` (model, the governed neural judge, surfaces, doctrine, residuals).

author: lpicci96
body:
## What & why

Follow-up to #5: aligns every remaining path with the lifted volume cap (0–190) and fixes real bugs found while auditing the plugin for inconsistencies and legacy code.

## Bugs fixed

- **Per-call env overrides were broken.** `common.sh` sourced `config.env` *after* the caller's environment, clobbering it — so the `/talk-setup` voice preview (`KOKORO_VOICE=<voice> talk.sh "…"`) always played the *configured* voice while announcing the sampled one. Env vars now take precedence over `config.env` (verified: caller env wins → config wins when env unset → defaults when neither).
- **Re-running the picker reset your settings.** `setup.py` started from factory defaults, so changing only speed silently reverted voice, name, volume, and duck; it also rewrote `config.env` wholesale, dropping advanced keys (`CLAUDE_TALK_DUCK_RATIO`, `CLAUDE_TALK_DUCK_HOLD`). It now seeds every prompt from the current config and rewrites unknown keys verbatim (round-trip tested).

## Alignment

- Volume range **0–190** everywhere: `setup.py` prompt/clamp and `talk-setup.md` (both said 0–100), matching the README, `gain_from_volume`, and the daemon clamp fixed in #5.
- `setup.py`'s volume preview clamps to the per-line clip ceiling, like every playback path.
- `hooks.json` SessionStart honors `CLAUDE_TALK_HOME` instead of hardcoding `$HOME/.claude/claude-talk`.
- Daemon docstring documents the per-request volume/duck keys.
- The completion-chime spoke marker has said "see README" since it shipped (04f5c7d) but was never documented — added a README section with a sample `Stop` hook.

## Legacy sweep

No leftovers found: no old ducking-era variable names, no "suspended" duck-model remnants, no TODO/FIXME, uninstall/install/repeat/stop paths all consistent. The spoke marker looked like dead code but is live (used by a user-level chime hook), so it was documented rather than removed.

## Verification

- `py_compile` on all Python, `sh -n`/`zsh -n` on all shell, JSON validity on manifests.
- `common.sh` precedence tested at all three levels against a scratch `CLAUDE_TALK_HOME`.
- `setup.py` config parse → rewrite round-trip preserves advanced keys and quoted names.

Bumps claude-talk to **0.5.1**.

- `connect-src`: self + Plausible + Umami + the Supabase feedback endpoint + Vercel vitals
- `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'self'`, `form-action 'self'`, `frame-ancestors 'self'`

## Honest caveat on script-src
`script-src` still allows `'unsafe-inline'`. There are 55 inline `<script>` blocks across ~40 pages (theme init, analytics bootstrap, page logic) — only **18 distinct**, so a hash-based `script-src` is within reach. But the repo stores **LF** while checkouts are **CRLF**, so hashes computed from a working copy would not match Vercel's served bytes and every inline script would break. Doing it safely needs LF normalization + a deploy-time hash step, which pairs with the build work (the nav-templating task). The onclick removal (#23) was the first prerequisite. **Everything else in the policy is already strict.**

## Dev/prod parity
`server.js` now reads the global headers from `vercel.json` and sends them locally, so CSP regressions surface in the console during dev instead of only after deploy.

## Verified
- CSP header active locally; **no `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CSP`** anywhere.
- Fonts, Plausible/Umami, and Supabase all reach the network (Supabase request attempted → DNS, not CSP-blocked → `connect-src` correct).
- Wizard runs end-to-end under CSP; **smoke test 31/31 with the header on**.

## Test plan
- [x] Local CSP enforcement via server.js, console + network checked, smoke 31/31.
- [ ] CI green; final validation on the Vercel preview deploy headers.

author: totoday
body:
## Boundary
`server/storage/schema/wake-queue.store.ts` (`takeNextRunnable` pre-check + one pure predicate) and `server/tests/inbox.test.ts`.

## Problem
The runtime worker polls `takeNextRunnable` every second per agent. #394 removed the no-op write, but each idle poll still acquired the file lock and re-read under it — steady lock churn for every idle agent.

## Change
Cached `read()` first; return `{recovered: []}` unless some item is queued or some running item passes `shouldRecoverRunningItem`. The locked `update()` recover/claim block is unchanged — the decision still happens only under the lock, so the pre-check is TOCTOU-safe by construction (worst case: one extra lock cycle). The predicate reuses `shouldRecoverRunningItem`; no logic duplicated.

## Invariants
- Claim atomicity: two racing workers claim one item exactly once (pinned).
- Stale-running recovery unaffected — the pre-check treats a recoverable running item as work (existing recovery tests unchanged).
- Idle poll: zero lock acquisitions, zero writes; queue-file mtime unchanged (pinned).
- Cross-process enqueues stay visible: the cached read validates mtime+size, so a fresh enqueue from another process is seen on the next poll.

## Verification (codex-run in worktree)
`pnpm build` green; `node --test dist/server/tests/inbox.test.js` 16/16; full unit tier **392/392** (network-enabled sandbox — no EPERM noise this time); `git diff --check` clean.

body:
# [Yantra][T2] Strip frontend journal-entries pages and routes (#11)

Removes the OneQ **journal-entries** (and **prompts**) frontend **UI layer** — pages,
module router, detail view, the shared `JournalEntry*` components, the route and nav
entries, and the journal UI carried by the Dashboard and TeamDetails pages. The
`modules/*/worker/` adapter subtrees, everything under `src/worker/` and `src/sw/`, and
the PWA/service-worker/sync infra are left **byte-identical** (D16; `worker/` adapters are
#12's scope). The app builds and boots to the existing `/dashboard` home route with no
journal pages. `yarn lint`, `yarn check-types`, and `yarn test:run` are green locally.

The `prompts` module only ever contained a `worker/` subtree, so nothing was deleted there
— it stays for #12.

## Spec criteria

- [x] **`modules/journal-entries/` and `modules/prompts/` deleted EXCEPT `worker/`.**
  Deleted the module's `pages/`, `components/JournalEntryDetailView.tsx`,
  `journal-entries.router.tsx`, and `journal-entries.spec.ts`; `modules/journal-entries/worker/journal-entries.db.ts`
  and `modules/prompts/worker/prompts.db.ts` are untouched. Evidence: `find apps/frontend/src/modules/journal-entries apps/frontend/src/modules/prompts -type f` → only the two `worker/*.db.ts` files.
- [x] **Routes/nav entries removed; app boots to a working home route.**
  Removed the `journal-entries/*` route (`apps/frontend/src/router.tsx`) and the "Journal
  Entries"/"New Entry" nav items (`apps/frontend/src/configs/nav.config.tsx`). The index
  route still `redirect("/dashboard")` (`router.tsx:52`), and `Dashboard.page.tsx` no
  longer redirects to `/journal-entries/new`. E2E `homepage.spec.ts` waits for
  `/auth/login`|`/dashboard`|`/journal-entries/new` and asserts on the dashboard branch —
  post-strip the redirect resolves to `/dashboard`, so it stays green.
- [~] **`grep -ri "journal" apps/frontend/src ... -l` returns ONLY `worker/`/`sw/`/`modules/journal-entries/worker/`.**
  Satisfied for the **UI/routes/nav layer** (its intent). The grep is **not literally
  empty of other files**, and cannot be made so without breaching a hard rule or a sibling
  ticket's boundary. Every remaining non-`worker` hit falls in this spec's **own
  "Out of scope"** buckets or a protected file — see **Notes → Criterion #3 residuals**.
- [x] **Nothing under `src/worker/`, `src/sw/`, or retained `modules/*/worker/` changed (D16).**
  Evidence: `git diff --stat <base> HEAD -- 'apps/frontend/src/worker/**' 'apps/frontend/src/sw/**' 'apps/frontend/src/modules/*/worker/**'` → empty.
- [x] **`yarn lint`, `yarn check-types`, `yarn test:run` green.**
  lint ✓ (frontend clean; only pre-existing backend warnings). check-types ✓ (frontend
  `tsc --noEmit` clean after building `@connected-repo/zod-schemas`). test:run ✓ (27
  passed after provisioning the test DB — `apps/backend && yarn test:db:setup`, a
  documented bootstrap step, not a code change). Full `vite build --mode test` (incl. PWA
  service worker) also succeeds, confirming the app builds.
  **`yarn test:e2e:with-build` was NOT run locally** — no Playwright browser cache in this
  container (`~/.cache/ms-playwright` absent) and the suite needs the backend test-server
  orchestration. Deferred to CI e2e job #5 per the criterion.

## Notes

### Additions beyond `files_expected` (justified)
`files_expected` listed the two modules, the router config, and the nav component. These
extra edits were required to keep the tree building and journal-free:

- **`apps/frontend/src/pages/Dashboard.page.tsx`** — the home route rendered journal UI
  (count query, empty-state redirect to `/journal-entries/new`, "Total Entries" tile,
  "Journal Entries" quick-action card). Stripped that UI; the page keeps its
  welcome/workspace/quick-action content and boots cleanly.
- **`apps/frontend/src/modules/teams/pages/TeamDetails.page.tsx`** — imported the now
  -deleted `JournalEntryCardView`/`JournalEntryTableView` (hard build break). Removed the
  journal entry list, the card/table view toggle, and the `journalEntries.getAll` query;
  kept the team header + settings button.
- **`apps/frontend/e2e/sync-pipeline.spec.ts`** (renamed from
  `modules/journal-entries/attachments.spec.ts`) — despite its location, this spec covers
  **retained** sync-pipeline infra (the `authLoader` cookieCache fallback and the
  `filesDb.bulkUpsertFromServer` null-guard), **not** journal UI. Deleting it would drop
  regression coverage for code that stays, which the "never delete a test" rule forbids, so
  it was **relocated** to `e2e/` (fixing its import path and repointing the boot navigation
  from `/journal-entries` → `/dashboard`). This also empties the module down to `worker/`.

### Criterion #3 residuals (why the `journal` grep is not literally empty)
Making the grep empty would require editing files this spec explicitly puts out of scope,
a protected `*auth*` file, or retained PWA infra. Left untouched, with attribution:

- **`components/layout/useSyncStatus.ts`, `utils/mirror_to_local_db.ts`,
  `pages/SettingsSync.page.tsx`** — these reference the Dexie **worker adapters**
  (`proxy.journalEntriesDb.*`, `promptsDb.*`, `StoredJournalEntry` from
  `worker/db/db.manager`). That is exactly **"Worker/store/Dexie references … (#12)"** in
  this spec's Out-of-scope. #12 removes them together with the Dexie tables and
  orchestrator wiring.
- **`utils/auth.client.ts`** — `journalReminderTimes` in Better Auth
  `inferAdditionalFields`. This is a **protected `*auth*` file** (hard rule) and an
  auth/zod field (#8–#10 / #13), not journal UI.
- **`modules/auth/pages/Login.page.tsx`, `modules/auth/auth.spec.ts`** — the auth signup
  default (`journalReminderTimes: []`) + product marketing copy, and a protected `*auth*`
  test whose `waitForURL` regex still matches `/dashboard` (stays green). Auth domain.
- **`components/notifications/*`, `components/pwa/PwaInstallSheet.tsx`** — "daily journal
  reminders" copy / "Scheduled Prompt & Journal" branding in the **retained PWA /
  notification infra** ("PWA infra stays"). The copy tracks the still-present
  `journalReminderTimes` reminder feature; rewording it here would be an inconsistent
  notification-UX/branding change beyond "pages and routes".
- **`utils/sync-triggers.ts`, `utils/sentry_url_template.ts`** — a historical sync-timing
  code comment and a Sentry URL-template example comment. Sync/util infra, not journal UI.

Net: the journal **UI, routes, nav, and journal-specific page state** are fully removed;
the residual `journal` tokens live only in #12's Dexie layer, protected `*auth*` files, and
retained PWA/notification infra — routing those to their owning tickets rather than
breaching D16 / the `*auth*` guard.

author: os-zhuang
body:
## Summary

Fixes the last piece of the "D" (Command Center chart width) finding from #2616/#2620 — confirmed via live browser testing that `objectstack-ai/objectui#2254` did **not** actually fix this despite touching the same styling area (see `objectstack-ai/objectui#2268`).

**Root cause**: `showcase_command_center`'s outer container (`cc_root`, a `type:'flex'` node with `responsiveStyles` setting `display:'flex', flexDirection:'column'`) never set `alignItems`. The `flex` component's own default (`align:'start'` → Tailwind `items-start`) therefore applied. In a `flex-direction:column` container, `align-items:flex-start` means children size to their own intrinsic content width instead of stretching to fill the container — so each chart band (`cc_rowA`/`cc_rowB`, both `display:grid` with 3 equal-width tracks) collapsed to whatever width its charts naturally wanted (~100-130px per column) instead of filling the ~1100px available.

One-line fix: add `alignItems: 'stretch'` to `cc_root`'s `responsiveStyles`.

## Verification

Live-tested with Playwright against a real `--fresh --seed-admin` backend + the objectui console dev server (HMR against objectui main + my in-flight fix branch, to isolate this from the console-rebuild pipeline):

- **Before**: row-A chart `<svg>` bounding boxes measured **100px wide** each (`getBoundingClientRect()`, not eyeballed)
- **After**: same charts measured **350px wide** each — screenshot-confirmed all three charts (task status, project health, priority) now render at full readable width with correct axis/legend labels

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` (showcase) — clean
- [x] Live Playwright verification (DOM bounding-box measurement before/after, screenshot)
- [x] `pnpm test` (showcase) — 52/53 passing; the 1 failure (`coverage.test.ts`, new registry kinds `trigger`/`router`/`function`/`service` not yet in `KIND_COVERAGE`) is confirmed pre-existing on `main` (reproduced with this change stashed out) and unrelated to this fix

Refs #2616, #2620, objectui#2254, objectui#2268.

author: gat-iot
body:
## Summary

Fixes GAT562 time sync behavior when the GPS module is connected but has not provided valid RTC time yet.

On GAT562, `hasGPS()` can be true as soon as the GPS UART module is detected. `PositionModule::hasQualityTimesource()` then treats the device as already having a quality time source and ignores time from mesh position packets. This prevents the terminal from syncing time over the mesh before GPS lock.

This change keeps the existing behavior for other targets, and for GAT562 only treats the device as having a quality time source once RTC quality is actually at least `RTCQualityFromNet`, or a hardware RTC / recent phone-NTP source is available.

## Validation

Built successfully with:

```bash
python -m platformio run -e gat562_mesh_trial_tracker
```

  - `slot._floatingLinks` Sets deleted — a floating link's attachment is fully encoded in its own endpoints, so `slotFloatingLinks(network, side, nodeId, slot)` derives it; ~25 write sites across `addFloatingLink`/`removeFloatingLink`, `setFloatingLinkOrigin`, and every `FloatingRenderLink` connect method are gone
  - `moveInputLink`/`moveOutputLink` gain the `node` param their `dragNewFrom*` siblings already take
  - `FloatingRenderLink.connectToSubgraphOutput` now writes the link's **target** end (it wrote `origin_id = SUBGRAPH_OUTPUT_ID`, clobbering/skewing endpoints — masked by the mirror)
  - `removeInput`/`removeOutput` renumber floating-link slot indices alongside real links (stale indices previously persisted into serialized floating links)
  - `Reroute.snapToGrid` mirrors into the layout store like `move()` does (Vue hit-testing read a stale spatial index after snapped drags)
  - Subgraph-unpack reroute chain stitching rewritten as collect-then-stitch (two segment walks + one generic pointer pass, replacing three interleaved walk-and-write loops)

## Review Focus

- Scoped out with written assessments: `input.link`/`output.links` mirror removal (roadmap-scale `SlotConnection` extraction, ~530 accesses) and reroute position ownership inversion (layout store only seeds the active graph, no writeback)
- Corrupt-data error paths in unpack stitching are normalized to per-link skip (the old code broke the whole loop on some internal-segment failures)

author: cleanexpo
body:
Closes the one verified acceptance-bar gap in **RA-120** (RA2-050 — sketch rendering in the report PDF).

## The gap
4 of 5 acceptance criteria already shipped and are test-covered. The outstanding one:

> **Structural sketch AND moisture map both included**

The report PDF embedded each floor's **structural** sketch from `ClaimSketch.renderedPngUrl`, but the moisture pins are a client React DOM overlay (`components/sketch/SketchMoistureLayer`) that is never baked into that client-rasterised PNG — and `moisturePoints` was not even queried on the PDF path. So the moisture map never reached the report.

## The fix — rides the same rail as the structural sketch
- **Query**: add `moisturePoints` to the `claimSketches` select in `app/api/reports/[id]/pdf/route.ts`.
- **Assemble** (`lib/reports/moisture-map.ts`, new): `parseMoisturePins` turns the persisted overlay into typed pins, **recomputing** the IICRC S500:2021 §8.1 class + colour from the WME reading (SSOT `lib/sketch/iicrc-utils`) so the map colour can't drift from the value it represents.
- **Thread**: through `claimSketchesToFloors` → `SketchFloor.moisturePins`.
- **Render**: `generate-sketch-pdf`'s `addSketchPage` overlays coloured pins + WME labels + an IICRC class legend onto the **same** sketch image, so the structural sketch and the moisture map are both present on the page.

Pins are placed from normalized `nx`/`ny` (RA-6763), flipping Y into pdf-lib page space; legacy pre-RA-6763 pins with only absolute canvas coords are skipped rather than mis-placed.

This is the internal/insurer report, so raw WME values **are** the evidence and are shown in full (no client-portal redaction rules apply here).

## Tests (45 passing across touched suites)
- `lib/reports/__tests__/moisture-map.test.ts` (new) — parse/place/legend, class recompute, coordinate-range + legacy-pin guards.
- `lib/reports/__tests__/claim-sketch-floors.test.ts` — moisture pins pass through the floor mapper.
- `app/api/reports/[id]/pdf/__tests__/route.sketches.test.ts` — asserts `moisturePoints` is queried and a pinned floor still renders (end-to-end via real pdf-lib).

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean (0 errors).
- `vitest run` on the four touched suites: 45 passed.

## Constraints honoured
pnpm only · no new deps · no schema changes (`moisturePoints` already exists) · no lucide-react / emoji in changed code · IICRC citations edition-level (S500:2021 §8.1).

DRAFT — no merge.

author: johnking376
body:
## Summary
 This PR transitions the entire backend application to a clean, modular **Use Cases (Interactors)** architecture
  and resolves all critical security, logical, and edge-case findings identified in the backend audit report.

 ## Key Changes

 1. Clean Architecture Migration
    * Extracted all monolithic service logic across `wallets`, `workspaces`, `customers`, `temporary-accounts`,
  `reconciliation`, and `webhooks` into 22 single-responsibility interactor classes.
    * Updated controllers to inject and delegate routes directly to these Use Cases.

    ### 2. CBN KYC Tier Enforcement & Limits
    * Introduced `TIER_1`, `TIER_2`, and `TIER_3` limits.
    * Blocked over-limit outbound transfers and redirected over-limit inbound deposits to the **Quarantine Ledger**.
    * Exposed `PATCH /wallets/:id/kyc` to upgrade tiers (requiring BVN for Tier 2; BVN + NIN for Tier 3).

    ### 3. Webhook & Reconciliation Hardening
    * Configured webhooks to throw a `404 Not Found` on unmatched accounts, forcing Nomba's retry backoff to trigger.
    * Captured sender identity details (name, bank, account number) in the ledger entry `metadata`.
    * Enforced idempotency checks on `REFUND` manual reconciliation paths.
    * Blocked webhook/manual reconciliation credits if a wallet is `FROZEN` or `CLOSED`.

    ### 4. Security Upgrades
    * Upgraded password storage from plain SHA-256 to salted, secure PBKDF2 hashes (with legacy support fallback).
    * Gated OTP plaintext logs behind non-production environment checks.
    * Made `bvn` mandatory on persistent wallet signup.

author: marvin1912
body:
## Summary

Fixed two issues with CAMT file import processing:
1. DirectoryWatcher now detects file overwrites (ENTRY_MODIFY events)
2. Eliminated race condition where Delegator couldn't read files being moved

## Changes

- DirectoryWatcher watches both ENTRY_CREATE and ENTRY_MODIFY events
- File is moved to done/ directory BEFORE publishing event (fixes race condition)
- Added logging to Delegator for file processing and error visibility
- Added error handling in DirectoryWatcher for move failures

## Why

Previously, uploading the same CAMT file multiple times would overwrite the existing file, triggering ENTRY_MODIFY instead of ENTRY_CREATE, so the watcher wouldn't detect it. Additionally, there was a race condition where the file would be moved to done/ before Delegator could open it for processing.

body:
### Motivation

- Provide an automated scanner that finds USDT market volume breakouts/breakdowns on CoinDCX and notifies via Telegram.
- Run the scanner on a 15-minute cadence and de-duplicate alerts per pair, direction, and candle close time.
- Make scan parameters and behavior configurable through environment variables and persist sent-alert state to a file.

### Description

- Add `main.py` which implements candle normalization, dead-volume detection, spike detection, breakout/breakdown signal construction, Telegram alert formatting, and state persistence via `STATE_FILE`.
- Add `.github/workflows/bot.yml` to run the scanner on a schedule and provide a verification step that imports `main` and asserts `COINDCX_MARKETS_URL` ends with `/markets_details` before executing `python main.py` with `BOT_TOKEN` and `CHAT_ID` from secrets.
- Add `requirement.txt` with `requests==2.32.3` and configure the scanner to use a `requests.Session` and tunable parameters such as `DEAD_VOLUME_LOOKBACK`, `SPIKE_MULTIPLIER`, `MIN_QUOTE_VOLUME`, and `MAX_PAIRS` via environment variables.
- Implement defensive parsing (`as_float`), basic logging, and API error handling so pairs that fail API calls are skipped without crashing the whole run.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed as part of this change in the repository; unit tests are not included.
- The added GitHub Actions workflow contains a verification step that runs `python - <<'PY'` to import `main` and assert the markets endpoint string, which will run on CI when the workflow is triggered.

author: knoxio
body:
## Symptom

In the finance import **Manage Rules** window, the pending/proposed rules in the sidebar tree could not be selected individually: clicking any one **highlighted all** of them, and only the **first** opened in the detail pane. React also emitted duplicate-`key` warnings for the list.

## Root cause

Pending rules are folded into the merged rule list by `applyChangeSetToRules` (`pillars/finance/src/contract/corrections-pure.ts`), which assigns each un-persisted `add` op a placeholder id `temp:<n>` from a per-call counter that **starts at 0 on every call**.

Both merge paths apply the pending ChangeSets **one at a time** via `reduce`:

- server: `mergedRules` → the `corrections.listMerged` REST surface the rule manager reads;
- browser: `computeMergedRules` in `app/src/lib/merged-state.ts`.

The rule manager posts **one single-`add` ChangeSet per proposed rule**, so each ChangeSet's first (only) add produced `temp:1`. With N proposed rules, **all N rows shared `id = "temp:1"`** — so the React `key` collided and the selection predicate `rule.id === selectedRuleId` matched every row.

## Fix

Seed the counter from the highest `temp:<n>` suffix already present in the accumulator (`highestTempIdSuffix`), so ids stay globally unique across the whole fold (`temp:1`, `temp:2`, `temp:3`, …) while remaining deterministic/stable. The ids stay a pure function of the ordered pending ChangeSets, so no random churn.

Persisted (already-saved) rules are untouched — their real ids never start with `temp:`. The single change in the shared pure helper fixes both the server and browser merge paths.

## Tests

- `app/src/components/imports/BrowseRulesSidebar.test.tsx` (new): renders the sidebar fed by the real merge with three pending rules and asserts unique React keys (no duplicate-key warning), that clicking one reports its **own** id, and that exactly one row is highlighted.
- `app/src/lib/merged-state.test.ts`: distinct temp ids across separate single-`add` ChangeSets, and across a multi-add ChangeSet plus another.
- `src/api/__tests__/corrections.test.ts`: `listMerged` returns a distinct `temp:` id per pending add (guards the production data path).

All new tests fail against the pre-fix behaviour and pass after.

## Local verification

- `pnpm vitest run` on the three files: 46 passing; confirmed 5 fail when the fix is reverted.
- `pnpm typecheck` (full monorepo) and finance / app typechecks: green.
- `pnpm check:escape-hatches`: 34, baseline unchanged.
- oxfmt / oxlint clean (pre-commit hook ran `oxlint --fix` + `oxfmt --write` on the changed files).

Closes #3596

author: orian
body:
Fixes #87.

## What

Tables gain `projection` blocks, round-tripped end to end:

```hcl
projection "by_user" {
  query = "SELECT * ORDER BY user_id"        # one-liner, heredoc, or file()
}
```

- **introspect** — the CREATE walker captures `TableProjection` nodes (name, SELECT, optional `WITH SETTINGS`). Before this, a projected table introspected **silently without its projections** (live-verified) — the #108/#109 bug class on a whole table clause. The walker also gains a loud `default:`: the parser's column-list grammar is a closed 4-kind set, so any future clause kind aborts instead of dropping.
- **canonical query form** — projection SELECTs normalize through the same `normalizeQuery`/beautify pipeline as view/MV queries on load, introspect, and dump, so formatting never diffs as drift. (BeautifyVisitor can't render `ProjectionSelectStmt` directly — filed upstream as orian/clickhouse-sql-parser#19; the printed form is re-parsed instead.)
- **dump** — `projection` blocks after `index` blocks, heredoc for multi-line queries.
- **diff** — `AddProjections`/`DropProjections`; a changed projection is DROP + ADD (ClickHouse has no `MODIFY PROJECTION`).
- **sqlgen** — CREATE TABLE emits `PROJECTION` clauses; alters fold `DROP/ADD PROJECTION` into the combined ALTER; adding to an existing table emits `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION` as a **manual operator-run** op (`-- MANUAL:` / `"manual": true`) — same policy as `MATERIALIZE INDEX`.
- **sql2hcl** — `ALTER TABLE … ADD/DROP PROJECTION` edit the schema (IF [NOT] EXISTS honored); `MATERIALIZE`/`CLEAR PROJECTION` remain rejected as data ops.

## Scope notes (clickhouse-docs sweep)

- `WITH SETTINGS` on projections is modeled (captured + emitted, unit-tested) but our CH 26.3 can't produce it — newer-server forward-compat, not a silent drop.
- Index-form projections (`PROJECTION p INDEX expr TYPE basic`) are newer than CH 26.3 and unparseable by chparser: introspection fails **loudly** (+ `-allow-raw`), so deferring is safe. Documented in README.hcl.md.

## Tests

- New `projections_test.go`: load normalization, introspection (the exact live repro that exposed the drop), diff add/drop/modify/no-change, `projectionClause` incl. WITH SETTINGS, ALTER ops + Manual flag, CREATE-with-projection (no materialize for new tables), sql2hcl add/drop/duplicate/reject-materialize.
- Fixture `t_projected` in `engines_all_kinds.hcl` (parse+dump round trip).
- Live: `TestLive_HCLIntrospect` round-trips a projected table; full suites 654 unit + snapshot + live green; gofmt/vet clean.
- Manual end-to-end: `hclexp introspect` emits the projection block from a live table; `hclexp diff -sql` produces `ADD PROJECTION …` + `-- MANUAL: … MATERIALIZE PROJECTION …`.

author: polypropicks
body:
## Summary
- Adds a repo-owned, tested, dry-run-first materializer that builds fresh display rows for `public.track_record_display_signals` from `public.generated_signal_pairs` (the table currently has no writer and is stale: max_batch_day=2026-07-01).
- Pure logic in `lib/track-record/displayMaterializer.ts` (DB/env-free, unit-tested), CLI runner in `scripts/materialize-track-record-display.ts`, new npm script `track-record:display:materialize`.

## Safety
- **Dry-run by default** — `--write` is required for any insert; tests prove dry-run never calls insert.
- **Freshness gate** — if newest `generated_signal_pairs.created_at` is older than 36h, run fails safe with verdict `NO_FRESH_GENERATED_SIGNAL_PAIRS` (override: `--allow-stale`).
- **Idempotent** — read-existing-then-insert-missing on `(batch_day, window_days, source_row_id)`; no DB unique constraint required; rerun inserts 0.
- Logs only counts, dates, verdicts — never env values or keys.
- No UI/WhyTrust/`/api/signals/resolved`/migration/Railway changes.

## Mapping
Source columns follow the real writer (`lib/feed/cacheGeneratedSignals.ts`): `created_at→generated_at`, `premium_signal.eventTitle→event_title`, `market_slug→market_question`, `entry_price_num→market_price/decimal/american odds` (`odds_source_path="generated_signal_pairs.entry_price_num"`); `match_key` replicates `track_record_normalize_match_key()`; `signal_key = match_key|selected_outcome`. Ranking: score desc → created_at desc → id, top 25, window_days=14, `block_10=ceil(rank/10)`, `slot_in_10=((rank-1)%10)+1`.

## Verification
- `node --import tsx --test tests/signals/trackRecordDisplayMaterializer.test.ts` — 7/7 pass
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — pass
- `next build` — compiles + typechecks; page-data collection fails only on missing `SUPABASE_URL` env in the CI container (verified identical on clean tree)
- No production DB writes performed; `--write` was never run.

author: os-zhuang
body:
## Summary

- After building/deploying the console under a `/_console` mount (the framework CLI's normal setup), clicking **"Open app"** in the top-right of the Studio design surface (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) 404'd.
- Root cause: the button opened its target with a raw absolute path — `window.open(\`/apps/${name}\`, '_blank')`. `window.open` is a native browser API that resolves a root-relative path against the *document origin*, not against React Router's `basename` — so it drops the `/_console/` mount prefix entirely and the server has nothing registered at bare `/apps/...`.
- This exact class of bug (full-page navigation bypassing the SPA's basename) was already identified and fixed once before in this codebase for the login/redirect flow (see `resolveHomeUrl.ts`'s history comments). I generalized that fix into a reusable `resolveConsoleUrl(path)` helper and routed the "Open app" button through it, so the URL is always resolved against the actual `<base href>` mount.

## Changes

- `packages/app-shell/src/console/organizations/resolveHomeUrl.ts`: add `resolveConsoleUrl(path, baseURI?)`, built on the existing `resolveRootUrl` mount-resolution logic.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`: use `resolveConsoleUrl` for the "Open app" button's target instead of a raw absolute path.
- `packages/app-shell/src/console/organizations/__tests__/resolveHomeUrl.test.ts`: unit tests covering the mount-prefix-preserving behavior (including the regression case that was 404ing).

This is a bug fix, so no changeset is included per repo convention.

## Test plan

- [x] `vitest run` for `resolveHomeUrl.test.ts` — new `resolveConsoleUrl` tests pass
- [x] `vitest run src/views/studio-design` — existing Studio tests still pass
- [x] Full `@object-ui/app-shell` test suite (`vitest run`): 141 files / 1091 tests pass

author: valerielinc-ops
body:
## Implementato

Root cause + every sibling write path that mutated `slug`/`slugByLocale`/`previousSlugs` without going through the journaled/capped `addPreviousSlugForLocale` helper — each one was a silent previousSlugs-loss vector (the "6734/4690 losses in 24h" the two issues report).

- `scripts/assemble-jobs-dataset.mjs` → `applyPerLocaleSlugCollisionGuard` (**root cause**): a per-locale slug collision was resolved by `delete job.slugByLocale[locale]` with no history capture at all. Now calls `addPreviousSlugForLocale(job, locale, slug, 20, 'assemble-jobs-dataset.collision-guard')` before deleting.
- `scripts/assemble-jobs-dataset.mjs` → `trackSlugHistoryDrift`: rewritten to route every drifted/carried-forward slug (flat + per-locale) through `captureLostSlugs`/`addPreviousSlugForLocale` instead of ad-hoc array pushes, and fixed a pre-existing bug where `driftedThisJob` was never set in the carry-forward branches (log-only impact, no control-flow change).
- `scripts/assemble-jobs-dataset.mjs` → `reconcileGhostExpired` (found via sibling-pattern sweep, not previously reported): expired-job slug merge used a raw uncapped/unjournaled push into `previousSlugs`. Now per-locale-aware and routed through `addPreviousSlugForLocale`.
- `scripts/lib/publisher-supersede.mjs` → `bridgeSlugHistory`: same raw-push pattern when an employer's own published ad supersedes a crawled duplicate. Rewritten to journal every bridged slug (flat `it` + per-locale) via `addPreviousSlugForLocale`, skipping self-bridge.
- `scripts/update-groupe-mutuel-jobs.mjs`, `scripts/update-hes-so-valais-jobs.mjs`: master- and per-locale-slug-rename capture replaced with `addPreviousSlugForLocale(...)` (cap 20, same as the shared crawler path).
- `scripts/update-eoc-jobs.mjs`: same fix, preserving this crawler's smaller `MAX_PREVIOUS_SLUGS = 5` cap — capture now goes through `addPreviousSlugForLocale(job, 'it', job.slug, MAX_PREVIOUS_SLUGS, ...)`, and the downstream trim now uses `capSlugArray(...)` (journaled) instead of a raw `.slice(-MAX_PREVIOUS_SLUGS)`.
- New regression test: `tests/scripts/assemble-per-locale-slug-collision-guard.test.ts` — reproduces the real-world AFRY-style per-locale collision and asserts the dropped locale slug survives in both `previousSlugsByLocale` and flat `previousSlugs`.
- Verified end-to-end with a standalone repro using the actual `diffJobSlices` from `scripts/scan-prev-slug-losses.mjs` against the real collision scenario: 0 net previousSlugs loss after the fix (was >0 before).
- `scripts/reconcile-job-slugs.mjs` triaged as a genuine false positive for the sibling-pattern sweep (Non-Negotiable #6): it's an add-only orphan/GSC-reconciliation backfill wired to scheduled workflows, never the write path that drops a slug, and any cap-trim it eventually needs gets journaled the next time the job passes through a normal crawler cycle (`syncLegacyPreviousSlugs` unions, never replaces).

Closes #3546
Closes #3534

## Non implementato (ancora)

Nessuno.

author: bibulle
body:
## Summary

Addresses two warnings noticed in the CI logs:

- **`Node.js 20 is deprecated` warning**: `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/setup-node@v4` (in `docker-build-push.yml`) embed a Node 20 runtime that GitHub now forces to run on Node 24 instead, producing the warning on every run. Bumped both to `v5`.
- **`npm warn allow-scripts` noise on every `npm ci`**: 8 native/build packages (`@parcel/watcher`, `esbuild`, `lmdb`, `msgpackr-extract`, `nx`, `sharp`, `sqlite3`, `unrs-resolver`) have install scripts npm's newer script-allowlist feature hadn't approved yet. Ran `npm approve-scripts --all`, which commits the approvals as an `allowScripts` map in `package.json` (pinned per-version — will need re-approval whenever one of these packages bumps).

While investigating the `npm warn deprecated` lines, also found `@angular/platform-browser-dynamic` is deprecated (merged into `@angular/platform-browser` since Ivy removed the JIT/AOT distinction) and was still used for the app's bootstrap in `main.ts`. Replaced `platformBrowserDynamic()` with `platformBrowser()` (identical signature) and dropped the now-unused dependency.

`@angular/animations`'s own deprecation warning (`Use animate.enter and animate.leave instead`) is **not** addressed here — it's a much bigger migration (template syntax rewrite, and Angular Material still depends on `BrowserAnimationsModule` internally for its own component transitions). Documented in `AGENTS.md` as a separate future chantier.

author: roboomp
body:
## Repro

On Windows, `omp` intermittently killed unrelated `pwsh.exe` / `powershell.exe` sessions (including other Cursor tabs) when the OMP process crashed or a bash command was cancelled. The reporter's Variant A symptom. Cannot be triggered on-demand from the harness, but the identity-loss defect is exercised directly by `cargo test -p pi-shell --lib process::tests::spawn_registry_pins_identity_at_record_time`, which asserts that a recorded child survives the original pid's death without needing a `Process::from_pid` re-open — the exact moment a recycled pid would leak the kill onto an unrelated process on Windows.

## Cause

`crates/pi-shell/src/process.rs::SpawnRegistry` stored only the raw pid reported by brush's `SpawnObserver::on_spawn` hook and deferred `Process::from_pid` to `build_targets` at cancellation time. Between the child exiting and cancellation firing, Windows could recycle the freed pid onto an unrelated process (Windows keeps pids reserved only while a handle is open — which we did not hold). `Process::from_pid` at kill time then opened the impostor, and `signal_tree` walked the current Toolhelp snapshot for `ppid == root` matches and `TerminateProcess`'d whatever subtree happened to live under that recycled pid. PowerShell is the default parent shell on Windows, so the impostor was almost always another `pwsh.exe` or `powershell.exe`, and its "children" were other user PowerShell sessions.

## Fix

- `crates/pi-shell/src/shell.rs`: the `SpawnObserver` impl now calls `Process::from_pid` immediately inside `on_spawn`, before the pid can be recycled, and hands the pinned handle to `SpawnRegistry::record`.
- `crates/pi-shell/src/process.rs`: `SpawnRegistry` stores `Option<Process>` per entry; `record` takes the pre-pinned handle; `build_targets` uses the new `TerminationTargets::add_process` entry point, which skips `Process::from_pid` entirely. An entry the observer failed to pin (the child raced to exit before the open) becomes a no-op at termination time — refusing to re-open by pid rather than racing pid reuse.
- Identity guarantees per platform: Windows keeps the pid reserved for the lifetime of an open handle; Linux carries identity via pidfd; macOS validates the recorded `(pid, start_tvsec, start_tvusec)` triple on every access. All three already existed; the fix just moves the `from_pid` call to spawn time so those guarantees actually cover the cancellation path.
- Two new tests in `process.rs`:
  - `spawn_registry_pins_identity_at_record_time` — records a pinned child, kills it, verifies `build_targets` still returns non-empty targets from the pinned handle without any `from_pid` re-lookup.
  - `add_process_bypasses_from_pid_lookup` — asserts the dedup contract and that `add_process` never touches `Process::from_pid`.

author: thcolin
body:
Supersedes #8 (rebased on current `dev`, with two follow-up fixes). Credit to @dragonflylee for the original change (commit preserved).

## What it does

Routes downloaded-file playback through `RemoteView::play` instead of a hand-rolled `VideoView` (drops ~40 lines) and gives the player a real title (`name`/`method` params, `remote::DirEntry{type, name, path}`).

## Follow-up fixes (on top of #8)

1. **`titles`/`urls` desync in directory browsing.** The new `titles.push_back(item.name)` in the `RemotePlayer` ctor also fired on the browse path, which calls `setList()` right after; `setList()` didn't clear `titles`, so the seeded title stayed in front → clicked item duplicated, off-by-one track switching, last entry closing the player. Fixed by `titles.clear()` at the top of `setList()` (the standalone `setUrl` path keeps its seeded title).
2. **Downloads keep the "Local" profile label.** The old downloads player used `profile->init("Local")`; a `method` argument is now threaded `RemoteView::play → RemotePlayer → VideoProfile::init`, and `download_tab` passes `"Local"`, so the profile overlay reads "Local" as before.

## Verification

- Merges cleanly on current `dev`; the merged `RemotePlayer` also picks up the audio/subtitle OSD wiring `dev` gained after #8's base, so downloads get working track menus too.
- `DownloadItem` carries every field used by the new `detail` string (`seriesName`, `seasonIndex`, `episodeIndex`, `productionYear`, `name`).
- The dropped `view/auto_tab_frame.hpp` include is still satisfied transitively via `tab/remote_view.hpp` (`AutoTabFrame::focus2Sidebar` at `download_tab.cpp:455/525`).

Reboots this repo as **`lunas-playground`** — a single Vite app whose UI will be authored in `.lunas` and compiled by the real Lunas compiler (dogfooding). First step of the rewrite; the playground UI, editor/LSP, and deploy land in follow-up PRs.

## What changed

- **Tests.** `test/plugin.test.mjs` verifies our plugin wiring with an injected fake compiler (no wasm). The real compiler is exercised by `pnpm build`.
- **Docs/CI.** New `CLAUDE.md` (compiler seam, no-absolute-paths rule, PR/merge/release rules), `README`, `roadmap.yml`. CI builds wasm, then `build`/`typecheck`/`test`.
