body: ## Summary Sets up and documents the development environment for this repo (the `vllm_qw4` vLLM fork + `testdata`) so future Cursor Cloud agents can lint, test, and run the vLLM server. Adds a repo-root `AGENTS.md` with a `## Cursor Cloud specific instructions` section. No source code was modified. ### Key findings / constraints - The fork targets **Qwen3.5-27B on Hygon DCU (ROCm/DTK)** (`version.py` → `0.18.1+das.dtk2604`). - The Cursor Cloud VM is **CPU-only (no GPU, ~4 cores / ~15 GB RAM)** — Qwen3.5-27B cannot be served here. - **The fork cannot be built from source on CPU/CUDA:** `vllm_qw4/setup.py` defines a custom `get_version()` (~L891) that shadows `setuptools_scm.get_version` (L21); only the `_is_hip()` path calls it without args, so non-HIP targets fail with `TypeError: get_version() got an unexpected keyword argument 'write_to'`. This is deliberate DCU-build behavior and was left untouched. - Dev/testing on CPU therefore uses the matching upstream **`vllm==0.18.1+cpu`** wheel (same base version) in `vllm_qw4/.venv`, exercising the real vLLM engine/server with tiny models. ### What the update script installs `uv` venv (Py 3.12) at `vllm_qw4/.venv` + `requirements/lint.txt`, `requirements/cpu-build.txt`, `requirements/cpu.txt` (`--torch-backend cpu`), `pytest`/`pytest-asyncio`/`tblib`, and the `vllm==0.18.1+cpu` wheel. System pkgs `libnuma-dev`/`libtcmalloc-minimal4`/`numactl` are documented in `AGENTS.md` (installed via apt, per policy not in the update script). ## Testing - ✅ Lint: `pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files` (runs; flags pre-existing fork issues, auto-fixes reverted) - ✅ Tests: `python -m pytest tests/test_outputs.py tests/test_logger.py tests/test_inputs.py tests/test_pooling_params.py -q` → 30 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed (pooling/embedding cases need model downloads / GPU) - ✅ Offline inference on CPU with `facebook/opt-125m` (coherent output) - ✅ OpenAI server: `vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --port 8001` → `/health` 200, `/v1/models`, `/v1/completions` return generations ### Walkthrough / evidence [vllm_server_cpu_demo.log](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-8f032044-63e0-43c2-be50-0462b4e41d1f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fvllm_server_cpu_demo.log) [vllm_serve_startup.log](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-8f032044-63e0-43c2-be50-0462b4e41d1f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fvllm_serve_startup.log) AI assistance (Cursor agent) was used for this change. author: maharshi-smallest
body:
## Why

`chat_with_agent` was cutting tool-using agents off mid-turn, making them look broken when they weren't.

Two causes in the WS client:

1. **Resolved on the first agent message.** [chat-client.ts] shifted a waiter and resolved `send()` on the *first* `transcript` event. For a tool turn that's the **filler** spoken when the tool starts ("Let me find your details…") — so `send()` returned before `identify_by_phone`/`verify_dob`/`get_fund_value` finished.
2. **Force-closed immediately after the last scripted message.** The `finally { client.close() }` sent `session.close` ~200ms after that filler, severing the WS mid-tool-round (`hangup_source: user`). The real answer never arrived.

## Fix

- **Collect a full turn**: agent messages accumulate until the turn settles, instead of returning on the first one.
- **Adaptive settle**: a filler (message ending in `…`) means a tool is still running → wait longer (`toolWaitMs`) for the answer; a substantive message settles quickly (`settle_ms`, default 2500ms). Keeps normal turns fast without cutting tool rounds.
- **Drain at the end**: `waitForClose()` lets the last turn finish — including a natural agent hangup via `end_call` — before teardown.

## Verified

End-to-end against the Bajaj Life agent (turn-by-turn, defaults): auth ladder → persona ack ("Thanks, Mr. Verma — you're verified") → multi-policy disambiguation → **fund value ₹8,45,568** → farewell — all captured. Previously every turn returned only the filler.

author: damilolaedwards
body:
When one discovery provider fails, its error was dropped and the incomplete network set was returned as a successful result. Callers then overwrite networks.json with a partial set, silently removing every network that the failed provider would have supplied. Downstream consumers read those missing networks as deleted.

## Change

`executeDiscovery` now records any provider that returns an error and fails the run when one or more providers failed, instead of returning a partial result with a nil error. A failed run is skipped by the caller, so the previously published data is preserved. The happy path where all providers succeed is unchanged.

## Tests

- `TestRunOnce_PartialProviderFailure`: one failing and one succeeding provider now yields an error and an empty result, so no partial data is published.
- `TestRunOnce_AllProvidersSucceed`: guards that the normal merge path still returns all networks with no error.

All package tests pass and the linter reports no issues.

author: mairat
body:
## Summary

Implements CSS Sizing 4 §4 `aspect-ratio` support for ordinary (non-replaced) in-flow block-level boxes. When a block has an `auto` height and a preferred aspect ratio, its used height is now derived from its used width, matching reference browser behavior. This fixes the `grid-lanes` auto-repeat WPT cluster (which falls back to block display but still honours aspect-ratio) and enables aspect-ratio sizing for general block boxes.

## Key Changes

- **New method `HasDefiniteAspectRatioBlockHeight()`**: Determines whether a box's block-axis size is definite via aspect-ratio transfer (auto height + block display + no float/positioning + aspect-ratio resolvable from width).

- **New method `TryResolveAspectRatioBlockHeight()`**: Transfers the used width to a border-box height via the aspect-ratio, respecting `box-sizing` (border-box vs. content-box). Replaces the removed `TryComputeGridLanesAspectRatioSize()` which was grid-lanes-specific.

- **Updated `HeightPercentageResolvesToAuto()`**: Now returns `false` when the containing block has a definite aspect-ratio-derived height, allowing percentage-height children to resolve against the transferred height.

- **Pre-resolution in layout**: Added aspect-ratio height pre-resolution (alongside explicit-height pre-resolution) so percentage-height descendants can resolve against the definite height before child layout.

- **Final height resolution**: Added aspect-ratio height transfer after explicit-height paths but before min-/max-height clamping, ensuring author heights still win and constraints properly floor/cap the transferred square.

- **Removed grid-lanes-specific code**: Deleted `TryComputeGridLanesAspectRatioSize()`, `TryGetInlineAutoRepeatTrackSize()`, `MaxChildInlineSize()`, and related helpers that attempted to synthesize grid-lanes sizing from min-height and track templates. The general aspect-ratio path now handles the fallback case.

## Implementation Details

- Aspect-ratio applies to the box named by `box-sizing`: under `border-box` the ratio squares the border box; under `content-box` it squares the content box then maps back to border-box.
- Only applies to in-flow block-level boxes (not floated, absolutely positioned, or replaced elements), matching the CSS spec's applicability scope.
- Percentage-height children now correctly resolve against the transferred height, which is definite even though the container's own `height` is `auto`.
- Definite `height`, `min-height`, and `max-height` constraints are honoured: explicit height suppresses the transfer entirely, and min-/max-height clamp the result.

## Tests

Added `AspectRatioLayoutTests` covering:
- Aspect-ratio height derivation from explicit width (square, wide, tall ratios)
- Auto-width blocks filling the containing block then transferring via aspect-ratio
- `box-sizing` (border-box vs. content-box) interaction
- Size constraint clamping (explicit height, min-height floor, max-height cap)

Updated `GridLanesFallbackTests` to verify the dropped `grid-lanes` container honours aspect-ratio and percentage-height children resolve against the transferred height.

## WPT Impact

Fixes cluster 32 (issue #1233): the `grid-lanes/track-sizing/auto-repeat` WPT tests now match reference (the reference is a viewport-wide 1/1 aspect-ratio square from the dropped grid-lanes container, not the 100×100 track-count square #1230 assumed). Broiler previously ignored aspect-ratio on ordinary boxes and rendered a min-height-tall bar (~8% match); now matches the reference.

author: aidiffuser
body:
## Problem

The runner scans **every** incoming prompt for the magic test strings (`EXO RUNNER MUST FAIL` / `OOM` / `TIMEOUT`) and kills/OOMs/hangs itself on a match. In normal operation that's a denial-of-service footgun: any prompt that happens to *contain* exo's own source trips it — a coding-agent session working on this repo, a pasted issue report quoting the constants, or (how we hit it) a source-padded long-context benchmark, where the runner raised the artificial test failure mid-prefill at ~370k-token depth.

## Fix

`_check_for_debug_prompts` returns immediately unless `EXO_DEBUG_PROMPT_TRIGGERS=1`. Failure-injection testing keeps working — armed explicitly — and production prompts can no longer assassinate the runner by quoting the codebase.

One file, default-off gate, no behavior change for anyone not setting the variable.

author: gudnuf
body:
## Thinking

Whisper's worst failure on a jobsite isn't mishearing — it's inventing fluent text from machinery-only audio, which breaks the product's core promise (R3: under-extract, never invent). Part C closes that with two complementary gates, and the SNR sweep proved they NEED to be two: hallucinated segments cluster at high no_speech_prob (0.82–0.97, the 0.6 gate catches them) but wind produces sub-0.6 outliers that only an energy gate structure covers. Neither alone suffices; the data said so.

The sweep also settled the model question with numbers: with speech present, neither model hallucinates even at 0 dB SNR, and base.en degrades gracefully (≤14.6% WER at 0 dB) — so base.en stays the bundled default and small.en (uniformly 2–4pp better) is the validated upgrade when download/ODR lands.

Design invariants verified by the independent final review (MERGE WITH NOTES, no defects): the flush window is never energy-gated (a quiet final utterance can't be silently dropped by VAD), skipped windows still advance the chunker cursor (timestamps don't drift), and append-only holds under mid-stream no_speech drops. Conservative defaults ship: VAD off (0.0), no_speech 0.6 — device-measurement-gated tuning.

## Review notes carried as follow-ups (non-blocking)

- The two thresholds aren't yet plumbed through EngineConfig→Swift (device tuning will need it).
- Quiet-flush behavior under real whisper no_speech scores goes on the device-walk validation checklist.
- Mid-walk audio route changes (headset plug) are a pre-existing tap-format caveat, unchanged by this branch.

## Numbers

295 workspace tests (289 + 6, name-diff verified — zero removed), clippy clean, whisper-feature build clean, sweep results in spikes/stt-whisper/RESULTS.md Table 4.

author: windowhyun
body:
## 배경

CI에 추가할 항목으로 코드리뷰 체크리스트 #4(보안)가 기존 CI에서 전혀 커버되지 않고 있었습니다. 기존 품질 5잡(lint·verify-data·unit·build·e2e)에 **보안 3잡을 `ci.yml`에 합쳐** push/PR마다 병렬 8잡으로 확장합니다.

## 추가 잡

| 잡 | 하는 일 | 차단 기준 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit` | `npm audit`로 의존성 취약점 스캔 | **배포 번들**(`--omit=dev`) high+ 취약점 |
| `secrets` | `gitleaks`로 전체 커밋 히스토리에서 시크릿(API 키·토큰·비밀번호) 유출 탐지 | 시크릿 패턴 매칭 |
| `codeql` | `github/codeql-action` JS/TS 정적 분석(`security-and-quality`: XSS·프로토타입 오염·안전하지 않은 DOM 등) | 분석 오류(경보는 Security 탭) |

## 설계 근거

- **`audit`가 `--omit=dev`인 이유**: 이 앱은 클라이언트 SPA라 사용자에게 실제로 나가는 코드는 프로덕션 의존성뿐입니다. 현재 high 취약점(`pdfjs-dist`·`undici`)은 빌드/스크립트용 dev 툴링에만 있어 배포물에 포함되지 않으므로, 차단은 프로덕션 트리 기준으로 하고 dev 트리는 `continue-on-error` 정보성 단계로 가시성만 확보합니다. (프로덕션 트리 `--audit-level=high`는 현재 통과 = exit 0 확인)
- **`codeql` 권한**: 이 잡만 결과 업로드용 `security-events: write`를 job 레벨로 부여하고, 나머지는 최상위 `contents: read`(읽기 전용)를 상속합니다.
- **시크릿 기준선**: 현재 커밋된 시크릿/키 없음(`google-services.json`·`.env` 미커밋) 확인 → gitleaks 즉시 통과.
- 공개 저장소라 CodeQL·gitleaks 모두 무료로 동작합니다.

## 주의

author: alextymosh
body:
## Summary

Completes the remaining runtime secret-masking hardening item for issue #328.

This PR converts the remaining secret-like runtime settings from plain `str`
fields to `SecretStr`, while preserving the existing runtime behaviour for Vault,
outbox invite encryption, Keycloak client secret fallback and local privacy
export signing.

## Changes

* Convert remaining secret-like settings to `SecretStr`:

  * `VAULT__TOKEN`
  * `VAULT__ROLE_ID`
  * `VAULT__SECRET_ID`
  * `SECURITY__OUTBOX_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`
  * `SECURITY__KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET`
  * `PRIVACY_EXPORTS__LOCAL_SIGNING_SECRET`
* Update validators to read raw secret values only at runtime boundaries.
* Update Vault provider authentication to unwrap `SecretStr` safely.
* Update outbox encryption key resolution to preserve the existing Fernet
  validation behaviour.
* Update Keycloak client secret helper to keep the provider-first fallback
  behaviour.
* Keep local privacy export URL signing compatible with `SecretStr`.
* Add regression tests proving secret values are masked in settings dumps.
* Update `SESSION_NOTES.md` to mark PR-328-9C as merged and record this final
  secret-masking hardening step.

## Why

The backend Docker runtime hardening was already completed, but several
secret-like runtime settings were still stored as plain strings.

Using `SecretStr` reduces the risk of exposing secret values through accidental
settings dumps, logs, tracebacks or debug output.

## Scope

This PR does not change DSR workflow behaviour.

Representative DSR fulfilment, export ownership and erasure targeting were
already covered by the previous PR-328-9C work. This PR only closes the remaining
runtime configuration hardening gap before final #328 closure.

## Risk

Medium-low.

The main risk is that some runtime call sites previously expected plain strings.
This PR keeps raw secret extraction limited to runtime boundaries by using
`.get_secret_value()` only where the actual secret value is required.

author: charith-dananjaya
body:
## Summary
Adds the core `Task` domain model and `Priority` enum under `com.cj.taskcli.task`. This is a pure domain layer — no storage, no persistence, no CLI wiring yet

## Changes
- Restructured base package from `com.cj` to `com.cj.taskcli` for better namespacing as the project grows.
- Added `Priority` enum (`LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`).
- Added `Task` class:
  - Fields: `id (UUID)`, `taskName (String)`, `dueDate (LocalDate)`, `priority (Priority)`, `isCompleted (boolean)`.
  - Constructor generates the `UUID` internally and defaults `isCompleted` to `false`.
  - `markComplete()` exposed as a dedicated no-arg method rather than a public setter, to prevent invalid state transitions (e.g. un-completing a task via a bare setter).
  - Constructor and setters validate non-null inputs via `Objects.requireNonNull`.
  - `equals()`/`hashCode()` implemented based on `id` only, since task identity shouldn't change even if other fields (name, date, priority) are updated later.

## Design notes / trade-offs
- Chose `LocalDate` over `Date` for due dates — modern API, immutable, clearer date-only semantics.
- Chose an `enum` for `Priority` over a raw `String`/`int` — compiler-enforced valid values, self-documenting at call sites.
- Class is mutable overall (matches the "update task" MVP requirement), with the one deliberate exception of `completed`, which is only mutable through `markComplete()`.

author: hmans
body:
Fixes cross-tab presence mode syncing so clearing Away in one tab forces other tabs' current-user badge back to Online instead of recalculating from the receiving tab's hidden or idle state.

The root cause was storage-synced `auto` mode being treated like passive auto-presence instead of an explicit user action from another tab.

Adds a unit regression for storage-driven mode changes and an e2e regression for the same-user two-tab lower-left badge flow.

Validated with `mise x -- pnpm --dir apps/frontend exec vitest --run src/lib/presenceTracking.spec.ts` and `mise x -- pnpm --dir apps/frontend exec playwright test e2e/presence-indicators.test.ts -g "same-user tab updates current user badge" --retries=0`.

author: naspirato
body: Fixes ydb-platform/ydb#45582 ## Problem After a successful fast-unmute, tests could be **re-muted on the next hourly run** even though the grace ladder was designed to prevent that. Example: `TGRpcCmsTest.AlterRemoveTest` on 2026-07-05 — unmuted at 01:06 UTC, re-muted at 01:57 UTC (issue #45555). ## Root cause Grace rows (`fast_unmute_grace`) were only inserted in Job 1 (`manual_unmute.py sync`) when `tests_monitor` already showed `is_muted=0`. Job 1 runs **before** Job 2 and reads monitor state from the **previous** hour, so on the first run after unmute PR merge grace was often missing → full **4-day** mute window → re-mute. ## Why not grace at unmute PR creation? An earlier approach wrote grace when `update_muted_ya` **decides** to unmute. That is wrong: the mute PR may merge hours or days later, so `grace_started_at` must reflect **actual** unmute on `main`, not PR open time. ## Fix New Job 2 step **after** `tests_monitor` refresh (reflects merged `muted_ya` on branch): ``` enter_fast_unmute_grace → sync_fast_unmute_grace → update_muted_ya ``` `enter_fast_unmute_grace_for_unmuted_tests`: - For `fast_unmute_active` rows where fresh monitor shows `is_muted=0` - Insert `fast_unmute_grace` with `grace_started_at = now` (actual unmute) - Skip if grace row already exists (idempotent with Job 1 cleanup) Job 1 `cleanup_manual_unmute` also skips grace upsert when row already exists, so it won't reset `grace_started_at`. ## Alternatives considered ### Why not fix it in `create_issues_for_muted_tests.yml`? That merge-triggered workflow already has the right ordering: job `create-issues-for-muted-tests` refreshes `tests_monitor`, then job `sync-manual-fast-unmute` (`needs:` the first) writes grace via `manual_unmute.py sync`. It is still not sufficient: - the grace write lags the monitor refresh by a **separate job** (new runner + `pip install` + `export_issues_to_ydb`) — during that gap the monitor already reads `is_muted=0` while grace is still empty; - the re-mute decision is made by a **different** workflow (`update_muted_ya.yml`) that runs on schedule **independently and concurrently**, and refreshes `tests_monitor` on its own. There is no ordering guarantee between the two workflows → the hourly run can read an empty `grace_map` before the merge-workflow writes grace (exactly the 01:06 → 01:57 case). The only race-free point is co-locating the grace write immediately before its read, in the same `update_muted_ya.yml` job, right after the same `tests_monitor` refresh. ### Why a dedicated function instead of reusing existing ones? - `cleanup_manual_unmute` (Job 1) also writes grace, but it cannot be called from Job 2: it performs GitHub side effects (reopen / comment / label / project-status), operates **globally** across all `(branch, build_type)`, and deletes `fast_unmute_active` rows. Job 2 is a per-`build_type` matrix (N parallel legs) → duplicate/racing GitHub calls and premature row deletion. The lifecycle is deliberately kept as a single point in Job 1. - `sync_fast_unmute_grace` does the opposite — it **deletes** grace rows for tests that became mute candidates again; it cannot create grace. - So `enter_fast_unmute_grace` is a narrow, idempotent, GitHub-free writer that reuses the low-level building blocks (`fetch_currently_muted`, `upsert_fast_unmute_grace_row`, `grace_ttl_calendar_days`). Only two queries are new: `fetch_fast_unmute_active_rows` (filtered by `branch`/`build_type` — the existing `fetch_all_rows` is global) and `fetch_grace_full_names` (idempotency guard so `grace_started_at` is not reset). ## Testing - `python3 -m py_compile` on modified mute scripts

author: martadams89
body:
Probe each configured provider's **live** model list, version-rank it (**"highest number wins"** within a tier — mini / sonnet / flash / sonar), default to the newest, and let each workspace **pick & choose**.

## What it does
- **`ai/models.ts`**: `probeModels()` queries OpenAI/xAI (`/v1/models`), Anthropic (`/v1/models`), Gemini (list models, `generateContent`-capable) and Perplexity (known `sonar` set). `pickLatest()` ranks by numeric version so `gpt-5.1-mini` beats `gpt-5-mini` beats `gpt-4o-mini`. `resolveModel()` returns the workspace override (`model_<provider>`, stored via the layered per-workspace settings) → else the safe default.
- **Citation checks + llms.txt generation** now call the resolved model instead of a hard-coded one (Brave unaffected — it's search, not chat).
- **Endpoints**: `GET /api/ai/models` (probe + current selection), `PUT /api/ai/models` (owner-only, per-workspace).
- **UI**: a **Models** picker on the AI Citations page — one dropdown per configured provider, options populated from the live probe, defaulting to the auto-detected latest, with an "auto" badge and a per-provider override.

## Verification
- `models.test.ts`: version ranker (5 cases incl. tier fallback + empty→default). Backend build + **38 tests** green; frontend lint (0 errors) + build green.

body:
Wires the existing Repousse.Projects.Policy into every ProjectController
action (read/edit/manage_members/manage_media/post_journal/moderate) and
fills out the previously-stubbed Projects context to match: invitations
(create/accept), member role changes with the "at least one admin" and
"can't self-remove as sole admin" guards, auto-archive when a project's
last admin is removed, author-only journal entry edits (project-admin
override on delete), a 10-file media cap, and platform-admin
unpublish/delete moderation with a mandatory reason emailed to project
admins (new additive Emails functions).

Along the way, fixes several pre-existing bugs that blocked any of this
from working: create_project never actually set owner_id (changeset
always failed validate_required), add_media referenced non-existent
uploader_id/position fields, update_project's changeset wrongly required
owner_id on every edit, and none of the Project/*Member/*Invitation/
*Media/JournalEntry schemas had a Jason.Encoder so any JSON response
would have crashed.

Adds OpenApiSpex operation specs to all 15 routed controller actions, and
ExUnit coverage: full Projects context tests plus a controller-level
reader/editor/admin/platform-admin authorization matrix, calling actions
directly via ProjectController.call/2 (no controller tests existed
anywhere in the app before this).

Deliberately deferred (out of epic-04's routed scope / no infra yet):
- No HTTP route accepts invitation tokens yet (only creation is routed);
  Projects.accept_invitation/2 is implemented and tested, ready to wire
  once that route/flow is decided.
- In-app notifications (only email exists in this codebase); member-removed
  and republish emails are not sent (only unpublish/delete/archive are).
- Auto-archive on account deletion (US-PROJET-08) only covers the
  in-app remove_member path — Accounts.delete_user's DB-level cascade
  delete is owned by another track.

author: hussain-coder-eng
body:
## Summary

Eight commits spanning three efforts: image-to-route accuracy, run-tracking (off-route) fixes, and the approved 23-item improvement batch.

### Image-to-route accuracy
- Fix aspect-ratio distortion: Gemini vision strokes arrive normalized [0,1] per axis, squashing non-square subjects; the source aspect ratio is now carried through and strokes are un-squashed + letterbox-refit onto the optimizer's rotation pivot.
- Drop decorative internal strokes (<18% of silhouette diagonal) whose pen-up connectors broke silhouette closure; tune the vision prompt (closed loops must close, skip sub-10% features).

### Run tracking ("already off the trail" fix)
- Off-route now requires distance > max(30m, GPS accuracy) on 3 consecutive usable fixes (accuracy ≤100m), and never fires before first on-route contact.
- GPS snapping constrained to a progress window (50m behind / 250m ahead): on closed-loop GPS-art routes a start fix could snap to the route END and instantly auto-finish the run; self-intersections could jump progress to the wrong pass.
- Pause actually pauses (position + timer); turn alerts refire on restart (no more navRoute mutation); auto-finish reports the real completed polyline; average pace now computed.

### Backend reliability & cost
- Gemini retry loop under a 90s wall-clock budget (was up to ~142s inside a 120s function timeout, stranding jobs in "processing").
- New `reapStaleJobs` scheduled function: fails stuck jobs, deletes expired jobs/cache entries; resolved jobs get `deleteAt` (+24h) and their ~1MB base64 image stripped.
- Rate-limit fairness (cache hits free, refunds on failure); server-derived cache keys (closes cross-user cache poisoning); `rateLimits` backend-only in rules; `firestore.indexes.json` added (routes query silently failed on fresh deploys); slot lease sharded.

### App UX & features
- Fix Fine-tune Route bug that showed no markers and could wipe the route on Save (waypoints never resynced after generation).
- Saved routes UI (save/load/delete), Download GPX button, working Share Your Art (canvas share image), mi/km toggle converts the value, Redesign bypasses the generation cooldown, geolocation-denied notice, location-search keyboard/loading/no-results UX, accessibility pass on core controls, ErrorBoundary, notch safe-areas + mobile meta, turn-alert voice reliability.
- Deleted dead `preprocessorService` (Math.random() scoring).

### Performance & platform
- Orientation scoring uses a spatial grid index (built once per `findBestOrientation`, identical scores) instead of scanning every edge per segment 18×.
- Bundle diet: `@turf/turf` → 12 per-function packages behind a `src/lib/turf.ts` barrel; removed 5 unused deps; vendor code-splitting (main chunk 1,182 kB → 396 kB).
- PWA: manifest + auto-updating service worker, generated icons, 7-day map-tile caching; Firestore/Overpass/OSRM/Nominatim stay network-only.

## Verification
- Full suite: 198/198 tests (17 files), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean (manifest + sw emitted), functions build clean.

## Deployment notes
- `firebase deploy --only functions` (first deploy prompts to enable Cloud Scheduler for `reapStaleJobs`)
- `firebase deploy --only firestore` (rules + new composite indexes)
- Optional: native TTL policies on `jobs.deleteAt` and `geminiCache.expiresAt` (gcloud commands in the `reapStaleJobs` docblock).

author: naito-7110
body:
# 概要

CLI からリリースの引き金(タグ作成 + タグ送信の便利コマンド)を撤去する。AI はオーナーと同一の gh 認証を共有するため**サーバー側で AI と人間を区別できず**、引き金を守れるのはクライアント hook だけ。その状況で磨かれたデプロイコマンドを全設置先のバイナリに配布するのは merge-policy の原則(デプロイ = 人間のタグ操作)と矛盾する — オーナー指摘(2026-07-05)。

## 関連 Issue

Closes #129

## 変更内容

- internal/release パッケージ・cli の該当サブコマンドとテスト・usage・main 配線を削除
- **gate は防御として維持・強化**: リリースコマンドの起動検出を旧名バイナリ(factory 名義)にも拡張(残存環境対策)・タグ送信判定に旧名タグ prefix を追加・撤去済みコマンドを案内していた文言を README 参照へ差し替え
- tools README のリリース節を「人間が手で打つ生 git の安全手順」(--tags 込み fetch → 既存タグ確認 → リモート ref にタグ → 送信)+ 認証共有の理由明記に書き換え。CLAUDE.md スタック事実・hooks README を同期
- テスト追加: 旧名バイナリ起動 2 形・旧名タグ送信 1 形(いずれも exit 2 + 理由の状態検証)

## 影響範囲分析の要約

- 撤去しても AI の能力自体(生 git)は消えないが、それは gate が引き続き塞ぐ。本 PR は「製品が用意した引き金」を無くし、防御対象を生 git 操作だけに絞る
- 旧版バイナリが残る環境では hook の判定が旧パターンのままという構造的限界あり(新リリースの取得で解消)
- 独立レビュア実測により pre-existing のすり抜け 3 種を確認(引用符付きタグ名など)— 本 diff の退行ではなく、#119(ゲート正規表現の頑健性)へ証拠をコメントで追記済み

## テスト

- tools/atelier: `go build ./...` / `go test ./...` / `golangci-lint run` すべて green
- **実測(ADR 0001)**: red = タグ送信 exit 2 / 旧名バイナリのリリース起動 exit 2。green = 新バイナリにサブコマンドが存在しない(usage 表示)
- 撤去の完全性 grep: コマンド形の残存は gate の防御コード・テスト・歴史注記のみ

## Feature Flag

なし

## セルフレビューチェックリスト

- [x] 独立レビュア(セキュリティ + 撤去完全性 + テスト品質)実行 — critical / major なし。minor の README 手順(--tags)は適用済み、すり抜け 3 種は #119 へ

## レビュー観点

- gate の起動検出パターンに旧名(factory)を含めた判断 — 受け入れ条件の grep とは「防御コードは歴史注記扱い」で整合させた
- 本 PR マージ後、#128(v1.0.0)の CHANGELOG に撤去の 1 行を追記する(段取り済み)

author: marandaneto
body:
## Problem

When browser extensions, ad blockers, CORS, or other client-side blockers cause requests to fail before an HTTP response, they surface as `statusCode: 0`. Analytics events already cap retries for this case, and the logs pipeline now has a similar circuit breaker, but two other browser SDK paths can still loop forever when blocked:

- `/flags/?v=2` refreshes periodically in long-running sessions.
- Conversations message/ticket polling runs every 5 seconds while the widget is active.

## Changes

- Added a status-0 circuit breaker for feature flag refreshes after 3 consecutive online status-0 failures.
  - Any HTTP response resets the counter.
  - Offline failures do not count.
  - The browser `online` event resets and immediately retries flags.
- Added a status-0 circuit breaker for conversations polling after 3 consecutive online status-0 failures.
  - Covers regular `_poll()` plus direct `_pollMessages()` / `_pollTickets()` entrypoints.
  - Any HTTP response resets the counter.
  - Offline failures do not count.
  - The browser `online` event reopens polling.
- Extracted the shared browser online check into `isBrowserOnline()` in `utils/globals.ts` so future status-0 handling can reuse the same semantics.
- Extracted shared status-0 circuit-breaker helpers into `utils/request-utils.ts` and reused them in feature flags and conversations.
- Added explicit `PostHogFeatureFlags.destroy()` cleanup for the `online` listener and call it from `posthog.shutdown()`.
- Added regression tests for both paths.
- Updated mangled private names and added a changeset.

## Release info Sub-libraries affected

### Libraries affected

- [ ] All of them
- [x] posthog-js (web)
- [ ] posthog-js-lite (web lite)
- [ ] posthog-node
- [ ] posthog-react-native
- [ ] @posthog/react-native-plugin
- [ ] @posthog/react

- [ ] @posthog/nuxt

- [ ] @posthog/browser-common

## Checklist

- [x] Tests for new code
- [x] Accounted for the impact of any changes across different platforms
- [x] Accounted for backwards compatibility of any changes (no breaking changes!)
- [x] Took care not to unnecessarily increase the bundle size

### If releasing new changes

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Follow-up to the status-0 logs circuit breaker review: I inspected the remaining repeated browser endpoints and implemented the same bounded behavior for `/flags/?v=2` refreshes and conversations polling. I left lower-frequency/cached endpoints such as surveys/product tours/web experiments alone because they either already have backoff or are not periodic by default.

## Required access model
- employees see only jobs assigned to them
- owner, admin, dispatch and God mode see every job
- higher roles can create, plan, open, edit, assign, add notes and reports, manage time logs, and delete jobs
- finance access remains unchanged and owner-only

## Root causes
- the Einsätze page still resolved roles in the browser and a stale employee staff row could override an admin profile

- centralize operational role resolution on the server with owner/admin/dispatch precedence
- verify every manager request using the authenticated Supabase bearer token
- proxy an allowlisted set of job tables and job RPCs through the service role only after manager verification
- preserve normal RLS fallback for employees
- load the verified job bridge on list, planning, and detail pages
- select the All date filter for managers so the complete planning list is visible

- GitHub CI and calendar validation are required before merge

author: sbarteau2022
body:
## What this is

The memory kernel ranked nodes by **semantic match + importance + recency** — it finds memories that *look like* the query. It cannot find the memory that *matters* to the query but shares none of its words: the decision a fact led to, the insight distilled from an observation, the correction that superseded an old belief. Those are **edges**, not similarity. This adds the graph layer over the same `elle_memory` nodes.

It's the **recall layer** both KV caches (hosted #72 and sovereign Elle#39) delegate to — the piece the graph-memory spec called P1.

## What's in it

- **`src/graph.ts`**
  - Typed, weighted edges: `assoc · causal · derived · refines · supersedes · contradicts · session · about · tool`, each with a tuned **conductance** (derivation carries signal, supersession is followed hard, contradiction is a faint pull that surfaces tension without dominating).
  - **`spreadActivation`** — a pure, store-agnostic core: bounded BFS that flows charge along edges damped by `weight · conductance · decay^hop`. Fully unit-tested with no D1.
  - **`GraphStore` seam** — `CloudGraphStore` over D1 today; a `LocalGraphStore` over SQLite drops in for the sovereign build with zero change to the traversal. Self-healing `elle_memory_edges` table, weight-reinforcing upserts (`ON CONFLICT … weight = MIN(cap, weight + bump)`).
  - **`graphExpand`** (2-hop reach in two indexed queries) and **`recordAssociations`**.

- **Self-bootstrapping — no LLM, no daemon.** Every recall records the co-occurrence of the set it returned as `assoc` edges (reinforced on repeat), so the graph learns which memories belong together simply by being used. A hot path strengthens; the next query landing on either end pulls the other in.

- **`memRecall` integration** — a best-effort graph-expansion pass after the base ranking: seed with the top hits, spread activation, fold in connected nodes the similarity search missed (`via: 'graph'`). Additive and non-fatal — on a fresh graph it's one empty query and a no-op; any failure returns the base recall untouched.

## Tests

`src/graph.test.ts` — 18 cases over the pure core (activation flow, hop limits, symmetry, weight/conductance ordering, floor pruning, self-loop guards) and the traversal + recorder against an in-memory `GraphStore`. Full suite **136/136**; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Note on the branch

My task branch (`claude/dynamic-kv-cache-13fxo4`) still points at the already-merged #72 commit, so this follow-up work is on a fresh branch to avoid a force-push over merged history.

author: hajiboy95
body:
## Description

Adds `KiwiDesk --version` (and `-v`), plus a matching `version`
IPC/Lua command, so users and bug reporters can report the
running build without needing a source checkout.

- `KiwiDesk --version` / `-v`: handled locally in the CLI
  (like `help`) — works even if the app is not running.
- `version` command in the `execute()` dispatcher, registered
  in `APIReference.commands` (so it also shows up in
  `help`/`list_commands` and is callable from Lua as
  `KiwiDesk.version()`). Returns `{"version": ..., "commit": ...}`.
- `KiwiDeskVersion` (Sources/KiwiDeskCore/App/KiwiDeskVersion.swift):
  a small enum holding `semantic` and `commit` constants plus a
  `displayString` used by the CLI.

## Related Issue(s)

Fixes #19

## Version-baking design decision (tradeoff)

Went with the **simplest, zero-build-tooling** approach: the
version and commit are plain checked-in Swift constants, bumped
by hand via `scripts/bump-version.sh <version>` as the last step
before tagging a release (it stamps the file with the current
short SHA; you commit the result).

Rejected alternatives and why:
- **SwiftPM build-tool plugin to inject a live git SHA** —
  `Package.swift` already documents that the SwiftLint prebuild
  plugin cannot run during build planning on this project's CI
  toolchain ("a prebuild command cannot use executables built
  from source"); a codegen plugin would hit the same wall.
- **Shell out to `git rev-parse` at runtime** — works for a
  source checkout, but breaks for an installed/distributed
  binary with no `.git` directory nearby (exactly the gap this
  issue exists to close).
- **`Info.plist` / `CFBundleShortVersionString`** — the
  executable target isn't packaged as an app bundle at build
  time (SwiftPM `.executableTarget`, no plist), so there's
  nothing to read this from without adding bundle packaging
  just for this.

Tradeoff: `commit` can go stale between the last bump and the
next commit (it reflects "as of the last release stamp", not
"this exact build"). For a pre-1.0 project with no release
cadence yet, this is an acceptable, low-maintenance starting
point; `commit` defaults to `"unknown"` so a stale-looking value
is never silently wrong — dev/local builds are unambiguous.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `CommandTests.versionCommand` asserting
  `execute("version")` returns `{version, commit}` matching
  `KiwiDeskVersion`.
- [x] Extended `CommandTests.helpCommand` to assert `version`
  is listed.
- [x] Manually ran `./.build/debug/KiwiDesk --version` and `-v`.

## Checklist

- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits format
  (see AGENTS.md §3)
- [x] New behavior is tested (pure logic / layout code
  required)
- [x] User-facing changes are documented in `docs/`
- [x] No contradictions between code and docs
- [x] `swift build && swift test && ./scripts/lint.sh`
  passes
- [x] Release build passes: `swift build -c release`
- [x] PR is focused; refactors separated from features

## Notes for Reviewer

`docs/cli.md`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml`, and
`CONTRIBUTING.md` are updated in this same change per the issue
scope. `scripts/bump-version.sh` is new tooling for cutting a
release; it isn't wired into CI (no release pipeline exists yet
in this repo) — happy to follow up separately if a release
workflow is wanted.

author: fdittgen-png
body:
## Problem
Searching for fuel stations "took a lot of time" — the results map was frozen. The field error log had **50 identical** throws:

```
LatLng is not finite: LatLng(NaN, NaN)
  Crs.checkLatLng → Epsg3857.latLngToOffset → MapCamera.projectAtZoom
  → TileRangeCalculator → _TileLayerState._onTileUpdateEvent
```

Startup itself was fine (trace: 299 ms). The map re-threw on **every** tile-update event because the camera was non-finite.

## Root cause (recurring-bug protocol — two modes, one symptom)
- **Mode A (field trigger):** a **zero-span** `LatLngBounds` reached `CameraFit.bounds`, which computes an **infinite fit-zoom** → the camera projects to `LatLng(NaN, NaN)`. All three framing helpers (`InlineMap._boundsOfPoints`, `DrivingMapView._boundsOf`, `RouteMapView._computeRouteBounds`) only epsilon-padded the `length == 1` case, so **≥2 stations at identical coordinates** (a chain returning a duplicate) collapsed `LatLngBounds.fromPoints` to `min == max` and slipped through.
- **Mode B (defensive):** a non-finite station coordinate propagating NaN into the centroid / bounds.

Proven RED on the old path: `CameraFit.bounds(fromPoints([identical, identical]))` throws `Camera zoom must be finite` (in release that becomes the field's NaN tile-range throw).

## Fix
- New canonical `StationMapGeometry.boundsOfPoints` — drops non-finite points, finite fallback box when empty, and **epsilon-pads any near-zero span in either axis** (single point OR co-located duplicates). `inline_map` + `route_map_view` delegate to it (removes 2 copies of the buggy logic); `boundsForRadius` routes its corners through it so a zero radius is safe too.
- `centerOf` skips non-finite members and returns a finite fallback instead of `0/0 = NaN`.
- `DrivingMapView` keeps its **own** self-contained NaN-safe centroid + bounds — no cross-feature import, so the `driving → map` feature-boundary baseline stays at 3.

## Tests
- New `station_map_geometry_test.dart` (13 cases): identical points, single point, empty, non-finite, zero radius — each must yield a **finite `CameraFit` camera**.
- `driving_map_view_test.dart`: NaN-safe `computeCenter` cases.
- Full `flutter analyze` clean; map + driving + lint suites green.

## Constraints honoured
- Pure geometry fix — **no new user-facing strings**.
- Keeps working on iPhone, Android **and** F-Droid (no plugin / platform surface touched).

Closes #3488

author: chiaminejp
body:
## Summary

Bumps `clvm` 4.0.1 → **4.1.0**, which upgrades the bundled `clvm_wasm` from 0.7.0 to 0.16.2 (~2 years of clvm_rs runtime updates for the Rust backend). Version: **0.11.0**.

## Behavior change: negative-operand `div` (consensus fix)

`brun` on the Rust backend now **allows `div` with negative operands** (floor division), matching current `clvm_rs` 0.18.0 consensus — the old wasm's `FAIL: div operator with negative operands is deprecated` was pre-hard-fork behaviour. The 4 affected fixtures (`brun/div-2`, `brun/div-3`, `edge-cases/div-07`, `edge-cases/div-09`) were regenerated and **verified byte-exact against `clvm_rs` directly** (`Program.run_with_cost`): cost 1125 / result −1096 for the `(/ 2 5)` cases, result 1 for the sign-cancelling ones.

**Deliberate divergence from the Python CLI**: Python clvm_tools' Rust backend is silently broken with `clvm_rs` ≥ 0.17 (`run_serialized_chia_program` no longer exists → ImportError → python-backend fallback), and Python's `clvm` evaluator still rejects negative operands. So the Python CLI currently prints the stale FAIL; this port now prints the consensus result.

## Erratum for the 0.10.0 notes

The 0.10.0 release notes attributed acceptance of `((X)...)` forms to the bundled wasm lagging `clvm_rs`. That was wrong — `clvm_rs` 0.18 accepts those forms too; the rejection exists only in Python's `clvm` evaluator. No consensus divergence there. Recorded in the CHANGELOG.

## Verification

- `pnpm audit` clean; all **962 tests pass**; build succeeds; lockfile resolves `clvm@4.1.0` from the registry with its published integrity hash.
- **5000-program differential fuzz** vs the Python CLI: 4993 byte-identical, 1 BLS-wording-only, and exactly the **6 expected negative-div divergences** (consensus-correct on our side, verified against clvm_rs). Nothing else moved.

## Release steps after merging

1. GitHub release `v0.11.0` on the merge commit (body = CHANGELOG section).
2. `pnpm build`, `npm publish` from `.dist/npm`.
3. Post-publish: bump `.example/*` to `^0.11.0` and refresh their lockfiles.

author: mwelwa-cyber
body:
## Why

securityheaders.com flags **`'unsafe-inline'` in `script-src`** as dangerous: with it present, an injected inline `<script>` still executes, defeating much of the CSP's XSS protection. It was only there because `index.html` shipped inline scripts and inline event handlers. Removing that dependency is the last step to a clean CSP (and pairs with #1585, which dropped `'unsafe-eval'`).

## What

**Externalise the inline boot scripts → `public/boot.js`** (served verbatim from `public/`, so a plain `script-src 'self'` covers it — no fragile per-build hash, which wouldn't survive HTML minification anyway):
- Pre-paint **theme guard**
- **White-screen watchdog** (boot recovery net) — its two `onclick` recovery buttons now use `addEventListener`
- The font stylesheet's inline **`onload="this.media='all'"`** is replaced by a promotion step in `boot.js` (the `<link>` gets `id="zed-fonts"`)

A `<link rel="preload" as="script" href="/boot.js">` in `<head>` starts the download during head parse, so the render-blocking `<script src="/boot.js">` resolves near-instantly and the boot skeleton still paints fast.

**CSP `script-src` now carries neither `'unsafe-inline'` nor `'unsafe-eval'`:**
```
script-src 'self' blob: https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com https://apis.google.com https://eu.i.posthog.com https://*.posthog.com https://cdn.jsdelivr.net
```

### Also fixes a latent CSP breakage: KaTeX

While auditing runtime-injected resources I found the KaTeX math renderer (`src/utils/quizRichText.js`) loads its **JS, CSS, and woff2 fonts from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net`** at runtime — an origin the enforced CSP (#1583) was **silently blocking**, so math in quizzes/notes would not render. Added `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net` to `script-src`, `style-src`, and `font-src`.

## Testing

- `npm run build` ✓ — built `dist/index.html` has **no inline executable `<script>`** (only `/boot.js`, the module bundle, and exempt `application/ld+json`) and **no inline event-handler attributes**
- `npm run lint` ✓, file-integrity ✓
- `npm run smoke` ✓ — 5/5 public routes render in headless Chromium with the externalised boot script
- `/boot.js` serves **200** (`text/javascript`) from the build output

### Note

`style-src` intentionally keeps `'unsafe-inline'` — React inline styles + the boot-skeleton inline styles need it, and securityheaders does not flag style-src `'unsafe-inline'` as dangerous. Because CI's mobile-smoke serves static `dist/` without Hosting headers, the CSP isn't exercised in CI; a quick production pass with DevTools open (especially a **math-containing quiz** for KaTeX, plus login/AI/payments) is the final confirmation.

Bucket B item 1 from #4814 (`mcp-registry-listed` 0/1, est **+1.2** — the best external ROI on the board). orank's check accepts "publish the server under your own domain" — the official MCP registry (registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) domain namespace is exactly that, and it's bi-directionally verified by construction (namespace = proven domain ownership). No account needed: the registry supports **HTTP domain verification** via a well-known file, so this is fully automatable.

## What ships

- **`public/.well-known/mcp-registry-auth`** — Ed25519 public key in the `v=MCPv1; k=ed25519; p=…` format the registry's verifier fetches. The private key lives only at `~/.config/worldmonitor/mcp-registry-ed25519.pem` (0600, outside any repo).
- **`server.json`** — the registry entry: `app.worldmonitor/mcp`, remote `streamable-http https://worldmonitor.app/mcp` (same apex dialect the server card proves against orank, #4806), `websiteUrl`, repository, version 1.13.0.
- **vercel.json** — explicit `text/plain` for the well-known auth file (extensionless).
- **`tests/mcp-registry-artifacts.test.mjs`** — format guard on the auth file (a 404 or drift bricks future `mcp-publisher login http`), name/remote parity with the server card, and version parity so a SERVER_VERSION bump also bumps `server.json` (+ republish, one command, documented in the test header).

## After merge + deploy

`mcp-publisher login http --domain=worldmonitor.app` + `mcp-publisher publish` runs from this session; then a follow-up adds the registry backlink to docs and the orank rescan verifies the flip.

body:
## Scope

- Migrates CliRelay runtime data stack work on branch `codex/clirelay-postgres-redis-ent-migration`; base is `dev`.
- Wei-Shaw/sub2api was used only as a technical reference; no external repo was modified.
- `codeProxy` was not changed because the management API response contract did not require a frontend/client adaptation.
- Adds Postgres/Redis migration validation, all-management-route API smoke coverage, focused CRUD regressions, concurrency/hot-path checks, Redis lock/queue/fallback checks, SQLite import dry-run/apply coverage, and deploy safety gates.

## Deploy Safety

- Pushes to `dev` now build the Linux binary but skip server deployment unless `workflow_dispatch` is used or repo variable `CLIRELAY_DEV_AUTO_DEPLOY=true` is set.
- `scripts/deploy-blue-green.sh` refuses deploy if `postgres.dsn` / `CLIRELAY_POSTGRES_DSN` is missing. If Redis is enabled, it also requires `redis.addr` / `CLIRELAY_REDIS_ADDR`.
- No merge, protected-branch push, online restart, production DB operation, or deployment was performed.

## Local Validation Run

PostgreSQL 15+ test container: `clirelay-pg15-test` on `127.0.0.1:55432`. Redis 7+ test container: `clirelay-redis7-test` on `127.0.0.1:56379`.

- `CLIRELAY_POSTGRES_TEST_DSN=... rtk go test ./internal/api/routes -run 'TestManagementAPIPostgres(DataStackRegression|AllRoutesSmoke)' -count=1 -v` -> passed, 224 tests/subtests. Covers every registered management route and detailed Postgres-backed CRUD/data-stack flows for API keys/profiles, model config/pricing, proxy pool, routing config, runtime settings, CCSwitch import configs, usage logs/content/chart/entity stats/dashboard/public summary.
- `CLIRELAY_POSTGRES_TEST_DSN=... CLIRELAY_REDIS_TEST_ADDR=127.0.0.1:56379 rtk go test ./internal/usage -run 'TestPostgresRuntimeDataStackIntegration|TestPostgresRuntimeDataStackConcurrencyConstraintsAndHotPaths|TestRedisRuntimeLockAndQueue|TestRedisUnavailableDoesNotBlockPostgresCRUD' -count=1 -v` -> passed, 4 tests. Covers concurrent request-log inserts, unique constraints, FK cascade, SQL EXPLAIN hot-path index use, Redis lock ownership, FIFO queue, and Redis-unavailable Postgres CRUD fallback.
- `CLIRELAY_POSTGRES_TEST_DSN=... rtk go test ./internal/storage/postgres/sqliteinventory -run TestImportSQLiteDryRunAndApply -count=1 -v` -> passed. Covers SQLite dry-run/apply import and row/checksum validation path.
- `rtk go generate ./internal/storage/postgres/ent` -> passed.
- `rtk python3 scripts/check-backend-structure.py` -> passed. Also fixes the previous PR CI failure by excluding generated Ent code from the large-file structure guard.
- `rtk bash -n scripts/deploy-blue-green.sh` -> passed.
- `CLIRELAY_POSTGRES_TEST_DSN=... CLIRELAY_REDIS_TEST_ADDR=127.0.0.1:56379 rtk go test ./...` -> passed, 2714 tests in 177 packages.
- `rtk go vet ./...` -> passed.
- `rtk go build -o test-output ./cmd/server` -> passed; temporary binary removed.

## Known Failures Fixed

author: sv-tmueller
body:
Closes #224

## Summary

`_backfill` only ever fitted and saved a calibration cell for lead-1 TMAX
(cli.py's `if 1 in leads` special case); higher leads and TMIN were
accuracy-only or unfitted. Since the live run bets leads 0-3 on both TMAX and
TMIN, `apply_calibration` was falling back to raw, structurally
underdispersed Gaussians on nearly every bet.

- `fetch_historical_lead_forecasts` (replaces `fetch_historical_point_forecasts`)
  fetches every requested lead (0-3) from the Open-Meteo Previous Runs API in
  one request per (station, variable), building a full per-lead Gaussian
  (mean/stdev across models) the same way the existing historical-forecast
  path does. Lead 0 is requested as `temperature_2m_previous_day0` but Open-Meteo
  normalizes the response to the un-suffixed `temperature_2m_<model>` key; this
  is handled and documented (day-0 archive values are slightly fresher than
  what the live morning run sees, so the lead-0 fit is mildly optimistic).
- `run_backfill` is reshaped to take a leads tuple and return a fitted
  `Calibration` + `Accuracy` per lead, omitting leads with no overlapping
  actuals rather than erroring. `run_backfill_accuracy` and
  `fetch_historical_point_forecasts` are retired (the reshape orphaned them).
- `_backfill` becomes a plain stations x variables loop, one `run_backfill`
  call per (station, variable), saving a calibration + accuracy row per
  returned lead. Defaults change to `--variable all` (both TMAX and TMIN) and
  `--leads 0,1,2,3`; single-variable values are still accepted. Partial-failure
  semantics are unchanged: a station-variable fetch failure prints and
  continues, all-fail exits 1.
- `.github/workflows/backfill.yml` passes `--variable all --leads 0,1,2,3`
  explicitly so the dispatch documents the grid.
- `fetch_historical_forecasts` (used by `backtest.py`), `fit_calibration`,
  `apply_calibration`, `load_calibration`, the store schema, and `edge.py`
  (owned by #225) are untouched.

No new dependencies.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run ruff check .`
- [x] `uv run mypy src`
- [x] `uv run pytest` (583 passed, 1 skipped, including the golden e2e)
- [ ] Operator step after merge: dispatch the `backfill` workflow and
      spot-check `calibration` rows cover the (station, TMAX/TMIN, lead 0-3)
      grid.

author: dormammu1997
body:
## Summary

Adds the **CPR Yearly Reversal** screener (`cpr_yearly`) — a deterministic strategy that flags potential multi-year downtrend reversals using the **yearly** Central Pivot Range (CPR).

### Logic
- **Yearly CPR** (`backend.indicators.yearly_cpr`): the CPR in effect during a year is derived from the **previous full year's** High/Low/Close — the intraday PDH/PDL pivot convention (from the source PDF) applied one timeframe up, to years. "Previous year high" is that prior year's High (the `H` term of the current year's CPR).
- **BUY** when both hold:
  1. the yearly **central pivots step strictly down** for three straight years (this < last < two-years-ago) — a structural downtrend; and
  2. a resampled **weekly close** has **recently reclaimed the previous year's high** (within `recent_cross_weeks`, default 4; latest weekly close still at/above it).
- **Universe:** `nifty_500`. **Chart:** weekly candles + the recent years' yearly CPR lines (TC/P/BC) + the previous-year-high level, via a new `backend.charts.add_cpr_overlay`.
- The app already renders the **Check Fundamentals** panel under every shortlisted chart, so no per-screener wiring is needed.

### Design decisions (confirmed with the requester)
- CPR convention = previous-year-derived (PDF PDH/PDL analog).
- "Pivot range above" = central pivot `P` comparison.
- "Recently crossed" = weekly close, last 4 weeks (tunable).

### Files
- `screeners/cpr_yearly.py`; `backend/indicators.py` (`yearly_cpr`); `backend/charts.py` (`add_cpr_overlay`).
- Tests: `tests/test_indicators.py`, `tests/test_real_screeners.py`, `tests/test_screener_golden_outputs.py` + `tests/golden/screeners/cpr_yearly.json`.
- Docs: screener catalog, indicators LLD, HLD component map (screener counts 10 → 11).

### Verification (local)
- `ruff` (CI scope) clean · `mypy` clean (113 files) · `compileall` clean.
- `pytest` green for indicators, golden snapshots (regenerated + reviewed), registry auto-discovery, and the new screener (hit / no-reclaim / uptrend / chart). Full suite + Docker gates run in hosted CI.

author: bappidas-git
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `Shadowfax` courier vendor at `Modules/Shared/Vendors/Shadowfax.php`, implementing the full `VendorParent` contract. The implementation follows the structure and conventions of the existing `Blitz` vendor, while the request/response handling is driven by the **Shadowfax Unified API** documentation and the behaviour of the legacy `Vendor_Wrapper_4` integration.

## Key design decisions

- **Authentication** — Shadowfax uses a static `Token` API key shared by their team (`Authorization: Token <token>`), so there is no token generation/refresh flow like Blitz. `getToken()` returns the configured key and `getAuthorizationHeader()` prefixes it with `Token `.
- **Order model** — the B2C forward flow (warehouse → customer, RTO back to warehouse) maps to Shadowfax's `warehouse` order model. `createForwardOrder()` posts to `/v3/clients/orders/` with `order_details`, `customer_details`, `pickup_details`, `rto_details` and `product_details`. Weights are converted to grams as the API expects.
- **Status mapping** — a `mapStatus()` helper translates Shadowfax `status_id`s (e.g. `delivered`, `ofd`, `rts`, `nc`) into the internal status codes used across the app (`DLV`, `OFD`, `RTOSR`, `UND`, …). Order-creation/intermediate noise maps to `NP` so it is not persisted as showable history.

## Methods implemented (all 14 abstract methods)

| Method | Shadowfax endpoint |
|---|---|
| `createForwardOrder` | `POST /v3/clients/orders/` (warehouse model) |
| `cancelOrder` | `POST /v3/clients/orders/cancel/` (200 = cancelled, 304 = queued → both success) |
| `trackingHistory` / `shipmentSummary` | `GET /v4/clients/orders/{awb}/track/` |
| `statusSync` | `GET /v4` tracking per waybill → `syncNormalizedStatusHistory` |
| `pincodeServiceability` | `GET /v1/clients/serviceability/` |
| `reattemptOrder` | `POST /v3/clients/order_update/` (`reopen_ndr`) |
| `getCouriers` | static courier metadata |
| `getShippingLabelData` / `rateCalculator` | not supported by the API (return graceful error) |
| `addWarehouse` / `updateWarehouse` | no-op (Shadowfax describes the warehouse inline via `unique_code`) |
| `shipOrder` | no-op (order is live on creation) |
| `registerPickup` | records pickup locally via `afterRegisterPickupWork` (auto-scheduled by Shadowfax) |

## Configuration

Reads the following env vars (staging vs production selected by `APP_ENV=local`):

- `SHADOWFAX_STAGE_BASE_URL` / `SHADOWFAX_PROD_BASE_URL` (defaults to the documented hosts)
- `SHADOWFAX_STAGE_TOKEN` / `SHADOWFAX_PROD_TOKEN`

## Notes

- `php -l` passes with no syntax errors.
- The repository was empty, so this PR targets a newly created `main` baseline branch; the diff is limited to the new `Shadowfax.php` file.

author: sedrak-hovhannisyan
body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who set `messages.visibleReplies` back to `automatic` could still get the old message-tool-only contract on later direct channel turns until the Gateway was restarted.

This was especially confusing in Telegram/Codex onboarding: `openclaw config set messages.visibleReplies automatic` could report that no Gateway restart was needed, but the next Codex turn could still expose `message(action=send)` as the source-reply path and suppress automatic final delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Visible-reply mode is a live dispatch policy, so changes to `messages.visibleReplies` and `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies` now go through the Gateway hot-reload path instead of the dynamic-read/no-op path. That refreshes the runtime config snapshot for the next dispatched turn without restarting channels or the full Gateway.

The change is intentionally scoped to the visible-reply fields; other `messages.*` settings keep their existing reload classification.

## User Impact

Operators can switch direct/source replies back to automatic delivery and have the next turn pick up the new contract. The CLI now prints the hot-reload hint for this change instead of the misleading `No gateway restart needed.` message.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` passed: 3 files, 252 tests.
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs --changed upstream/main` was also run. It failed in unrelated Windows/path and temp-file-lock tests outside this diff, including symlink permission, Windows path normalization, and SQLite temp unlink failures; no failure pointed at the changed files.

body:
## Summary
Replaces the podium-only Plackett-Luce predictor with a **dynamic Bayesian rating engine** (`dbpl-v2`): every driver and car carries a Gaussian log-worth rating filtered over all 26,049 race classification rows since 1950 plus 11,168 qualifying rows since 1994, with era-relative DNF hazards, circuit chaos character, and a Rao-Blackwellised podium simulation. The v1 model stays as fallback when the new datasets are absent.

Walk-forward evaluation (tuned on 2010-2018 only, scored once on the frozen 2019-2026 test window, 160 races):

| model | top-1 | top-3 | top-5 | logLoss | brierNew |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| recent-frequency | .125 | .269 | .362 | 4.303 | .237 |
| current (product) | .131 | .281 | .394 | 4.194 | .242 |
| plackett-luce | .131 | .269 | .394 | 4.175 | .238 |
| PL + tuned (v1 chosen) | .125 | .294 | .412 | 4.078 | .240 |
| v2 pace | .156 | .312 | .400 | 4.089 | .236 |
| v2 +attrition | .156 | .312 | .400 | 4.089 | .236 |
| v2 +chaos | .150 | .312 | .400 | 4.083 | .232 |
| **v2 full (chosen)** | **.181** | **.350** | **.438** | **3.916** | **.238** |

Acceptance gate (beat v1 on test logLoss AND brierNew) passed. Ablations: pace+reliability already beats v1, qualifying order gives the biggest jump, attrition earned zero weight (off in the tuned defaults).

## Changes
- New committed datasets: `race_results.json` (1950-2026, compact single-line storage) + `qualifying.json` (1994-2026), fetched by two new incremental fetchers wired into `update.py` (with `--full` propagation and deepened 429 backoff)
- `src/compute/model_v2.py`: closed-form truncated-PL Gaussian updates (Weng-Lin/ADF style), race/season/regulation-reset diffusion, constructor lineage across rebrands, ReliabilityTracker (Beta-shrunk decayed hazards, mech->car / incident->driver), CircuitStats (displacement temperature + DNF log-odds delta), leakage-free HistoryFilter, deterministic `predict_race` (exact conditional trio probabilities per draw; P(new) is the exact complement of seen trios, bridge-tested against the v1 closed form)
- `backtest.py`: v2 ablation ladder rungs + `--tune-v2` coordinate-descent tuner; `model_eval.json` regenerated with `chosenModel: v2 full`
- `compute_podigami.py`: v2 path (v1 fallback preserved); regenerated `podigami.json` - P(new trio next race) 51.9%, top pick Antonelli/Norris/Russell 6.84%
- datalib: schemas + compact storage for the new datasets, `PodigamiParamsV2`/`ModelParamsV2` unions, `DriverStrength.finishProb/uncertainty`, `ModelEval.chosenModel`
- Landing page FAQ + current-form copy explain the new engine; README predictor section, architecture diagram, file map and test counts updated; release notes entry added
- New integrity test: podiums.json <-> race_results.json positions 1-3 agree across all 1157 shared races (zero mismatches)

body:
`ThemeMediaStreamController` (the library-level `/stream/theme-media/{libraryId}/audio|video` endpoints) read `$_SERVER['HTTP_RANGE']`, which the Workerman daemon never repopulates per request — so every ranged request fell through to a full 200 and seeking was dead. Same class of bug as #409 fixed in the sibling `ThemeMusicStreamController`.

This mirrors #409: thread `$request->getHeader('Range')` into `streamFile()` and adopt the hardened range parser (open-ended `bytes=start-`, suffix `bytes=-N`, EOF clamp per RFC 7233, `416` for malformed/unsatisfiable). The unused `$duration` param is dropped.

Tests: 206 slice, suffix range, EOF clamp, malformed→416 for both audio and video. Full controller suite green (27 tests); PHPStan L9 + PHPCS clean.

author: takuma-shishido
body:
## 🐛 概要
`deploy.yml` のワークフロー構文エラーを修正する。PR #63 が**この修正の直前にマージ**されたため、develop 上の `deploy.yml` が無効なままになっている(push のたびに deploy が 0s 失敗)。

## 症状(GitHub)
```
Invalid workflow file: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
(Line: 38): Unrecognized named-value: 'secrets'. ... secrets.DEPLOY_HOST != ''
(Line: 46): Unrecognized named-value: 'secrets'. ...
(Line: 64): Unrecognized named-value: 'secrets'. ...
```

## 原因
`secrets` コンテキストは **step の `if:` では参照できない**(利用可能なのは `env`/`github`/`inputs`/… で `secrets` は含まれない)。旧 `deploy.yml` から引き継いだ `if: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_HOST != '' }}` が、無効化解除で push トリガーに戻したことで顕在化した。

## 修正
`DEPLOY_HOST` を **job レベルの `env:`** に移し(`secrets` は job env では使える)、各 step の `if:` は **`env.DEPLOY_HOST`** を参照する(`env` は `if:` で使える)。挙動は不変(Secrets 未登録なら Tailscale/SSH をスキップし warning)。

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy:
    env:
      DEPLOY_HOST: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_HOST }}   # job env 経由
    steps:
      - if: ${{ env.DEPLOY_HOST != '' }}        # env で分岐(secrets を if で使わない)
```

## ✅ 検証(actionlint 1.7.12)
- 修正版: **PASS**(エラーなし)
- develop 上の旧版: 上記 3 行で `context "secrets" is not allowed here` を再現(= GitHub のエラーと一致)

> マージ後、develop への push で deploy が **緑(Secrets 未登録のため skip + warning)** になることを確認予定。実 SSH デプロイは Secrets(5つ)+ Tailscale OAuth/ACL 登録後。

Refs #40

author: hannahchan
body:
## Summary

Adds a public "what is this" page at `#/about` for first-time visitors who land on the app without knowing what it is (a curious member of the public, a clinician weighing it up, or a parent sent the link). The copy is a distilled subset of the README, in the app's companion-not-curriculum voice.

The page sits **before** the grown-up gate on purpose: the gate keeps children out of caregiver data and settings, not adults out of an explanation. It is **not linked from the child screens yet** (that placement decision is still open), so today it is reachable by URL, which also makes `…/#/about` a clean, shareable "here's what this is" link that lands people directly on the explainer.

### What's here
- **New `/about` route and page** (`src/ui/About.tsx`), styled with the existing grown-up cards and added to the axe route sweep in `tests/a11y.test.tsx`.
- **A top bar** mirroring the grown-up pages (brand on the left; "Go to the app" and "Share" on the right), so the page reads as part of the same app without widening its reading column. A "Go to the app" also sits at the end for readers who finish.
- **A Share action**: opens the native share sheet on mobile (`navigator.share`), or copies the link with a "Link copied" confirmation on desktop. It sends nothing itself, staying true to the app's no-network, no-analytics stance.

### Copy and metadata tidy-ups (surfaced while building this)
- Removed the "has not been tried with children with CVI" caveat from the framing copy (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the Dashboard about card). The separate "not clinically reviewed / not a clinically validated tool" caveat stays.
- Widened the link-preview descriptions (meta, Open Graph, Twitter) from "babies" to "from babies to teens" so a shared link no longer undersells the age range, and fixed the web manifest (`light-and-song` typo, the same narrow wording, and an em dash).

## Test plan
- `npm run build` (tsc + vite) passes.
- The axe a11y sweep is green, including the new `/about` route.
- Verified in-browser on desktop and mobile (375px): the top bar wraps cleanly with no horizontal overflow, a cold load of `…/#/about` lands directly on the page, and the copy-link fallback path is wired (the native share sheet is used where available).

## Not in scope / open questions
- Whether and how to add a "door" to `/about` from the child screens (Landing/Chooser). Left unlinked deliberately for now.
- Grown-up prose pages (Guide, Dashboard) run wide (~136 characters per line); pulling them toward a readable measure is a possible separate cleanup.

author: chris-walton
body:
## Summary

The home page's credibility strip and stats cards read the `home.*` `stats_cache` keys, which are never live-aggregated (§10) and were written only by the daily 07:00 UTC cron — so a promote updated `/products` live while the home banner stayed frozen at the last cron snapshot for up to a day. A successful `POST /api/promote` now recomputes those keys post-commit via the same `runHomeStats` core, then purges a new `index:home` `Cache-Tag` so the home page repaints with the fresh counts. Ordering is load-bearing (recompute `stats_cache` first, purge `/` second), so `index:home` is deliberately excluded from the concurrent `cacheTagsForPromote` set and runs in its own ordered refresh-then-purge task; it's best-effort and post-commit, emitting the existing `aeci.stats.compute*` family under a new `trigger:promote` tag and self-healing at the next cron on failure.

Docs were updated in lockstep: `CACHE_STRATEGY.md` (`index:home` tag), `OBSERVABILITY.md` (promote trigger), `REVIEW_APP_PROMOTE_API.md` §6c, and `STAGE_1_SPEC.md` §10.

## Testing

- `pnpm --filter @aeci/web exec vitest run src/server/cache-tags.spec.ts src/server.spec.ts` — 172/172 pass

Closes AECI-305

# Phase 2 PR Summary

This is the pull-request handoff note for the Phase 2 closeout branch.

## Scope

- Closes the Phase 2 productization baseline for API, auth/session, authorization, admin operations, media governance, task workflow APIs, notifications, and quality gates.
- Keeps remaining creative/catalog simulations explicitly out of scope for Phase 2 and tracks them as Phase 3 candidates.
- Adds closeout-ready documentation for deployment validation, GitHub Environment setup, release checks, quality gates, and accepted residual items.

## Notable Changes

- Adds and wires the API server, Prisma-backed repository option, OpenAPI route inventory, permission matrix checks, production smoke profiles, and GitHub quality-gate workflow.
- Hardens auth with email login/registration, OAuth provider metadata and dev callbacks, JWT access tokens, refresh rotation, HttpOnly refresh-cookie mode, CSRF/trusted-origin checks, session management, and account-link controls.
- Updates frontend auth UX with session-verified success states, provider status badges, field-level validation, API error mapping, production-hidden local test shortcuts, logout handling, and registered-user profile mapping.
- Expands product workflow coverage for tasks, proposals, submissions, media uploads/scanning, points escrow/settlement, notifications, admin audit, finance, permissions, security alerts, and operations metrics.
- Adds E2E coverage for email auth, dev OAuth, admin permissions, and the proposal-to-submission-to-review workflow.

## Verification Plan

Run before merge:

```bash
npm run check:deploy
```

Run after deployment secrets and environment variables are configured:

```bash
npm run check:deploy:env
```

## Accepted Residual Items

- Real GitHub Environment validation still needs deployment-owned secrets and variables.
- Real OAuth, scanner, object storage, and alert delivery integrations need staging/prod smoke validation outside fixture mode.
- Prometheus/OpenTelemetry exporters and shared rate-limit storage are deferred unless the target deployment requires them.
- Creative/catalog demo flows remain Phase 3 scope.
- Full OpenAPI response schemas are deferred to external-integration hardening.

## Reviewer Notes

- Treat this branch as a closeout package, not a feature-expansion branch.
- Prefer blocker fixes only: quality-gate failures, deployment-readiness gaps, documentation drift, or security/auth correctness issues.
- Do not merge Phase 3 work into this branch.

author: andremmartins
body:
## Problem

`findFreeProfilePort` (`src/lib/browser/profiles.ts`) probed candidate ports by shelling out to `lsof`, which doesn't exist on Windows. The ENOENT was swallowed by the assume-free catch, so **every** port in 9222-9399 scanned as free. The first `agents browser profiles create <name>` without `--endpoint` was assigned `cdp://127.0.0.1:9222` — and when the user's own browser was already listening there (Comet/Chrome running with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`), the new profile silently **attached** to that browser instead of launching its own sandboxed instance. Tabs then opened in whatever profile the user had on screen, not the automation profile.

Found while debugging exactly this on a Windows machine: an `idealista` profile that kept driving the user's open daily-driver Comet profile.

## Fix

- Export `isPortInUse` from `chrome.ts` — the platform-aware probe the launcher already used (`lsof` on POSIX, `netstat -ano` on Windows) — and route `findFreeProfilePort`'s scan through it, replacing the inline `lsof` call.
- `profiles.test.ts`: mock the `isPortInUse` seam instead of `execFileSync`-with-lsof-semantics, so the tests no longer encode POSIX-only behavior.
- `chrome.test.ts`: new regression test that binds a **real** TCP socket (no mocks) and asserts `isPortInUse` sees it and its release — so CI exercises the netstat path on the `windows-latest` legs and the lsof path on POSIX.

## Evidence

Unit tests (Windows, worktree):

```
Test Files  15 passed (15)
     Tests  226 passed | 8 skipped (234)
```

`tsc --noEmit` exit 0.

Real-flow probe on the affected Windows machine (Comet live on 9222 with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`, `idealista` profile claiming 9223 in agents.yaml):

```
isPortInUse(9222) [Comet live here]: true
isPortInUse(9399) [nothing here]:    false
findFreeProfilePort():               9224
```

Old behavior on the same machine: `findFreeProfilePort()` returned 9222 (the port the running Comet holds), which is how the silent-attach bug reproduced.

author: lu-zero
body:
## Problem

Once a script `declare -a`s or plain-array-assigns a dynamic well-known variable such as `PIPESTATUS`, brush **never updates it again** on later pipelines in that shell — it stays frozen at whatever was last assigned. Real bash keeps the variable live and refreshes it on every pipeline.

Minimal repro:

```bash
declare -a PIPESTATUS=([0]="1")
true | true | true
echo "${PIPESTATUS[@]}"
```

- **bash**: `0 0 0`
- **brush** (current `origin/main`): `1` (frozen)

Same freeze happens with a plain array assignment (no `declare`):

```bash
PIPESTATUS=([0]="9")
true | false | true
echo "${PIPESTATUS[@]}"
```

- **bash**: `0 1 0`
- **brush**: `9`

## Root cause

`PIPESTATUS` (and other dynamic well-known variables: `RANDOM`, `SECONDS`, `FUNCNAME`, `BASH_LINENO`, `BASH_SOURCE`, `BASH_ALIASES`, …) are backed by a `ShellValue::Dynamic { getter, setter }` whose `getter` is consulted on every read and whose `setter` is a no-op (`|_| ()`) for all of them.

Two write paths in `brush-core/src/variables.rs` unconditionally overwrote `self.value` with a static array, discarding the `Dynamic` binding and permanently freezing the variable:

1. **`convert_to_indexed_array`** — the `_` arm hit for `Dynamic` values and replaced `self.value`. Triggered by `declare -a VAR=(...)` via `brush-builtins/src/declare.rs`.
2. **`assign`** (non-append Array-literal arm) — explicitly matched `ShellValue::Dynamic { .. }` in the overwrite set. Triggered by a plain `VAR=([0]="...")` assignment.

From that point on the getter closure was gone, so the variable stopped refreshing for the rest of the shell's life.

## Fix

- `convert_to_indexed_array`: add an explicit `ShellValue::Dynamic { .. } => Ok(())` arm so the binding survives.
- `assign`: drop `ShellValue::Dynamic { .. }` from the overwrite set; the existing `(ShellValue::Dynamic { .. }, _) => Ok(())` arm below now handles it correctly.

### `convert_to_associative_array` intentionally unchanged

`convert_to_associative_array` has the same overwrite pattern, but real bash is asymmetric here: `declare -A PIPESTATUS=([x]="9")` **does** permanently freeze it in bash itself (PIPESTATUS becomes a plain associative array that pipelines don't refresh). Pre-fix brush already matched bash's `-A` behavior, so changing it would diverge from bash compat.

## Verification

All four behavioral cases now match bash:

| op | bash | brush (after) |
|---|---|---|
| `declare -a` then pipe | `0 0 0` | `0 0 0` ✓ |
| `declare -A` then pipe | `9` | `9` ✓ |
| plain `=([0]="9")` then pipe | `0 1 0` | `0 1 0` ✓ |
| plain pipe | `0 0 0` | `0 0 0` ✓ |

Adds three compat test cases under `brush-shell/tests/cases/compat/well_known_vars.yaml` (`declare -a`, plain array assign, `declare -A`). `cargo fmt --check` clean.

This surfaced in the wild: a worker-env dump/restore mechanism restored a `declare -a PIPESTATUS=([0]="1")` line and a downstream `pipestatus || die` check fired incorrectly, misreporting a successful pipeline as failed.

author: yashbhalodi
body:
Closes #259.

Ships **relationship resolution** — the two-anchor question of the kinship query engine (PRD 0005, epic #253): given persons `x` and `y`, return *all* the ways they are related, each a terminology-neutral descriptor, with **honest emptiness**. `kul query rel <x> <y>` works end-to-end.

## What's here

**Core (`resolve(x, y, config)`)** — a separate two-anchor entry point on the query seam that **reuses the kin-set traversal engine and descriptor derivation, no forked logic**:
- `AffinalWalk` is generalized with a per-segment cap and a pluggable emit-gate, so kin-set queries and resolution share one walk (kin-set behaviour and snapshots unchanged).
- Enumerates every simple path within the per-blood-segment generation budget (`maxApexGenerations`, default 5), *plus* an **unbounded pure-lineal detection** so a direct-line tie is never hidden by the cap.
- `x == y` → a single `self` descriptor (empty path).
- **Honest emptiness**: returns a result object with `disconnected` vs `noneWithinBounds` (present iff empty), computed via full-relation-graph connectivity.
- The 2-affinal-hop ceiling stays fixed semantics; only the generation budget is a knob (the semantics-vs-budget line).
- Typed `UnknownPerson` error for a bad/wrong-kind id at either anchor — never an empty result.

**WASM** — `queryResolve(files, manifest, xId, yId, config?)` → `QueryEnvelope<ResolveResult>`; committed TS types (`ResolveResult`, `ResolveConfig`, `EmptyReason`) refreshed.

**CLI** — `kul query rel <x> <y> [--max-generations N] [--format human|json]`. Terminology-neutral human output (descriptor facts + hop-by-hop path with ids/display names, marriage status on `across` hops), empty-reason wording, exit 0 for empty results, nonzero for bad ids. `--format json` byte-identical to WASM.

**Docs** — ADR-0028 (NCA bounding, unbounded lineal, semantics-vs-budget); CONTEXT.md gains *relationship resolution*, *emptiness reason*, *generation budget*, *semantics-vs-budget line*.

## Tests

Core-seam insta snapshots (self, disconnected, none-within-bounds, unknown id) + targeted fixtures: per-segment cap vs unbounded lineal, cousin-marriage (spouse **and** cousin descriptor), adoption-into-relatives, double cousins, step subsumption, deterministic ordering, and a shared-engine equivalence check (resolution's blood tie == the kin-set descriptor). WASM + CLI wiring/serialization tests. `just check` green (800 tests).

body:
## 무엇을 변경했나요?

- `/self-quote`의 기존 슬롯 보드 UI를 메인보드형 구성 관계도 화면으로 보강했습니다.
- 슬롯 보드에 메인보드 배경, 의존성 연결선, 연결/비연결 범례, 부품 이미지, 부품 요약 스펙을 표시하도록 개선했습니다.
- 셀프 견적 상단에 총액, 장착 슬롯 수, 호환 상태, 스토리지 요약을 보여주는 상태 영역을 추가했습니다.
- 빈 슬롯은 placeholder 상태로 표시하고, 선택된 슬롯은 실제 장착 부품 중심으로 읽히도록 구성했습니다.
- 홈에서 부품 카테고리로 진입했을 때 슬롯 후보 패널이 열리는 흐름을 새 슬롯 보드 구조 기준으로 갱신했습니다.

## 왜 변경했나요?

기존 `/self-quote` 화면은 부품 카드가 단순 배치되어 있어 목표 UI처럼 “어떤 부품이 어떤 슬롯/전원/규격 관계로 연결되는지”를 한눈에 파악하기 어려웠습니다.

이번 변경은 셀프 견적 화면을 단순 목록이 아니라 메인보드 기반 구성 관계도처럼 보이게 만들어, 사용자가 CPU, RAM, GPU, SSD, PSU, 케이스, 쿨러의 장착 관계와 호환 상태를 더 직관적으로 확인할 수 있도록 하기 위한 작업입니다.

## 주요 변경 파일

- `apps/web/src/features/parts/components/slot-board/SlotBoard.tsx`
  - 메인보드형 배경, 슬롯 배치, 연결선, 부품 이미지, 스펙 요약, 연결 라벨 표시를 추가했습니다.

- `apps/web/src/features/parts/components/slot-board/SlotStatusBar.tsx`
  - 총액, 장착 슬롯, 호환 상태, 스토리지 요약을 보여주는 상태 바를 구성했습니다.

- `apps/web/src/features/parts/components/slot-board/slotBoardConfig.ts`
  - 목표 UI에 맞게 CPU/RAM/GPU/SSD/PSU/CASE/COOLER 슬롯 좌표와 기본 fallback edge를 조정했습니다.

- `apps/web/src/features/parts/pages/SelfQuotePage.tsx`
  - 셀프 견적 페이지를 새 슬롯 보드 중심 흐름으로 연결하고, 미선택 슬롯/후보 패널/요약 상태를 함께 표시하도록 정리했습니다.

- `apps/web/tests/self-quote.spec.ts`
  - 메인보드형 구성 관계도 렌더링, 부품 이미지 표시, edge label 표시, 홈 카테고리 진입 흐름을 검증하도록 테스트를 갱신했습니다.

## 충돌 해결 근거

- `apps/web/src/index.css`
  - 충돌 원인: 이 브랜치의 슬롯 보드 애니메이션 CSS와 `origin/main`의 홈 fullpage 레이아웃 CSS가 같은 전역 CSS 파일에 추가되어 충돌했습니다.
  - 해결 근거: 두 스타일은 서로 다른 화면을 대상으로 합니다. 슬롯 보드의 `slot-attach-flash`, `slot-empty-pulse`, `slot-panel-in`은 `/self-quote` 상호작용에 필요하고, `home-fullpage-shell` 계열 스타일은 `origin/main`의 홈 화면 변경에 필요하므로 둘 다 유지했습니다.

- `apps/web/tests/self-quote.spec.ts`
  - 충돌 원인: 이 브랜치는 새 슬롯 보드 selector와 후보 패널 구조를 테스트하고 있었고, `origin/main`은 AI 챗봇이 현재 draft를 서버에 전달하되 quote draft를 자동 변경하지 않는 정책으로 테스트를 바꿨습니다.
  - 해결 근거: 최신 main 정책을 따라 챗봇 테스트는 `currentQuoteDraft` 전송과 draft 비변경을 검증하도록 유지했습니다. 동시에 슬롯 보드 구조 변경에 맞춰 GPU/쿨러 후보 패널 테스트는 `slot-*` test id와 실제 접근성 이름 기준으로 갱신했습니다.
  - 추가로 `쿨러` 버튼 selector가 여러 요소와 겹쳐 strict mode 실패가 발생해, 실제 슬롯 버튼 이름인 `쿨러 슬롯 열기`로 좁혔습니다.
