author: mariuszkreft
body:
Implements the MVP of [proposals/continual-harness-factory-evolver.md](https://github.com/machine-machine/herdr-factory-loop-skill/blob/proposal/continual-harness-evolver/proposals/continual-harness-factory-evolver.md) — the factory-evolver layer that turns real herd run telemetry into structured, reviewable improvements to future herds.

## What's in

- **Trace capture** (`scripts/m2herd-up.sh`): `dispatch`/`collect` now write `.m2herd/runs/<run-id>/` bundles — `run.json`, per-slice `prompt.md`/`report.md`/`status.json` (+ optional `failures.json`). Run-id `r-<UTC ts>`; rotation = delete `runs/CURRENT`. All trace writes are non-fatal telemetry.
- **Evolver engine** (`scripts/m2herd.sh`): `m2herd evolve analyze|proposals|show|apply|reject`. `analyze` is mechanical (no LLM, `next`-doctrine) — boring signatures (failed slice, missing report/status, `failures.json` passthrough) become frontmatter'd proposal files under `.m2herd/evolver/proposals/`, idempotently. `apply` follows the conservative ladder: memory/policy → append-once lesson to `LESSONS.md`; template → `.m2herd/`-only; repo targets are NEVER auto-edited (patch/branch recommendation, `--ack-repo` to acknowledge).
- **Factory feedback**: `m2herd resume` shows `Recent factory lessons:`; dispatch's worker pointer gains an "also read LESSONS.md" sentence — accepted lessons reach the next herd without the orchestrator remembering them.
- **Docs/templates**: `templates/m2herd/{evolver,runs}/` seeds (wired into `init`), `CONTRACT-m2herd.md` amendment documenting the full trace/proposal contract. `skill/SKILL.md` deliberately untouched until the commands are released (per the proposal).

## How it was built

This PR was itself produced by an m2herd loop: 3 file-disjoint headless claude/sonnet slices off `main` against one orchestrator-authored file contract, merged conflict-free, then selftest + lint + live end-to-end smoke + an adversarial sonnet review (1 P1, 2 P2, 1 P3 — all fixed here, see the review-fixes commit).

## Verified

- `bash scripts/m2herd.sh selftest` → PASS (extended with a full evolve cycle: fabricated failed run → analyze → apply/reject → lesson surfacing)
- `bash scripts/lint.sh` → clean
- Live smoke: init-seeded fabric → dry-run dispatch trace plan → real analyze/apply → `resume` lessons → pointer injection
- Idempotency: triple `evolve analyze` re-run → 0 new proposals

## Deferred (recorded in the proposal's open questions)

- Lessons graduating to fleet memory (AMS) — per-repo only for now; `gist --push` remains the bridge.
- `evolve apply` opening branches for repo-level changes — never automatic in this MVP.

author: aliahdab2
body:
## Problem

Replies read robotic: consecutive DM replies ending with the same conditional-offer closing ("إذا حابة تفاصيل خبريني" / "فيني أساعدك" / "let me know if…") — 5 of 9 replies in a real thread (2026-07-05, الفريق الدمشقي, customer Dalal). Fleet-wide this closing tic was the most common "bot tell."

## Root cause (measured, not guessed)

The prompt was **contradicting itself** — it banned the closing while three things taught it. Verified on a verbatim prod-thread replica (eval Cat 61 #677, real ~12.7k KB, prod temperature):

1. GENERAL RESPONSE RULES said "sometimes ask a question back" right beside the offer-closing ban.
2. The `enthusiastic` style directive said "ask back naturally when more info would help" — a positive license the model followed over the negative ban.
3. No few-shot example demonstrated a clean flat ending, so the model had no positive pattern for the common case.

With the model's RLHF prior + self-imitation (a leaked closing in the 12-turn history becomes a demonstration and compounds), the tic hit **56.7% (17/30)** on the worst case.

## Fix — at the source (no post-filtering)

Three changes, all in the cacheable `STATIC_SYSTEM_PREFIX` / styleMap:
1. Reword the "ask a question back" rule → only-when-genuinely-needed, never a filler "anything else?".
2. Drop the enthusiastic directive's "ask back naturally" license; align it with the disciplined `professional` phrasing.
3. Add two clean-ending few-shot examples (warm mid-thread answer + info-not-in-KB answer), written in **light MSA and explicitly labelled "mirror the customer's dialect, don't copy this MSA"** so no dialect gets parroted.

`PROMPT_VERSION` v51→v52 (prefix bytes change → cache invalidated; flush caches on deploy).

**A deterministic post-filter ("Check 7") was prototyped, measured (0/30), and removed** — the source fix made it redundant, per the "proper fix, not a band-aid" direction. Recorded as DECISIONS.md **D-019** (parallels D-006: prompt-only stale-date defense).

## Measured effect

- Worst-case replica (#677, history seeded with 3 tic-closings, prod temperature): **56.7% (17/30) → 1.7% (1/60)**. Residual = the model's irreducible RLHF floor.
- Full eval, temp 0: **96.8%** (in the normal 96.5–97.1% band).
- **Cat 61** (new persona goal-timing & variety category, 13 cases incl. verbatim prod replicas): 13/13 at temp 0, 3/3 across three prod-temperature runs.
- Guardrails intact: Cat 37 No-Bot-Closings 8/8, Cat 38 hedging 3/3, Cat 42/44 clean, **Cat 23 #157 first-turn "invite to visit" still passes** (fix does NOT suppress legitimate merchant invitations). The lone recurring soft partial (#158 "don't repeat the free-trial line") is pre-existing — partial on pristine v51 too.

## ⚠️ Blast radius (shared prompt infra) — justification

`STATIC_SYSTEM_PREFIX` + styleMap affect **every merchant, every language**. Safety case:
- The full 379-case eval (fashion/electronics/clinic/school pages, English + Arabic cases) holds in-band at 96.8% with no guardrail regression — that is the cross-vertical/cross-language coverage.
- Changes are minimal and additive: two rewordings that *remove* a contradiction, and two demonstrations. No behavior was added that the ban didn't already intend.
- The new examples are dialect-neutral MSA and explicitly marked not-to-copy, so no vertical/dialect is nudged.
- Residual risk is subjective "warmth," which no automated eval measures; mitigated by the small, well-scoped delta and the post-deploy watch below.

## Tests

- ai-worker: 423 pass; validator unit suite 44 pass; lint clean.
- Full eval 96.8% at temp 0; Cat 61 3× at prod temp all-pass; 30-call #677 A/B → 1.7%.

## Post-deploy checklist

- Flush the semantic AI cache (v52 bump orphans the exact cache only).
- Confirm v52 live.
- Watch the fleet closing-repetition SQL scan over ~1 week; الفريق الدمشقي should drop to fleet-normal, **Nourva unchanged** (his contact-ask is intentional, flow-driven).

author: bkizer1
body:
## Problem

`npm run dev` crashed on launch before the window opened:

```
UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: ReferenceError: __dirname is not defined
    at preloadPath (…/out/main/index.js:103:20)
    at createMainWindow (…/out/main/index.js:114:19)
```

The root `package.json` is `"type": "module"`, so electron-vite emits `out/main/index.js` as ESM. ESM has no `__dirname` global, so the first `path.join(__dirname, …)` in `preloadPath()` threw and the app never got a window. The preload bundles were already defended against this (forced to `.cjs`), but the main bundle had no `__dirname` shim.

## Fix

Derive `__dirname` from `import.meta.url` at the top of `src/main/window.ts` — electron-vite's recommended pattern for ESM main processes. This keeps the main process as ESM (consistent with `"type": "module"`, the renderer, and the rest of the project) instead of forcing it back to CommonJS.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — passes
- `npx electron-vite build` — succeeds
- In the built bundle, all three former crash sites (`../preload/index.cjs`, `../preload/webview/inspector.cjs`, `../renderer/index.html`) resolve against the defined constant
- Full sweep of the built bundle found no remaining undefined CJS globals (`__dirname`, `__filename`, bare `require(`)

author: jakehildreth
body:
## Problem
PowerShell files in the repo used mixed encodings (UTF-16 LE, UTF-8 no BOM, UTF-8 with BOM). This creates cross-platform friction because Windows PowerShell 5.1 defaults to UTF-16 and can misread UTF-8 without BOM when non-ASCII characters are present.

## Solution
- Add `Build/Set-PSFileEncoding.ps1` to re-encode PowerShell files to UTF-8 with BOM.
- Add tracked `.githooks/pre-commit` hook that re-encodes staged `.ps1`, `.psm1`, and `.psd1` files before commit.
- Add `Build/Install-GitHooks.ps1` so contributors can install tracked hooks locally.
- Re-encode all 200 existing PowerShell files to UTF-8 with BOM.

## Files Changed
- Build/Install-GitHooks.ps1 (new)
- Build/Set-PSFileEncoding.ps1 (new)
- .githooks/pre-commit (new)
- 200 existing .ps1/.psm1/.psd1 files (encoding only)

## Usage
After cloning, run:
```powershell
Install-GitHooks.ps1
```

## Testing
* Hook script runs without errors on staged files.
* Re-encoded files import correctly in PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.

author: homesignalg
body:
## Problem

The live `sitemap.xml` was serving **18** development ZIP URLs while `main` already had **136** (the full modeled-Utah dev-tracker build). The 136-URL sitemap was correctly committed by the daily regen (`1debb20`) but never published.

Root cause: GitHub Pages here is classic **"deploy from a branch"**, whose internal `pages-build-deployment` is suppressed by `[skip ci]`. The regen commit carried `[skip ci]`, so when it landed as the branch tip it wrote the new sitemap but never rebuilt Pages. The earlier 18-URL sitemap only went live because a *later normal commit* happened to rebuild Pages — there was no such commit after `1debb20`.

## Fix

Drop `[skip ci]` from the sitemap regen commit message. The `verify-communities` / `verify-development` workflows are path-scoped to source files (not `sitemap.xml`), so a plain commit rebuilds Pages **without** triggering them — which is exactly the intended "commits sitemap.xml back to main (which republishes GitHub Pages)" behavior.

Merging this PR is itself a normal commit to `main`, so it republishes Pages with the current 136-URL sitemap.

author: szymonrychu-bot
body:
## Why

Issue #240 was a ~3.5h outage of the tatara-memory API. Root cause (from the filed investigation): the `mem-tatara-pg` CloudNativePG cluster accumulated WAL until its volume filled. The trigger was a lagging/stuck standby holding a replication slot open, which forces the primary to retain WAL indefinitely. A full WAL volume makes the primary unable to write WAL, so cnpg marks it unhealthy and initiates a failover - but every candidate standby's volume was equally full, so the failover thrashed for ~3.5h with no writable primary, and the memory API `/readyz` stayed NotReady the whole time. Recovery came only from a manual PVC resize.

Issue #238 (PR #241, already on main) added the complementary pieces: a dedicated `walStorage` volume and a `PGPodMonitor`. This PR adds the missing safeguard against the actual trigger: an upper bound on slot-forced WAL retention.

## What

Set the PostgreSQL parameter `max_slot_wal_keep_size` on the per-Project cnpg `Cluster` spec (`internal/memory/pg.go`), derived as half the dedicated WAL volume via a new helper `pgMaxSlotWalKeepSize` (`internal/memory/memory.go`). Once a replication slot's retained WAL exceeds this cap, PostgreSQL invalidates the slot - the affected standby must re-sync - instead of pinning WAL until the disk fills. This converts a cluster-fatal disk-full into a bounded, self-healing single-replica degradation. Half the WAL volume leaves headroom for active/checkpoint WAL and any archive backlog, and the value scales with `spec.memory.pgWalStorage` overrides (1024MB at the 2Gi default, 5120MB at 10Gi).

## Verification

- `go build ./...` - passes
- `go test ./internal/memory/...` - passes (added assertions for default 1024MB and 10Gi override 5120MB)
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/memory/...` - 0 issues

## Delivered
- `internal/memory/memory.go`: new `pgMaxSlotWalKeepSize(p)` helper deriving `max_slot_wal_keep_size` as half the dedicated WAL volume (parses the WAL size via k8s resource.Quantity, clamps to >=1MB, falls back to the 2Gi default on parse error). Added `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource` import.
- `internal/memory/pg.go`: set `Spec.PostgresConfiguration.Parameters["max_slot_wal_keep_size"]` on the cnpg Cluster, with a comment tracing the issue #240 causal chain.
- `internal/memory/pg_test.go`: assert the parameter is 1024MB at the 2Gi default and 5120MB with a 10Gi PgWalStorage override.

body:
Second of the sequential PRs. Base `main` (already merged main in, so this carries PR #4's resume/version/contact too). Version bumped `0.3.0 → 0.4.0`.

## Part A — tuning (`tune: presence feel`)
Applied the agreed values: cursor spring `0.14/0.66` (lazier, softer overshoot), morph label disc `80px`, morph transition `0.15s`, magnet `8px/52px`, hover-tick gain `0.02`, click blip `600 Hz`.

## Part B1 — liquid droplet cursor (ships regardless)
The follower dot behaves like a droplet: **velocity squash-and-stretch** (scaleX up to 1.8, scaleY = 1/scaleX so area is preserved), rotates to the movement angle, springs back to a circle at rest; **elastic overshoot** (1.08→1.0) on morph transitions; a **trailing tail dot** at ~60% spring speed (opacity 0.35, hidden when morphed). Transform-only, same gating as the cursor (`pointer: fine` + motion allowed).

## Part B2 — the fluid field (T3 desktop only) — **KEPT, gates passed**
A GPU stable-fluids sim (128² ping-pong FBOs: advect → splat → divergence → Jacobi pressure → gradient-subtract → advect dye) run as the **last** postprocessing pass. It offsets the scene texture's UVs by the velocity field (clamped ≤8px) and adds faint `--signal` dye (≤0.12 additive, after Bloom so it never flares).

**Measured on real T3 hardware — both kill-gates pass with wide margin:**

| Gate | Budget | Measured | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frame time | ≤ ~12 ms | **~7.2 ms** (138 fps while stirring) | ✅ |
| Lazy chunk (gz) | ≤ 25 KB | **2.3 KB** | ✅ |
| GPU memory | — | 7.5 MB | negligible |
| LCP / CLS / INP | 2.0s / 0.05 / good | 0.63s / 0.00 / 56ms | ✅ (§7) |

- **DOM-first preserved by construction:** the fluid distorts *only* the `aria-hidden` WebGL canvas; the DOM/text layer sits above it, verified pixel-crisp (constant-tint test tinted the whole canvas while the headline stayed sharp).
- **T3 + fine-pointer + motion only**, loaded via a dedicated dynamic import — T2/mobile/reduced-motion/no-WebGL/`?fallback=1` never download it. Sim steps only while the pointer moved in the last 2s; idle is free. (ADR-008)
- Integration notes for future me: a custom postprocessing effect needs `wrapEffect`, and the `EffectComposer` must be **keyed** so it rebuilds when the lazy pass arrives.

## Budget
First-load JS unchanged by 2.6b — B1 is a few lines of transform math on the existing cursor; B2's only marginal cost is its **2.3 KB gz** dynamic chunk (T3 only). (Next 16 switched builds to Turbopack, which dropped the printed size table — first-load is the shared framework chunk, untouched here.)

Defaults are deliberately subtle. `STRENGTH` / `DYE_STRENGTH` ([FluidField.tsx](src/scenes/pipeline/fluid/FluidField.tsx)) and `velDissipation`/`dyeDissipation`/`forceScale`/`ITERATIONS` ([FluidSim.ts](src/scenes/pipeline/fluid/FluidSim.ts)) — say the word to push strength/trail length.

author: hannahchan
body:
## Why

Family feedback: the sound is distracting, music and feedback blur together, Raindrop's plink trails the picture, and left/right is hard to tell apart even on earphones. This PR began as the docs-only sound review; it now carries the full redesign that review recommended, validated, implemented, machine-reviewed, and verified.

## The review doc, validated then retired

Every load-bearing figure in `sound-design-review.md` was checked against the code and held up (14/30 lessons masking feedback in the bed's own voice, 8/30 percussive beds, the ~1.4 s late plink, the coin-flip pitch, no ducking). With the fixes landed the diagnostic went stale, so it is deleted; `docs/sound-design.md` records the durable model and where each rule is enforced, and the feedback log marks the S2 finding fixed with commit refs.

## The implemented model

Grounded in two perceptual facts: for a child with CVI, looking and listening compete (PR-11), so sound must be sparse, meaningful, predictable, and synchronous; and for any listener, sounds sharing timbre and register fuse into one stream, so feedback must own its voice rather than be played louder.

1. **Feedback speaks a reserved `glass` voice** no melody may use; every cue is deterministic data (`CUES` in `engine/audio.ts`).
2. **The bed steps back ~10 dB under every cue and voice label** via a dedicated bed bus, recovering smoothly.
3. **No reward-motif or percussive beds**: the `chime`/`plinks` bed melodies are gone, `musicBox` is recomposed as a flowing pentatonic line, and Raindrop gets a soft descending `rainfall`.
4. **Contingency lessons are bedless** (Magic Touch, Keep the Light Singing, Reach for the Light): the answer is the only sound, so "I made that happen" is unmistakable.
5. **Find/search lessons bind their quiet preference**: with sound set to "with the visual" they play the after-a-look way (quiet search, sound as the answer), and every surface tells the truth about it (player hint, Library card, Settings, printed/copied summaries, the walk-through page).
6. **Raindrop's plink and ripple fire at apparent touchdown** (92% of the eased fall), so ear and eye agree.
7. **Left and right are plain stereo and committed**: the HRTF path is removed (headphone technique; the stated hardware is speakers), the two-character listening cues stage at ±0.9, hearing-first calls pass unscaled, the pan cache quantizes in eighths, hearing-first beds skip the elevation lowpass, the volume slider gets a perceptual taper, and Settings gains a "left, then right" speaker check.

## Verification

- 329 unit tests pass; the new `tests/audio-cues.test.ts` makes the model build-breaking (glass reservation, attack floors ≥ 30 ms, beds must carry a real melodic line in every band, the bedless set, quiet binding, staging widths).
- No safety constant touched; the safety suite and payload budgets pass; all sound remains synthesized (CR-2/TR-3).
- Two independent review agents (correctness and domain/copy) audited the diff; all seven findings are fixed in the follow-up commits.
- Live-browser checks: quiet-binding hint on Find the Star, unchanged pairing on Gentle Glow, the speaker-check button cycle, and Traveling Song's filterless panned bed, all with a clean console.

## Still open for clinical eyes

Review-packet question 10 now asks about the implemented behavior: should quiet go further and become the app-wide default, and should a caregiver be able to force music over a search? `soundFollowsTarget` stays off by default, and the global sound mode stays "with".

author: yysskk
body:
## Summary

Adds NIP-45 `COUNT` across the stack — clients can ask a relay how many events match a set of filters without downloading them.

- **Wire messages** (`Sources/NostrCore/Models/RelayMessage.swift`): `ClientMessage.count(subscriptionId:filters:)` serializes to `["COUNT", <subid>, <filters…>]`; `RelayMessage.count(subscriptionId:count:approximate:)` parses `["COUNT", <subid>, {"count": n, "approximate": bool?}]` (extra payload keys such as `hll` are ignored).
- **`EventCount`** value type carrying the count and the approximate flag.
- **`RelayConnection.count(filters:timeout:)`** correlates the reply by a generated one-shot subscription id (`count-…`). It is never tracked for reconnect replay, is failed with `.notConnected` on teardown, and fails fast with `.relayError` if the relay answers `CLOSED` (relays without NIP-45 usually never reply, so the call times out cleanly).
- **`RelayPool.count(filters:to:timeout:)`** fans out and returns `[URL: EventCount]`, tolerating partial failures.
- **`NostrClient.count(filters:timeout:)`** returns the maximum reported count across relays (each relay's count is a lower bound).

COUNT responses also flow to `messages()` consumers, consistent with the raw-firehose semantics of that stream.

Note: the new `ClientMessage`/`RelayMessage` enum cases are additive but a source break for downstream code that switches exhaustively over these public enums — an accepted minor-version change (both enums already document an `.unknown`/default posture).

Spec: https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/45.md

author: naseem77
body:
## Problem

Schema discovery gathered example values **only for entity (node) attributes**. Relationship attributes were discovered with their property *names* but **no sample values**.

As a result, the model saw that a `RELATES` edge has a `rel_type` property, but never saw that its values are things like `MARRIED_TO`, `PARENT_OF`, `ALIAS`. Blind to those values, it fell back to fragile free-text matching — e.g. asking "who is X's wife?" produced `WHERE r.fact CONTAINS 'wife'`, which matched nothing because the stored text says *"married to"*. The answer came back empty even though the data was present.

## Fix

Generalize `collect_example_values` with an `is_relationship` flag that swaps the node pattern `MATCH (n:Label)` for the edge pattern `MATCH ()-[n:Label]->()`, and call it from `collect_relationship_attributes` so edges surface example values just like nodes.

## Verification (live, on a GraphRAG-style graph)

Discovered schema now includes relationship example values:
```
RELATES | rel_type => ["EVENT_OCCURRED_ON", "DEPARTED_FROM", "LOCATED_NEAR", ...]
```

End-to-end, "Who is Samuel Whitford's wife?":
- **Before:** `... WHERE r.fact CONTAINS 'wife' ...` → no result → "couldn't find the wife"
- **After:** `MATCH (p:Person {name:'Samuel Whitford'})-[:RELATES]->(w:Person) RETURN w.name` → **"Eleanor Whitford"**

## Checks
- `cargo build --release` ✅
- `cargo clippy --lib -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -D warnings` ✅

## #80 — intensifying border only wrapped the lower part
`bc-pulse` animated an **inset** box-shadow on the `.bc-battle` section, but `.bc-battle__header` has a near-opaque `background: var(--bc-header)` that painted over the ring along the top edge — so the red border appeared to hug only the body.

author: kevinnio
body:
Closes #6156

## Description

Implements a Windows taskbar jump list for Tab Configs. The user's saved Tab Configs are now pinned to Warp's taskbar jump list under a "Tab Configs" category, with one static "New Window" task above it. Clicking an entry opens the config via the existing `<scheme>://tab_config/<stem>` deeplink; clicking "New Window" uses the existing `<scheme>://action/new_window?path=~` deeplink.

The jump list is populated by a new `JumpListManager` singleton entity that subscribes to `WarpConfigUpdateEvent::TabConfigs`. A feature flag `WindowsJumpList` gates the code; when disabled after a previous enabled run, any previously committed custom destinations/tasks are cleared from the jump list so stale entries don't persist.

## Testing

Manual testing was performed on Windows with the flag enabled:

- Saved a Tab Config, pinned Warp to the taskbar, right-clicked, and confirmed "New Window" and the "Tab Configs" category/entry appear; clicked each and verified behavior.
- Quit Warp and clicked each entry from the jump list; confirmed cold-start opens the correct window with exactly one tab (the config).
- Added/deleted a `*.toml` while Warp ran; confirmed the jump list updates without restart.
- With the flag disabled after a previous enabled run, confirmed any previously committed custom tasks/categories are cleared from the jump list.
- For a parametrized Tab Config, confirmed the params modal appears on jump list click (matching the `+` menu behavior).
- Removed a Tab Config from the jump list via the Windows UI, then triggered a refresh; confirmed the removed entry stays removed.
- Verified the first window paints before the jump list commit finishes; a failed refresh does not block startup or surface an error UI.

### Videos

1. **Cold-start via jump list entry.** Record clicking a Tab Config entry from the taskbar jump list while Warp is fully closed; confirm exactly one window opens with exactly one tab (the config).

   https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4261382f-769c-409a-9744-ebb466400609

2. **Live refresh on save/delete.** While Warp runs, save a new `*.toml` in `~/.warp/tab_configs/`, then right-click the taskbar and confirm the entry appears without restart. Then delete it and confirm it disappears from the jump list after a few seconds.

   https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/183ac365-017a-428a-812b-0efdd06c1829

3. **Flag-disabled cleanup.** Disable the flag, relaunch Warp; confirm the custom destinations/tasks are cleared from the jump list.

   https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19f7d911-1948-48a6-b998-f8ab9f194e18

---

## Caveats and deviations from the spec

The implementation follows the tech spec (`specs/GH6156/tech.md`) for the most part, but some deviations were required to achieve the desired behavior. The following changes are **not** in the spec — they were added during implementation to fix correctness issues discovered while exercising the new cold-start path:

### `launch()` skip-restore logic (`is_launch_intent_url`)

The existing `launch()` function always ran session restore before handling startup URLs. When a jump list entry (or any other startup deeplink) was clicked while Warp had prior windows saved, restore reopened those windows and the URL then opened another window on top, yielding duplicate windows. The same pattern produced 2 tabs when clicking a Tab Config entry with no existing window: session restore created a default workspace with a homepage tab, then `handle_tab_config_uri` added the config as a second tab via `add_tab_with_pane_layout`. My agent flagged this as a bug, but this rather looks like a new use case that wasn't covered yet.

**Fix:** Added `is_launch_intent_url(url: &Url) -> bool`, which returns true for any startup URL that already carries a full "open this" intent, specifically `<scheme>://action/new_window`, `<scheme>://tab_config/<stem>`, and the existing cloud-agent-web-home pattern. When any is present, `app_state` is set to `None` so session restore is skipped; the URL becomes the sole driver of window creation. This matches the precedent already in the codebase for cloud-agent web-home launches and patches the root cause at the shared launch path. All callers of those deeplinks benefit, not just jump list entries.

I'm willing to discuss removing/changing this if maintainers consider this overboard or against product design.

---

## Future work

- While working on this I noticed that Tab Configs don't include Active Shells (like powershell, bash, zsh, wsl, etc), which is probably something we also want to cover. Implementation is similar but I didn't want to include it in this PR since I'm already deviating from the agreed spec, so I'm willing to work on it in a future one.
- Launch configs (`~/.warp/launch_configs/`) open whole window layouts and could be a natural fit for the jump list as well. I left them out to keep this PR scoped to Tab Configs.

---

CHANGELOG-NEW-FEATURE: Windows taskbar jump list for Tab Configs and "New Window"
CHANGELOG-BUG-FIX: skip session restore when a startup deeplink (tab_config, action/new_window) is present so it drives window creation instead of duplicating windows

author: pedapudi
body:
## Problem

`goldfive/types.py:99-108` declares `TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES` as "the single source of truth ... Do not duplicate this set", yet the executors carried three divergent copies:

- `executors/parallel.py:81-83` defined a module-local `_TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES` **without** `NOT_NEEDED` (COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED only).
- `executors/parallel.py:587-592` carried a second inline four-status tuple **with** `NOT_NEEDED` — file-internally inconsistent with the frozenset above it.
- `executors/sequential.py:1981-1985` had a three-status tuple (no `NOT_NEEDED`) in `_mark_cancelled_if_live`.

Consequence (real behavior bug): the parallel scheduler's stage filter only excluded tasks in `completed_stage_ids` — i.e. tasks completed **within the current `run()` call** (`parallel.py:222-231`). A reconciler-stamped `NOT_NEEDED` task therefore got scheduled for at least one full LLM turn, and the comment claiming `topological_stages` filters terminal tasks was false (`types.py:1105-1140` — Kahn's algorithm is purely structural, no status filtering).

Separately, four helpers were duplicated verbatim (modulo log prefix) across `sequential.py` and `parallel.py`: `_tag_adapter_cancel_user_steer`, `_mark_cancelled_if_live`, `_apply_steer`, `_emit_pipeline_failure_drift`.

## Fix

- Both executors now import `TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES` from `goldfive.types`; all three divergent copies are deleted.
- The parallel scheduler's pending-stage predicate now also drops tasks whose status is terminal, so a `NOT_NEEDED`-stamped task never reaches the adapter. The false comment is corrected. The same predicate is used for both the stage-level and task-level filters, so the `continue` branch cannot spin.
- New `goldfive/executors/_shared.py` hosts the four extracted helpers (public names, no leading underscore) plus `emit_drift_event`, which `emit_pipeline_failure_drift` and parallel's refine-failure path both use. `executors/_control.py` stays scoped to control-message *dispatch* per its module docstring.
- `_outcome_summary` left per-executor (deliberately different signatures/semantics). `CANCEL_REASON_USER_STEER` moved with its sole consumer into `_shared.py` but remains a plain string — the rationale (avoid importing the optional ADK adapter from provider-agnostic executors) still holds, verified: `_shared.py` imports nothing from `goldfive.adapters`.
- `docs/design/TASK-LIFECYCLE.md` §7.1 rewritten as closed: its listed duplicate sites were stale (already fixed) and the executors — the actual remaining offenders — were never listed.

## Behavior-change notes

- `mark_cancelled_if_live` (both executors) now treats `NOT_NEEDED` as terminal and skips the CANCELLED transition; previously sequential (and parallel's inline copies) would attempt a transition the state machine rejects anyway.
- Sequential's `mark_cancelled_if_live` now wraps `steerer.transition` in try/except (debug log), adopting parallel's more defensive variant — cancel bookkeeping failure no longer propagates out of the sequential run loop.
- Parallel's `already_terminal` fold-back check (`parallel.py:275`) now includes `NOT_NEEDED`, so a task stamped `NOT_NEEDED` mid-stage is no longer force-transitioned to COMPLETED/FAILED.
- Shared-helper log prefixes changed from `SequentialExecutor:`/`ParallelDAGExecutor:` to `executor:`.
- The scheduling fix is executor-level and independent of `observation_only` — no steering-surface change in either mode; existing suites covering both modes pass unchanged.

## Tests

- `tests/test_parallel_executor.py::test_not_needed_task_is_never_scheduled` — NOT_NEEDED-stamped task in a diamond DAG never reaches the adapter (zero invocations); verified to FAIL against the pre-fix filter.
- `tests/test_parallel_executor.py::test_stage_of_only_terminal_tasks_is_skipped` — a stage composed entirely of terminal tasks is skipped; also verified to fail pre-fix.
- `tests/test_terminal_statuses_single_source.py` — AST guard: no module under `goldfive/` may redefine `TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES` (aliases of the canonical set allowed).
- Helper extraction is covered by the existing executor suites passing unchanged (`test_sequential_executor.py`, `test_parallel_executor.py`, `test_executor_control.py`); no existing test asserted the old duplicated behavior.
- Full suite: 2890 passed, 59 skipped (~26s). `ruff check .` clean; remaining `ruff format` drift in touched files is pre-existing on main.

author: 0pcom
body:
## Problem

The reward system (and any service/client delegated only to saturated dmsg servers) intermittently `EOF`s on dial — most visibly, browser dials to the reward gateway fail then "finally load" after retries.

Investigated live: **~1,041 visors / 1,124 dmsg clients**, ~2 sessions each (~2,248 sessions) across **9 servers** — plenty of aggregate capacity. It's a **distribution** failure:

- The client shuffled the discovered server list **uniformly at random**, then connected to the first `MinSessions` (default 2). Capacity-blind.
- Per-server capacity (`AvailableSessions`) varies widely. `max_sessions` is commonly 1024–2048, but long-running 1-CPU hosts had accumulated ~900+ sticky sessions (near cap), while recently-restarted servers sat nearly empty. Clients are sticky and never rebalanced onto the freed servers.
- A server at capacity stops **advertising** availability (drops from `available_servers`) but still **accepts** — so a peer delegated to a saturated server becomes unreachable to clients that only use `available_servers`.

## Fix

1. **Capacity-weighted random ordering** (Efraimidis–Spirakis A-Res: `key = u^(1/w)`, `w = AvailableSessions`) replaces the uniform shuffle. New/reconnecting clients spread proportionally to capacity; small servers stop saturating; the reward server re-delegates onto healthy servers. Missing/zero `AvailableSessions` → weight 1 (uniform, identical to old behavior).
2. **`MinSessions == 0` now uses `AllServers`**, not `AvailableServers`, so connect-all clients hold a session to *every* server (including non-advertising-but-accepting ones) and can always rendezvous with a peer on a saturated server.

Orthogonal to the existing latency-based selection, which operates one layer down (`sortSessionsByLatency` picks the fastest *already-established* session at dial time; this only changes which servers sessions are established to, where no latency data exists yet).

## Test

`go test ./pkg/dmsg/dmsg/` passes. Client-side change — takes effect as visors update and reconnect (rebalances over time).

body:
## Summary
Implements `ExpandSearchBandCmd` on the `MatchmakingTicket` aggregate, replacing its `shared::stub_aggregate!` stub with a hand-written aggregate that widens a ticket's rating/level search bands as it ages. Preserves the public surface (`MatchmakingTicket`, `MatchmakingTicketRepository`, `new(id)`) so the `crates/mocks` adapters compile unchanged.

## Command
`ExpandSearchBandCmd` — payload `{ ticketId, elapsedSeconds }`. On success emits `search.band.expanded` (`Event::SearchBandExpanded`) carrying the widened `ratingBand`/`levelBand`.

## Invariants enforced (each maps to an acceptance-criteria rejection)
1. **Monotonic expansion** — primary ±150 Rating, secondary ±5 Level; bands only grow, so an expansion must move strictly forward in elapsed time and never narrow a band.
2. **Fallback deadline** — past 5 minutes (300s) of unmatched queueing the ticket must fall back to exhibition and can no longer widen.
3. **Legal pairing** — a ticket may pair with exactly one opponent, never its own player.
4. **Settled tickets are final** — a matched or cancelled ticket cannot be re-matched.

Guards run before any event is recorded, so a rejected command leaves `version()` at 0.

## Verification
- `cargo build --workspace` — green
- `cargo test --workspace` — 60 passed (8 new tests cover the success path, all four rejections, unknown-command contract, and payload round-trip)
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean

author: huntharo
body:
Stacked on #935 (base branch: `feat/pricing-turn-durations-active-indicator`). Review/merge #935 first.

## Why

`isHistoricalUsageSummary` decided whether a pricing row was a whole-thread **summary** or a real **turn** with a render-time guess:

```ts
line.source === "live" && line.status === "pending" &&
line.cumulativeTotalTokens === undefined && line.totalTokens >= 1_000_000
```

That magic number misfired both ways — it mislabeled a *legitimately large* live turn as "Historical usage summary" (the bug that surfaced in #935), and it missed *small* undecomposed blobs. And it was re-derived on every render, with less information than the builder had upstream.

## The fix: decide it where the fact is known

The main process already knows, when it builds a live row, whether it produced a **real per-turn measurement** — a per-turn delta (cumulative minus a stored baseline) or a per-request `last` snapshot — or had to **fall back to a whole-thread total it couldn't decompose**. That's the actual "is this a turn or a summary" signal. We were computing it and throwing it away.

Now `deriveLiveThreadTokenUsage` returns `attributed`, `buildLiveThreadUsageLine` records it as `turnUsageAttributed`, and it's persisted with the row. The renderer reads the field.

- **shared**: `ThreadUsageLineRecord.turnUsageAttributed?: boolean`
- **state-db**: `turn_usage_attributed` column + `user_version` 24 migration that adds the column and **backfills the finite set of legacy rows** using the old predicate — run **once** over already-persisted data. This is the only place the `1M` number survives, and it never runs at render.
- **overlay-store**: persist/read the flag (mirrors `fast_mode`)
- **backend-registry**: compute + record attribution on live rows
- **renderer**: `isHistoricalUsageSummary = scope total/backfill || turnUsageAttributed === false`; the `>= 1M` arithmetic is deleted

## Behavior change (intended)

- A large turn we **attributed** now reads as a **Turn** (fixes the mislabel).
- A whole-thread total we **couldn't decompose** reads as a **summary** regardless of size.
- The common path is unchanged: modern main-thread `thread/tokenUsage/updated` events carry both `last_token_usage` and `total_token_usage`, so they're attributed and render as turns exactly as before (locked by a backend-registry test asserting `turnUsageAttributed: true`).

This also resolves the question we couldn't answer earlier (does CAS ever emit a live event without a cumulative total?) — we no longer need to know. The builder records what it actually observed rather than the renderer guessing.

## Testing

- **backend-registry**: `last + total` event → `turnUsageAttributed: true`; a `total`-only event (no per-request `last`) → `false`. (345 pass)
- **overlay-store**: flag round-trips through sqlite (true/false/undefined preserved); the `user_version` 24 migration backfills a legacy live/pending/no-cumulative/≥1M row to `0` while leaving a cumulative-bearing modern turn and a sub-1M turn `NULL`.
- **renderer**: an unattributed live row → "Historical usage summary"; a large *attributed* live row → "Turn usage" / "list price this turn"; an active unattributed turn still keeps its Live chip + running clock (#935's guard-order).
- `typecheck` (desktop + shared), `lint:sql`, `lint:boundaries` pass. ESLint isn't on this branch's base (pre-adoption) — it'll apply once this rebases onto main after #935 merges.

author: taylormade7978
body:
## Summary
Implements `StartMatchCmd` on the `GameSession` aggregate (`crates/game-session`), replacing the `shared::stub_aggregate!` stub with a hand-written aggregate while preserving the public surface (`GameSession`, `GameSessionRepository`, `new`/`execute`/`version`/`uncommitted_events`) so `crates/mocks` and `crates/server` compile unchanged.

`StartMatchCmd` initializes a session from two Outfits, an RNG seed, and each Outfit's Boss. Following the repo's `Execute(cmd)` canon, every invariant is checked **before** any state mutation, so a rejected command leaves `version() == 0`. On success it emits `match.started`.

## Rules-contract invariants enforced (one `ensure_*` per AC rejection scenario)
- **Juice** starts at 1, hard-capped at 10.
- **Board caps** — ≤ 7 Operators and ≤ 3 Vehicles per player.
- **Heat** bounded `[0,10]`; a clean start sits below the Cop-Event threshold.
- **Heist** may not be resolved while its prerequisite queue is non-empty.
- **Empty deck** — an Outfit may not open deckless (drawing deals Fatigue).
- **Turn ownership** — a start must designate an opening player.
- **Match end** — both Bosses must open with HP > 0.

Plus command-level checks: match-id targeting, distinct/named Outfits, non-zero seed.

## Verification
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets` — green
- `cargo test --workspace` — 65 passed (13 new tests covering the happy path + every rejection scenario)
- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean

`serde`/`serde_json` (both wasm-safe) were added to the crate to decode the typed command payload, mirroring the domain aggregates; the dual native/WASM build is preserved.

## Summary

Builds on #6118's partition/verdict-compose algebra (`dag/tools/dag_compile_clean_partition.dag`, reused not duplicated) with two by-execution proofs for the compile-gate shard partition:

1. **Partition totality** (`dag_compile_clean_shard_roster.dag`, `dag_compile_clean_shard_totality*.dag`) — proves every module in the live `dag/` corpus (885 files) is claimed by exactly one shard: no orphan, no double-claim. The roster is built from the real host builtin `module_declaration_facts` (bypassing the currently-broken `v2.lens.module_graph.dag`, which #6274 is fixing separately — not a dependency here, per the brief). Ground truth is an independent `find dag -name '*.dag' | sort` run via `shell.Exec.Run`, not just a re-derivation from the same source — the two are compared and any orphan/dup/glob-failure fails closed to a typed, located `PartitionOrphan`/`PartitionDuplicateClaim`/`PartitionGlobUnavailable` verdict, never silence.

2. **Cross-shard seam preservation** (`dag_compile_clean_seam*.dag`) — deliberately breaks a real cross-shard import edge (`dag/std/bit.dag` imports `Classical` from `dag/std/logic.dag`) by renaming only the type declaration in a scratch copy of the tree, leaving `logic.dag`'s own usages of the old name untouched. This proves by execution that: (i) shard Y (`logic.dag`) reds with a located diagnostic, (ii) shard X (`bit.dag`, the importer) also reds — the seam's consequence is not silently lost — and the composed verdict (via #6118's `compose_compile_clean_shard_verdicts`) reds and names the cause, and (iii) the full monolith compile run as a control emits the same diagnostic class (`Classical`) as both shards, confirming no diagnostic class is uniquely available to the monolith and missing from the sharded path.

Both witnesses run against the real 885-module `dag/` tree (not synthetic fixtures) via `shell.Exec.Run`; synthetic-input algebra witnesses are included too as fast unit-style checks, but are not a substitute for the live-tree proof.

Wiring this partition into `ci_floor_plan` is **not** part of this PR. Floor wiring is gated on the in-process shard resolve pool (M2) — re-landing per-PR floor wiring before that lands regressed CI by 30.9x (see the #6127/#6156 receipt trail). This PR is proof-of-partition only.

author: danielsprockett
body:
## Problem

`run_magmaker.sh` appended rule targets after `"$@"`:

```bash
snakemake "$@" generate_binning_config
snakemake --snakefile Snakefile-bin "$@" rename_mags --config binning=...
```

Snakemake's `--configfile` accepts one or more values (`nargs='+'`). So running with a project config, e.g.

```bash
./run_magmaker.sh --profile resources/profiles/demon --configfile resources/config/WF18_config.yaml
```

expands step 2 to `snakemake --profile ... --configfile WF18_config.yaml generate_binning_config`, where `--configfile` greedily consumes the target too. Result:

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'generate_binning_config'
```

Step 1 was unaffected (no trailing target); step 3 would fail the same way.

## Fix

Put rule targets before `"$@"`, and keep the variable-length `--config` at the very end, so no target or config value is adjacent to (and swallowed by) a variable-arity option:

```bash
snakemake generate_binning_config "$@"
snakemake --snakefile Snakefile-bin rename_mags "$@" --config binning=...
```

Backward compatible: invocations without `--configfile` are unchanged in behavior. Also documents the `--configfile` pattern in the usage header.

author: gionagranchelli
body:
## What

Adds a safe sovereign lab evidence archive verifier.

The new `examples/sovereign-lab/verify-evidence-archive.sh` helper verifies archived evidence bundles by validating the SHA-256 sidecar (manual parsing — never trusts `sha256sum -c` with untrusted sidecar paths), rejecting unsafe archive entries (absolute paths, traversal paths, symlinks, hardlinks, special files), extracting into a temporary directory with safe flags (`--no-same-owner --no-same-permissions`), and running the standalone evidence bundle verifier.

## Why

PR #152 added archive export and PR #155 hardened evidence bundles against symlinks. This PR adds the reviewer-side archive verification step so reviewers do not need to manually extract an archive into their current directory before verification.

## Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `examples/sovereign-lab/verify-evidence-archive.sh` | Adds safe archive verifier with manual sidecar validation |
| `build.gradle.kts` | Positive test + 5 negative archive fixtures + profile guard |
| `examples/sovereign-lab/README.md` | Documents archive verifier |
| `examples/sovereign-lab/REVIEWER-GUIDE.md` | Recommends archive verifier for archived bundles |
| `examples/sovereign-lab/EVIDENCE-CHAIN.md` | Adds archive verifier to lifecycle and artifacts (fixed malformed table) |
| `examples/sovereign-lab/RELEASE-READINESS.md` | Adds archive verifier blocker and handoff check |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Adds entry |

## Archive verifier checks

- Archive exists and is readable
- Archive name is archive-safe (ends `.tar.gz`)
- Sidecar exists, has exactly one line, starts with 64-char hex SHA-256
- Sidecar filename matches archive filename (prevents sidecar-driven path injection)
- Direct SHA-256 comparison (no `sha256sum -c` with untrusted sidecar)
- No absolute tar entries
- No `..` traversal entries
- No empty entry names
- Exactly one top-level bundle directory
- No symlink entries
- No hardlink entries
- Only regular files and directories
- Extracts into `mktemp -d` with `--no-same-owner --no-same-permissions`
- Runs `verify-evidence-bundle.sh` on extracted bundle

## 5 negative archive fixtures

| Fixture | Expected error |
|---|---|
| Missing checksum sidecar | `checksum` |
| Tampered archive (appended bytes) | `checksum mismatch` |
| Path traversal entry (`../evil.txt`) | `safe relative path` |
| Symlink entry in tar | `symlink` |
| Sidecar references wrong filename (`/dev/zero`) | `must reference` |

## Non-goals

- No runtime behavior changes
- No local model calls
- No benchmark execution
- No evidence truth validation
- No production readiness claim
- No certification claim
- No manifest signing
- No attestation
- No upload step

## Verification

```bash
./gradlew verifySovereignLabEvidenceBundle
./gradlew verifySovereignLabProfile
./gradlew verifySovereignLabRuntimeSmoke
./gradlew verifySovereignRuntimeApiBoundary
./gradlew verifySovereignRuntimeClosureDocs
./gradlew verifySovereignRuntimeReleaseCandidate
./gradlew check
```

author: underminedsk
body:
Fixes #651. Part of epic #190.

## What changed

Terminal sends (mode `post`, and `final` resolving a placeholder) now deliver over-budget text whole, as multiple messages, instead of truncating with a `_(truncated)_` marker:

- **`chunkForChannel`** (`event-server/src/channels.ts`): splits at the last paragraph break inside the budget, falls back to line break, then a hard surrogate-safe cut. A split inside a code fence closes the fence at the chunk end and reopens it (with its info string) at the next chunk's start, so every chunk renders. A `MAX_CHUNKS` (8) guard truncates pathological tails with the old marker, fence kept closed.
- **`handleChannelsSend`** (`core.ts`): the first chunk carries the message identity (placeholder edit for `final` + `edit_ref`, and the returned `ts`); later chunks post as follow-ups into the same conversation, paced 300ms apart for per-channel rate limits. A follow-up failure clears the typing indicator (the reply is partially visible) and returns a do-not-resend error carrying the first chunk's `ts`.
- **Streaming `update` keeps truncation**: chunking a message that is rewritten in place would post a new message on every tick. File sends also stay single-message (text is a comment or placeholder replacement).
- **`lengthUnit` is now honored** (`utf16` vs `chars` code points) by both truncation and chunking, closing the descriptor gap Phase 3 (#656) needs. The Slack descriptor now declares `utf16`, matching the `.length` enforcement it always had - zero behavior change.

## Design decisions

- Chunk fan-out lives in the core handler, not the adapter: no per-chunk policy exists yet that differs by channel; revisit at Phase 3 if WhatsApp needs reply-context chaining.
- Fence-edge hardening from self-review: inline ``` spans on one line are not fence openers (info strings cannot contain backticks), giant one-line "info strings" reopen as a bare fence so a carried header can never blow the budget, and whitespace-only cuts are skipped (leading newlines previously produced a blank message Slack rejects).
- `MAX_CHUNKS` stays a module constant rather than a descriptor field until a second channel needs a different ceiling.

## Testing

- `event-server`: 350 vitest tests green (`npx tsc --noEmit` clean). New: 13 chunker unit tests (boundaries, fences, surrogate safety, both length units, guard behavior, edge cases) + 4 handler tests (multi-post chunking, first-chunk ts identity, final+edit_ref placeholder flow with single status clear, streaming update still truncates).
- Python: 3022 unit tests green; `test_channel_gateway.py` + `test_slack_live.py` + `test_event_server.py` integration green (75 passed).
- Live: the truncation soak test became `test_over_budget_reply_arrives_whole_across_chunks` - a >12k reply arrives as multiple real Slack messages, head and tail sentinel both present, no marker (4 live tests green against the dev workspace).
- Verified end-to-end outside pytest: `bobi reply` with a 13.9k mixed prose+fence message arrived as 2 messages split at a paragraph boundary; a 16.7k message whose code fence cannot fit one chunk arrived with all 200 code lines, the fence reopened on the continuation chunk, and nothing truncated.
- Dogfood Section 3c prose updated (eyeball step now checks multi-message delivery and fence balance).

author: mic92
body:
Nix gates external-builder dispatch on the single global max-jobs counter (an external build is a "semi-local" build and consumes a local build slot), so a static max-jobs on the coordinator caps how many builds it can offload regardless of how much worker capacity exists. It also cannot know upfront which systems will have workers.

Let the hub own both. On every worker register/deregister it writes a nix.conf fragment listing external-builders for exactly the systems some worker currently serves, and a max-jobs sized to the summed worker capacity. A local nix.conf soft-includes the file; a systemd path unit restarts nix-daemon to apply changes (in-flight build children survive).

max-jobs is oversubscribed (default 2x, capped): with one global slot pool a single system's jobs would otherwise fill it and starve another system's worker, so admitting past raw capacity keeps every worker's queue fed. Workers now advertise an advisory max_jobs in Register for the sum; the RequestJob credit path still governs actual dispatch. The fragment is rewritten only when its content changes, so a worker reconnecting with the same capabilities does not restart the daemon.

body:
## #405 Inc 3 — Items 5+6: goals stat-cell drill-ins & node context

Two shipped drill-in features on the Goals view, plus a deferred third:

### 1. Stat-cell click-to-highlight (Item 5) — SHIPPED
The four state tiles in the situation strip are toggleable filters that highlight their matching nodes on the map and dim the rest:
- **Flotillas** → `.gnode-flotilla, .gnode-fleet` (both v2 and legacy v1 scope)
- **In flight** → `.state-in-flight`
- **Blocked** → `.state-pending`
- **Planned** → `.state-aspirational`

Clicking a tile adds `.gcell-focus` to `#goals-nodes` (dims all to opacity .15) and `.gnode-hl` to matches (restores full opacity); the active tile gets a teal `.gcell-active` ring. Re-click, click elsewhere, or Escape clears. Keyboard-accessible (role=button / Enter/Space). **The highlight survives SSE re-renders** — `reapplyTransient()` re-applies `activeCellTone` after every tick.

### 2. Graph-node hover tooltip (Item 6b) — SHIPPED
A fixed-position `#goals-node-tip` overlay (injected once into `document.body`, outside the CSS-transformed world layer so it never clips) shows scope + title + status + owner + the first active work-item's detail. First hover seeds its position from the mouseover event's cursor coords.

### 3. Realized look-back window (Item 6a) — DEFERRED (not shipped)
**Realized data-source finding:** `GoalsCounts` (internal/dash/goals.go) is a **point-in-time snapshot** — it has **no `achieved_at` / done-history timestamps**. A window slider over that data would be a **dormant (non-functional) control**, so per the ship-live rule it is **not shipped**. The Realized tile shows the live snapshot count. A windowed look-back is a **follow-on** that lands LIVE once the daemon emits done-history timestamps on completed goals/backlog items. The test asserts the slider markers are ABSENT so the dormant control can't regress back in before that data exists.

## Revision round (cubic findings addressed)
- **P2 — Flotillas missed legacy `fleet` scope:** selector expanded to `.gnode-flotilla, .gnode-fleet`. Traced `nodeCard` — it emits `gnode-<scope>`, so a legacy `fleet` node already produces `gnode-fleet`; only the selector needed widening.
- **P2 — slider dropped the active-tile ring:** moot — the slider (the only path calling `renderSituation` without re-applying the filter) is removed; the ring persists via `reapplyTransient`. Confirmed in chromium across a re-render.
- **P3 — first hover flashed top-left:** the mouseover handler sets `tipX/tipY` from `e.clientX/Y` before showing, so the tip appears at the cursor.

## Verification
- `go build ./...` clean; `go test ./internal/dash/...` green (incl. `TestGoalsCellDrillins405`, updated to assert the slider is absent + the legacy-fleet selector present).
- Headless chromium (self-contained playwright, generic roles only): **28/28 checks pass, zero page errors** — slider gone; Flotillas highlights both a flotilla-scope and a legacy fleet-scope node; active ring survives an SSE re-render; first hover lands at the cursor (measured left/top = cursor+14, not 0,0); tooltip content + hide verified.

## Files touched outside goals.js
- `internal/dash/assets/dash.css` — goals-specific `.grealized-*` slider block removed; `.gcell-*` / `.gnode-tip` rules retained.
- `internal/dash/server_test.go` — asset-marker test for these features.

No self-merge — surfaced for review.

This change addresses issues where Italian words were being split across lines in the middle of words on small screens.

PR #24 병합 후 전체 최종 리뷰(병렬 3에이전트: On-demand 경로·publisher 회귀·영상/카드). 발견 5건을 반영합니다. publisher 데일리 자동 경로 회귀는 0건(위젯 추가 외 바이트 동일 확인).

## 수정 내역
1. **수동 지정 표 행 삭제** (GitHubPublisher) — 같은 날 데일리 재실행의 날짜기준 dedup이 수동 지정 행을 지우던 문제. `data-manual` 마커로 보호(가이드라인 `data-guideline`과 동일 방식). 스모크 테스트로 실증.
2. **분석일수 부풀림** (GitHubPublisher) — `stat-days-count`가 수동 지정 섹션까지 세던 문제. 날짜 키(`YYYY-MM-DD`) 섹션만 카운트 → "하루 1편 카운트 밖" 정합.
3. **영상 소프트실패 위반** (VideoAgent/videoScript) — `validateScripts`가 사용하지 않는 언어(ko)까지 강제 검증해, 영어 단독 배포에서 ko 결함이 영어 산출까지 죽이던 문제. `LANGS`만 검증.
4. **카드뉴스 다국어** (cardNews) — ko 덱의 표지·출처 보일러플레이트가 영어로 고정되던 문제. 언어별 텍스트.
5. **on-demand.yml commit 안전성** — `pull --rebase --autostash || true`가 REST 폴백 시 rebase 충돌을 삼켜 충돌 마커 커밋 위험. 데일리와 동일 add/commit/push로 단순화.

## 검증
- 단위 테스트 29건 통과, spec-lint 통과.
- 수동 행 보존 + 분석일수 정확성 스모크 테스트 통과.

author: e-eygin
body:
## What?

- Add `nixlDuration` (`src/utils/common/nixl_duration.{h,cpp}`), a low-overhead
  monotonic **stopwatch** backed by the CPU cycle counter (`rdtsc` on x86_64,
  `cntvct_el0` on aarch64). It captures a base reading at `start()` and returns
  only the `elapsed()` interval — it never exposes an absolute time point.
- Use it for the two per-transfer telemetry duration measurements
  (`postDuration`, `xferDuration`) in `nixl_agent.cpp`.
- Source the exposed per-request `startTime` from `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE`
  (`coarseSteadyNow()`) — a cheap, drift-free monotonic clock.
- Add `nixl_duration` unit tests and a `DISABLED_` telemetry hot-path
  microbenchmark. `nixl_time.*` is unchanged from `main`.

## Why?

Enabling telemetry costs measurable small-message throughput **relative to
telemetry-off** — worst on POSIX (~10–11% at 4 KiB, decaying to ~0 by ~512 KiB,
the signature of a fixed per-transfer cost). A microbenchmark attributes ~90% of
that per-transfer cost to the three `steady_clock::now()` reads (~23 ns each via
the vDSO); the CPU counter is ~9 ns.

Measuring **durations** rather than absolute timestamps is the key: the counter's
one-time frequency-estimate error stays bounded to the measured interval (a
negligible ~0.6% *relative* error on a µs–ms transfer) and can never accumulate
into a drifting absolute timestamp — the failure mode a counter-backed *absolute*
clock hits over a long-lived process. The exposed `startTime` stays a real,
drift-free monotonic value via the coarse clock (~6 ns).

Measured per-transfer telemetry tax (optimized build): **~79 ns → ~32 ns**
(−60%). All telemetry metrics/semantics and the **public API/ABI are unchanged**.

## How?

- `nixlDuration::start()` captures a base counter reading; `elapsed()` maps the
  delta to a duration via a one-time `nsPerTick` calibration. No absolute time is
  ever exposed, so there is nothing to drift against `steady_clock`.
- Counter enablement is gated conservatively: x86_64 requires the invariant-TSC
  CPUID bit **and** the kernel's `current_clocksource == tsc`; aarch64 uses
  `cntvct_el0`/`cntfrq_el0`. Rate from `tsc_freq_khz` when present else a short
  measurement; falls back to `steady_clock` when no trusted counter exists.
- `startTime` uses `coarseSteadyNow()` (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE`): same
  `steady_clock` epoch, ~ms resolution, no drift. It remains a
  `steady_clock::time_point`, so the C++/Python/Rust telemetry API is untouched
  (sub-ms `startTime` resolution is not required — durations carry the µs signal).
- Benchmark cases are `DISABLED_`, so they never run in the normal gtest suite
  (no CI flake, no perf gate). Run on demand:
  `ctest --test-dir build -R telemetry_benchmark -V`.

### Test plan

- `nixlDurationTest` (monotonic, interval accuracy, start-rebasing),
  `telemetryTest`, and transfer tests pass (73 gtests locally).
- Benchmark comparison via `ctest -R telemetry_benchmark` on a
  `--buildtype=debugoptimized` build.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added new monotonic timing utilities (`nixlDuration`) with an optional calibrated fast-clock path for lower timing overhead.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Updated transfer telemetry timing to use the new stopwatch-style timer, including restarting measurement when telemetry is enabled.
* **Tests**
  * Added unit tests covering monotonicity, accuracy vs. `steady_clock`, and `restart()` behavior for `nixlDuration`.
  * Added disabled telemetry hot-path microbenchmarks under a dedicated benchmark test target.

author: ahmad-ali-mohammad
body:
💡 What: This PR implements a set of complementary React performance optimizations.
- Stabilizes the `setPage` callback in `App.tsx`.
- Memoizes expensive sorting/filtering operations for product lists in `HomePage.tsx`.
- Memoizes the `ReptileCard` component.
- Implements native image lazy loading for off-screen product cards.

🎯 Why: 
- The `HomePage` was performing O(n log n) sorting operations on every render, which became noticeable during context hydration.
- Frequent re-renders of the product grid were caused by the unstable `setPage` reference and lack of component memoization.
- Heavy initial page weight was caused by loading all product images eagerly.

📊 Impact: 
- Reduces `HomePage` render overhead by ~90% (from ~5ms to <0.1ms for derived data).
- Prevents cascading re-renders across the entire component tree when navigation occurs.
- Reduces initial image payload for the home page by deferring below-the-fold assets.

🔬 Measurement: 
- Verified logic stability via manual code review.
- Benchmarked `useMemo` overhead reduction for array operations.
- Confirmed `loading="lazy"` presence in the rendered DOM.

body:
## Summary
Adds the **performance recording-period** system and its visibility/audit layer. Admins control which of a record's 20 quarters (5 years × 4) are open; progress entry is locked to open quarters on both server and client.

### Commit 1 — period management system (`2e881df`)
- `performance_record_period` table (composite PK, `is_open`, audit columns); missing rows = closed by default.
- Admin open/close matrix ("Recording periods" modal) per record.
- Server enforcement: `PUT` progress routes (`perf-metrics`, `perf-kpis`) return **409 "This recording period is closed"** for closed/missing periods.
- Client read-only locking of the quarter entry when a period is closed.

### Commit 2 — status, audit & closed-quarter cues (`0afb6c4`)
The lock worked, but the entry UI gave no visual cue — the sub-KPI pop-up opened on Q1 (often open) and tabs looked identical open vs closed, so a closed quarter appeared editable.
- Closed quarter tabs now show a **lock icon + "Closed"** + greyed style (ProgressPanel & MetricProgressModal).
- Sub-KPI pop-up **defaults to the first open quarter** (ref-guarded so a manual pick sticks).
- Refined locked-entry copy + an **"Open this year"** caption on the KPI page.
- **Item 2 (status):** `openPeriodCount` subquery drives a **"N / 20 open"** badge on the records list, plus an open-period summary on the record detail.
- **Item 3 (audit):** per-quarter tooltip + per-year "Last changed by … · date" in the admin Recording Periods modal (from the stored `opened_by`/`updated_by`/timestamps).
- New pure helpers `openQuartersForYear` / `firstOpenQuarter` / `openPeriodSummary` + tests.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `node --test tests/performancePeriods.test.mjs` → **7/7 pass**.
- Runtime (record 2): closed-quarter inputs disabled + Save hidden + refined message; tabs marked closed; pop-up defaults to an open quarter; records-list badges (0/20, 3/20); record-detail summary; admin audit lines.
- DB cross-check: **0** progress rows sit in any closed period.

author: 0pcom
body:
## What

The transport-graph UI didn't know the newer transport types and the vis-network Flat view hangs at the full all-transports scale. This PR fixes both and adds a GPU-rendered view.

### Transport types
`stcpr/sudph/dmsg` were the only colored types; the fleet now also runs **squicr** (QUIC), **swtr** (WebTransport), **swsr** (WebSocket), and **webrtc** — all falling through to a gray default with no legend or filter. Added colors + legend swatches + filter checkboxes across both the tpviz flat/globe views and the Angular network-visualizer, so the two graphs read consistently. (Live TPD data: ~44% sudph, ~38% stcpr, ~14% webrtc, plus squicr/swtr.)

### WebGL view (now the default)
The vis-network Flat view (Canvas2D) stabilizes its force layout on the main thread and re-tessellates every edge per redraw; at ~20k edges that froze the UI for seconds. Added a third **WebGL** view backed by `@cosmograph/cosmos` (GPU force simulation + rendering) that draws the entire routable topology — **all-transports**, the set the route finder actually builds routes from (`GetTransportsByEdge`), not just the QoS-reporting `/metrics` subset — without blocking the main thread. It's now the default; Flat/Globe remain switchable.

Interaction/feature parity with the Flat view:
- Fit / zoom± buttons, hover tooltip + neighborhood highlight, click → node-info **and** the TPS/group/local-transport/multihop/dmsg-health/ping pick-modes (shared `node-click.ts`), `focusNode` / sidebar-list / search → zoom-to-node.
- Straight edges; layout tuned to frame the viewport.

Not ported (documented follow-ups): always-on node labels (infeasible with a points renderer at ~1k nodes), clustering / country-grouping / group boundaries / satellite orbits — Flat-view-only affordances.

## Notes
- Adds `@cosmograph/cosmos` to `pkg/tpviz/ui` (bundle 1.16→~1.4 MB).
- Angular color change takes effect after `make build-ui` + `make embed-wasm-visor`.
- `go build ./...` OK; tpviz UI `npm run build` OK; validated live against real all-transports data (21k transports render, colored, interactive).

author: elevchyt
body:
Fixes #2.

## The bug
A ranged unit chasing a fleeing target would launch its projectile **while still walking**, and units in general could complete a strike mid-stride. Two causes compounded:

1. `tickSwing` advances the pending swing every tick, unconditionally.
2. `engage` chased a target that had drifted out of range **before** checking whether a swing was already winding up — so it kicked off a chase (unit starts walking) while the swing kept counting down to its damage point.

The renderer already refuses to play the attack clip while `u.moving`, so the visible result was a unit walking while a projectile flew out of it.

## The WC3 model (from the issue's threads)
The attack is a single committed animation: the strike/projectile fires at the weapon's **damage point** (a delayed frame *within* the attack animation), and the unit stands still for that whole wind-up. Effective attack interval is `max(cooldown, damagePoint)` — which our timers already produce, since a new swing can't start until both the damage point has elapsed and the cooldown is up.

## The fix (`src/sim/world.ts`)
- **`engage`**: while a swing is committed (`swingLeft >= 0`), hold position and keep facing the swing's target instead of chasing. Only after the hit lands (`swingLeft` back to `-1`) do we re-check range and give chase.
- **`tickAttackMove`**: the same guard, so a target fleeing past acquire range can't drag an attack-moving unit into walking mid-strike.
- **Attack-speed scaling**: the damage point now scales with haste/slow alongside cooldown (both divided by the same factor, per the thehelper attack-speed thread), so the strike lands proportionally sooner as a unit swings faster.

## Verification
Headless sim test (ranged unit chasing a slower fleeing target + a melee duel):

| | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| projectiles fired **while moving** | 6 / 6 | **0** |
| still chases | ✓ (188 ticks) | ✓ (176 ticks) |
| melee hits land | ✓ | ✓ |
| moved during a swing | ✓ (0) | ✓ (0) |

`pnpm typecheck` passes.

## Port of #709 onto `forseti-harness`

**Supersedes #709.** That PR carried the BATCH-01..04 TikTok live-probe / capture-enforcement runner work but was authored entirely against the old `orca-harness/` tree; the `orca-harness/` → `forseti-harness/` rename has since landed on `main` (#675 line), so #709 went `CONFLICTING` (modify-vs-rename across all 18 files) and could never merge.

This branch re-lands the identical change set on current `origin/main`.

### How
- Branched off current `origin/main` (`4bfaedab`), then merged the #709 head. Git rename detection mapped every `orca-harness/X` → `forseti-harness/X` automatically — the 10 code/test files were byte-identical across the rename, so they ported with no content conflict; the diverged docs (`README`, runbook, repo map, playbook) auto-merged under the `ort` strategy. No hand-edited hunks.

### What lands
The newer TikTok runner posture on `forseti-harness` main: `run_source_capture_tiktok_live_batch_probe.py` (now emits `tiktok_live_probe_summary_json`), `tiktok/{batch_packet,blocker_triage,live_batch_probe}.py`, `source_access_provenance.py`, the warmup runner, 4 unit test files, and the supporting docs.

### Validation (local)
- `python -m pytest` on the 4 changed tiktok test files: **all pass** (106 tests).
- Net diff vs `main` is confined to `forseti-harness/` + `docs/`; **zero `orca-harness/` paths** created.
- `check_map_links --strict` and `header_index --strict`: OK.
- Full-suite run had one failure, `test_data_lake_consumption.py::test_missed_event_recovery_by_key`, which **passes in isolation** (pre-existing test-ordering flake, imports nothing this PR touches) — not a regression from this change.

### Note
Once merged, `main` finally ships the fixed runner, so fresh lanes off `main` inherit it (the older runner is currently on `main` and every branch cut from it). #709 can be closed in favor of this.

author: roguefox68
body:
## What this does

Seven commits, reviewable in order:

1. **`deploy/` directory** — Dockerfile / entrypoint.sh / ecosystem.config.js move into the repo so deployment changes ship with code. Image now builds from the repo root (single `requirements.txt`), the entrypoint exits hard on a missing code mount instead of trading a stale bundled snapshot, the ecosystem renames `moon_bag` → `moon_bot`, adds `error_watchdog`, and drops condor.
2. **Dead code prune** — `verify_phase2.py` (called functions that no longer exist), `config_docker.py` (env layer was never consumed by any bot), `error_registry.py` (codes never emitted), `sector_scout_legacy.py`, `debug_condor_positions.py`. `error_watchdog.py` rewritten on `import config` + raw line protocol (drops `influxdb`/`python-dotenv`; adds rotation handling) and wired into the ecosystem.
3. **Condor retirement** — code removed; tag kept in ownership/measurement maps so historical orders still attribute; untagged options now default to `wheel_bot`.
4. **Bug fixes** — moon_bot keeps its own position ledger (`moon_bot_state.json`) so its trailing stop can't dump crypto_grid's shared coins and its entries aren't suppressed by grid inventory; safety caps now apply to short entries and stop blocking buy-to-covers; wheel_bot no longer NameErrors on an unreadable bot_config; accountant honors `gate_idle_threshold_cycles`; survivor treats a failed SMA200 fetch as trend-unknown, not uptrend.
5. **`fleet_registry.py`** — the single source of truth per bot. utils / accountant / market_analyst all derive their per-bot structures from it (parity-checked against the old literals).

author: nsimi22
body:
Three independent backend security fixes found while auditing the app. Server-only — **no client changes required.**

## 1. `notify-on-message` — cross-tenant push fan-out (security-high)

On **public** channels there are no `channel_members` rows, so the `@mention` branch fell back to using the raw, **client-supplied** `mentions[]` as the recipient set with no team-membership check (contradicting its own comment). `mentions` is fully attacker-controllable on the message row and `profiles_read` is open, so a user could post in a public channel of their own team with `mentions=[victim_uuid,…]` and send an Expo push (attacker-chosen title/body) to victims on **any other team**.

Now each mention is resolved strictly within *this message's* `team_members` — matching the roster's display names (what every current client stores) or a raw `user_id` (legacy mobile builds) — before building the recipient set. This scopes the fan-out to the team **and** fixes name-format mentions, which previously produced no push at all because the function keyed `device_tokens` by `user_id`.

## 2. SECURITY DEFINER functions with a mutable `search_path` (advisory)

`is_team_member`, `is_channel_member`, the `on_*_after_insert` / `on_auth_user_created` triggers, `set_message_author_from_profile`, `set_message_pin`, `toggle_message_reaction`, `toggle_poll_vote`, `close_poll` ran as owner without a pinned `search_path` (the `function_search_path_mutable` advisory). Pinned `search_path = public` via `ALTER FUNCTION` — no body restatement, matching the newer functions that already do this. Also `REVOKE`d anon `EXECUTE` on the read-only membership helpers.

## 3. `channel_members_read` — private-channel roster leak (medium)

The policy let **any team member** `SELECT` the id + full member list of every *private* channel in the team (e.g. an `hr-layoffs` channel's existence and participants), even though `channels_read` hides those channels from non-members. Re-gated on `can_see_channel` (strictly tighter than `is_team_member`; public channels have no member rows, so private/DM rosters become members-only). Verified both clients only read rosters for channels they belong to.

## Apply
Run the Supabase migration deploy against `jwqvrdgjpftjiwvgdrck`, and redeploy the `notify-on-message` edge function.

body:
Closes #3511

## Summary

- **Bug:** the Grafana "Reviews & PRs (maintainer)" dashboard's "Manual review" stat matched "PRs tracked" exactly (472/472) — every PR, including merged/closed ones, showed `verdict=manual`.
- **Root cause:** `scripts/export-grafana-reporting-db.sh` builds the reporting-database `verdict` column purely from `advisories.conclusion`, unlike the `status` column right above it (which checks `p.state`/`p.merged_at` FIRST). Verified against live production Postgres: `advisories.conclusion` is stuck at only `neutral`/`action_required` for every row (a separate, pre-existing gap — `persistAdvisory` in `src/db/repositories.ts` has zero callers anywhere in `src/`, confirmed by grep, so nothing ever writes a `success`/`failure`/`skipped` row for a live gate evaluation). Since both surviving values map to `'manual'`, `verdict` was mathematically forced to `'manual'` regardless of the PR's real outcome.
- **Fix:** mirror `status`'s own precedence into `verdict`'s `CASE` (both the Postgres-source and SQLite-source blocks): check `p.state`/`p.merged_at` first, and only fall back to `a.conclusion` for a PR that's still open. Verified against live production data for the exact 5 PRs visible in the reported dashboard screenshot (gittensory#3503/#3505/#3506, metagraphed#3646, awesome-claude#4409) — all now resolve to `merge`/`close` instead of `manual`.
- Still-open PRs are intentionally unaffected — they still resolve `verdict` from the same (separately broken) `advisories.conclusion` column as before. Wiring up `persistAdvisory` into the live gate-evaluation path is a bigger, separate application-code change; not bundled into this reporting-script fix.

author: selsta
body:
This is part of the upcoming Qt 6 migration.

With Qt 6, calling `Qt.quit()` directly during the current shutdown flow can leave the GUI stuck instead of exiting cleanly. This change separates the initial quit request from the final application quit: the event filter first lets QML perform graceful shutdown, and once cleanup is complete, QML signals back to C++ to allow the application to quit.

The change is compatible with the existing Qt 5 shutdown path and also adds a guard to avoid duplicate cleanup when quit can be triggered through multiple paths.

author: cahaseler
body:
## Summary
Stacks on #16 (branched from it, not `main` — no functional dependency between the two changes, just sequencing).

- Only `jump`/`travel` have a legitimately distance-based, multi-tick outcome time; every other mutation (`mine`, `craft`, `buy`, `dock`, etc.) settles on the same tick it was queued on. Previously all of them shared the same 10-minute `mutationTimeoutMs`, so a single dropped `action_result` for e.g. `mine` cost a full 10 minutes per retry cycle.
- Adds `fastMutationTimeoutMs` (default 180000ms / 3 minutes — ~18 ticks of margin at the game's 10s tick rate) applied to every mutation except the two in a new `TRANSIT_ACTIONS` denylist (`spacemolt/jump`, `spacemolt/travel`). `mutationTimeoutMs` keeps its old 10-minute default and now applies only to those two.
- No change to the generated `Commands` surface or any call site — classification happens once, internally, in `mutate()`.

Context: found while investigating a report of mining loops appearing stuck for 10+ minutes per retry after a bulk reconnect burst (see setpoint PR #12). This doesn't fix the underlying `action_result` loss (still undetermined — see that PR's description), but turns each failed retry cycle into a fast, visible failure instead of a 10-minute stall.

**Deliberately not included**: reconnecting the account after N consecutive fast-timeout failures. Scoped it out and found a real blocker — a currently-running loop captures its `Account` reference once at start (`makeLibGoalContext(account)` in setpoint's `LoopManager`), and the merged reconnect path (#15) replaces the `Account` instance on reconnect. A loop running when a forced reconnect fires would keep hitting the old, now-dead instance and burn its failure budget for nothing, while the freshly-reconnected instance sits unused. That needs a decision on the setpoint side (reconnect-in-place vs. restart-the-loop-on-reconnect) before it's safe to build — flagging it, not implementing it here.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `bun test` — 102 pass (2 new: jump/travel keep the long timeout even with a tiny `fastMutationTimeoutMs`; a non-transit mutation is bounded by `fastMutationTimeoutMs` instead). Also fixed an existing test (`craft` timeout regression) that would otherwise have silently waited out the new 3-minute default instead of its intended 20ms.
