author: mekwall
body:
## Summary

Closes #381, closes #382, closes #388.

Three security fixes hardening the approval / execution / containment boundary per ADR-0007 and ADR-0013.

### Fix 1: Require control proofs for `Contained` assurance (ADR-0007, #381)

`ExecutionContextBuilder::build` now **fail-closes** when `AssuranceLevel::Contained` is requested without proof of every mandatory ADR-0007 control. Previously the builder accepted `Contained` with no evidence that any isolation control was actually active — a receipt could carry an unearned containment claim.

- New `EffectiveControls` struct (per-control capability matrix: filesystem / network / process-tree / privilege-suppression / syscall-filtering / resource-limits), serialized into receipts.
- New `ControlProofs` builder input — each `Option<String>` holds a mechanism/attestation name (e.g. `"landlock"`, `"no-new-privs"`). Any `None` mandatory control yields `ExecError::MissingContainmentProof`.
- New `ExecError::MissingContainmentProof { control }` variant naming the missing control.
- `ReceiptBuilder::effective_controls(...)` emits the matrix; `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` keeps non-contained receipts compact.
- `native.rs` test helper downgraded from `Contained` → `Mediated` (no proofs available in test env).

### Fix 2: Plan-bound CLI approval (spec §28.5, ADR-0013, #382)

CLI `approve` previously wrote a digest-only JSON object (`sha`/`verdict`/`timestamps`) — replayable across interpreters, argv, env, and network policy per C-08. Now writes a schema-versioned `ApprovalFile` (v2) binding **every** material plan dimension:

`artifact_sha256`, `operation`, `release_mode`, `interpreter`, `interpreter_arguments`, `environment_profile_digest`, `working_directory_policy`, `filesystem_grants`, `network_isolated`, `sandbox_capabilities`, `release_destination`, `policy_snapshot_digest`, `detector_snapshot_digest`, `plan_digest`, `nonce`, `approver`, `approved_at`, `expires_at`, `verdict`.

- `ApprovalFile::compute_plan_digest()` hashes the plan-bound fields in deterministic order (excludes `nonce`/`approver`/`expires_at`/`schema_version`/`plan_digest` itself).
- `ApprovalFile::verify(now)` checks schema version, recomputes the digest and rejects any mismatch (post-approval tampering), then checks expiry.
- CLI `execute` calls `approval.verify(now)` and additionally checks the to-be-executed network flag matches the approved flag.
- `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` rejects rogue fields.
- Aligns CLI path with the MCP `ApprovalTokenIssuer` plan-digest model.

### Fix 3: Durable approval nonce persistence (ADR-0013, #388)

MCP `ApprovalTokenIssuer.spent_nonces` was `Arc<Mutex<HashSet<String>>>` — in-memory only. A token spent before a process restart could be replayed after restart (especially relevant when a CI signing secret is stable across restarts). Now optionally backed by a redb table:

- New `arbitraitor-store::SpentNonceStore` — redb-backed table mapping nonce → `()`. `open`, `contains`, `insert` (returns `false` on duplicate), `load_all`.
- New `ApprovalTokenIssuer::with_durable_store(store)` and `with_secret_and_durable_store(secret, store)` constructors: warm the in-memory cache from durable storage on startup; persist every spent nonce.
- `validate()` writes through to the durable store on every spend and rolls back the in-memory insert on durable duplicate / failure.
- In-memory-only path (`new` / `with_secret`) unchanged — regression-guarded.

## How this was validated

TDD: failing tests written first, then implementation. **19 new tests:**

| Area | Tests |
|---|---|
| Exec containment proofs (#381) | 6 — fail-closed w/o proofs, fail-closed w/ partial proofs (names missing control), all-proofs records enforced matrix, mediated/inspect need no proofs |
| ApprovalFile plan binding (#382) | 14 — schema/expiry/tamper rejection for every plan field, nonce/approver/expiry excluded from digest, JSON round-trip, `deny_unknown_fields`, empty-approver rejection, network/artifact digest distinction |
| SpentNonceStore durability (#388) | 9 — insert/contains/load_all semantics, persistence across reopen, duplicate-across-reopen rejected, fresh-nonce-after-reopen succeeds |
| MCP durable issuer (#388) | 3 — pre-restart spend rejected post-restart, fresh token accepted post-restart, in-memory-only regression guard |

## Pre-PR checks (all green locally)

```
cargo fmt --check                                                  ✅
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings  ✅
cargo build --workspace --all-targets --all-features               ✅
cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features                        ✅ 1140 passed, 15 skipped
rumdl check .                                                       ✅ 76 files clean
cargo run -p xtask -- docs-check                                    ✅ 26 ADRs match SUMMARY
```

## CHANGELOG

`[Unreleased] / Fixed` updated with three entries.

## Scope

Touches only `exec`, `cli`, `mcp`, `receipt`, `store` crates + `CHANGELOG.md` and `Cargo.lock`. No files outside the allowed set.

## Reviewer notes (adversarial review)

Things a reviewer should verify:
- [ ] `ControlProofs::require` treats every mandatory control identically — no control is silently optional.
- [ ] `ApprovalFile::compute_plan_digest` field order is stable and covers every materially-distinct dimension; no plan field is accidentally excluded.
- [ ] `SpentNonceStore::insert` rollback semantics in `ApprovalTokenIssuer::validate` are correct: durable-duplicate removes the in-memory entry before returning `Reused`.
- [ ] No new dependencies without justification (`redb`, `tempfile`, `uuid`, `hex`, `sha2`, `serde`, `thiserror` all already in workspace).

author: isukharev
body:
Fixes #65. Groundwork for #18 (Q3: Sync at scale + safety).

## Problem

`JiraService.Pull` re-fetched every issue via `GetIssue` after `Search` already returned the same fields — the adapter forwards the pull's field list to the search verbatim and maps both endpoints through the same `issueDTO`/`mapIssue`, so the sequential per-issue `GET` doubled HTTP round trips (and 429 exposure) on large `--limit 0` pulls for zero data gain. Nearby, the `.json` snapshot write error was discarded (`_ = safepath.WriteFile`), so a disk-full run reported issues as pulled with missing/stale snapshots.

## Fix

- The pull loop consumes the search projection directly; the per-issue `GetIssue` is gone. Field parity is structural: `jiraPullFields` always produces a non-empty list including `description`, so the adapter's thin search default can never kick in during a pull, and the old `GetIssue`-failure fallback already returned the identical search projection — removing the re-fetch changes no bytes, only halves the requests.
- Snapshot marshal/write failures now abort the pull with `snapshot KEY: …` context (partial results returned alongside the error, mirroring `conf pull` semantics).

## Tests

- `countingPullTracker` pins **0** per-issue `GetIssue` calls for a multi-issue pull (on revert the old loop increments it and the test fails).
- A pre-planted read-only snapshot aborts the pull loudly (skips as root; CI is non-root).
- The CLI httptest fixture now serves the full projection from `/search` and asserts **no** request touches `/rest/api/2/issue/` — a reintroduced re-fetch trips it even though the old code would swallow the 404.

## Verification

- `make test` — ok; `make lint` — 0 issues
- Live smoke on the configured test backend: a 3-issue pull produced `.md`+`.json` pairs with the description and 11 fields from the search projection alone.
- Adversarial review (Opus): no P1/P2; confirmed field parity (incl. `fields=nil`), no aliasing in the loop rewrite, unchanged limit/pagination semantics, and that inline `comment`/`attachment` projections behave identically on both endpoints (pre-existing behavior).

author: gkovbasenko
body:
## Summary

**Conventions Extractor** — analyzes a repo's source and config files, has a cheap LLM propose candidate coding conventions, and lets a user review/edit/accept/(soft-)reject each candidate in a new `/repos/:repoId/conventions` UI. Accepted candidates bundle into a `repo-conventions` skill and can be linked to an agent, reusing the existing Skills CRUD + agent-linking feature.

- Sample selection is entirely code-driven (repo-intel file ranking + explicit config-file reads) — no model call involved in choosing what to show the model.
- Every LLM-claimed candidate is verified against the actual repo clone (file exists, snippet found near the claimed line) before it's ever persisted or shown — hallucinated evidence is dropped silently.
- Reject is soft (`rejected_at`, not a delete); re-running extraction filters out already-rejected rule text (case/whitespace-normalized) so a repeat run doesn't resurface what the user dismissed.
- A `(workspace_id, repo_id, rule)` unique index + `onConflictDoNothing` prevents duplicate rows from concurrent extraction requests racing on the same empty rejected-rules read.
- A composite `(workspace_id, repo_id, created_at)` index backs the two ordered listing queries and the rejected-rules lookup, matching every other workspace/repo-scoped table in the schema.

**Security hardening** (found and fixed during self-review, each with a negative-control regression test):

- **Path traversal via LLM output**: the extraction pipeline reads files off disk using paths the LLM cited as evidence. Added `resolveClonePath`, a pure containment guard applied before every clone-relative read, closing a `../../etc/passwd`-style escape.
- **Symlink escape**: `resolveClonePath` alone doesn't catch a symlink *committed inside the clone* pointing outside it — worse, this path is hit unconditionally while reading config files for the prompt, no LLM cooperation needed. Added `resolveRealClonePath` (realpath + re-check) as the actual read boundary.
- **`isWithinRoot` hardening**: normalizes a trailing-separator root defensively (previously could double-up and silently reject everything) with a length guard so a literal `/` root can't collapse to an empty string and accept everything.
- Extraction is now rate-limited at 10/min (matching the other LLM-triggering route, `POST /pulls/:id/review`) instead of the app-wide 120/min default.
- `PATCH /conventions/:id` now validates `category` against the shared enum instead of accepting a bare string, and rejects an empty `{}` body (previously reached Drizzle's `.set()` with no fields and threw an unhandled 500).

**Correctness fixes:**

- `verifyEvidence` normalizes CRLF before splitting, so multi-line snippet citations from a CRLF file match correctly.
- `toConventionDto` safe-parses `category` instead of a raw type assertion — an invalid value now degrades to "no badge" for one row instead of failing the whole list's contract validation client-side.
- `BundleSkillModal` closes on a failed bundle-fetch or a failed agent-link (post skill-creation-success) instead of leaving a blank/stuck form that could double-create a skill on retry.
- `useConventions` hooks are now re-exported from the `lib/hooks` barrel, matching every other domain hook file (was silently `undefined` via the barrel import style used elsewhere).

**Skills UI** (reused by the Conventions → bundle-into-skill flow, gaps found while wiring it up):

- Added a delete button to the skill preview panel (the API and hook already existed; no component called them).
- Made `description`, `name`, and `type` editable in the skill preview panel via the existing Edit/Save/Cancel flow (all three were already patchable server-side but not exposed in the UI). Description uses a 3-row Textarea, matching the body field's widget.
- Moved Conventions into the Skills Lab nav group next to Skills/Agents, and added an inline evidence snippet + "merged from N accepted conventions" banner to the bundle modal, matching provided design mockups.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean on both `server/` and `client/`
- [x] Server hermetic tests: `verifyEvidence`, `resolveClonePath`/`resolveRealClonePath`/`isWithinRoot`, `buildSkillBody`/`buildConventionsPrompt`, repository field-by-field patch logic, route validation — all passing
- [x] Server integration tests (`conventions-extract.it.test.ts`): evidence verification, full accept/bundle lifecycle, soft-reject + no-resurface-on-re-extraction, mutual exclusivity (both directions + un-accept/un-reject), concurrent-extraction dedup, LLM failure path, 404 on missing candidate, repo-not-cloned / no-indexed-source-files errors — verified against a real Postgres directly, since this sandbox's testcontainers can't reach its Colima docker socket (pre-existing, documented limitation also affecting every other `*.it.test.ts` here)
- [x] Negative-control security tests: reverting the path-traversal fix lets a file outside the clone get read and persisted; reverting the symlink fix lets a symlinked evidence path and a symlinked config file's content escape the clone boundary
- [x] Client component tests across `ConventionCandidateCard`, `ConventionsPanel`, `BundleSkillModal`, `SkillPreview`, `SkillsView` — nullable-field branches, pending/error states, evidence-link positive/negative cases, delete/edit flows
- [x] `pr-self-review` ran clean (READY, no findings) after each hardening pass
- [ ] Manual: run extraction against a real seeded repo, accept a few candidates, bundle into a skill, confirm it links to the chosen agent's Skills tab

author: machuz
body:
Closes #333.

## What

`git subtree ... --squash` collapses an imported repo's whole history into a single commit authored by the integrator, so `git blame` credits every untouched imported line to them. On a real monorepo (`arsenal`, ~10 subtree-imported service repos) this put the integrator **#1 in survival gravity by 6.4×** over the actual top contributor across 454 modules — 45 subtree-squash commits, all theirs, one adding 6,731 files. The repo uses `Co-authored-by` **0 times**, so the co-author split has nothing to work with, and `--squash` discards the originals so `blame -C` can't recover them.

## How

- `git.SubtreeSquashCommits(ctx, repo, rev)` — scans for the machine-written `git-subtree-split` trailer. Exact (zero false positives — ordinary commits have an empty trailer), cheap (~0.2s over 24k commits, one log pass).
- `git.DropSubtreeSquashBlame` — drops blame lines still pointing at a squash commit, applied beside the existing excluded-author filter in all three blame pipelines (analyze / analyzer / timeline). A line edited after import blames to that editor and is **kept**, so only untouched imported code is suppressed.
- Config `attribute_subtree_squash` (**default false = suppress**), opt-in to restore prior behavior. Mirrors how the co-author split shipped the correct behavior as the default.
- Timeline scans squashes reachable from the **period boundary**, not HEAD, so a later import can't retroactively suppress an earlier window.

## Honest limitation

Removes the false credit; does **not** recover the true authors from the monorepo (their commits are gone). They remain correctly credited in the **source repos**, observed as their own galaxies.

## Tests

`internal/git/subtree_test.go`: trailer-only detection (no false positives), end-to-end blame suppression (integrator's 2 untouched imported lines dropped, real author's later edit kept), empty-set no-op. Full suite green; `go vet` + `gofmt` clean.

**Diff completo: 2 archivos `.md` nuevos en `docs/rewards/` (+321 líneas). Cero código funcional. Cero writes en Odoo/n8n** (la auditoría se hizo con métodos exclusivamente de lectura y el plan es diseño puro).

| Doc | Qué es |
|-----|--------|
| `ODOO_REWARDS_B2B_READONLY_AUDIT.md` | Auditoría del Odoo productivo: stack loyalty nativo completo instalado pero SIN programa real (solo el seed "Gift Cards", 0 cards, 0 historial); customizaciones existentes (`gf_w14_loyalty_engine`, `gf_partner_loyalty`); pedidos PWA como sale.order normales con IVA 0 real; **decisiones de negocio confirmadas por Yamil** (tasa 1%, 1pt=$1 promocional, 180d+gracia 90, 1 canje/mes, matriz por plaza/SKU); paquete de trabajo S1–S10 para Sebastián + 13 preguntas técnicas. Con corrección fechada sobre W14 tras leer su código fuente |
| `ODOO_REWARDS_B2B_TECHNICAL_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` | Plan técnico ejecutable: módulo hermano **`gf_b2b_loyalty`** (no tocar W14/B2C); nativos como capa de datos; matriz comercial `gf.loyalty.point.rule` (plaza×SKU×multiplicador×vigencia, exclusiones por config); libro `gf.loyalty.accrual` idempotente (unique por documento fuente) con expiración FIFO 180d y cron que nace INACTIVO (gracia 90d); `gf_loyalty_redeem` atómico (límite mensual dentro de la transacción, folio, errores tipados, replay por idempotency key); acumulación contado al picking-done y crédito proporcional a conciliación; reversa con saldo negativo controlado; contrato Odoo→PWA; **8 fases con S/N por fase** |

### Para Codex (focos de auditoría sugeridos)

## Summary
- Production is currently 500ing on every request because `CLOUDINARY_URL` is set in Vercel without the required `cloudinary://` scheme. The `cloudinary` package parses that env var at import time and raises `ValueError`, which happens during `django.setup()` and takes down the whole app before any view can run — including static assets and the admin.
- Only enable `cloudinary_storage`/`cloudinary` when the URL actually starts with `cloudinary://`; otherwise log a warning and fall back to local media storage instead of crashing the site.
- Adds `oghie/test_settings.py` with regression tests covering: malformed `CLOUDINARY_URL` is ignored, well-formed `CLOUDINARY_URL` enables cloudinary storage, and missing `CLOUDINARY_URL` falls back to default storage (plus existing serverless connection-pooling tests).

## Test plan
- [x] `python manage.py test` — 14/14 passing, including the 3 new `CloudinaryUrlConfigTests`
- [ ] After merge/deploy, confirm `oghie-store.vercel.app` returns 200 again
- [ ] Separately fix the malformed `CLOUDINARY_URL` value in the Vercel project settings (using a newly rotated secret) so real image uploads to Cloudinary work

🎯 **What:** The procedural drawing functions (`put`, `line`, `ellipse`, etc.) inside several monster entity definitions (`blood_plant.ts`, `borshchevik.ts`, `trubnyy_avtomat.ts`) previously accepted individual `r, g, b, a` parameters, resulting in excessive function arity (up to 10 parameters). They have been refactored to accept a single packed `color: number` instead.

💡 **Why:** This improves readability and maintainability by keeping the parameter counts much lower and avoiding excessive boilerplate when repeatedly pushing pixels to the canvas buffer.

✅ **Verification:** Verified by compiling the Typescript codebase successfully via `npm run typecheck` and running generation tests (`npm run test:generation`) and unit tests (`npm run test:unit`) which did not catch any regressions or runtime errors.

✨ **Result:** Drawing helper function signatures are simpler and procedural sprite codebase is significantly cleaner without altering visual behavior.

author: dacoburn
body:
# Pull Request Checklist

**Before submitting, make sure you've checked the following:**

- [x] **Linked Issue/Discussion:** This PR references an existing [[Issue](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues)](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues) or [[Discussion](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions)](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions) — Closes #XXXXX
- [x] **Target branch:** The pull request targets the `dev` branch. **PRs targeting `main` will be immediately closed.**
- [x] **Description:** A concise description of the changes is provided below.
- [x] **Documentation:** N/A — spec-compliance bug fix, no user-facing configuration or documented behavior changes.
- [x] **Dependencies:** N/A — no dependency changes.
- [x] **Changelog:** A changelog entry following [[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/)](https://keepachangelog.com/) format is included at the bottom.
- [x] **Testing:** Manual tests have been performed to verify the fix/feature works correctly and does not introduce regressions. Screenshots or recordings are included where applicable.
- [x] **No Unchecked AI Code:** This PR is either human-written or has undergone thorough human review AND manual testing. Unreviewed AI-generated PRs may be closed immediately.
- [x] **Self-Review:** A self-review of the code has been performed, ensuring adherence to project coding standards.
- [x] **Architecture:** Smart defaults are preferred over new settings. Local state is used for ephemeral UI logic. Major architectural or UX changes have been discussed first.
- [x] **Git Hygiene:** The PR is atomic (one logical change), rebased on `dev`, and contains no unrelated commits.
- [x] **Title Prefix:** The PR title uses the **fix** prefix.

# Changelog Entry

### Description

- The Anthropic-compatible streaming converter (`openai_stream_to_anthropic_stream` in `backend/open_webui/utils/anthropic.py`) tracks `prompt_tokens` from upstream OpenAI usage chunks into its `input_tokens` variable, but the final `message_delta` event only emits `output_tokens`. Since `message_start` is emitted before upstream usage is known (and therefore carries `input_tokens: 0`), the final `message_delta` is the only event where a client can receive the real input token count — and it was missing. As a result, every Anthropic-format client received `input_tokens = 0` on all streamed responses. For Claude Code pointed at Open WebUI via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, this broke the context meter (`/context` read near-empty regardless of prompt size), prevented auto-compaction from ever triggering, and undercounted cost, since the prompt is typically the majority of billed tokens.
- This change adds the already-tracked `input_tokens` variable to the emitted `message_delta` usage object — a one-line diff. It also makes the streaming path consistent with the non-streaming converter (`openai_response_to_anthropic`), which already maps `prompt_tokens` → `input_tokens` correctly.

### Added

- N/A

### Changed

- N/A

### Deprecated

- N/A

### Removed

- N/A

### Fixed

- Anthropic-compatible streaming responses now include `input_tokens` in the final `message_delta` usage object, matching the Anthropic Messages streaming specification and the existing non-streaming converter. This fixes context tracking, auto-compaction, and cost accounting in Anthropic-format clients such as Claude Code.

### Security

- N/A

### Breaking Changes

- N/A

---

### Additional Information

- Root cause: `message_delta` was emitted as `'usage': {'output_tokens': output_tokens}` while `input_tokens` was captured from upstream usage chunks a few lines earlier but never included in the emitted event.
- The non-streaming path already emits `input_tokens` correctly, so this is an internal consistency fix rather than a behavior change.
- No new settings, no dependency changes, single-line diff.
- Searched existing issues/PRs for duplicates; none found. Nearest related (all closed, different layers): #23322 (usage-key normalization in chat persistence), #21347 (analytics token tracking), #22861 (Anthropic compat endpoint availability on the Ollama proxy). None address the streaming translator's `message_delta` usage.

### Screenshots or Videos

Streaming request through `/api/v1/messages` against an OpenAI-compatible backend that reports usage.

Before (real input token count never reaches the client):

```
event: message_start
data: {"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": "msg_...", "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [], "model": "...", "stop_reason": null, "stop_sequence": null, "usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}}}

event: message_delta
data: {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "max_tokens", "stop_sequence": null}, "usage": {"output_tokens": 32}}
```

After:

```
event: message_delta
data: {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "max_tokens", "stop_sequence": null}, "usage": {"input_tokens": 17, "output_tokens": 32}}
```

Verified end-to-end with Claude Code configured against Open WebUI via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`: the context meter and cost reporting now reflect real prompt size, and auto-compaction has a real value to trigger against.

author: smsag
body:
## Summary

Fixes the reported drag issue: **a card was picked up the instant you pressed it.**

- **Touch (mobile):** drag started on `touchstart` with no threshold at all — any tap picked up the card.
- **Mouse (desktop):** a 5px threshold, no time delay — hair-trigger, so a slightly imprecise click dragged.

This introduces a shared pointer-drag gesture, `src/shared/drag-gesture.ts`, used by all four draggable card canvases (card blocks, Story, Roadmap, SCQA grid):

- A drag begins **only after the pointer moves past an 8px threshold** — a plain click or tap never drags.
- On touch, the card is **no longer picked up on `touchstart`**; the initial touch can still scroll until the threshold is crossed, then the drag takes over and suppresses scrolling.
- `hold-still` is deliberately left free for the **long-press preview** gesture coming in a later PR.
- SCQA grid gains touch drag it didn't have; the four renderers now share **one** gesture implementation instead of four near-identical copies.
- Window-aware (binds listeners on the card's own document, so pop-out Obsidian windows keep working).

## Decisions baked in (from discussion)

- Movement-threshold gating (no literal time-delay), so it never collides with the future long-press-for-preview.
- Unified across all four draggable card types.

## Test plan

- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` — clean.
- `npx vitest run` — 376 tests pass, including 6 new gesture tests. Key regressions covered: a tiny-movement click and a bare `touchstart` do **not** drag; a drag starts once movement passes the threshold; stray moves after release are ignored; `shouldStart` guards (buttons) are respected.
- Not yet verified live in Obsidian (no isolated dev vault here); manual check recommended: click a card without dragging (shouldn't move), then drag deliberately (should reorder), on desktop and mobile.

This is **PR 1 of 3** in the linked-card hover-preview effort. PR 2 wires the link affordance into the card types; PR 3 adds the clipped-section preview (desktop Cmd-hover + mobile long-press), which reuses the hold-still gesture seam this PR leaves open.

## [1.12.0] - 2026-07-05

### Added
- Editable layout partials: `layout`, `header`, `footer`, and a new `styles`
  partial join the templates admin API (`partial.{name}` keys in the same
  override store — body-only, engine-linted, reset-to-default). The layout's
  embedded CSS moved into the `styles` partial (included bare in the layout
  `<head>`; the partial carries its own `<style>` wrapper so the templates
  stay IDE-parseable), making a styles override the clean way to restyle
  every email without touching layout structure. The `default` template
  became body-only like the other four — it previously shipped as a full
  document with a duplicated, drifting copy of the CSS that bypassed the
  layout entirely; it now renders through the layout + shared styles. Partial resolution
  is DB-first everywhere: the engine and the layout wrapper consult the
  override store before shipped files.

author: mendesleo1986-droid
body:
## Resumo

- **Bug crítico DM**: badge de mensagens não lidas não aparecia para a pedagoga (e qualquer usuário que fechasse o painel sem clicar "←")
- **Proteção de dados**: guarda adicional impede sobrescrever Firestore com lista de usuários vazia
- **Recuperação expandida**: escaneia mais fontes para reconstruir contas apagadas

## Detalhes

### Correção do badge DM (bug da pedagoga)

**Causa raiz:** quando o painel de chat era fechado sem clicar "←", o listener do thread DM (`_chatDMUnsub`) continuava ativo em background. Ao receber uma nova mensagem, o listener disparava `chatMarcarVisto('dm')`, atualizando o `seenTs` no localStorage para `Date.now()` — mesmo sem o usuário ver nada. Quando o `_dmInboxUnsub` verificava `inboxTs > seenTs`, o resultado era `false` (os dois timestamps eram aproximadamente iguais) e o badge nunca aparecia.

**Por que funcionava para o diretor:** o diretor normalmente não abre a conversa com a pedagoga, então `_chatDMAtivo` era null e `_chatDMUnsub` não estava subscrito para aquela conversa.

**Correções aplicadas:**
1. `_chatDMUnsub` callback: só chama `chatMarcarVisto('dm')` se o painel estiver aberto
2. `fecharChatPanel()`: chama `voltarListaDM()` para cancelar a subscription do thread e limpar `_chatDMAtivo`
3. `toggleChatPanel()` (fechar): idem

### Proteção de dados

```js
// Antes
if (_usuariosCarregado) batch.set(FSREF('usuarios'), { data: db.usuarios });

// Depois
if (_usuariosCarregado && db.usuarios.length > 0) batch.set(FSREF('usuarios'), { data: db.usuarios });
```

Impede que qualquer bug futuro sobrescreva o documento `usuarios` no Firestore com uma lista vazia.

### Recuperação de usuários expandida

`reconstruirUsuariosApagados()` agora escaneia 4 fontes em vez de 2:

| Fonte | ID original preservado? |
|-------|------------------------|
| `chatGeral` (autorId/autorNome) | ✅ Sim |
| `horaAtividade` (professoraId/professoraNome) | ✅ Sim |
| `turmas` (t.prof — nome) | ⚠️ Novo ID gerado |
| `planejamentos` (p.prof — nome) | ⚠️ Novo ID gerado |

Professoras encontradas apenas em turmas/planejamentos (que nunca enviaram mensagem nem preencheram hora-atividade) agora também são recuperadas, com aviso de que o histórico não será revinculado automaticamente.

author: zzwong
body:
## Summary

Closes #7. Previously there was no way to find a WiiM/Linkplay device without already knowing its host/IP — a hard blocker for first-run setup, and for an agent asked to control "my WiiM speaker" with nothing configured yet.

`wiim discover` multicasts an SSDP `M-SEARCH` (`ST: upnp:rootdevice`) to `239.255.255.250:1900` and collects the source IP of every UDP reply — stdlib `net` only, no new dependency. Since any UPnP device answers that search (smart TVs, printers, routers — not just Linkplay speakers), every responding IP is then validated with a direct `getStatusEx` call; only hosts that actually answer the WiiM HTTP API make it into the result. This also means `discover` works for any Linkplay device, not just WiiM, since validation doesn't check for anything WiiM-specific — it ties into the existing `docs/api.md#compatibility` story.

```bash
wiim discover
wiim --json discover
wiim --timeout 5 discover   # override the default 3s SSDP wait window
```

Scope note per the issue: this deliberately doesn't go as deep as `pywiim`'s discovery (no `--no-validate` network-scan fallback, no UPnP `description.xml` capability enrichment) — just enough to remove the "how do I even get a host" blocker.

### Design for testability
Network I/O (`ssdpSearchFunc`) and the validation HTTP call (`newDiscoveryClient`) are both swappable package vars, mirroring the existing `newDevice` pattern used throughout `cli_test.go`. Command wiring, filtering (non-WiiM responders dropped), sorting, and formatting are all unit tested against fakes — no real network needed. One test does exercise the real UDP socket path directly (`ssdpSearch` with a 150ms timeout), asserting it completes without error/hanging when nothing responds; confirmed this doesn't require joining the multicast group, just an outbound send + a normal unicast-reply listen on the same socket.

### Docs
- `README.md`: `discover` added to the command list, a "Configuration" callout for "don't know your host yet," and a usage note on what it filters and why.
- `docs/api.md`: new "Discovery" section explaining the SSDP mechanism and its limits (IPv4 only, no cross-subnet discovery), plus a `discover` row in the command table.
- `skills/wiim/SKILL.md`: tells an agent to try `wiim discover` (no `--host` needed, read-only, safe to run unprompted) before asking the user for a host.

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`
- [x] `go test ./... -race` — all passing, including new discovery/format/command tests
- [x] `gofmt -l .` — clean, `golangci-lint run ./...` — 0 issues
- [x] Manual: built the binary and ran `wiim discover`, `wiim --json discover`, and `wiim --timeout 1 discover` on this sandbox's network (no WiiM device present) — all completed cleanly in the expected time with "No devices found." / `[]`, exit code 0 (not treated as a failure)
- [ ] Manual verification against a real WiiM/Linkplay device on an actual LAN would be good to confirm end-to-end, since this sandbox has no such device to test against

## Summary

**PR 2 of the #182 build** (the deterministic retrieval core landed in #209). This slice is the **corpus generator** — it turns an instrument's candle history into the set of past setups the retriever searches, still entirely pure/LLM-free.

- **`SetupFeatureExtractor`** (pure) — fingerprints a formed count into the `SetupFeatures` the analog search compares: direction and confluence strength from the `WaveLevels`, and **reward:risk + distance-to-invalidation from the same `RiskCalculator` the risk box uses** (entry = current price). Query setup and every historical setup are therefore described on identical terms. Momentum regimes (RSI/MACD) are passed in already-normalised, since they come from the indicator calculator, not the geometry.
- **`SetupHistoryBuilder`** (pure) — replays the deterministic pipeline over history with the **same no-lookahead sweep as the backtest** (`CandleWindow` bounded at each cutoff, `AnalysisOutcomeEvaluator` scoring only the candles that *follow*). Each row records where the setup formed, its fingerprint, and how it actually resolved — structurally incapable of leaking the future. The momentum regimes arrive through a `Func<CandleWindow, (double, double)>` delegate so the sweep stays a pure, testable function (the indicator calculator supplies it in production; tests stub it).

Advances #182 (corpus generator; endpoint + narrator + frontend remain).

## Type of change

- [x] `feat` — new feature (deterministic corpus generator)

## How was this tested?

- **9 new unit tests**; full backend suite **585 passed / 12 skipped** against native Postgres.
- **Coverage 92.37%** (gate 90%); **both new files 100% line-covered**. ArchitectureTests green.
- Key test — **no-lookahead**: poisoning the post-cutoff candles with a violent crash cannot change the *features* of any setup formed before the poison point (`SetupHistoryBuilderTests.Build_NoLookahead_PoisonedFutureDoesNotChangeEarlierSetupFeatures`). Plus determinism, momentum-delegate application, and the reward:risk / distance / confluence-strength math (`SetupFeatureExtractorTests`).

## Checklist

- [x] `dotnet test` passes locally (585/12-skipped)
- [x] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits

- `IHistoricalSetupCorpus` + an Infrastructure provider wiring candles + the Skender indicator delegate into `SetupHistoryBuilder`
- `GET /api/wave-analysis/analogs` endpoint returning the deterministic `AnalogReport`

author: carpenike
body:
## Summary
The definitive fix for the persistent **STALE** banner, found by live in-browser debugging of the deployed app.

**Symptom:** on load the coach never left `connecting`. Both WS clients sat at `state: "disconnected"` with **no socket**, and **zero sockets were ever created** — `connect()` never landed — even though auth was ready (`authReady` true) and CAN telemetry was fresh (`canbus: "active"`). Only a manual **Retry** recovered it.

## Root cause
`useWebSocket`'s connection-creation effect depends on the memoized message handler, whose identity **changes every render**: callers pass an inline handler / a fresh array each render —
- `useEntityWebSocket` → `subscriptions: [{ type: 'entity_update', handler: … }]`
- `useSystemStatusWebSocket` → inline `onMessage: () => …`

So the effect re-ran on **every render**, releasing and recreating the connection, while the one-shot autoConnect effect (keyed only on `[autoConnect]`) never re-fired to reconnect the fresh client. The socket was torn down before it could finish connecting. Manual Retry calls `connect()` directly, which is why it recovered — the "loads disconnected, force connect" behavior.

This is a pre-existing latent bug; my earlier #208/#213 (WS auth-gating + token refresh) just added re-renders that made it fire *reliably*.

## Fix
Hold `onMessage` and the prop `subscriptions` in refs and make `memoizedOnMessage` referentially **stable** (empty deps). The connection is created once and survives re-renders, so the autoConnect effect connects a stable client on load.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` and production `vite build` pass; changed lines have no new ESLint findings.
- **Verified live in-browser after deploy**: on a fresh hard-reload the coach reaches LIVE on its own — `websocket: "connected"`, a real socket is created and stays open, no manual Retry. (Results in the PR thread / session.)

Follow-up still worth doing: migrate the entity/telemetry stream to SSE so the browser owns reconnection and this class of lifecycle bug goes away for good.

author: mikelward
body:
## Problem

A dismiss (a lone **Done** or a **Sweep**) triggers a momentary, self-inflicted document collapse: a beat *after* the row-removal paints, the list reflows to a far shorter height for ~2 frames, then recovers. The scroll-jump diagnostics captured it cleanly:

```
10702ms  Done … max=561          ← ceiling already collapsing at the flip
10738ms  scroll y=561 (-433) max=1339 lock=off   ← clamped 994→561, freeze already gone
10801ms  resize … max=1339       ← only ~75px (one row) permanently shrinks
```

The height-freeze is taken correctly (at the tall pre-collapse height, while the row is still on screen), but the no-refetch release path cleared it on the row-removal commit — *before* the dip bottoms out. So the collapse landed unguarded (`lock=off`), the browser clamped `window.scrollY` toward the top, and the clamped offset stuck once the height recovered. Net damage: a ~433px jump-to-top from a change that only permanently removed one row.

## Fix

Defer the release a few animation frames past the removal commit so the `min-height` freeze stays engaged through the collapse and the document never gets short enough to clamp. The release then lands on the recovered height.

- Lives on the **shared no-refetch release effect**, so it covers *every* local-removal dismiss — single Done and Sweep alike — not just one path. (The earlier Done at 4033ms in the trace also collapsed to `max=847`; it only escaped a jump because its offset happened to sit below that floor.)
- A background refresh grabbing the lock, a fresh dismiss, or unmount cancels/supersedes the pending release.
- `releaseBodyHeight`'s existing `holdFor` still restores the offset if a frame happens to land mid-collapse, so the exact frame count isn't load-bearing.

## Tests

- New: `installScrollModel` gains a transient-collapse injector; two regression tests assert the scroll offset survives the collapse for a single **Done** and for a **Sweep**, driving the settle frames deterministically via a manual-rAF helper.
- Updated the three bottom-sweep deferred-release tests to flush the settle frames before their scroll dispatch (the deferred-on-scroll slack is now armed a few frames later).
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (2120 tests) all green.

## Deploy

Frontend-only — no backend migration or Edge Function deploy required.

author: michaelfisher1997
body:
## Summary

Fixes #729

`InputBinding.eql()` collapsed the `.key` and `.key_alt` variants into a shared code path (`modules/engine-input/src/interfaces.zig:77-100`), comparing only the underlying `Key` value and discarding the variant tag. This made `InputBinding{ .key = .w }.eql(InputBinding{ .key_alt = .w })` return `true` when the variants are distinct.

## Impact

The input mapper's `isBindingStateActive`/`isBindingStatePressed`/`isBindingStateReleased` (`modules/game-core/src/input_mapper.zig:141-166`) all rely on `eql`, so querying a `.key` binding would incorrectly match a `.key_alt` binding with the same physical key. The `InputBinding` union explicitly defines `.key` and `.key_alt` as separate variants so an action can have both a primary binding (e.g. `W`) and an alternate binding (e.g. `Up Arrow`) — the old behavior defeated that distinction.

## Changes

- **`modules/engine-input/src/interfaces.zig`** — Rewrote `eql` to compare variant tags explicitly. `.key` only equals `.key`; `.key_alt` only equals `.key_alt`; matching requires both the variant and the underlying value to be equal.
- **`modules/game-core/src/input_mapper.zig`** — Updated the `InputBinding equality` test that previously asserted the buggy equality (now verifies `.key != .key_alt` with the same key, and `.key_alt == .key_alt`).
- **`src/game/input_mapper_tests.zig`** — Replaced the `key vs key_alt same key` test (which documented the bug) with tests asserting the variants are distinct, plus a positive test confirming same-variant equality.

## Verification

- `zig fmt src/ modules/` — clean
- `zig build test` — **277/277 tests pass**
- Confirmed the new test `InputBinding.eql key vs key_alt same key are distinct` **fails** against the old buggy `eql` (verified by temporarily reverting the fix) and **passes** with the fix in place, proving the test catches the regression.

## Acceptance Criteria (from issue)

- [x] `eql` returns `false` when comparing `.key` against `.key_alt` (same key)
- [x] New unit tests verify `.key` and `.key_alt` are treated as distinct
- [x] No regression in existing `eql` tests

body:
## Why

`GET /routines` (and single-routine reads) already surface static and
scheduling facts about a routine — `enabled`, `agent_registered`,
`schedule_description`, `next_run_at`, etc. — but nothing about whether the
routine's agent is executing **right now**. The only way to know is to shell
into the host and run `tmux ls`. Closes #438.

The daemon already has the exact primitive needed: `tmux_session_prefix` +
`tmux_session_prefix_alive` (`src/routines/command.rs`,
`src/routines/cleanup/session.rs`) is the overlap-guard probe `svc_trigger`
uses (#514) to detect "is a previous fire of this routine still running" —
matching any live tmux session under the routine's `moadim-{slug}-` prefix,
not a single fixed name. It was already `pub(crate)` and used from
`service_trigger.rs`, just never surfaced on the read path.

## What changed

- `RoutineResponse` (`src/routines/model.rs`) gains a derived, non-persisted
  `is_running: bool` field, computed in `from_routine` by reusing the
  existing overlap-guard probe — no new tmux-probing logic.
- Regenerated `apis/openapi.json` via the repo's existing self-healing test
  (`committed_spec_is_current`).
- Added a changeset (`.changeset/routine-is-running-field.md`, `minor`,
  matching the precedent set by the sibling `next_run_at` field addition).

## Not in scope

The linked issue's acceptance criteria also ask for a UI "RUNNING" badge.
Keeping this PR to the backend field only, since the UI treatment is a
separate, independently reviewable change; the field is available on the
API today for anyone who wants to build that next.

## Testing

- `cargo build` — clean
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean

author: ianbrandt
body:
Fixes #178.

`SyntheticClassIntegrity.checkOwner()` required a non-null `referencedModule` on `FILE_FACADE` / `MULTI_FILE_CLASS_PART` owners. That field is populated only by `KotlinModuleReferenceInitializer`, which needs the caller to have first read a real `META-INF/*.kotlin_module` resource into a `ResourceFilePool`. A caller running `KotlinMetadataAsserter` as a general Kotlin-metadata sanity check, without wiring that resource, gets a spurious "has no referenced module" warning for every top-level function or property callable reference, and the reference's metadata is discarded.

This drops the `referencedModule` check, keeping the `owner` null-check (which `KotlinCallableReferenceInitializer` always populates). It matches the sibling constraints `FileFacadeIntegrity` and `MultiFilePartIntegrity`, which already omit the same check, and nothing on the owner path (`getOwner()`, `getName()`, `getSignature()`, `ownerAccept()`) reads `referencedModule`.

- Adds a regression test running the asserter on a freshly-compiled top-level function reference with an empty `ResourceFilePool`, asserting the callable-reference metadata survives.
- Adds a release-notes entry under 9.3.3.

Full `:proguard-core:test` suite passes (1063 tests, 4 skipped); `spotlessCheck` is clean.

author: ionfwsrijan
body:
## Description
The `ParserSandboxError` exception includes captured stderr output (up to 2000 chars) in its message, which propagates through the call stack into `task.error_message` in the database and ultimately to the API response. Additionally, `_BOOTSTRAP_TEMPLATE.format()` uses user-influenced `parser_path` which can cause format-string injection.

### Changes
1. **`backend/secuscan/parser_sandbox.py:ParserSandboxError`** — Apply `redact()` to the stderr excerpt and reduce limit from 2000 to 500 chars. This ensures secrets in parser diagnostic output are sanitized before they reach the API layer.
2. **`backend/secuscan/parser_sandbox.py:_BOOTSTRAP_TEMPLATE`** — Replace `str.format()` with `str.replace()` using sentinel markers (`__MAX_INPUT_BYTES__`, `__PARSER_PATH_REPR__`) to prevent format-string injection via user-influenced `parser_path`.
3. **`backend/secuscan/executor.py:execute_task()`** — Apply `redact()` to `str(e)` before storing as `error_message` in the general exception handler.
4. **`backend/secuscan/executor.py:_parse_results()`** — Apply `redact()` to the error message in the generic exception handler.
5. **`backend/secuscan/parser_sandbox.py`** — Updated module docstring with security notes about stderr sensitivity.

### Impact
- Secrets in parser stderr output are redacted before reaching the API response
- Format-string injection via plugin file paths is eliminated
- Error messages stored in the database are sanitized
- Diagnostic stderr is still captured for logging but sanitized before user-facing exposure

### Files Changed
- `backend/secuscan/parser_sandbox.py` — ParserSandboxError sanitization, template injection fix, docstring update
- `backend/secuscan/executor.py` — redact() applied in exception handlers

Closes #1626

author: wi-wissen
body:
## Was ist kaputt

Der CI-Lauf auf `main` (Commit `94ff09c`, *„fix upgrade laravel routing priorities"*) schlägt fehl — **nicht** wegen falscher Runtimes. PHP 8.5 und Node 24 sind korrekt: `composer.json` verlangt `php: ^8.5` und `laravel/framework: ^13.0`, und die Node-20-Deprecation ist nur eine Warnung (Actions laufen automatisch auf Node 24).

Der Fehler ist genau ein Test:

```
FAILED Tests\Feature\Admin\StaticControllerTest > noad page renders
Expected response status code [200] but received 404.
```

## Ursache

Der Routing-Refactor hat `/noad` aus einer domain-agnostischen Route in die Hub-Subdomain-Gruppe verschoben (`routes/web.php:105`, Gruppe `config('app.domain_hub')` = `{subdomain}.localhost`). `artisan route:list` bestätigt:

```
GET|HEAD  {subdomain}.localhost/noad ... StaticController@noad
```

Der Test rief aber weiter `http://localhost/noad` auf — die Hauptdomain kennt die Route nicht mehr → 404. Das Route-Placement ist gewollt (der Kommentar dort: „relative ad links like `/noad` resolve on hubs"), also muss der Test die Hub-Subdomain ansteuern.

## Änderung

`tests/Feature/Admin/StaticControllerTest.php`: Der `noad`-Test ruft nun `http://example.localhost/noad` auf, konsistent mit der übrigen Hub-Test-Konvention (`http://<hub>.localhost/`).

## Verifikation

- `artisan route:list --path=noad` bestätigt die Subdomain-Bindung als Ursache.
- Der DB-gestützte Feature-Test läuft in der CI (PHP 8.5 + MariaDB); lokal ist MariaDB hier nicht installierbar.
- `pint` grün.

author: kensuenobu
body:
## What was done and why

Implements **MFX-6.3: Preview + download** — the third step of the Export UI epic (MFX-EPIC-6, #3819). After the fidelity acknowledgement, the ExportDialog no longer downloads the emitted document blindly: it emits via the existing `POST /api/export/document` proxy and shows the artifact in a **preview card** first, per the design mockup.

- **`ArtifactPreviewCard.tsx`** — the emitted document's filename, scrollable content, size/media-type meta line, and the mockup's **"valid · round-trip OK"** status badge.
- **`exportArtifactPreview.ts`** (pure, unit-tested) — badge derivation with honest claims only:
  - the **valid** half re-parses the document client-side (JSON via `JSON.parse` — including Avro `.avsc` — YAML via the existing `yaml` dep). Formats without a browser parser (`.proto`, `.graphql`) make **no** validity claim instead of faking one; a failed parse renders a red `invalid JSON/YAML` badge.
  - the **round-trip** half reads the MFX-2.5 dry-run loss report already fetched for the fidelity step: a clean report → `round-trip OK` (green), predicted degradation → `lossy round-trip` (amber). The hint line under the preview states both bases. The *empirical* server-side round-trip surfaces later with MFX-5.3/6.4 (the round-trip modules exist in `apiome-rest` but have no REST surface yet).
- **Download single/zip** — two on-demand buttons on the preview: the single file (served media type + `Content-Disposition` filename), or a **`.zip`** built client-side by **`zipBundle.ts`**, a dependency-free stored-ZIP writer (UTF-8/EFS names, fixed DOS-epoch timestamp for deterministic output, duplicate-path guard). It takes a file *list*, so multi-file bundles (e.g. Avro per-subject `.avsc`) flow through unchanged once the MFX-4.2 bundle endpoint returns them; today the document proxy returns the emitter's primary file (MFX-4.1 scope).

Scope note: all backend packaging/validation tickets (epics 3/4/5) are still open, so this stays strictly within `apiome-ui` against today's endpoints, as the ticket's affected-modules field specifies.

## How to test

- `cd apiome-ui && yarn test` — full suite: 312 suites / 4388 tests green, including:
  - `tests/exportArtifactPreview.test.ts` — syntax detection, JSON/YAML validation, badge matrix, size/zip-name helpers (25 tests with `zipBundle`).
  - `tests/zipBundle.test.ts` — ZIP format-level assertions: CRC-32 check vectors, local/central/EOCD record layout, offsets, UTF-8 flag, determinism, duplicate rejection. Also verified externally: archives pass `unzip -t` and read back via Python `zipfile` (names + content intact).
  - `tests/ExportDialog.test.tsx` — 7 new MFX-6.3 tests: preview-before-download, badge wording per case (`valid · round-trip OK`, `lossy round-trip`, `invalid JSON`), on-demand single and zip downloads with correct filenames/media types.
- `yarn build` (turbo) — green.
- Manually: open a version's Export dialog → pick a target → acknowledge if lossy → **Export** → review the preview + badge → **Download `<file>`** or **Download .zip**.

## Risk / notes

- The Export step's behavior changes from *immediate download* to *preview, then download on demand* — intentional per the mockup and ticket. `onExported` now fires when the emit succeeds (doc updated).
- The zip currently wraps the single returned file; correct multi-file bundles depend on MFX-4.2 (server) and need no further UI changes here.
- Badge claims are deliberately conservative — nothing is asserted that wasn't actually checked or predicted.

Closes #3857

## Key Changes

- **GitExecutor interface** — default `exec.Command("git", …)` implementation with package-level swappable executor and `IsInstalled()` helper

- **Branch operations** — `CurrentBranch`, `BranchExists`, `CreateBranch`, `ListBranches`, `DeleteBranch` with `ErrBranchExists`/`ErrBranchNotFound` errors
- **Worktree operations** — `CreateWorktree`, `ListWorktrees` (with porcelain parsing), `RemoveWorktree` with `ErrWorktreeExists` error
- **Working tree status** — `GetStatus`, `IsClean` via `git status --porcelain`
- **Test coverage** — table-driven tests for all operations against real temp repos; `internal/git/testutil/` package with `CreateTempRepo`, `CreateCommit` helpers

CLI commands (`lane new`, `ls`, `done`) and config system are Sprint 2/3 scope.

author: artraccoon
body:
### Motivation
- The bot must be able to route Telegram polling and provider HTTP requests through a local SOCKS5/HTTP proxy when the server cannot reach Telegram directly. 
- The change provides an opt-in `PROXY_URL` configuration so a local proxy (e.g. `socks5://127.0.0.1:1080`) can be used without hardcoding addresses. 
- Preserve current behavior when no proxy is configured by allowing an empty/blank `PROXY_URL`.

### Description
- Add `proxy_url: str | None` to `Settings` with a `@field_validator` that normalizes empty strings to `None` in `app/config.py` and expose `PROXY_URL` in `.env.example` and `docker-compose.yml`.
- Create `create_bot` factory in `app/bot.py` that constructs `aiogram.Bot` with an `AiohttpSession(proxy=...)` when `settings.proxy_url` is set and otherwise constructs a normal `Bot`.
- Update `BaseProvider` in `app/providers/base.py` to accept `proxy_url` and pass it to `httpx.AsyncClient` via the `proxy` kwarg, and forward `settings.proxy_url` into each provider from `app/providers/__init__.py`.
- Add SOCKS-related dependencies to `pyproject.toml` by switching to `httpx[socks]` and adding `aiohttp-socks`, and document proxy usage in `README.md`.

author: mabry1985
body:
## Problem
On every boot, fleet **members** log:
```
[fleet] autostart: no workspace 'matt-7689' — skipping (create it first)
```
for every id in the roster — even though the fleet is healthy and those members are running. Confusing and noisy.

## Root cause
`start_autostart_members()` is meant to be hub-only. The guarantee was *"by construction"*: a member runs `PROTOAGENT_INSTANCE`-scoped, so its own **config** carries no autostart roster → no-op.

But that only covers the **config** source. `autostart_members()` falls back to the `PROTOAGENT_FLEET_AUTOSTART` **env**, and a member inherits that env from the hub that spawned it. So inside a member the roster is non-empty, and the loop scans the member's *own* (empty) workspaces root (`<member>/workspaces`) → `_find` returns `None` → the spurious warning, once per id.

Verified live: a member's env carries `PROTOAGENT_FLEET_AUTOSTART=cindy-0ccd,matt-7689`, its `workspaces_root()` is its own empty dir, and `is_workspace_member()` is `True`.

## Fix
Enforce hub-only rather than assume it: bail when `manager.is_workspace_member()` — the same guard `shutdown_all` already uses. `reconcile_on_boot` is unaffected (it self-scopes harmlessly).

## Test
`test_start_autostart_is_hub_only_even_with_inherited_env` — a non-empty roster + `is_workspace_member()=True` returns `[]` and spawns nothing. Full autostart/reconcile suite green (6 passed).

body:
## Summary

Adds an **additive** self-employed-profits and employer-secondary case family to the UK oracle grid, comparing the composed rulespec-uk pilot pipelines against CeMPA's UKMOD B2026.03 (system UK_2026, dataset training_data).

## Suites and match rates (executed against UKMOD)

| Suite | UKMOD var | Cases | Mismatches | Match |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uk-self-employed-nic` | `tscse_s` | 5 | 0 | 100% |
| `uk-employer-nic` | `tscer_s` | 5 | 0 | 100% |

- **Self-employed** (SSCBA 1992 s.15 Class 4): Class 4 is an annual charge, so the annual statutory formula reproduces `tscse_s` **exactly** on the 30k/45k/60k/130k/360k grid. Class 2 is nil after the 6 April 2024 abolition (confirmed live: `tscse_s`=£0 for Class 2 at all profit levels).
- **Employer secondary** (SSCBA 1992 s.9, 15% above £5,000/yr): UKMOD computes week by week on the weekly-rounded secondary threshold, leaving a ~£0.86/yr residual absorbed by the concept tolerance (2).

## Verification discipline

- UKMOD output variable names `tscse_s` / `tscer_s` **verified from the model's `VARCONFIG.xml`** (the brief flagged them as guesses).
- Every expected value comes from an executed UKMOD run reconciling against corpus-grounded statute arithmetic (see the RuleSpec companion tests in the paired rulespec-uk PR).
- **O5 additive**: existing case sets are untouched; the byte-preserving extraction guard proves `grids/uk.yaml` and the suites describe the identical case list.
- No dispositions needed — both suites match exactly within tolerance.

## Changes

- `axiom_oracles/suites/uk_self_employed.py` (new) + registration in `suites/__init__.py`
- `axiom_oracles/core/case.py`: `UK_WORKER_SELF_EMPLOYED_NIC`, `UK_WORKER_EMPLOYER_SECONDARY_NIC` concepts

author: bdfinst
body:
## Summary

Removes the Classic TDD opt-in from the build workflow based on experimental evidence, and consolidates the graph-tooling (CodeGraph/Graphify) and `/setup` vs `/project-init` overlap from issues #844's slices.

### Single build cadence (#840)

The plugin now runs a single per-behavior cadence — **Code-First Small Batches** (IMPLEMENT → TEST → REFACTOR) — with no `--tdd` flag, no plan `**Cadence**:` metadata field, and no cadence-resolution precedence step.

Experiment 5 (`docs/experiments/05-final-results.md`) measured both cadences head-to-head on quality-per-dollar with n=24 cells/arm. Code-First Small Batches ranked #1 (0.968 qual/$) vs. Classic TDD at #2 (0.608 qual/$) — a clean, statistically defensible separation driven entirely by cost (~60% more per cell), not quality (0.961 vs. 0.966 raw scores are indistinguishable). Maintaining both cadences as a live dual-path build option carried ongoing coordination cost across three skills (`build`, `plan`, `ship`) and duplicated hard-gate logic with no efficiency justification.

- **`/build` skill**: Removed `--tdd` argument, dual-cadence description language, and the cadence-resolution precedence step (formerly step 3.5). Per-behavior cycle section now describes IMPLEMENT → TEST → REFACTOR only.
- **`/plan` skill**: Removed `**Cadence**: tdd` opt-in mention and the plan-template's `**Cadence**:` metadata field and its RED/GREEN/REFACTOR labeling alternative.
- **`/ship` skill**: Removed "TDD opt-in" phrase from build-phase description.
- **`test-driven-development` skill**: Reframed as an **advisory methodology reference**, not a build cadence toggle. `/build` never dispatches into it automatically.
- **`systematic-debugging`**: Clarified Phase 4 hard gate — "no fix without a failing test that reproduces the defect first" — applies to every defect fix regardless of build cadence (per maintainer direction: TDD is not used for general development, but defect fixes always start with a failing test that reproduces the bug).
- Swept remaining dual-cadence references across `orchestrator.md`, `request-processing-flow.md`, `skills-registry.md`, `implementer.md`, and the `docs/` index pages.
- New `docs/adr/0017-single-build-cadence-remove-classic-tdd-opt-in.md` records the decision.

### Graph-tools consolidation (#844, #846, #848, #849)

- New `plugins/dev-team/knowledge/codegraph-vs-graphify.md` — comparison doc and "when to use which" guidance (#849).
- Graph-consultation guidance wired into `codebase-recon.md`, `architect.md`, and once into `code-review/SKILL.md`'s dispatch procedure covering the whole review panel — all gated on tool presence, no hard dependency (#848).
- CodeGraph's opt-in install migrated from `/init-dev-team` into `/project-init` (new Step 4c), and changed from committing `.codegraph/` + a project `.mcp.json` to a personal/user-scope MCP registration — resolving the contradiction with the plugin's stated "CodeGraph stays personal, not committed" policy. Graphify added as a new opt-in capability tool with a CLAUDE.md corruption guard (snapshot → diff → restore-or-append) and a pytest suite exercising that guard logic (#846).

### `/setup` vs `/project-init` de-duplication (#850)

- `/setup` now delegates stack/tool detection and installation to `/project-init` instead of re-implementing it, keeping only its own job: `.claude/project-stack.json`, agent template activation, the PostToolUse formatting hook, and the generated `/pr` command.
- `/project-init`'s description states it's the canonical toolchain-install source of truth.
- `/init-dev-team` detects when it's running inside this repo and bootstraps the full plugin-dev toolchain via `scripts/dev-setup.sh`, which stays a separate bash entry point (documented inline) since it's also reused as a generic template by `/new-marketplace`.

## Notable details

- **Backward compatibility**: Existing plans authored with `**Cadence**: tdd` metadata are unaffected retroactively — this is a forward-only removal from the skill surface, not a migration of historical plan files.
- **Not a quality claim**: Classic TDD ranked a clean #2 of 7 arms with statistically indistinguishable maintainability (blast radius 39.7 LOC/change vs. 40.0). Teams that have process reasons to prefer test-first discipline can still invoke `test-driven-development` directly; they lose only the flag/metadata shortcut into `/build`, not the discipline itself.
- **Future-proof**: If a larger-corpus run of Experiment 5 shows Classic TDD closing the cost gap, or `/build`'s users want test-first discipline as a first-class cadence again, that's a new decision to make with new evidence — this ADR does not preclude reintroducing an opt-in later.

Closes #840

Closes #848
Closes #849
Closes #850

author: lalalune
body:
Closes #14180. Parent: #13452.

## What this ships

The `sandboxed-iframe` isolation level was catalogued but had **no shipped consumer** — `surface-isolation.ts` recorded `examples: []`, and every dynamic/plugin view loaded in the host realm via dynamic `import()`. This PR implements the actual sandboxed-iframe embedding path plus the postMessage capability broker backing the `navigate` / `storage` grants for iframe-hosted views. It does **not** touch the same-realm agent-interact broker (#14068) — it mirrors its deny-by-default doctrine at the cross-realm boundary.

New / changed files (all under `packages/ui/src/`):

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `components/views/sandbox-policy.ts` | Owns the one MDN invariant: never emit `allow-scripts` + `allow-same-origin` together. `resolveSandboxTokens` is the single constructor of the `sandbox` attribute; `assertRealSandbox` throws rather than render a decorative sandbox. Default token set is `["allow-scripts"]` (opaque origin — no ambient host access). |
| `components/views/sandboxed-view-broker.ts` | Pure, directly-testable postMessage broker. `parseSandboxedViewRequest` is the untrusted-input boundary (J3): wrong channel / wrong kind / empty id / non-brokered capability → `null`. `brokerSandboxedViewRequest` checks the requested `SurfaceCapability` against the resolved manifest and returns a **typed denial** (`ok:false` + reason) when ungranted — the facility never runs. A facility throw is translated (J1) to an observable failure frame, never a fabricated success. Only `navigate` / `storage` are brokered. |
| `components/views/SandboxedViewFrame.tsx` | Renders the real `<iframe sandbox>`, installs the parent-side `message` listener bound by **frame-window identity** (an opaque-origin frame reports origin `"null"`, so identity, not origin string, is the spoof-proof gate), and binds the broker to the live shell `navigate` (`dispatchNavigateViewEvent`) + a **per-view-namespaced** `localStorage` facility (so even a granted view can only touch its own keys). |
| `components/views/DynamicViewLoader.tsx` | When `resolvedManifest.isolation === "sandboxed-iframe"`, delegates to `SandboxedViewFrame` and **skips** the in-realm bundle-load / interact-registry path — untrusted content never executes in the shell realm. |
| `components/views/sandbox-probe-view.tsx` | The shipped first-party (developer-only) consumer: a real opaque-origin framed document that requests `navigate` + `storage` over postMessage and renders the shell's granted/denied replies. Registered idempotently at boot from `App.tsx`. |
| `surface-isolation.ts` | Catalogue `examples` for `sandboxed-iframe` now names `sandbox-probe` (was `[]`); rationale updated to describe the shipped mechanism. |

## Real test evidence

Three test files drive the **real** path (no stub stands in for the iframe or the broker):

- `SandboxedViewFrame.test.tsx` (`@vitest-environment jsdom`) mounts the actual component and posts messages in as the framed document (`event.source === iframe.contentWindow`):
  - ungranted `navigate` → typed denial **and** `NAVIGATE_VIEW_EVENT` never fires (shell route unchanged);
  - ungranted `storage` write → typed denial **and** `localStorage.length === 0` (no key written);
  - granted `navigate`/`storage` → serviced (event fires; **only** the namespaced key `eliza:sbxview:<viewId>:<key>` is written, no bare shell key);
  - a message not from this frame's window is ignored (identity gate);
  - a granted-but-bad payload → typed failure, not a fake success.
  - The header documents the red→green property: deleting the grant check turns the two negative-path assertions red.
- `sandboxed-view-broker.test.ts` — pure broker: deny-without-grant (facility spy never called), service-with-grant, non-brokered capability rejected at parse, facility-throw → typed failure.
- `sandbox-policy.test.ts` — the MDN foot-gun guard: the `allow-scripts` + `allow-same-origin` pairing is flagged / throws; scripts-alone and same-origin-alone are fine; `resolveSandboxTokens` refuses a request that would defeat the sandbox.
- `surface-isolation.test.ts` — asserts `SURFACE_ISOLATION_CATALOGUE["sandboxed-iframe"].examples` is non-empty and contains `sandbox-probe`; the existing catalogue-completeness test still holds.

### Test-run status

Local `bun run --cwd packages/ui test` and `bun run verify` were **deferred in this environment** (the working tree is a partial/oscillating-disk checkout that can't complete a workspace build; branch was pushed via the Git Data path). All imports the new code uses were verified to resolve against `origin/develop`: `NAVIGATE_VIEW_EVENT` / `dispatchNavigateViewEvent` (`@elizaos/shared/events`), `logger` (`@elizaos/logger`), and `registerAppShellPage` + the `developerOnly` / `surface` fields (`app-shell-registry.ts`). **N/A here:** a full `bun run verify` and a real framed-view render walkthrough need a buildable env — please let CI exercise `bun run --cwd packages/ui test`.

## Acceptance criteria mapping

- Real iframe render path with ungranted navigate→denied (route unchanged), ungranted storage→denied (no write), granted→serviced, red→green — `SandboxedViewFrame.test.tsx`. ✅
- Sandbox never combines `allow-scripts` + `allow-same-origin` for same-origin content — `sandbox-policy.ts` + `sandbox-policy.test.ts` + a frame-level assertion. ✅
- `surface-isolation.ts` `examples` non-empty, names the shipped consumer, completeness test passes — `surface-isolation.test.ts`. ✅

## Non-goals (unchanged)

Native child web-content surfaces (`native-webview`), in-process host-realm scoping for trusted views, reworking the #14068 agent-interact broker, mobile native surface-manager, new `SurfaceCapability` values — all out of scope.

## Sync

Branch is 2 commits behind `develop` (`#14248` agents-table comments, `#14249` orchestrator git-env) — **zero file overlap** with this change, so it merges cleanly.

author: vharmain
body:
## Summary

`enrich-elevation` resolves elevations **only at geometry vertices**, but selected its MML chunks by line-corridor intersection over the whole buffered geometry envelope — a 4-vertex test route fetched **165** 250m chunks where 3 suffice, firing them all as **concurrent unbounded requests** against the rate-limited MML API, then resolving each vertex with a linear scan over the fetched grids and `nth` over lazy lists.

The rewrite derives the chunk set from the vertices and plans requests adaptively (`plan-fetches`):

- **Small geometries** (vertices span ≤ 250m — points and most single sports sites): one request tightly around the vertices, like the old implementation fetched
- **Dense clusters**: ≥ 3 vertex chunks inside a 1000×1000m tile merge into one tile request (measured MML cost: 250m chunk ~255ms, 1000m tile = 16 chunk areas ~740ms, so a merged tile costs MML no more server time and is always fewer requests)
- Remaining chunks are fetched as individual fixed-grid 250m chunks

Fetches run in **bounded waves of 8** (was: all at once) over a shared keep-alive connection pool, and each vertex resolves via an **O(1) chunk-key index** with pre-reversed row vectors (was: O(#chunks) scan + O(ncols) lazy-list `nth` per vertex), CRS-transforming each vertex once.

**Output values and fcoll shape are unchanged** — all request envelopes keep 2m-aligned corners, so every vertex resolves to exactly the same MML coverage cell as before. Dispatcher/registry semantics (circuit breaker, `still-valid?` re-enqueue, trigger and dedup rules) untouched.

## Measured impact

Chunk-selection sweep over **300 real route sites** (types 4401–4412, prod-snapshot dev DB; deterministic, no MML calls):

| | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| Total MML requests | 92,638 | **24,095** (3.8x fewer) |
| Median per-route reduction | – | **3.8x** (max 7x) |
| Heaviest route (lipas-id 613762, 4,367 vertices) | 5,619 | **1,427** |
| Routes needing *more* requests than old | – | 1 of 300 (4 → 5) |

Real MML API, one run per implementation per site (old = full pre-optimization pipeline):

| Site | Requests old → new | Wall time old → new |
|---|---|---|
| Point (502944) | 1 → 1 | 740ms → 397ms |
| Medium route (517341, 184 vertices) | 33 → **10** | 3.0s → 3.0s |
| Long sparse route (607816, 394 vertices) | 73 → **11** | 2.2s → 4.1s |

Wall time on already-fast MML is a wash: the old code "won" the sparse-route case by firing all 73 requests concurrently — exactly the abusive pattern this PR removes (a route like 613762 fired **5,619 concurrent requests** at a circuit-breaker-guarded external API). Merged tiles also transfer more grid bytes than the vertex-minimal chunk set (15MB vs 6MB on the sparse route) but cost MML *less* total server time per its measured cost curve. Ascii-grid parsing switched from a regex scan to whitespace split: same values, ~2x faster (a 1000m tile parses in ~240ms on the 2-core dev box).

## Correctness

- **Exact-equality bar** (same 2m source cells, so unlike the diversity sweep there is no snapping nondeterminism excuse): the committed test suite asserts old-vs-new outputs are `=` against a copy of the pre-optimization implementation on synthetic grids with cell-unique values
- **Real data**: point + medium route z-vectors exactly equal old-vs-new; the sparse route initially showed differing values between the old and new *runs*, and re-fetching both pipelines fresh gave **0/394 differing vertices** — the difference was transient MML response content between the two benchmark fetches, not framing. In response, parsed grids are now **validated against their headers** (truncated/malformed responses previously shifted every subsequent row lookup silently; now the job fails and retries)
- NODATA (-9999) passthrough, Point/LineString/Polygon walks, feature order, property passthrough, and out-of-coverage failure behavior preserved (degenerate envelope → MML error → job failure, as before)
- A vertex exactly on the coverage envelope's max edge maps into the last chunk inside coverage and resolves via the col/row edge cap, like the old inclusive containment + cap did
- **E2E with real data**: `dispatcher/handle-job "elevation"` unmocked for lipas-id 502944 → one MML request, robot revision in DB and ES doc both carry `[x y 106.69]` (identical z to the old pipeline's value for that site); test revision cleaned up afterwards

## Resilience (two high-effort review passes, findings fixed)

- **MML timeouts now actually trip the dispatcher's circuit breaker**: `SocketTimeoutException` and Apache's connect/pool timeouts extend `InterruptedIOException`, which `patterns/interrupt?` classifies as a watchdog interrupt and rethrows *without counting* — so MML degradation never opened the `mml-elevation-service` breaker (pre-existing on master; load-bearing here, so fixed at the fetch layer by rethrowing as `ex-info` without the original cause)

- Shared connection pool sized 32/32 (well above 2 concurrent jobs × wave of 8) with a lease timeout above the socket timeout, so MML slowness or abandoned requests holding leases make jobs *slow*, not *failed* (failing fast here would feed the dispatcher's circuit breaker and block all enrichment); pool built lazily on first MML call
- Retry once on connection-establishment IOExceptions, **never** on `SocketTimeoutException` (the server keeps computing the abandoned response; learned in #207)
- `resolve-elevation` bounds-checks its grid: only an exact max-edge point may cap into the edge cell; a grid that doesn't cover its vertex fails loudly instead of silently resolving a wrong edge cell
- Any chunk failure still fails the whole job so the queue's retry + circuit breaker machinery stays in charge (per-chunk degradation would write partial nonsense)
- Deliberate tradeoff, documented in code: under severe MML degradation a many-hundred-chunk route may exceed its 30-min job timeout and retry later, instead of "succeeding" by hammering the degraded API with unbounded concurrency

## Tests

`lipas.backend.elevation-test` rewritten from 4 constant-existence assertions to **17 tests / 276 assertions**: grid parsing (CRLF headers, NODATA, negatives, truncation validation, locale-safe oracle), chunk-key/tile/small-mode planning math incl. coverage-edge cases, resolution at cell boundaries and grid corners (edge cap vs loud failure), walk-order lockstep between vertex collection and z-appending, mocked-MML integration with a cell-unique synthetic elevation oracle (exact z per vertex, multi-chunk borders, tile merging, request dedup, failure propagation, timeout wrapping, concurrency bound actually bounding), and the old-vs-new equivalence suite. Dispatcher + patterns tests green. The batch CRS transform was verified bit-identical to the per-vertex transform on 394 real vertices.

Mocking note: the suite mocks the MML fetch layer with `with-redefs` — the CLAUDE.md fixture preference can't apply to an external, authenticated, rate-limited API.

author: kstruck
body:
## What

The daily sweep that closes stuck-open finished pools — the last deferred T2 piece, built **safe-first** so it can't mis-close a live pool.

### Three safety layers
1. **Kill-switch** — no-ops unless `system/config.autoClose.enabled === true` (default **OFF**; any config read error → disabled).
2. **Dry-run by default** (`dryRun !== false`) — only **reports** what it would close (one `admin_audit` summary per run), closing nothing, until an admin reviews reports and arms live.
3. **Conservative eligibility** (`isAutoCloseEligible`, unit-tested) — requires an over-signal (`scores.gameStatus:'post'` or `isFinal`), **never a date guess**, and skips terminal / already admin-closed pools.

### Trigger-safe
Closes via the shared `adminCloseUpdate` (extracted from `closePool`, now used by both), so the T2 guards fire → **zero member emails, zero stats deltas**, same as a manual close.

### Admin control
System → Settings tab gets an **Auto-Close Sweep** toggle (enable/disable) + a typed-confirm to switch from dry-run to live. Ships disabled.

## Verification

- functions + frontend `tsc` clean; **200 frontend + 96 functions** tests (incl. `adminCloseUpdate` + `isAutoCloseEligible` predicates); both builds clean.

## Deploy

Functions + Coolify. **Ships DISABLED** — after deploy, enable it and review the dry-run `admin_audit` reports (System tab) for a week before arming live, per the plan.

body:
## 概要

UX改善プランのP2フェーズ(Task 8/10/11)を実装。PR #11(P0/P1: モバイルナビ、カラートークン統一、追従目次、コードコピー、前後記事ナビ等)への積み上げPR。

## 対応タスク

| Task | 内容 | 主な変更 |
|------|------|---------|
| Task 8 | シェアボタン(X / はてなブックマーク / URLコピー) | `src/components/blog/ShareLinks.astro`(新規)、`src/pages/blog/[slug].astro` |
| Task 10 | 読了プログレスバー + Back to top | `src/pages/blog/[slug].astro`、`src/styles/global.css` |
| Task 11 | クリーンアップ(未使用ファイル削除、ダミーURL修正) | `src/layouts/Layout.astro`・`src/components/Welcome.astro` 削除、`src/components/layout/Header.astro` の GitHub リンクを `github.com/naoya5` に修正 |

**Task 9(giscusコメント)はユーザー判断でスキップし、今回は実装していません。** GitHub Discussions有効化などリポジトリ設定変更を伴うため、着手前に別途承認が必要です。

## 実装メモ

- ShareLinks は記事末尾のシェア導線として、X intent URL とはてなブックマーク追加URLを静的リンクで設置。URLコピーのみ小さな `<script>` で実装し、コピー成功時に2秒間ラベルを切り替える。
- 読了プログレスバーは記事上端に固定表示し、`IntersectionObserver` は使わず `scroll`/`resize` イベントで進捗(記事本文のスクロール割合)を算出して `scaleX` を更新する軽量実装。`prefers-reduced-motion` 設定時は transition を無効化。
- Back to top は記事見出し(`#article-top`)への静的アンカーリンクのみで実装(JS不要)。
- **CSPの罠**: `ShareLinks.astro` と `[slug].astro` のスクリプトはページ単体でしか使われないため、Astroのビルド時に自動的にインライン化された。`node calc-hash.mjs` で新しい sha256 ハッシュを算出し、`public/_headers` の `script-src` allowlist に反映済み(`fix(csp)` コミット)。
- 未使用ファイル(`src/layouts/Layout.astro`、`src/components/Welcome.astro`)は `grep` で参照ゼロを確認してから削除。

## テストプラン

- [x] `pnpm astro check` — 0 errors
- [x] `pnpm build`(`astro check` → `astro build` → `pagefind`)— 成功
- [x] `node calc-hash.mjs` の出力と `public/_headers` の allowlist が一致することを確認
- [x] `wrangler pages dev ./dist` に対し agent-browser で確認:
  - 記事ページ(`/blog/ai/`)390×844(モバイル)・1440×900(デスクトップ)、ライト/ダーク両テーマでスクリーンショット確認、レイアウト崩れなし
  - シェアリンク(X / はてブ / URLコピー)がSHARE見出しの下に表示され、Back to topが同じ行に表示される
  - URLコピー実行後、ラベルが「コピーしました ✓」に切り替わり2秒後に戻ることを確認
  - スクロールに応じて読了プログレスバーの `scaleX` が0→1へ変化することを確認(トップで0、記事末尾で1)
  - `agent-browser console` でコンソールエラー・CSP違反なしを確認

## マージ順について

このPRは `feat/ux-improvements-p0-p1` をベースにしています。**先にPR #11(`feat/ux-improvements-p0-p1` → `main`)をマージしてから、このPRをマージ**してください(逆順だとdiffにP0/P1の変更が混ざります)。

author: iamstuffed
body: First of two batched-LoRA perf follow-ups noted on #218/#219. The GPU LoRA upload allocated a separate `b_batched` (scale-only B) buffer per target, even though it's **byte-identical to `b_scaled`** (scale·residual·B) whenever `b_factor == t.scale`: - the **5 non-residual targets** (q/k/v/gate/up) — *always* (residual only applies to attn-output/ffn-down) - **attn-output/ffn-down** when `residual_mult == 1` — i.e. every arch except Granite So on any non-Granite model, all 7 `b_batched` buffers were exact duplicates. Now `b_batched` shares the `b_scaled` buffer (a cheap retain on Metal / `Arc` clone on wgpu) in that case, and only uploads a distinct buffer for Granite's two residual-fed targets. **No behavior change:** `b_factor == t.scale` is exact (`×1.0` is exact in f32) — the shared case is genuinely identical data. Saves one B upload + GPU allocation per shared target. ### Verification - Metal + wgpu batched-LoRA **varied-fill** parity unchanged: attn/ffn/all-7 still ≈0.999; existing per-token parity passes. - `cargo build -p cera --features metal` + `--features gpu` clean; `clippy --workspace --features metal` + `--features gpu` clean. --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is disabled.
