author: nivintw
body:
## What

Retargets the docs pipeline from a hand-rolled HTML site to MkDocs Material, in four parts (one commit each, plus a /simplify pass, two review-fix passes, and two polish passes):

1. **Template catch-up** — `copier update` from v1.4.0 to v1.9.0, pulling in the `include_docs_site` feature (`mkdocs.yml`, `docs/index.md`, favicon, caller workflow) plus unrelated upstream fixes from the intervening releases.
2. **`generate-docs` skill rework** — retargets the skill to author Markdown + a `mkdocs.yml` nav tree instead of hand-rolled HTML/CSS/JS. Hard cutover: the skill now requires an existing `mkdocs.yml` to run at all. `check_docs.py` reworked to validate Markdown/nav instead of HTML; castify's `embedding.md` gets an MkDocs-specific wiring section.
3. **This repo's docs migration** — regenerates `docs/` as Markdown + nav (landing + one page per plugin), reconciling several drift/omission findings surfaced along the way. Ports the release-please-driven per-plugin version badges to `mkdocs.yml`'s `extra_javascript` instead of per-page `<script>` tags.
4. **Polish + gold-standard passes** — the initial migration was functionally correct but visually flat. First pass: admonitions, code-copy, a command summary table, a real recorded demo cast. Second pass, at explicit request to make this "the gold standard the rest are held to": instant navigation (the payoff feature for the document$-based JS hydration already in place), a full Material icon set, a homepage card grid, content tabs, and a real custom 404 page (via the documented `overrides/404.html` mechanism, after discovering `docs/404.md`'s content is silently discarded by Material's static-template handling for that page).
5. **Design pass** — the dev-kit overview gains a hand-built HTML/CSS loop diagram (deliberately not Mermaid: its `click` directives let the site's link color override the diagram's text color with theme-dependent, sometimes-invisible results, and its edge labels are illegible in the dark scheme; the component styles nodes as the site's code chips from Material's CSS variables, correct in both schemes by construction). All eleven dev-kit command pages get one fixed reference anatomy (lead / Usage / What it does / When to reach for it / Related, one boxed gotcha each), distilled from each skill's SKILL.md. Homepage cards become fully clickable (stretched-link overlay, inner links preserved) with the odd third card spanning the row. The lessons are folded back into `generate-docs`'s SKILL.md generically, so future docs runs produce this shape by default — including the newly-documented markdown-auto-fixer hazards (frontmatter-title H1 demotion, adjacent-italics mangling, ignore globs that miss subdirectories), which bit this very branch and are fixed in `.config/rumdl.toml`.

## Why

Closes #107, closes #108.

The hand-rolled HTML site needed repeated "reconcile docs-site drift" fixes and had no navigation/search/theme infrastructure beyond what was hand-built. Part of the fleet-wide MkDocs epic ([repo-management#85](https://github.com/nivintw/repo-management/issues/85)) — full design rationale in that epic and its sub-issues.

**Deliberately not done here** (gated behind [repo-management#88](https://github.com/nivintw/repo-management/issues/88)'s batch Pages-config flip): flipping this repo's Pages source, or deleting the old `docs/*.html` + `app.js` + `style.css` + `search-index.js`. Both stay live until that batch flip confirms the new build actually works.

**Upstream template gaps found and filed** (not blocking, all non-blocking follow-ups in `copier-everything`): #160, #162, #163, #166, #172, #176, #177, #178. The last is the big one — a proposal to fold this PR's fleet-general improvements (theme features, markdown extensions, edit_uri, the 404-override mechanism) back into the template baseline, so this repo actually becomes the reference other repos get by default.

## Verification

- [x] The quality gate passes (`uvx prek run --all-files`)
- [x] Full bats suite passes (125/125, `bats tests/`)
- [x] `check_docs.py` (the new Markdown/nav validator) passes against the regenerated site

- [x] Playwright smoke check of the built site across every page: nav/search/version badges/code-copy/admonitions/content tabs/card grid all work, instant navigation re-hydrates the version badges and cast player correctly on in-app transitions (not just hard loads), the embedded demo cast plays back, dark/light mode and a mobile viewport both render cleanly, zero console errors anywhere
- [x] Full review battery run (`/code-review`, `/security-review`, `/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr`, plus a bespoke adversarial pass) — all findings applied or explicitly noted as skipped in commit messages
- [x] 5 rounds of automated Copilot review, converged each time; a 6th round requested after the gold-standard pass
- [x] Design pass verified by rendered-screenshot inspection of every changed page in **both** color schemes (Playwright CLI), with full-card click targets hit-tested (card body navigates; inner links still independently clickable)

## Decisions made without asking

- The design-pass review battery was right-sized down: the final three commits are docs/CSS/lint-config only, developed and approved interactively with per-change rendered-screenshot review; the full gate, bats suite, and strict build all pass. The security/adversarial passes from the earlier battery were not re-run against them.
- `feat(dev-kit)` (minor bump) for the SKILL.md design-playbook commit — it substantively changes what the shipped skill instructs, not just its wording. The site/config commits are `docs:`/`chore:` and touch no plugin path, so they don't affect any plugin release.

author: mekwall
body:
## Summary

Two security hardening fixes:

- **Closes #387** — The daemon in-process `ArbitraitorApi::release()` previously published approved bytes with a bare `std::fs::write(dest, &bytes)`. It now routes publication through the ADR-0015 safe-release primitive (`arbitraitor_exec::release::release_artifact`), which re-verifies the digest before *and* after writing, rejects symlink/hard-link/special-file destinations, writes via a sibling temporary file with `0600` permissions, and publishes atomically. Release additionally requires a prior inspection receipt and a release-permitting policy verdict (defense in depth — the wire protocol does not expose `release`).
- **Closes #386** — The Tirith subprocess detector spawned its binary with a raw `Command::new(binary)`. It is now hardened with `arbitraitor-sandbox`: pre-exec `setrlimit` resource limits (CPU, memory, fd count), seccomp network isolation, Landlock filesystem restrictions scoped to the binary/library/ temp-artifact paths, `no_new_privs`, and inherited-fd closure. The detector also captures binary provenance (SHA-256, version, ruleset digest) via a new `Detector::provenance()` trait method that flows into the receipt as `detector_provenance`, making the exact detector build that produced each finding auditable.

## Changes

- `arbitraitor-daemon/src/api.rs` — `release()` delegates to `release_artifact`; adds `NoReceipt` / `PolicyBlocked` / `Release` error variants and a `lookup_verdict_for_release` gate; `ReleaseResult` now carries `bytes_written` and `method`.
- `arbitraitor-analysis/src/tirith.rs` — subprocess hardening (`apply_subprocess_hardening`), Landlock rule construction, binary SHA-256 + version probing, `provenance()` impl.
- `arbitraitor-analysis/src/lib.rs` — `Detector::provenance()` default trait method; `DetectorResult.provenance` field plumbed through `run_detector`.
- `arbitraitor-model/src/finding.rs` — `DetectorProvenance` struct (`binary_sha256`, `binary_version`, `ruleset_digest`).
- `arbitraitor-receipt/src/lib.rs` — `Receipt.detector_provenance` field + `ReceiptBuilder::detector_provenance`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `[Unreleased]` → Fixed.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo nextest run --workspace` — 1113 passed, 15 skipped
- [x] `rumdl check .`
- [x] `cargo run -p xtask -- docs-check`

New tests:
- `release_without_inspection_receipt_is_rejected` — fetch-only artifact cannot be released.
- `release_after_block_verdict_is_rejected` — `Verdict::Block` denies release.
- `release_after_inspection_uses_safe_primitive` — happy path asserts `bytes_written`, `0600` perms, digest equality.
- `release_rejects_symlink_destination` — ADR-0015 symlink rejection.
- `provenance_is_none_when_binary_not_found` / `provenance_captures_binary_sha256_when_available` / `metadata_version_reports_binary_version_not_crate_version` — Tirith provenance capture.

## Notes for review

- `Detector::provenance()` is a default trait method (returns `None`) so pure-Rust detectors are unaffected; only subprocess detectors override it.
- The provenance triple lives in the receipt (audit surface), not in `DetectorMetadata` (capability surface) — version remains in `metadata()` as the binary version; `binary_sha256`/`ruleset_digest` are receipt-only.
- The verdict gate reads the persisted receipt JSON; release is denied when no receipt exists, proving the artifact was never analyzed through the inspection pipeline.

author: jpoley
body:
## Problem
#153: no single glanceable view of every active agent session with a derived live status.

## Approach
- **Pure, wire-decoupled derivation** (`lib/attention/status.ts`): working / waiting-for-input / idle / done / error from watchtower events, with recency decay, out-of-order/duplicate/malformed handling, finality tie-breaks.
- **Board UI** (`app/attention`, `components/attention/*`): one card per active session, status orb (pulses via `motion`), current/last tool, time-in-state, activity sparkline, deep-link to the existing TurnGroup view; empty / disconnected / loading states; semantic color tokens only.
- **Authed aggregation** (`app/api/watchtower/attention/route.ts`): reuses the existing REST-proxy pattern with a bounded fan-out; `ok` flag distinguishes disconnected from empty.
- **Live updates via ≤2s polling** (documented fallback): watchtower exposes REST + only an unauthenticated ingest/echo `/ws` (not a scoped consumer subscription), so bridging a durable upstream socket through App Router across both deploy modes was judged fragile/disproportionate. Polling pauses on hidden tab, aborts in-flight, replaces state (no memory growth), 5s upstream timeout.

## Tests
49 new tests: derivation (all 5 states + edge cases), support libs, the aggregation route, and the board component (empty/disconnected). typecheck ✓, lint ✓, 1634 pass, build ✓ (`/attention` + route compiled).

## Deferred (documented, with reason)
- 🟡 waiting-for-input: derivation implemented+tested, but watchtower has no REST endpoint to read Notification events yet (surfaces once it grows `/api/sessions/{id}/events`).
- ✅ done: transient — board is scoped to watchtower *active* sessions; derivation supports/tests `done` while a session is still displayed.
- No shared-nav edit (stayed in own-files lane); add an `/attention` nav link if desired.

CI on self-hosted runner. Copilot not requested (org billing; check non-blocking).

Closes #153

**Round 3 (Copilot re-review of the round-2 fixes):** Raise the attention cache TTL above the 2s poll interval so regular polls actually reuse the cached scan (the round-2 TTL equalled the interval and missed every time).

## Promotion Trigger — Slice A (backend)

Wires the two sourcer triggers to `promoteSubject` behind the identity gate, per the ratified sourcing-surface model (v2 recon). Base `7d0be0a`. Slice B = the sourcing-surface read/UI.

### Identity gate (`promoteSubject`)
Before mint: `TalentTrustRepository.listMatchAdvisories(tenant, {subjectId, status:'PENDING_REVIEW'})` — non-empty → new outcome `deferred_unresolved_identity` (no record). author: rafaelburlet
body:
Several managed pool-key spends made **outside the top-level turn boundary** were tracked only locally and never reported to the control plane, so the tenant balance under-counted them. All own-tenant, all bounded by existing session/daily caps.

- **spawn_agent child runs** — debit the child's actual cost to the parent's metered host. CP-only (not the in-run-helper path): the per-session cap already reserves an estimate for the child and deliberately never reconciles it, so a session-cost call here would double-count the local ceiling.
- **Voxtral STT** — the debit was skipped whenever the ffprobe duration probe returned `null`, which is the norm for the browser's chunked WebM/Opus. Decouple the debit from the probe; fall back to a conservative byte-length audio estimate so a real transcription is never billed at zero.
- **save_workflow annotation** — account the Haiku annotation spend to the session cap + tenant balance when the metered context is wired (no-op on self-host / BYOK).

Deferred (not smallest-safe): the memory-extraction (`maybeUpdate`) helper call — wiring the metered context into the engine-scoped Memory class would thread new params through the `IMemory` interface + several call sites. Tracked separately.

Tests: added for the spawn double-count invariant, the STT byte-length fallback, and the save_workflow debit/no-op paths. typecheck clean; touched-area vitest green.

author: brendankowitz
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new `codegen` feature area (`docs/features/codegen/`) for investigations about this repo's build-time code generation tooling itself — a topic not covered by any existing feature area (search/validation/package-management cover downstream *consumers* of codegen output, not the tooling's own architecture).
- Adds the first investigation: whether to absorb FHIR-package parsing (currently delegated to the vendored `fhir-codegen` submodule and its Firely-SDK-typed model) into our own JSON-based loader, with the eventual goal of dropping the submodule dependency entirely.

## Why now

The R6 ballot2→ballot4 upgrade (`docs/adr/adr-2607-fhir-r6-ballot4-upgrade.md`, #305) found this dependency is a recurring source of friction: `fhir-codegen`'s vendored Firely SDK bakes FHIR codes as fixed enums tied to whatever ballot was current at the SDK's release, causing an `InvalidCastException` every time a later ballot introduces a new code — hit 4 separate times during that one upgrade. This investigation explores a structural fix rather than continuing to patch reactively.

Key finding: this repo already solved the equivalent problem at the *runtime* layer (`JsonNodeSourceNode`/`ISourceNavigator`, a schema-less JSON-based FHIR navigator with no Firely SDK POCOs) — a build-time replacement would extend an already-proven pattern, not invent a new one.

author: thevladbog
body:
Implements the two highest-value DSR executors that previously threw `409 EXECUTION_NOT_AUTOMATED`: **EXPORT** (GDPR Art. 15/20) and **account-holder DELETION** (Art. 17). Both run synchronously inside the admin `execute()` flow (iteration-13 queue), closing the compliance gap where those rights were only manually executable. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-05-dsr-executors-design.md`.

## Backend
- **Flyway V15**: `DATA_EXPORT` file purpose, `user_account.deleted_at`, `data_subject_request.export_file_id`. Config `verifolio.privacy.export-link-ttl` (7d). V1–V14 untouched.
- **EXPORT executor**: assembles a structured JSON package (metadata + references, no raw file bytes) from new subject-scoped read ports (`identity.AccountExport`, `profiles.ProfileExport`, `contacts.ContactExport`, `requests.RequestExport`, `documents.DocumentExport` + privacy's consent/DSR reads), stores it as a `DATA_EXPORT` object, emails the subject a presigned GET link (the one sanctioned object-storage URL — subject's own data, short-lived, never logged), audits `DATA_EXPORTED`. Recommender subjects get a thin package.
- **Account-holder DELETION executor**: tombstones the subject's owned document versions (retains sha256/version/lockedAt), anonymizes profile + contacts, tombstones the account (status DELETED, email → tombstone, sessions + magic links deleted), pseudonymizes the subject's audit actor (rows retained). Consent records retained (lawful-basis evidence). Audits `ACCOUNT_DELETED`. Idempotent.
- **Wiring**: `execute()` now runs EXPORT + account-DELETION to EXECUTED; recommender-DELETION unchanged; REGION_MIGRATION/CORRECTION keep 409.
- Module boundaries stay one-way (privacy → identity/profiles/contacts/requests/documents/files/audit/…); ModularityTests green.

## Frontend
- No code change needed: the admin queue already handles a successful execute (200 → EXECUTED); the "manual execution required" state now only fires for REGION_MIGRATION/CORRECTION.

## Tests
- Backend: 240 tests, 0 failures (full `--rerun`); export package assembly (account-holder + recommender), each erasure port + audit pseudonymizer, full account-deletion matrix + idempotency, recommender-DELETION regression.
- Frontend: 92 unit; E2E extended (owner submits EXPORT → admin executes → EXECUTED + subject receives the presigned export link; the fetched JSON has the account-holder sections).

## Checklist
- [x] Module boundaries respected (ModularityTests green)
- [x] Locked versions immutable except the sanctioned tombstone path (content NULL, hash/version/lockedAt retained)
- [x] Consent + audit retained; audit actor pseudonymized on deletion; every execution audited
- [x] Region/residency: executors operate in-cell; no cross-region flow
- [x] Flyway V15 added; V1–V14 untouched; no OpenAPI change (no new endpoint/DTO)
- [x] Docs updated (DATA_MODEL, AUDIT_EVENTS, PRIVACY_AND_DATA_CLASSIFICATION, IMPLEMENTATION_HISTORY it. 14)
- [x] Only object-storage URL is the subject's own short-lived presigned export link; no new Maven deps

## Deferred
Audit log inside the export package; REGION_MIGRATION / CORRECTION executors; async job orchestration; S3 orphan-reconciliation sweep; audit-retention window enforcement.

author: rafaelburlet
body:
Four dogfooding defects (all pre-existing, none a release regression), folded into the stabilization set.

- **Queued messages never sent after reattach** — `reattachRun`'s finally reconciled the thread but never drained a message typed mid-resume, so it sat in the queue forever. Drain it, mirroring the normal-path drain (guarded so a pending changeset still gates).
- **Message timestamps absent** — the server already sends `created_at`; the client dropped it. Plumb it through the message type + both projection map sites and render a subtle per-message time (undefined-safe for older rows).
- **Artifact card dropped on the legacy (no-`blocks`) render path** — the fallback only rendered tool rows, silently dropping an `artifact_save` card. Render it, with inline de-dup so a card already fenced in prose doesn't double-render.
- **Artifact id non-idempotent on update-of-missing** — when a save supplied an id absent from the index, the create branch minted a fresh random id, silently forking a divergent duplicate. Honor a well-formed supplied id (traversal guard preserved) so a retry updates in place.

A fifth reported item (a no-output run persisted as `completed`) is genuinely present on main but its fix is owned by a separate branch in this same set — not duplicated here.

body:
## Summary

`copy_table` built plain column definitions for generated columns, dropping the `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED/VIRTUAL` clause. Even though `columns()` correctly threads `generatedType`/`defaultFunction` (via `newColumnFromField` reading the `table_xinfo` `hidden` flag), the *copied* table's column was emitted as a normal column, so `isVirtualStored()`/`defaultFunction` no longer reported the generated state.

author: rrhester
body:
## Why

Bulk upload is primarily a **first-run roster migration** — a DSP importing their existing, already-hired staff when they sign up. Creating those drivers in `onboarding` status caused two problems the operator hit:

1. They were **hidden from the default Active roster view** (roster defaults to `status = 'active'`), so imports looked like they "didn't show up."
2. They were **routed through the I-9 / onboarding gates**, which doesn't fit staff who were already vetted before the migration.

## Change

- Imported drivers are created as **`active`** instead of `onboarding`, tagged with `metadata.import = { source: 'bulk_spreadsheet', at: … }` so a batch stays identifiable.
- **Compliance (I-9, background check, drug test) is left blank** — the operator verifies/backfills later. Per the operator's decision, we do **not** fabricate cleared I-9/BG/drug records (no fake federal forms).
- After an import, the roster snaps to a view that shows the new drivers (Active) if the operator happened to be on On-leave / Inactive.
- Modal copy updated: "imports join the active roster instantly."

## Note on the already-imported batch

The ~50 drivers imported before this change are still in `onboarding` status. This code only affects new imports; the existing batch is being fixed separately with a small dated SQL update (pasted to the operator to run in the Supabase SQL Editor) so it can be previewed before it runs.

## Verification

`npm run smoke` passes; `node --check dashboard/live.js` clean. The insert already wrote `status`/`hire_date` directly; this adds `status: 'active'` + a `metadata` jsonb (same column the Finch import and the availability autosave already write).

author: jpoley
body:
## Problem
#104 (F9): hard-coded `deploy:kinsale`/`deploy:muckross` scripts; no env-based targets, no fail-closed preflight, no rollback.

## Stacked on #100
Uses the web+terminal split (gh-100). Merge #310 (#100) first.

## Approach
- **Env-file target selection**: `scripts/deploy.sh <target>` sources `deploy/env/<target>.env` (kinsale/muckross/cloud). Adding a target = adding a file; the script never changes. Env files hold **non-secret config only** + declare required-secret NAMES (`DAAX_REQUIRED_SECRETS`); values come from the environment.
- **Phased orchestrator** (`deploy.sh` + sourceable `deploy-lib.sh`): preflight → capture → build/pull → db → migrate → up → health → done. **Fails closed** on missing/empty required secret, failed image preflight, or unreachable Postgres. Mid-flight failure **rolls back** to the prior images / tears down a fresh deploy. `.logs/*.jsonl` deploy log.
- Provenance (`DAAX_DEPLOY_BY/VIA/MODE/HOST` — the names `build-info.ts` actually reads) feeds the F8 Build page.
- Cloud IaC: working `DATABASE_URL` connection-string swap + fail-closed reachability + a documented provider-parameterized skeleton (`deploy/iac/cloud`); full Terraform graph deferred per AC5 ("don't half-build broken Terraform").

## Self-caught + fixed
- **Critical:** `mktemp` pre-created the statefile, so a preflight failure hit rollback's "fresh deploy" branch and would `compose down` a **running prod stack** → fixed with a `CAPTURED` flag (rollback no-ops if capture never ran) + a negative test asserting no `compose down` on preflight failure.
- Concurrent deploys corrupting the shared `:rollback`/`:latest` baseline → non-blocking `flock` guard.

## Tests / validation
9 script tests (hermetic, faked docker/curl/tcp): preflight fails closed on missing/empty secret + unreachable PG asserting **no build/up/down** fired; happy-path ordering; mid-flight migrate failure → rollback; pg host/port parse; CLI surface. shellcheck clean. typecheck ✓, lint ✓, audit:auth ✓, 1612 pass, build ✓.

**Needs a real host** (not exercised in CI): real `docker compose` build/up, real Postgres health + pg_dump, live `/api/health`, image `:rollback` restore, flock under true concurrency. Remote/SSH orchestration intentionally not built (runs on-target: `ssh vm; source ~/.secrets; scripts/deploy.sh <target>`).

CI on self-hosted runner. Copilot not requested (billing; non-blocking). Closes #104


---

## Review fixes (3 rounds, gh-104)

**Round 3 (Copilot re-review of the round-2 fixes):** Correct the resolve_env_file error text to match the permitted charset (dots allowed).

Supersedes #339. CI on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` (public repo). Verified green locally: lint, typecheck, audit:auth, test, build.

**Validation:** produced by Claude Fable 5; three adversarial review rounds (a separate Claude reviewer + GitHub Copilot on rounds 2 and 3); all confirmed findings fixed. Non-bug nits and stack-staleness flags (resolved by the required parent-first merge order) are intentionally not chased.

author: kevpay
body:
## Context

Follow-up to #98 (which merged only the diagnostic). This is the actual fix for terminal-order auto-match finding nothing.

## Root cause (found via the #98 diagnostic)

The `[auto-match debug]` payload from a real run showed:
```
placeAccount: 0xc0ca… ✓   tokenDecimals: 6 ✓   incoming: 100   matched: 0
sampleAmounts: all dated 2026-07-04 …   (orders are 2026-06-30)
```
Place account, decimals, amount scale, and hydrated dates were all correct. The problem: the place is **very active** (100+ incoming transfers in a 33-min window), so walking its transfers newest-first from `latest` never reaches an old payout — the load stopped after one page of recent (07-04) transfers and never saw the 06-30 mints. Hence "instantly, nothing matched."

## Fix

Load the place's incoming transfers **bounded to the payout's block range** instead of walking from head:
- `estimateBlockRange` (new, `services/alchemy/transfers.ts`) samples recent average block time to convert the orders' date window (`min..max` order time ± a lookback margin) into a `fromBlock`/`toBlock` range.
- `listIncomingTransfersInRange` (new) does a single-direction, block-bounded, oldest-first `getAssetTransfers` page with pagination — the right shape for "find the mints on this account during a past window". `fetchTransfersPage` gained optional `fromBlock`/`toBlock`/`order` (defaults preserve existing behavior).
- `planPlaceMintMatchesAction` loads over that bounded range instead of the newest-first walk.

## Validation (production data)

For this payout's 06-30 block range the bounded query returns ~31 incoming transfers and contains **both** selected orders' mints (€21.26 @ 20:56:35, €15.73 @ 20:22:05) — which now match.

## Note

The `[auto-match debug]` console payload from #98 is still in place; I'll strip it in a small follow-up once matching is confirmed live.

## Testing

- ✅ `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run guard`, `npm run test` (34)

author: natosys
body:
## Summary

- Adds a named scenario profile overlay mechanism: a top-level `scenarios` block in `env_data.json`, `merge_scenario_vars()`/`resolve_scenario()` in new `R/scenario.R`, and `load_scenario(path, scenario)` in `R/environment.R`, which overlays only scenario-eligible `vars` (casualty generation, DOW ceiling/treatment efficacy, priority/DNBI/surgery/evac probabilities, transport times) onto the base configuration — structural config (`elms`, `transports`, `pops`) is never overridden.
- Implements the `moderate_intensity` profile (Falklands 1982 exemplar), disentangling the co-dependence between the Falklands-calibrated DOW ceiling and the OIF/OEF-era treatment efficacy factors flagged as a known gap in the existing README. Era-appropriate treatment efficacy factors are paired with an independently re-calibrated ceiling, validated by Monte Carlo replication against the historical 0.52% DOW/WIA target.
- Implements a `high_intensity` profile (Okinawa exemplar, demonstration skeleton), sourced by fetching and reading the actual FORECAS report (Blood, Zouris & Rotblatt, 1998) rather than assuming its methodology. This surfaced several corrections along the way:
  - FORECAS fits an **exponential** (not lognormal) distribution to combat-troop WIA/KIA at high intensity, parameterised directly by its mean (`W ~ exponential(mean)`). Adds `generate_exp_arrivals()` and a `generate_casualty_arrivals()` dispatcher (keyed off a new explicit `distribution` field per generator).
  - The paper's real Appendix A tables gave different values than initially assumed: Table A.7 (Okinawa combat WIA) is `Expon(6.86)`, Table A.9 (Okinawa combat KIA) is `Expon(1.63)`. There is **no standalone Vietnam combat-troop WIA/KIA table** in the document — a `vietnam` profile was dropped rather than citing a table that doesn't contain those numbers.
  - Scenarios are named `moderate_intensity`/`high_intensity` (FORECAS's own battle-intensity framing) rather than by conflict name.
  - The exponential distribution applies to **both** `combat` and `support` population groups under `high_intensity`, since this project models a single brigade (division and below) with no FORECAS-equivalent extra-divisional "service support" population.
  - The per-minute rate cap (`cap = 5`, an undocumented engineering constant with no citation, present since the casualty generator's first commit) was found to truncate a wildly uneven, mean-dependent share of draws once applied to the new exponential streams — ~48% for `high_intensity` WIA (mean 6.86, *above* the fixed cap) vs. ~1–7% for the existing lognormal streams. `generate_exp_arrivals()` now computes `cap = cap_multiplier × mean_daily` (default multiplier 3), which truncates a constant ~5% of draws regardless of intensity (since `P(Exponential(mean) > kmean) = exp(-k)` is mean-invariant) instead of an unbounded share as the mean approaches a fixed ceiling. `generate_ln_arrivals()` (used by `default`/`moderate_intensity`) is untouched, so the validated seed-42 baseline is unaffected; `high_intensity`'s realised WIA count rises from 398.5 to 733.0 (30-rep) now that it isn't half-truncated.
- Exposes a scenario selector in `controller.R` for previewing effective parameters per scenario; saving is gated to `default` so the override mechanism can't be accidentally flattened into the base file.
- Updates `README.md`: new "Scenario Profiles" section; the "Casualty Generation" section now documents both the lognormal and exponential models (previously it only described lognormal, which under-documented the mechanism this issue added); updated forward-references in the Died of Wounds MODEL ASSUMPTION blocks; a new Limitations entry (L12) documenting the pre-existing KIA:WIA ratio discrepancy, the `high_intensity` skeleton's incompleteness, and the missing Vietnam source.

This unblocks Issue #10 (comparative scenario runner), which depends on this schema per its own issue body.

## Test plan

**Setup:** R 4.3.3 with `simmer`, `simmer.bricks`, `triangle`, `jsonlite`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `stringr`, `shiny`, `shinyBS` installed. All runs from repo root.

**Steps and expected outputs:**

1. **No-regression check (default scenario):**
   ```r
   source("R/environment.R")
   identical(load_elms("env_data.json"), load_scenario("env_data.json", "default"))
   ```
   Expected: `TRUE`. Confirmed.

2. **Seed-42 baseline regression:**
   ```r
   set.seed(42); env_data <<- load_scenario("env_data.json", "default")
   # run_once(30) via run.R pipeline
   ```
   Expected: 400 total casualties (154 WIA, 70 KIA, 176 DNBI), matching the `CLAUDE.md` Key Parameters baseline exactly. Confirmed — unaffected by the `generate_casualty_arrivals()` dispatch refactor or the exponential-only rate cap change.

3. **Moderate Intensity calibration (30 replications, 30 days, seed=NULL):**
   Expected: DOW/WIA rate within ±2 percentage points of the 0.52% historical target (Payne 1983; Jolly 2018). Observed: mean DOW/run 0.767 (95% CI [0.431, 1.102]), DOW/WIA rate 0.498% (95% CI [0.280%, 0.715%]) — well within tolerance.

4. **High Intensity skeleton (30 replications, 30 days), post rate-cap fix:**
   Expected: casualty count materially higher than `moderate_intensity`, without the exponential-specific truncation artefact. Observed: mean WIA/run 733.0, mean KIA/run 173.4 — WIA+KIA ratio 4.05× `moderate_intensity`.

5. **Unknown scenario name (e.g. the dropped `vietnam`):**
   ```r
   load_scenario("env_data.json", "vietnam")
   ```
   Expected: explicit error listing available scenarios (`moderate_intensity`, `high_intensity`). Confirmed.

6. **Full pipeline smoke test:**
   ```
   Rscript run.R --seed 42 --days 5 --iterations 1
   Rscript run.R --seed 42 --days 5 --iterations 3
   ```
   Expected: completes without error, writes outputs. Confirmed (both single-run and multi-replication paths).

7. **`controller.R` scenario selector (headless, via `shiny::testServer()`):**
   Confirmed: scenario dropdown populates with `default`/`moderate_intensity`/`high_intensity`; selecting a scenario correctly previews its overridden parameters; save is blocked (no file write) while previewing a non-default scenario.

**Regression checks:** Seed-42 single-run output is byte-for-byte consistent with the documented baseline (400/154/70/176). `default` scenario output is structurally identical to the pre-existing `load_elms()` path. No changes to `elms`, `transports`, `pops`, or any existing `vars` value in the base configuration. `generate_ln_arrivals()` (the lognormal path used by every existing scenario) is untouched by the rate-cap fix.

**Known limitations (documented in README):**
- The `moderate_intensity` profile's KIA:WIA ratio (0.452) differs from the published 255:777 (0.328) record — a pre-existing characteristic of the Issue #1 casualty generator calibration, not introduced or corrected by this issue.
- The `high_intensity` profile is an explicitly unvalidated skeleton: only casualty generation rate and distribution family are sourced; DOW ceiling, treatment efficacy, priority, DNBI, and transport times are inherited from the Falklands-calibrated base.
- No Vietnam-calibrated profile exists: FORECAS does not tabulate a standalone Vietnam combat-troop WIA/KIA distribution in this document, so none was fabricated.
- The lognormal rate cap (`cap = 5`, used by `default`/`moderate_intensity`) remains an undocumented, un-derived engineering constant; only the exponential path's cap was fixed in this issue, since the lognormal cap was not shown to be materially distorting any currently validated scenario.
- The "support population treated as combat-exposed" reclassification under `high_intensity` (documented as a MODEL ASSUMPTION in the README) is a considered judgment call about this project's brigade-level scope, not a literature-derived value.
- Full interactive verification of the `controller.R` Shiny app (visual rendering) was done headlessly via `shiny::testServer()` in this sandbox, not

body:
## Summary

M1's first request-serving surface on the ENG-63 scaffold (TDD §7 / §4.2 / §4.3 / §3.2). Establishes two conventions every later M1 router inherits: the RFC 9457 **problem+json** error shape and the **`AuthContext`** dependency contract.

- **POST /v1/setup** — first-run workspace+owner creation, valid only while zero users exist; concurrent setups serialized by a transaction-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock` (loser sees `count>0` → **409** `already-initialized`). Owner auto-login. Zero schema change. ENG-65 `workspace.created`/`user.joined` emission seam marked (not stubbed).
- **POST /v1/auth/login** — argon2id verify with **settings-pinned** params (t=3 / 64 MiB / p=4), offloaded to a threadpool. Unknown/deactivated email runs a **dummy hash** and returns a byte-identical generic **401** (no enumeration by timing or shape). Device mint-or-reuse (reuse only if owned, else **400** `invalid-device` after auth). Opaque 256-bit token → `sha256` hex `token_hash`; raw token returned **once**, never logged (logging redaction filter).
- **require_auth → frozen `AuthContext`** with a throttled rolling bump (writes at most once/hour per session). **require_role** factory → **403**. `GET`/`DELETE /v1/auth/sessions` (`id` = `token_hash`, ruled acceptable — not a credential, owner-scoped).
- **POST /v1/admin/invites** (owner/admin) + **POST /v1/auth/accept-invite** — single-use enforced by atomic `UPDATE ... WHERE used_by IS NULL RETURNING`; expired → **410**. Invites can't mint `owner` (schema Literal → 422).
- **RateLimiter** — in-process fixed-window, per-IP **and** per-email 10/min, checked before argon2; **429 + Retry-After**; injectable clock; reusable `rate_limit(limiter, key_fn)` dependency for ENG-66; `trust_proxy`+XFF; single-worker honesty docstring.
- **api/problems.py** — app-wide problem+json (`ProblemException`, `RequestValidationError`→422, `HTTPException`).
- **Docs gating** — `/docs`, `/redoc`, `/openapi.json` gated by `settings.docs_enabled` (default OFF).
- **sessions.user_id index** + migration `0002` (kept `compare_metadata` parity green). `argon2-cffi` added.

Did **not** touch the repo-root Dockerfile/compose/.env or CI (owned by ENG-72 in parallel).

## Acceptance checklist

- [x] `POST /v1/setup` zero-user guard + advisory-lock race safety + 409 after + auto-login
- [x] `POST /v1/auth/login` argon2id, dummy-hash enumeration defense, device mint/reuse, opaque hashed token
- [x] `require_auth`/`AuthContext`, throttled rolling bump, `require_role` 403
- [x] `GET`/`DELETE /v1/auth/sessions` with instant revocation
- [x] Invites: create (owner/admin) + accept, single-use, TTL 410
- [x] Rate limiter 429 + Retry-After, per-IP and per-email, reusable factory
- [x] RFC 9457 problem+json app-wide
- [x] Docs gating on/off
- [x] Raw token never logged (redaction filter + capture test)
- [x] Password min length 12; argon2 weakened in tests, prod defaults pinned by a test

## Verification outputs

```
uv sync                  → resolved, up to date
uv run ruff check .      → All checks passed!
uv run ruff format --check .  → 84 files already formatted
uv run mypy              → Success: no issues found in 83 source files
uv run pytest            → 291 passed in 53.36s   (server suite: 209 passed)
```

Tests against the real container-backed harness: setup race (dedicated committing fixture), login + rolling-bump-throttle + instant-revoke, enumeration shape (unknown email vs wrong password → identical 401 body), rate-limit 429 with Retry-After (injected clock), invite single-use + TTL 410, docs gating both states, raw-token-never-in-logs (captured output), problem+json shape on 401/403/404/422, and the `AuthContext`/`require_role` contract via a throwaway probe route.

author: euphorialux
body:
## Purpose
* Implements **"one read per Drop"** for Crush Connect. A member's first gate submission from a Daily Drop — hit *or* miss — consumes that Drop's single "read", and every other card in the Drop locks until the next Drop.
* Stops a member from reading/answering multiple cards out of the same Drop; the selection itself is the choice.

## Does this introduce a breaking change?
```
[ ] Yes
[x] No
```
Additive schema only (`ConnectDailyDrop.read_target` nullable FK + `read_at`); `NULL` means "no read used yet" and also covers Drops that predate the mechanic.

## Pull Request Type
```
[ ] Bugfix
[x] Feature
[ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
[ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
[ ] Documentation content changes
[ ] Other... Please describe:
```

## How to Test
```
git checkout feature/connect-one-read-per-drop
pytest crush_lu/tests/test_crush_connect_gate.py crush_lu/tests/test_crush_connect.py --create-db
```
**125 passed** locally, and `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` reports **No changes detected**.

Manual: from a Drop with 2+ cards, answer one card's gate → the other cards render the "You've already read someone from this Drop — your next Drop arrives tomorrow." locked state; `crush_connect_spark_compose` for another card redirects with the same message.

## What to Check
* **Concurrency:** `submit_gate_answers` claims the read with `ConnectDailyDrop.objects.filter(pk=..., read_target__isnull=True).update(read_target=..., read_at=...)` — first-write-wins, so two simultaneous submissions can't both consume the read. It raises `ValueError("drop_read_used")` once spent.
* **Gate coverage:** the lock is enforced in the service (`submit_gate_answers`), the compose view (pre-check + redirect), and the template — confirm all three agree.
* **Migration `0179`** also folds in two pending `iosappdevice` index renames that `makemigrations` had wanted since `0178` (pre-existing drift). Functionally fine in one migration, but flag if you'd rather split the unrelated renames into their own migration.

## Other Information
* No backfill required — `read_target=NULL` is the correct default for existing/pre-mechanic Drops.
* Model state is fully captured by `0179` (`makemigrations --check` clean).
* Opened via Claude Code after validating tests + migration state on the working branch.

body:
## Problem
#103: no backup/restore, no no-outage secret rotation for the WS token, no explicit migration-rollback verification.

## Approach
- **Postgres backup/restore**: `scripts/pg-backup.sh` (`pg_dump -Fc`, atomic `.partial`→rename, retention prune) + `scripts/pg-restore.sh` (`pg_restore --clean --if-exists`, confirm-gated, `--latest`). Connection resolution mirrors `lib/db/config.ts` (DATABASE_URL or PG* triple, fail-closed). Runbook `docs/postgres-backup-restore.md` (backup, restore, drill, pre-deploy snapshot, client-≥-server-major note).
- **Secret rotation (no outage)**: added `DAAX_WS_TOKEN_SECRET_PREVIOUS` — `verifyTicket` accepts current-OR-previous (constant-time per candidate); unset previous = byte-for-byte pre-rotation behavior (no weakening); mint always uses current. (`DAAX_PROXY_SECRET` dual-value was already on main.)
- **Migration rollback**: all 3 migrations already ship working `down`; added an up→down→up round-trip integration test.
- New profiled `pg-backup` compose service + `daax-pg-backups` volume in both files; **did not** touch the `daax`/`postgres` hardening stanzas (owned by #185).

## Deferred (documented)
`reconcileRoles --dry-run` — depends on #101's reconcile code; noted in runbook §8 + decision log to avoid colliding with the in-flight #101.

## Tests
+12 WS dual-secret cases; migration up→down→up **ran against real throwaway Postgres** (not skipped) and asserted schema return. typecheck ✓, lint ✓, 1593 pass, shellcheck clean. Full live backup→drop→restore drill: 3/3 rows recovered. CI on self-hosted runner. Copilot not requested (billing; non-blocking).

Closes #103


---

body:
## Summary

Trust-bundle writer composability cluster — bug sweep Delivery A:

- **#270** — `record-gate-claim` accumulates instead of clobbering: all five writers share a lossless read-modify-write compose path (`readBundleState`/`mergeChecksById`). Gate-claim typing persists in additive `claim.metadata.gate_claim` and is preserved verbatim across rebuilds and step transitions, validated on restore against the flow definition's full `expects[]` enumeration (all steps, incl. composed `uses_flow` children). Fail-closed everywhere: a stamp matching no real expectation dies as forged/corrupt; an unstamped legacy (pre-cluster) gate claim dies with a re-record remedy — never silently re-typed; an unloadable FlowDefinition gets its own distinct message. The `gate-claim-` check-id namespace is reserved at writer intake: novel ids rejected, correction of unstamped (wedged) claims permitted, live stamped gate claims immutable outside `record-gate-claim` itself.
- **#298** — `checksFromBundle` round-trips every field: `artifact_refs`/`standard_refs` now persist; waiver round-trip (landed in #344) eval-pinned; `recordCritique`/`recordLearning` consolidated onto the shared read.
- **#380** — new `record-check` subcommand: executes a command (argv exec, no shell; `--command` string mode gated by the runnability heuristic) and records a capture-backed check with loud exit semantics and a sha256 output digest (hash of the clamped capture — never raw output) in one compose-safe step. Registered in the CI baseline manifest and workflow.
- **#412** — `kind:"command"` acceptance evidence refs validated literally runnable at record time via the shared `scripts/hooks/lib/runnable-command.js` (verbatim extraction from `stop-goal-fit.js`, byte-identical heuristic, single source of truth); `parseCriterion` routes prose Evidence text to `ref.summary`; logged `--skip-evidence-ref-runnability-guard` for operator recovery. Also `record-gate-claim --command` so gate claims carry a runnable verification command distinct from the human summary.
- **#381** — deliver SKILL.md documents the manifest-lane constraint (only reconcile-manifest commands may be `kind:"command"`; everything else is `kind:"external"`/`"policy"`) with the reconciler's divergence message quoted verbatim and one worked example of each.
- **#361** — closed with evidence, no code: part 1's repro is the *python* sidecar in a survey/campfit session (no `workflow-sidecar.py` exists here; no TS code path merges string check-ids into structured `evidence_refs` — cross-repo routing noted). Part 2 is moot: `critique.json` was retired by ADR 0010 Phase 4c; `trust.bundle` is the sole verification artifact.

## Review/verification history (6 iterations, every guard exploit-driven)

Two reviewers (code + security) and a verifier ran per iteration; five real defects were caught and fixed inside the loop, each locked by a mutation-tested eval negative: the original clobber; silent re-typing of legacy gate claims on rebuild (reproduced against a real prior-session bundle); forgery laundering via hand-edited stamps; a reserved-namespace collision false-positive that could brick legitimate writes; and a supersession exemption that let a caller silently destroy a live gate claim's stamp. Final iteration: review clean, verify PASS, full sweep green (build/typecheck/validate:source/static/antigaming/writer+record-check+gate-lockdown+trust-reconcile evals), integration failures triaged byte-identical to the unmodified merge base (3 pre-existing files, not this change).

**Accepted follow-up polish** (documented, non-blocking, per review): the pre-cluster remedy message is imprecise for a synthetic caller-collision legacy shape that no real bundle has; one stale sentence in `resolveAllFlowGateExpects`'s JSDoc. Known accepted residual (documented in code): stamp validation checks structural conformance against the flow definition, not authorship — equal to the pre-existing local-trust floor; provenance binding is future work on the #270 thread.

Trust seal at `delivery/kontourai-flow-agents-270/` (per-session path, #379).

Closes #270. Closes #298. Closes #380. Closes #412. Closes #381. Closes #361.

## Measure salience for the in-browser ensemble — it's a wash

Follow-up to #107: does applying the server's image-salience multiplier help the
2-model in-browser combo? `tools/tune_inbrowser.py` now compares salience
strategies (off / boost-only / full) using each record's `mult` already in the
eval reports — no JS port needed to find out.

**Result: no.** At `timm_w=0.5, cw=0.0` over both eval datasets:

| strategy | recall @ FPR ≤ 0.10 |
|---|---|
| off (current, 1.0) | **0.876** |
| boost-only | 0.837 |
| full | 0.837 |

Salience slightly helps OpenImages but hurts the harder iNaturalist set (boosting
large *benign* images lifts their scores too), netting a ~4 % recall loss on the
combined set. So the in-browser ensemble keeps the flat `1.0` multiplier and the
`voters/salience.py` JS port isn't worth doing for now.

- `tools/tune_inbrowser.py`: salience comparison (off / boost-only / full).

author: emadshaaban92
body:
## Problem

Any SMTP connection using the verify-by-default TLS (`verify: :verify_peer`, the default) failed the STARTTLS handshake with `{:tls_alert, {:bad_certificate}}`, surfaced as `SMTP rejected: :tls_failed` (classified `:response`). Verified against `smtp.gmail.com:587`.

**Root cause.** On a STARTTLS upgrade, gen_smtp calls `ssl:connect(Socket, Opts, Timeout)` on the existing TCP socket (`smtp_socket:to_ssl_client/3`) and does **not** inject `server_name_indication`. `TlsOptions.build/1` sets the HTTPS hostname-match fun (`customize_hostname_check`) but only added SNI when an explicit `:sni` was present — and the SMTP config exposed no `sni` field. With no reference hostname, `verify_peer` + the hostname match fun reject the otherwise-valid cert.

A direct implicit-TLS connect to `:465` with the same opts verifies fine, so OS roots / cert chain are not the issue — only the STARTTLS path lacked an SNI.

## Fix

- `TlsOptions.build/2` now takes an optional `default_sni:` fallback, used only when the config has no explicit `:sni`.
- `Transports.Email.adapter_config/2` passes the relay host (`smtp.relay`) as `default_sni`, so the STARTTLS upgrade presents a reference hostname the `verify_peer` match_fun can check.
- `verify: :verify_none` still bypasses SNI entirely; an explicit `sni` always wins.
- Added an `sni` field to the SMTP adapter resource (parity with the Kafka TLS variants) and a corresponding form input in the transport config UI.

This is the same "verify-by-default breaks our SMTP" family as #67, and complements the content-type fix in #76.

## Tests

Added to `adapter_config/2 TLS options`:
- `verify_peer` defaults `server_name_indication` to the relay host (as a charlist).
- An explicit `sni` overrides the relay host.
- `verify_none` omits `server_name_indication` even with a relay host.

All 28 email transport tests and 11 Kafka TLS tests pass; clean compile with `--warnings-as-errors`.

## Version

Bumped to `0.2.1` and added a `Fixed` entry to the changelog.

body:
## Rung R3 — HEXA-OWN L5-E5: HX3027 use-while-mutably-borrowed (Rust E0503)

Rung R3 of `state/hexa-own/round3_dual_lane_batch_plan.json` §3. **opt-in** (`HEXA_BORROWCK=1`), byteeq-neutral (every new site gated on `_bck_active`, default false). **`types.hexa` UNTOUCHED.** Pure clone-extension of the merged E4 write-through machinery.

### What
The E-ladder's spec'd next rung after E4 (E4 changelog: "다음 rung=E5"). E1/E2/E3/E4 cover E0515/E0502/E0506; the remaining rustc sibling that fits the substrate (no place projection) is **E0503 — "cannot use `x` because it was mutably borrowed"**: a READ (use of value) of `x` while a live `&mut x` loan exists. E5=E0503 is this plan's design decision (E5 was never independently spec'd).

Unlike E4 write-through (invalidates BOTH `&`/`&mut` loans), **E0503 keys on the mutability bit** — a use of `x` while only a shared `&x` loan is live is SILENT.

### Diffs (re-anchored vs current `origin/main`)
- `compiler/lower/hir_to_mir.hexa` — `_bck_in_borrow_rhs` flag · `_bck_ref_find_mut_loan` (E4 END-scan narrowed with `_bck_ref_mut`) · `_bck_emit_use_while_mut` (HX3027 + STRICT caller-severity-override, builder.hexa:244) · `_bck_check_use` E5 rule **before** the `ti<0` aggregate early-return (scalar origins are never group-tracked) · unop arm sets the borrow-RHS suppression flag.
- `compiler/diag/catalog.hexa` — HX3027 DiagSpec after HX3023 (mirror: Severity::Warning, STRICT→Error, flow-insensitive FP class, Rust E0503 cite). catalog-uniqueness gate: **61 codes, all unique**.
- `compiler/check/borrowck_test.hexa` — `_run_use_while_mut_probe` + `_run_reborrow_suppress_probe` + sources.
- `ARCHITECTURE.json` — L5 cell current-ized (E1–E5 all merged; stale "#4557 미배선" removed). Single-line **record-only** edit.
- `state/hexa-own/e5_hx3027_use_while_mut_design.md` — design note.

### §5.2 double-fire audit (required)
- **first-borrow self-fire**: `let m = &mut x` lowers the RHS **before** `_bck_ref_track` → loan absent at inner read → harmless (flag also suppresses).
- **RE-borrow double-fire — CONFIRMED, SUPPRESSED**: `let m = &mut x  let n = &mut x` — the 2nd `&mut x` RHS read of `x` matches the live loan `m` and (without suppression) fires HX3027 **while** registration fires HX3021 (E3) = double-report of one mistake. A re-borrow is E0499/E0502's (our HX3021), not E0503's (use-of-value). Fixed with `_bck_in_borrow_rhs`; probe `fp_reborrow_suppress` asserts **HX3027=0, HX3021=1**.
- **assign-LHS double-fire (E4)**: an ident assign-LHS (`x = 5`) resolves via `_mir_lookup`, never through the ident READ hook → E5 cannot fire on a write target → E4 (HX3023) is the sole reporter. **CLEAN, no suppression needed.**

### Test matrix (`_run_use_while_mut_probe`, keyed HX3027)
| probe | source | ON |
|---|---|---|
| hz_use_while_mut | `let m=&mut x  let y=x+1` | 1 |

## Summary

Adds a full book-ingestion pipeline to the Dagster + Neo4j knowledge-retrieval stack, mirroring the existing paper pipeline. Books are discovered as PDFs, parsed per-page with outline extraction, split into a Chapter/Section tree, chunked with embeddings, and written to the graph with concept extraction and resolution per chapter.

Implemented from the design spec and 14-task TDD plan in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-05-book-ingestion.md` (each task: implement → dual review → fix, executed via the workflow script in the same directory).

## What's included

- **Schema**: `Chapter`/`Section`/`Document` node labels, book hierarchy relationships (`PART_OF`, `HAS_DOCUMENT`, `STATES`, cross-chapter `DEPENDS_ON`)
- **Identity**: book id from ISBN > title; deterministic chapter/section node ids
- **Parsing**: per-page PDF parsing with outline extraction; outline → chapter/section tree with page ranges and heading fallback; fixture book generator for tests
- **Dagster assets**: `books`/`book_chapters` partitions, `BOOKS_SOURCE_DIR`, raw + parsed assets, `book_metadata` (frontmatter + ISBN regex, duplicate check), `book_structure` (tree artifact + chapter partition registration), `book_chunks` (page-aware section chunking, batched embeddings)
- **Graph writes**: structure write (Book/Chapter/Section/Chunk), chapter extraction with context headers and page attribution, `book_chapter_resolved` reusing the paper `resolve_concepts` stack, chapter graph write
- **Orchestration**: `ingest_book` + `extract_book_chapter` jobs, discovery + auto-enqueue sensors
- **Tests**: unit coverage throughout (204 passing) plus 4 end-to-end integration tests (structure e2e, section grounding, shared Lévy concept across chapters, idempotency)

Also carries two small earlier commits on this branch: Paper→Document `HAS_DOCUMENT` link fix and per-chunk extraction progress logging.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest`: **204 passed**, 8 deselected (integration), exit 0
- Dagster definitions load cleanly (17 asset keys)

author: jpoley
body:
## Problem
#155: no way to redact secrets in the live terminal / recording playback for safe screen-sharing. Spike confirmed **nothing was redacted today** — live writes, playback, and `.cast` recordings all stored/rendered raw.

## Approach
- **Pure engine** (`lib/redaction/mask.ts`): masks known secret shapes (`sk-`, AKIA/ASIA, JWT, `Bearer …`, `ghp_`/`github_pat_`, `xox[baprs]-`, hex≥32) + explicit `knownValues`. ANSI/OSC/DCS/control sequences pass through untouched; a stream masker carries unsafe trailing bytes (partial token incl. `Bearer ` introducer, or incomplete escape) across chunk boundaries; bounded 4096 carry; backtracking-safe regexes; flush on close.
- **Global toggle** (`lib/presentation-mode.ts` via `useSyncExternalStore` + localStorage): app-wide, persists across nav, syncs across tabs; visible active banner ("best-effort, not a security guarantee").
- Applied at the live-write boundary (`Terminal.tsx`, `GhosttyTerminal.tsx`) and playback boundary (`TerminalPlayer.tsx`). Visual-only + reversible — recording data never modified; a future redact-at-capture mode is stubbed.

## Tests
23 redaction tests (no false-negative on listed shapes + true-negative bounds: prose, versions, dotted ids, sub-threshold hex) + a property test asserting streaming == whole-string across every split point + a persistence-store test. typecheck ✓, lint ✓, 1615 pass, build ✓.

## Known limitation (in UI copy)
Scrollback rendered *before* toggling on is not retroactively masked (xterm write-boundary); new output is masked, no data altered. Best-effort visual masking, not DLP.

CI on self-hosted runner. Copilot not requested (org billing; non-blocking).

Closes #155


---

**Round 3 (Copilot re-review of the round-2 fixes):** Guard the presentation-mode localStorage write for non-browser/SSR runtimes.

Supersedes #332. CI on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` (public repo). Verified green locally: lint, typecheck, audit:auth, test, build.

author: ptr727
body:
Documents the governing motivation behind the branch, release, and versioning rules, which were previously captured only as mechanics.

- **Pull vs push distribution** grounds release restraint (no release on push, no-op republish, maintainer-gated bumps): a release can reach push-channel users (HACS, main-vendoring consumers) unasked, so it must mark a real functional change, not churn.
- **Dual-target branch sync** (Dependabot/codegen hit both develop and main) is what makes the signed + linear + no-backport model possible - forward sync means a develop->main promotion never needs a main->develop back-merge.
- **Two version numbers**: the 2-digit major.minor carries human meaning at the maintainer's discretion; NBGV always increments the build.
- **Contracts state what, not how**, and favor reuse (the orchestration/build seam).

Placed as a new top section in AGENTS.md so the why is read before the specific rules. References existing sections rather than restating them.

body:
Enhancements:
- Narrowing inlays render as `▶` at an introduction and `◀` at a kill, with the narrowed-to (or reverted-to) type moved into the hover tooltip. The previous `▸<type>` / `◂<type>` labels were unreadable at Fira Code's inline size.
- Hover on a flow-narrowed symbol renders the narrowed type on a `▶` line beneath the declared type, matching the direction sigil used by narrowing-introduction inlays.

Bugs fixed:
- A narrowing site in the left operand of `/\` or `\/` emitted its inlay twice - three times when nested. `compile_operators.pre_binary` pre-analyses the left to thread the right operand's narrowing env, and the enclosing `if` / `while` / `assert` then analyses the whole condition; both walks emitted. `CONDITION_ANALYZER` gained an `analyze_condition_facts_only` entry that increments a silent-recursion counter around the walk, so the pre-analysis in `compile_operators` computes facts without emitting inlays and the enclosing walk stays the one emit site.
- Inlay hover text no longer refers to "the then edge" / "the else edge". The analyser flips these for `!` after the inlay is recorded, so a narrowing under a negated condition described the wrong branch. Tooltips now read "narrows {name} to {T} where the {test} succeeds" (and "... where the {test} fails" for the else-side complement inlays), which stays honest under any enclosing negation.

author: lucaagrippino
body:
## Summary

Implements `ISpi` (docs/lld/drivers/spi-driver.md) for SPI3 on the
STM32L475 (B-L475E-IOT01A): `spi_create`, `spi_transceive`. Sole
consumer is `WifiDriver` (ISM43362-M3G-L44 WiFi module, CON-001).
Gateway-only module — no Field Device counterpart.

## What this PR contains

- `firmware/gateway/drivers/spi_driver/spi_driver.{c,h}` — ADT pattern
  (opaque `spi_handle_t`, static pool of 1 — only SPI3 is used on this
  board, but the pattern is applied for API consistency, SPID-D6)
- `tests/gateway/drivers/spi_driver/test_spi_driver.c` — 14 unit tests,
  all passing
- `firmware/gateway/integration-tests/spi_driver/main_test_spi_driver.c`
  — hardware bring-up test (not compiled by default)
- `tests/mocks/stm32l475xx.h`/`.c` — new `SPI_TypeDef`, `SPI3` macro,
  `RCC_APB1ENR1_SPI3EN` (bit 15) and CR1/CR2/SR bit definitions,
  verified against the real vendor CMSIS header
- `tests/project.yml` — new `:test_spi_driver:` block (`STM32L475xx`,
  `TEST`)
- `docs/lld/drivers/spi-driver.md` — companion bumped to v0.2 (Phase H
  complete, ADT pattern, both open items resolved)

## Design decisions

- **Mode 0, 16-bit frames, FRXTH=0.** The ISM43362 requires 16-bit SPI
  frames; on STM32L4, FRXTH must be 0 for RXNE to assert correctly at
  16 bits (companion §3.3) — FRXTH=1 would fire RXNE after only 8 bits,
  corrupting reads.
- **Polling only, no ISR/DMA.** `WifiTask` is the sole accessor by
  construction (single task, no concurrent access possible), so a
  blocking transfer is the simplest correct model; DMA would add
  complexity with no benefit at these transfer sizes.
- **NSS/DATARDY out of scope.** `WifiDriver USES SpiDriver, GpioDriver`
  independently — NSS timing is part of the AT command protocol
  (WifiDriver's concern), not the byte-transfer concern. SpiDriver
  never touches NSS or DATARDY.
- **Bounded polling timeout, no CpuDriver dependency.** `SpiDriver`'s
  `USES` is CMSIS only per `components.md`; timeouts use a decrementing
  iteration counter (matching the existing `QspiFlashDriver` idiom),
  not `cpu_delay_ms`/DWT, to avoid widening the USES footprint.

## Test evidence

- `test:all`: 498 tests, 0 fail, 7 ignored (pre-existing) — 484 + 14
  new, no regressions
- cppcheck (`--enable=style,warning,performance`): clean
- clang-format: clean
- `tests/support`/`tests/mocks`/`tests/project.yml` diff against
  `origin/main` confirmed additive-only

body: ## Problem #185 (CRITICAL): the app container ran as root with the host Docker socket mounted — any RCE/SSRF elsewhere escalated straight to host root. ## Approach - **Dockerfile**: final stage runs `USER node` (uid 1000); pre-creates node-owned write paths (`.secrets.json` location, data, logs, next cache) so cwd writes and the `daax-data` volume seed land node-owned. - **compose (daax service, both files)**: `group_add: ${DOCKER_GID}` + `cap_drop: [ALL]` + `no-new-privileges` — socket access is now group-based, not uid-0. - **rebuild.sh**: local `docker run` path derives the host docker GID and passes `--group-add` / `--cap-drop ALL` / `--security-opt no-new-privileges` (without this the non-root image can't reach the socket in local dev). - **tests/deploy/nonroot-hardening.test.ts**: regression guard (final USER non-root; both compose files keep the three hardening flags). ## Verified live `docker build` ✓; `docker run --rm id` → `uid=1000(node)`; socket access group-gated (correct GID → `docker version` works, wrong GID → permission denied); terminal server boots non-root and creates the spawn-target dirs `1000:1000` with no root chown. ## ⚠️ Operator actions before prod (also in compose comments) - **`DOCKER_GID` must equal the host socket GID** (`stat -c '%g' /var/run/docker.sock`). `deploy-local.sh`/`rebuild.sh` derive it; plain `docker compose up` needs it set if host GID ≠ 999. - **Existing `daax-data` volume** (created by the old root image) is root-owned — `docker volume rm daax-data` once after upgrade, or app writes EACCES. - `read_only` rootfs **deferred** (documented) — app writes scattered cwd paths + `/home/node/.mcp-gateway`. ## Tests / CI typecheck ✓, lint ✓ (0 err), test ✓ (1600 pass incl. new), both compose `docker compose config` ✓. author: mikemcdougall
body:
# Pull Request

## Issue Link
Related to #2482
Related to #1948

<!-- #2482 acceptance covered by THIS PR: promote a completed analysis job's result artifact into a queryable/renderable published layer (the analyze → render link). NOT covered here (out of scope): styling tools and Build App `deployment` promotion — so Related to (not Closes) #2482. -->

## Summary

Adds `honua_publish_result`, the geospatial-mcp `publish_result` reference tool, which promotes a **completed analysis job's** materialized FeatureLayer/Table artifact into a **hosted, queryable/renderable layer**. This is the missing link in the north-star workflow ("parcels within 500m of flood zone → STYLED MAP"): until now analysis results lived only at `honua://jobs/{id}/results` and could not become a layer, so an agent could never render what it computed.

The tool does **not** reimplement publishing or invent a parallel materialization path. It resolves the job's result package through the canonical `IGeoprocessingJobService` (the same seam `honua://jobs/{id}/results` reads), reads the selected artifact's materialized-table coordinates, and routes the promotion through the **very same `service.publish` operation (`IOperationInvoker`)** that `honua_publish_service` uses — sharing the operator-approval gate, metadata revision, and multi-outcome (`Completed` / `Queued` / `RequiresApproval` / `Denied`) contract. A completed promotion returns `serviceId` + `layerId` the agent chains straight into `honua_query_features` / `honua_render_map`.

Supported artifact kinds: **FeatureLayer** and **Table** (vector/tabular datasets the job materialized into a table). Scalar/Raster/File/Report/Map/AppBundle are rejected with a structured error. Large artifacts are promoted **by reference** (the tool publishes the materialized table, never the artifact bytes), so payload size is irrelevant. Structured errors flow through the shared `McpErrorMapper` channel: `not_found` (unknown job/artifact), `failed_precondition` (job not terminal, artifact not a materialized table, `deployment` target), `invalid_argument` (unsupported artifact kind / ambiguous selection), `unauthenticated`.

author: oussamalakhdar90
body:
## Why (the "Unchanged caveat" — placeholder info/servers)

The overlay itself (`#274`) is correct, but `ContractValidationService` took `req.specs().get(0)` **blindly** as the metadata source. A scan can supply several sources (a Confluence page, a fragment, the real OpenAPI doc); if the metadata-rich spec isn't first, the overlay has nothing to lift → the corrected "drop-in" YAML keeps placeholder `info`/`servers`.

## Fix

- `CorrectedSpecBuilder.carriesMetadata(spec)` — true when the spec parses **and** has a non-empty `info`/`servers` (or Swagger-2.0 `host`); reuses the raised-limit YAMLMapper.
- `ContractValidationService.pickMetadataSpec(specs, builder)` — the first spec that `carriesMetadata`, else first non-blank, else null. Replaces the blind `get(0)`.

## Tests (reproduce the real failure)

- `carriesMetadata` detects info/servers/host, rejects fragments/blank/non-mapping.
- `pickMetadataSpec` picks the metadata spec **even when it is not first** (`[fragment, real] → real`).
- **End-to-end:** the selected spec makes the corrected YAML carry the real `CIAM Policies / 1.0.5 / servers` (not the unit builder in isolation).
- Fallback to first-non-blank / null. Full suite green (2572).

## If a single metadata-rich spec still shows placeholders after this
That's a **deployment lag** (rebuild `C:\TestAuto\veritas` from latest main) or a source genuinely lacking `info`/`servers` — `#274`'s `@Slf4j` guard logs (`grep "CorrectedSpecBuilder:"`) say which.

author: killerqueen-z
body:
## What

Tags every x402 payment XClawRouter signs with the **ERC-8021 Schema 2 service code** `s: ["blockrun"]`, so payments routed through XClawRouter are attributed to BlockRun on-chain.

Reference: [CDP Builder Codes](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/x402/core-concepts/builder-codes)

## How

- New `src/builder-code.ts`: `withBuilderCodeServiceCode()` merges `s: ["blockrun"]` into a payload's `builder-code.info`, **preserving any app code (`a`)** the server echoed back. Pure, non-mutating.
- In `proxy.ts`, an `onAfterPaymentCreation` hook stamps it onto `context.paymentPayload.extensions`.

## Why a hook (not `registerExtension` / a dep bump)

The official `BuilderCodeClientExtension` only enriches when the **server advertises** `builder-code` in its 402, and needs `@x402/*` bumped 2.11 → 2.17. The hook mirrors that extension's output but fires **unconditionally** with **no dependency change**. Safe because the EIP-712 signature covers the authorization, not `extensions`; the CDP facilitator reads `builder-code.info.s` and does the CBOR/ERC-8021 encoding.

## Test

- `src/builder-code.test.ts` (4 cases). Full suite green: **510 passed**, typecheck + build (ESM + DTS) clean.

## Related

Mirror of BlockRunAI/ClawRouter#198. Tracked in BlockRunAI/blockrun#199. Sibling PRs: blockrun-llm-ts#9, blockrun-llm#21, blockrun-llm-go#2.

body:
## Reverts #574 to restore a green main

**Why:** #574 ("feat: emergency pause, milestone withdrawals, and per-campaign tokens") was merged on 2026-07-01 while its own CI was red, and it does not compile. main has been broken ever since, which is why **every open stellar PR shows the same errors** (fmt/clippy/test) — they all rebase/merge onto a broken main.

The breakage in #574:
- duplicate `set_emergency_pause_signers` import vs the local fn (E0255)
- missing lifetime on `token_client_for_address` (E0106)
- `Vec::iter_mut` in `verify_milestone` (unsupported by soroban Vec, E0599)
- `s == &caller` type mismatch in `emergency_pause` (E0308)
- unused imports `Vec`, `token_client`, `set_emergency_pause_signers` (fail `-D warnings`)
- ~33 test call-sites missing the new `token`/`uses_milestones` fields on both `CreateCampaignParams` and `Campaign` (E0063)
- **E0277**: `token: Option<Address>` in a `#[contracttype]` struct is not ScVal-convertible in the pinned soroban-sdk — this one is a real data-model issue, not mechanical.

This revert restores the last green commit (368b0f61). The feature should be re-submitted as a fresh PR with passing CI (the `Option<Address>` representation needs rethinking so it satisfies `#[contracttype]`).

author: jpoley
body:
## Problem
#101 (F5): daax had no identity store and enforced nothing — admin was gated only by the client-visible `NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_MODE`.

## Approach
- **Migration** `1781568000300_rbac-identity.js` (reversible): `users` (subject PK = stable Pocket ID subject; username/email/name mutable), `roles` (seeded admin+user), `user_roles` (with `granted_by` provenance), `pending_grants` (first-admin bootstrap before a users row exists), `auth_audit` (append-only). Permission catalog in-code (§3); roles/user_roles are DB tables.
- **JIT** (`lib/rbac/store.ts`): `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (subject) DO UPDATE … RETURNING (xmax=0)` — default role granted **only when new**; a user with all roles revoked is **not** re-granted (revocation-safe).
- **Reconcile** under `pg_advisory_xact_lock`: allow-list matches subject OR email/username; pre-creates a pending admin grant (no first-login lockout); prunes only `granted_by='reconcile'`; maps groups→roles.
- **Enforcement**: `requireRole(perm)` in `lib/auth.ts` — JIT-provisions, resolves DB roles, **fails closed** on unconfigured/unreachable Postgres, audits every decision. Provenance-admin routes upgraded `requireAuth`→`requireRole`. `NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_MODE` retired for settings/provenance via server-resolved `/api/auth/access` (fails safe to non-admin).

## Tests (all green except one honestly-unrun)
- Unit: 34 new (permission/role resolution, allow-list matching, reconcile diff, requireRole deny/allow/**fail-closed**+audit). Total 1617 pass.
- Integration (throwaway Docker PG): 8/8 — xmax JIT insert-vs-update, **revoked-no-regrant**, first-admin bootstrap (email+subject), reconcile prunes only reconcile-grants, group→role sync, migration up/down round-trip.
- E2E: operator/admin-allowed half passes; the strict unauth→blocked spec is **implemented but unrun** here (needs real Traefik + Pocket ID / `DAAX_AUTH_BASE_URL`) — not faked.
- typecheck ✓, lint ✓, build ✓. CI on self-hosted runner.

## Honest scope caveats
- In-process terminal-server `requireRole` not added (terminal server/components owned by other branches; `/api/terminal/ticket` already auth'd, default `user` role holds `terminal:exec`).
- Middleware authN 401s (pre-identity default-deny) are **not** DB-audited — a per-request DB write on unauthenticated probes would be a DoS amplifier. All `requireRole` authZ decisions are audited.
- Enforcement applied to the admin/provenance surface (D2 destructive/admin-first), not swept across every mutating route.

Copilot not requested (org billing; non-blocking). Closes #101


---

## Review fixes (3 rounds, gh-101)

**Round 3 (Copilot re-review of the round-2 fixes):** Upgrade group-sync provenance to reconcile on allow-list/reconcile grants so an allow-listed admin is not revoked when they leave the IdP group.

Supersedes #333. CI on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` (public repo). Verified green locally: lint, typecheck, audit:auth, test, build.

**Validation:** produced by Claude Fable 5; three adversarial review rounds (a separate Claude reviewer + GitHub Copilot on rounds 2 and 3); all confirmed findings fixed. Non-bug nits and stack-staleness flags (resolved by the required parent-first merge order) are intentionally not chased.

author: silverbucket
body:
Closes #127

## Summary

Two small, backward-compatible additions to `SecureStore`, per the spec in #127:

### 1. `ttl` config option (sliding expiry)

- `ttl?: number` (milliseconds) on `SecureStoreConfig`. Validated in the constructor: must be a positive integer, otherwise `ValidationError`.
- `save()` pipelines `HSET` + `PEXPIRE` in a `MULTI` transaction; `get()` refreshes the window with `HGET` + `PEXPIRE`. Both commands in each transaction target the same Redis key, so this is Cluster-safe. `PEXPIRE` on a missing key is a no-op, so `get()` needs no existence check.
- A shared `assertExecSucceeded()` helper surfaces aborted transactions and per-command errors as `ConnectionError`.
- Unset (default) → no expiry, zero behavior change for existing users.

### 2. `deleteAll(postfix?)` method

- `DEL {uid}[:postfix]` behind the usual `isConnected` guard, mirroring `delete()`'s structure. Returns 0 or 1.
- Also exposed on `TypedNamespace` (`namespace(name).deleteAll()` delegates with the namespace as postfix).
- Per the issue's non-goal, no `SCAN` sweep — one Redis key per call; namespaced stores need one call per namespace (documented).

### README

Documents both features, including the idle-expiry caveat (TTL is refreshed only by operations — size it as a backstop, not a session timeout) and the per-namespace `deleteAll()` scope.

## Tests

author: pos-ei-don
body:
## Problem
A proxy host with a **Custom Location** pointing at a *different* upstream (e.g. `/paperless` -> a Paperless container) **and** `Cache Assets` enabled returns **404** for static files under that path (`/paperless/static/app.js`, `.css`, ...). The Custom Location's HTML/API paths work; only asset extensions break.

## Root cause
`Cache Assets` includes a server-level regex location `location ~* \.(css|js|png|...)$ { proxy_pass <main upstream>; }`. In nginx, **regex locations take precedence over prefix locations**, so this regex beats the Custom Location `location {{ path }}` (plain prefix) generated by `_location.conf`. Asset requests under custom paths are routed to the **main** upstream (which doesn't know them) -> 404. The UI offers no way to raise the custom location's priority.

Related: #2557, #1981, #4423.

## Change
Emit custom locations as `location ^~ {{ path }}`. `^~` gives the prefix location precedence over regex locations, so the cached-asset regex no longer hijacks custom-location paths.

## Caveat
`^~` disables regex matching *within* that path. Users who intend a Custom Location path as a regex would be affected. If custom paths may be regex, a guarded variant (only `^~` for plain prefixes) would be safer — happy to adjust based on maintainer preference.

## Test
1. Proxy host `example` -> upstream A; Custom Location `/sub` -> upstream B serving `/sub/x.js`.
2. Enable `Cache Assets` -> `/sub/x.js` = 404 (bug).
3. With this change -> `/sub/x.js` = 200 from B; main-upstream assets still cached.

author: mayurkhera-health
body:
Fixes the recurring `scheduler_calendar_sync failed: last run 428 min ago (> 420)` alert.

**Root cause:** in-memory APScheduler timers reset on every deploy/restart; a mid-cycle restart pushes the next 6h calendar-sync run up to 6h past schedule, tripping the 420-min watchdog (the notifications 15-min job is unaffected because its timer stays well under its threshold).

**Fix (Option B), calendar_sync only:**
- initial (no prior run) → one immediate sync, logs "no prior run — running initial sync"
- stale (>6h) → one immediate catch-up
- fresh (≤6h) → re-anchor the interval's first run to `last_success + 6h` (fresh branch only; a past-dated `next_run_time` elsewhere would double-fire)
- concurrency: atomic CAS claim (gated on `last_run_at`) + in-process skip-if-running lock
- notifications job and the 420-min alert threshold unchanged

**Tests:** `tests/test_scheduler_catchup.py` — 4h (re-anchor, no catch-up), 7h (one catch-up), NULL heartbeat (initial sync + row creation + log line), concurrency CAS single-winner. Existing `test_health_service` / `test_ics_sync` green.
